en: *The Compendium of the Reality of All Tathāgatas*, edited by Horiuchi (STT volume, page, section) [marginal numbers]
The Great King of Rituals named *Sarvatathāgatamahāyānābhisamaya* (The Realization of the Mahāyāna of All Tathāgatas),
the Detailed Procedure for the Great Maṇḍala of the Vajradhātu.
Thus have I heard:
At one time (STT 1,1,2),
the Blessed One was endowed with the various distinctions of the wisdom of the commitment (*samaya*) empowered by the vajra of all Tathāgatas (STT 1,1,2).

He has attained the consecration into the sovereignty over the Dharma of the triple world, with the jeweled crown of all Tathāgatas. He is the great Lord of Yogins possessing the omniscient wisdom of all Tathāgatas.
Having realized the equality of all mudrās of all Tathāgatas, he performs universal activities and fulfills every aspiration of the entire realm of sentient beings, leaving none remaining.

The Great Compassionate One, Vairocana, the Eternal, established in the samaya of the three times, the Tathāgata who is the vajra of all actions, speech, and mind, dwelt in the palace of Akaniṣṭha, the king of gods— a place praised and extolled as the abode of all Tathāgatas, inlaid with great precious jewels, adorned with bells of various colors, and graced by wind-swayed silk streamers, garlands, chowries, necklaces, half-necklaces, and crescent moons. (STT 1,2,3–4)
Together with ninety-nine koṭis of bodhisattvas,
such as the bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi.
And by the bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara,
and by Ākāśagarbha,
and by Vajramuṣṭi.
And with Mañjuśrī;
and with Sahacittotpādadharmacakrapravartin;
and with Gaganagañja.
And with Sarvamārabalapramardin at their head,
there were ninety-nine billion bodhisattvas;
and Tathāgatas equal in number to the sands of the river Gaṅgā were also seen, such that Jambūdvīpa appeared completely filled, like a sesame pod.

And by means of those immeasurable bodies of the Tathāgata, from each single body of the Tathāgata, immeasurable and incalculable Buddha-fields are manifested; and in those Buddha-fields, they teach this very method of the Dharma.
(STT 1,23,6) Then the Blessed One Mahāvairocana, whose vajra-body, speech, and mind are eternally present throughout the entire realm of space, (STT 1,9,7) [taught: ...
He is the Knowledge Being (*jñānasattva*) who awakens to the entire vajra-realm by means of the convergence of all Tathāgatas;
he is the womb of knowledge arising from the vajra-consecration of the atoms of dust within the entire realm of space;
he is the jewel of the great vajra-knowledge consecration due to the infinity of all Tathāgatas.

He has attained the perfect awakening to the knowledge of suchness that pervades all space; because the self-nature of all Tathāgatas is pure, he is one for whom all phenomena are pure by their very nature. He is the supreme practitioner who disciplines the entire realm of sentient beings without exception through the knowledge that manifests all forms pervading all space; because he carries out the unerring commands of all Tathāgatas, he performs all diverse activities that are peerless and unsurpassed. He is the steadfast being of the great enlightenment of all Tathāgatas.
The pledge of summoning all Tathāgatas; the Lord of Wisdom who delights all Tathāgatas; the one who grants the cry of "Well done! to all Tathāgatas.
The great jewel of the consecration of all Tathāgatas; the solar orb of light of all Tathāgatas; the crest-jewel of the wish-fulfilling king-gem of all Tathāgatas.
The great laughter of all Tathāgatas;
the great pure dharma of all Tathāgatas; the wisdom-knowledge of all Tathāgatas.
The wheel of all Tathāgatas;
the intentional language of all Tathāgatas;
the unfailing performance of all diverse activities of all Tathāgatas.
He possesses the extremely firm armor of the great heroism of all Tathāgatas;
he is the Vajra-yakṣa who provides protection and guardianship for all Tathāgatas;
and he possesses the knowledge of the mudrās that bind the vajras of the body, speech, and mind of all Tathāgatas.
Samantabhadra, Svayambhū, Amogha, Māra, Prāmodyanāyaka; Khagarbha of great majesty, Ratnaketu, Mahāsmita; Avalokiteśvara, Maheśa, and Mañjuśrī, who encompasses all mandalas.
Avāca, Viśvakarman, Vīrya, Caṇḍa, and Dṛḍhagarbha;
(STT 1,13,11) Vajra, Aṅkuśa, Śara, Tuṣṭi, Ratna, Sūrya, Dhvaja, and Smita; (STT 1,13,14,12) Padma, Kośa, Sucakra, Vāk, Karma, Varma, Bhaya, and Graha. (STT 1,14,12)
Without beginning or end, peaceful, fierce, wrathful, and greatly patient;
a yakṣa, a divine rākṣasa, steadfast, the son of Sūrya, Śauri, and the great pervasive lord;
the husband of Umā, the lord of wisdom, Viṣṇu, the victorious one, and the great sage.
He is the world-protector, the sky, and the earth; he is the three worlds and the triple realm.
He is the great element, the one whose purpose is the welfare of all beings, the All, Śarva, and the Grandfather (Pitāmaha).
He is saṃsāra and nirvṛti, the eternal, the ever-present, the one of right conduct, and the Great Festival.
The Buddha is pure; he is the Mahāyāna, the three realms of existence, and indeed eternal.
He is the conqueror of the three worlds, Śambhu, the Lord Śambhunātha, and the Bestower.
He is Vajranātha, the foremost of the excellent grounds, primordial wisdom, and the method of the Pāramitās.

Liberation, the Bodhisattva, the practice, and all the Tathāgatas; the meaning of Buddhahood, the heart of the Buddha, all supreme enlightenment; Vairocana, the Victor, the Protector, the Self-Existent One, the dhāraṇī, and mindfulness.

The Mahāsattva, the Great Seal, is the samādhi that performs the deeds of a Buddha; he has become the essence of all Buddhas, a being who awakens to the meaning of the eternal. He is the Great Pillar, the Great Time, the Great Passion, and Great Bliss.

The great means, the most supreme of the supreme, the foremost of all, the Lord of the World— (STT 1,15,16) the Blessed One, the Great Bodhicitta, Samantabhadra, the Great Bodhisattva, dwelt within the hearts of all the Tathāgatas. (STT 1,22,17)
Then this buddha-field was completely filled by all the Tathāgatas, just as a sesame pod is full of seeds.

Then indeed, all the Tathāgatas, having assembled in a great gathering, approached the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Sarvārthasiddhi, who was seated at the seat of awakening (bodhimaṇḍa). Having approached, they revealed their vision to the Bodhisattva with their bodies of enjoyment (sāṃbhogika-kāya) and spoke thus:
"How, noble son, will you realize unexcelled, perfect enlightenment, you who venture upon all these difficult tasks while remaining ignorant of the reality of all Tathāgatas?

(STT 1,23,18) Then the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Sarvārthasiddhi, having been thus exhorted by all the Tathāgatas, arose from the *āsphānaka* concentration, prostrated before all the Tathāgatas, and having summoned them, spoke as follows: (STT 1,24,19)
"Blessed Tathāgatas, please command me! How should I practice? What is the nature of reality? When he had spoken thus, all the Tathāgatas spoke with one voice to that Bodhisattva:
"Practice, noble son, by means of the concentration on the examination of one's own mind, with the mantra that is naturally accomplished and recited according to one's inclination!"
"Oṃ, I perform the penetration of the mind. (STT 1,24,20) Then the Bodhisattva spoke thus to all the Tathāgatas:
"I have understood it, Blessed Tathāgatas; I see the form of a moon disc within my own heart. All the Tathāgatas replied: (STT 1,25,21)
“Noble son, this mind is luminous by nature; it becomes exactly as it is cultivated. It is just like dyeing a white cloth.

Then, in order to clarify the knowledge of the mind that is luminous by nature, all the Tathāgatas once again caused that Bodhisattva to generate the mind of awakening (*bodhicitta*) with this mantra, which is perfected by its very nature: *oṃ bodhicittam utpādayāmi*.
Then the Bodhisattva, once again generating the thought of awakening (*bodhicitta*) by the command of all the Tathāgatas, spoke thus:
"That which has the form of a lunar disc, I see as that very lunar disc.
All the Tathāgatas said:
"Your resolve for universal goodness (*samantabhadra-cittotpāda*) is the heart-essence of all Tathāgatas and has become perfectly realized.
Therefore, practice it well! For the sake of strengthening the resolve for universal goodness of all Tathāgatas, contemplate a vajra-form within the moon-maṇḍala of your own heart with this mantra:
*Oṃ tiṣṭha vajra!*"
The Bodhisattva said:
“I see, O Blessed Tathāgatas, a vajra within the lunar disc.
All the Tathāgatas said:
"Make firm this Samantabhadra-vajra of the mind of all Tathāgatas with this mantra:
*Oṃ, I am of vajra-nature!*" (STT 1,27,252).

Then, as many vajra-realms of the body, speech, and mind of all Tathāgatas as there are, encompassing the entire realm of space—all of them entered that Sattva-vajra through the empowerment of all the Tathāgatas. (STT 1,27,26)

Then that Blessed One, the Great Bodhisattva Sarvārthasiddhi, was consecrated by all the Tathāgatas with the vajra-name consecration: “Vajradhātu! Vajradhātu! (STT 1,27,26). Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajradhātu spoke thus to all those Tathāgatas:
“Blessed Tathāgatas, I see myself as the body of all the Tathāgatas. (STT 1,28,27)
All the Tathāgatas said:

“Therefore, O Mahāsattva! Visualize yourself as the body of a Buddha, the Sattvavajra, endowed with the excellence of all aspects! Having recited this mantra, which is accomplished by its very nature, according to your preference: ‘Oṃ, as all the Tathāgatas are, so am I.’”

Then, when this had been said, the Great Bodhisattva Vajradhātu, having realized himself as the Tathāgata, prostrated to all those Tathāgatas, summoned them, and spoke thus: "Empower me, O Blessed Tathāgatas! Make firm this perfect awakening! When this had been said, all the Tathāgatas entered that Sattvavajra of the Tathāgata Vajradhātu.

Then, at that very moment, the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Vajradhātu, having fully awakened to the wisdom of the equality of all Tathāgatas, entered the secret samaya of the mudrā of the vajra-equality wisdom of all Tathāgatas; purified by the realization of the nature of the wisdom of the equality of the Dharma of all Tathāgatas, and having become the embodiment of the wisdom-aspect of the natural luminosity of the universal equality of all Tathāgatas, he became a Tathāgata, an Arhat, a perfectly Awakened One. (STT 1,29,31)

Then all the Tathāgatas, having again emerged from those *sarvatathāgatasattvavajras*, were consecrated with the consecration of the great *ākāśagarbha-maṇiratna*; having generated the *dharmajñāna* of Avalokiteśvara and established him in the state of the universal activity (*viśvakarmatā*) of all the Tathāgatas, they proceeded to the summit of Mount Sumeru and to the gabled pavilion on the peak of the *vajramaṇiratna*.
Having approached the Tathāgata Vajradhātu and empowered him in the state of all Tathāgatas, they established him facing in every direction upon the lion-thrones of all the Tathāgatas.

(STT 1,30,32) Then indeed, the Tathāgata Akṣobhya, the Tathāgata Ratnasaṃbhava, the Tathāgata Lokeśvararāja, and the Tathāgata Amoghasiddhi—having themselves empowered their own selves in the state of all Tathāgatas—[did so] because of the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Śākyamuni’s, thorough penetration of universal equality. (STT 1,31,33)

Having taken recourse in the equality of all directions, they are seated in the four directions. (STT 1,31,33) Then the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Vairocana, who had recently attained perfect awakening; whose heart is that of Samantabhadra of all Tathāgatas; who was consecrated with the great jewel-gem consecration arising from the space of all Tathāgatas; who has reached the supreme perfection of the Dharma-knowledge of Avalokiteśvara of all Tathāgatas; whose teaching is unfailing and unimpeded in its universal activity for all Tathāgatas; whose work is fully accomplished; and whose desires are completely fulfilled—(STT 1,32,34)

Having himself empowered his own self as the state of all Tathāgatas, he entered the samādhi called the Vajra Empowerment of the Being Arising from the Samaya of the Universal Bodhisattva Samantabhadra of All Tathāgatas, and from his own heart issued forth this Heart of All Tathāgatas called the Realization of the Mahāyāna of All Tathāgatas:
"Vajrasattva."

Then, as soon as he had emerged from the hearts of all the Tathāgatas, that very Blessed One Samantabhadra became moon-maṇḍalas, issued forth, purified the great bodhicitta of all sentient beings, and stationed himself at every side of all the Tathāgatas.
(STT 1,36,36) Then, from those moon-maṇḍalas, the vajras of the gnosis of all the Tathāgatas issued forth and entered the heart of the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Vairocana. (STT 1,36,36)

And because of the extreme firmness of the *vajrasattva-samādhi* and through the empowerment (*adhiṣṭhāna*) of all the Tathāgatas, there appeared a vajra-form consisting of the vajra of the body, speech, and mind of all the Tathāgatas—a single mass, equal in measure to the entire expanse of space, garlanded with rays of light, five-headed. Emerging from the hearts of all the Tathāgatas, it came to rest in [the practitioner’s] hand.
Then, from that vajra, rays of light in the form of vajras, possessing various colors and forms, issued forth, pervading and illuminating all world-systems.

And from those vajra-ray mouths, Tathāgata-forms as numerous as the atoms in all world-systems issued forth, [proceeding] to all convergences within the entire realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*), reaching the limits of the entire realm of space, throughout oceans of clouds of the expansion of all world-systems, due to the perfect awakening to the universal gnosis and supernormal knowledges of all Tathāgatas.

Having manifested all the miraculous transformations of the Tathāgatas—beginning with the generation of the great bodhicitta of all Tathāgatas, the accomplishment of the various practices of Samantabhadra, the gathering of the families of all Tathāgatas, the approach to the seat of great enlightenment (mahābodhimaṇḍa), and the turning of the wheel of the sublime Dharma, up to the protection of the entire realm of sentient beings without exception, the bestowal of all benefit and happiness, and the accomplishment of the supreme siddhis of the wisdom and supernormal powers of all Tathāgatas; (STT 1,3637,39)

Due to the samādhi of Vajrasattva, which is universal excellence (*samantabhadratva*), and because of its extreme firmness, the single solid body of the Great Bodhisattva Samantabhadra was manifested. Abiding in the heart of the Blessed One Vairocana, he uttered this inspired utterance (*udāna*):
"Aho! I am Samantabhadra, the firm being (*dṛḍhasattva*) of the self-arisen ones; for through my firmness, though I am bodiless, I have attained the state of a being-body (*sattvakāyatva*)."
Then the body of the Great Bodhisattva Samantabhadra, having emerged from the heart of the Blessed One and taken his place upon a moon disc in front of all the Tathāgatas, awaited an instruction.

Then the Blessed One, having entered the meditative absorption called the "Vajra of the Samaya of the Wisdom of All Tathāgatas," [manifested] the great samaya of the wisdom of great knowledge, power, and vigor, which constitutes the great skillful means for the benefit of sentient beings through the turning of the wheel of Dharma characterized by the ethical discipline, concentration, wisdom, liberation, and the vision of the knowledge of liberation of all Tathāgatas; and for the sake of protecting the realm of sentient beings without exception or remainder, and for the sake of experiencing all sovereignty, happiness, and mental well-being—up to...

For the sake of attaining the fruit of the supreme accomplishment of the realization of the Great Vehicle—the superknowledge of the wisdom of the equality of all Tathāgatas—he consecrated that Vajra of the Accomplishment of All Tathāgatas with the jeweled crown and ribbon of the body of all Buddhas for the sovereignty of all Tathāgatas over the Great Bodhisattva Samantabhadra, and bestowed it upon him with his two hands.
Then, by all the Tathāgatas, he was consecrated with the vajra-name-consecration: "Vajrapāṇi! Vajrapāṇi! (STT 1,40,42).
Then the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi, cradling the left vajra with joy, held that vajra at his own heart by means of the yoga of drawing it upward, and uttered this inspired utterance:
"This is that unsurpassed *siddhivajra* of all the Buddhas;
the vajra given into my hand is established as a vajra."

Then the Blessed One again entered the samādhi called the Vajra of the Empowerment of the Being Arising from the Samaya of the Great Bodhisattva Amogharāja, and from his own heart he emitted this Heart-mantra of all Tathāgatas:
"Vajrarāja."

Then, as soon as it had issued forth from the hearts of all the Tathāgatas, that very Blessed One Vajrapāṇi became the great hooks of all the Tathāgatas and, having issued forth, entered the heart of the Blessed One Vairocana. Having appeared as a single mass, the great form of the Vajra-hook, he was established in the hand of the Blessed One.
Then, from that great form of the Vajra-hook...

As many Tathāgata-forms as there are atoms in all world-systems issued forth; having performed all the miraculous displays of the Buddhas, such as summoning all the Tathāgatas, and because of his own state as Amogharāja and the extreme firmness of the Vajrasattva-samādhi, they merged into a single, solid mass—the body of the Great Bodhisattva Amogharāja—and standing in the heart of the Blessed One Vairocana, he uttered this inspired utterance:
"Aho! I am indeed Amogharāja, the hook born of the vajra."
"By which all-pervading Buddhas are drawn forth as accomplishments.

(STT 1,42,46) Then that body of the Great Bodhisattva Amogharāja, having emerged from the heart of the Blessed One, took its place upon the lunar mandala to the right of all the Tathāgatas and once again sought their command. (STT 1,42,47)

Then the Blessed One, having entered the samādhi called the Vajra of the Samaya for Attracting All Tathāgatas, gave that vajra-hook with both hands to the Great Bodhisattva Amogharāja in the same manner as before, for the sake of the samaya of attracting all Tathāgatas, for the purpose of attracting the entire realm of sentient beings without exception and for them to experience all happiness and mental well-being, and so on, up to the supreme accomplishment of the empowerment of the assembly of all Tathāgatas.
Then he was consecrated by all the Tathāgatas with the vajra-name consecration, saying: “Vajrākarṣa, Vajrākarṣa! (STT 1,43,48).
Then the Bodhisattva Vajrākarṣa, drawing in all the Tathāgatas with that vajra-hook, uttered this inspired utterance:
“This is that unsurpassed vajra-knowledge of all the Buddhas. (STT 1,43,49)

"That which is the supreme summoning for the sake of accomplishing the purpose of all Buddhas. (STT 1,43,49) Then the Blessed One again entered the samādhi called the Vajra of the Empowerment of the Being Arising from the Samaya of the Great Bodhisattva Māra, and from his own heart he emitted this Heart-mantra of all Tathāgatas, called the Samaya of the Enamouring of all Tathāgatas: (STT 1,43,50) "Vajrarāga" (STT 1,43,50).

Then, as soon as it had issued forth from the hearts of all the Tathāgatas, that very Blessed One Vajradhara became the weapons of the flowers of all the Tathāgatas; having issued forth and entered the heart of the Blessed One Vairocana, he appeared as a single mass in the form of a great vajra-arrow and was established in [the Buddha's] hand.

Then, from that form of the Vajra-Arrow, Tathāgata-forms as numerous as the atoms in all world-systems emerged. Having performed all the miraculous displays of the Buddhas, such as the enchantment of all Tathāgatas, and because of the extreme gentleness [of his intent] and the great firmness of the Vajrasattva-samādhi, he became a single, solid mass—the body of the Great Bodhisattva Māra. Abiding in the heart of the Blessed One Vairocana, he uttered this inspired utterance:
"Aho! I am pure by nature, the self-arisen one’s passion!"
"For it is for the sake of purification that those who are detached indeed discipline [themselves] through passion.

(STT 1,44,51) Then that body of Māra, the Great Bodhisattva, having emerged from the heart of the Blessed One and taken its place upon the moon-maṇḍalas to the left of all the Tathāgatas, once again sought the command. (STT 1,44,51)

Then the Blessed One, having entered the samādhi called the Vajra of the Empowerment of the Passion of All Tathāgatas, for the sake of the Vajra-samaya of the Slaying of All Tathāgatas—in order that all beings without exception or remainder might experience passion, and all happiness and mental well-being, up until the attainment of the fruit of the supreme accomplishment of the activity of slaying by all Tathāgatas—bestowed that Vajra-arrow upon that Great Bodhisattva Māra with his two hands in the same manner.
Then he was consecrated by all the Tathāgatas with the vajra-name initiation, “Vajradhanu, Vajradhanu! (STT 1,44,54).
Thereupon, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajradhanu, slaying all the Tathāgatas with that vajra-arrow, uttered this inspired utterance:
(STT 1,44,55) “This is that stainless passion-knowledge of all the Buddhas. (STT 1,44,55)
"By slaying passion with passion, they indeed bestow all happiness.

(STT 1,44,55) Then the Blessed One again entered the samādhi called the Vajra of the Empowerment of Beings Arising from the Samaya of the Great Bodhisattva Pramodyarāja, and from his own heart he emitted this Heart-mantra of all Tathāgatas, called the Samaya of the Joy of all Tathāgatas: (STT 1,45,56) "Vajrasādhu! (STT 1,45,56)

Then, as soon as it had issued forth from the hearts of all the Tathāgatas, that very Blessed One Vajradhara became expressions of approval (*sādhukāra*), entered the heart of the Blessed One Vairocana, and having become a single solid mass, manifested in the form of Vajra-joy (*vajratuṣṭi*) and took his place in the hand of the Blessed One.

Then, from that [source], as many forms of the Tathāgata as there are atoms in all the atomically minute world-systems emerged from the body of Vajra-Joy. Having performed all the miraculous displays of the Buddhas, such as the "Well Done! (*sādhukāra*) to all the Tathāgatas, they became a single, solid mass—the body of the Great Bodhisattva Pramodyarāja—due to the intense joy and the extreme firmness of the Vajrasattva-samādhi. Abiding in the heart of the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Vairocana, he uttered this inspired utterance (*udāna*):

"Aho! Indeed, I am the one who utters the cry of 'Well done,' the best among all those who possess all-knowledge, since I certainly produce satisfaction for those who have abandoned conceptual construction.

Then that body of the Great Bodhisattva Pramodyarāja, having descended from the heart of the Blessed One Vairocana and taken his place upon a moon disc behind all the Tathāgatas, once again sought their command.

Then the Blessed One, having entered the samādhi called the Vajra that Satisfies All Tathāgatas, bestowed that Vajra-Contentment with both hands upon that Great Bodhisattva Pramodyarāja, for the sake of the commitment (*samaya*) of the supreme joy-knowledge of all Tathāgatas, in order that he might experience the great bliss and mental well-being that satisfies the entire realm of sentient beings without exception, and for the purpose of attaining the fruit of the supreme accomplishment of the essence of the unsurpassed delight of all Tathāgatas.
Then he was consecrated by all the Tathāgatas with the vajra-name consecration, saying: “Vajraharṣa, Vajraharṣa! (STT 1,46,60).
Thereupon, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajraharṣa, gladdening all the Tathāgatas with that vajra-joy through shouts of “Well done!”, uttered this inspired utterance:
(STT 1,46,61) “This is that which sets in motion the ‘well done! of all the Buddhas. (STT 1,46,61)
"The vajra that brings satisfaction to all, divine, and increasing joy" (STT 1,46,61).

The great bodhicitta is the commitment (*samaya*) for the summoning of all Tathāgatas, the gnosis (*jñāna*) for the enchantment (*anurāgaṇa*) of all Tathāgatas, and the great satisfaction (*mahātuṣṭi*). (STT 1,46,62).
These are the Great Samaya-beings (*mahāsamayasattva*) of all Tathāgatas. (STT 1,46,62)

Then the Blessed One again entered the samādhi called the Vajra of the Abiding Place of Jewels Arising from the Samaya of the Great Bodhisattva Ākāśagarbha, and from his own heart he emitted this heart-mantra of all Tathāgatas called the Samaya of the Empowerment of All Tathāgatas:
*vajraratna*.

Then, as soon as this had issued forth from the hearts of all the Tathāgatas, because of the thorough penetration of the wisdom of the equality of all space through the samādhi of Vajrasattva, that very Blessed One, Vajradhara, became rays of light filling all space and issued forth. By those rays of light filling all space, all world-systems were illuminated;
they became composed of the entire realm of space.
Then, through the empowerment (*adhiṣṭhāna*) of all the Tathāgatas, this entire realm of space (*ākāśadhātu*) became established within the heart of the Blessed One Vairocana.

And because of his thorough cultivation of the *vajrasattva*-samādhi, a great body of vajra-jewels appeared—consisting of the essence of the womb of the entire realm of space and equal in measure to the convergence of all world-systems—and it was established in the hand of the Blessed One.

Then, from that body of vajra-jewels, as many bodies of Tathāgatas as there are atoms in all world-systems emerged. Having performed all the empowerments of the Tathāgatas and all the miraculous transformations of the supernatural powers of the Tathāgatas in all world-systems, because of the perfect arising from the womb of the entire realm of space and the extreme firmness of the Vajrasattva samādhi, they became a single solid mass—the great Bodhisattva body of Ākāśagarbha. Abiding in the heart of the Blessed One Vairocana, he uttered this inspired utterance:
"Aho! I am indeed the self-consecrated one, the unsurpassed Vajraratna, by whom even the Victors, though free from attachment, are remembered as the lords of the three realms.

(STT 1,47,66) Then that body of the Great Bodhisattva Ākāśagarbha, having descended from the heart of the Blessed One and taken his place upon a moon disc in front of all the Tathāgatas, once again requested permission. (STT 1,48,67)

Then the Blessed One, having entered the samādhi called Sarvatathāgatamaṇiratnavajra, for the sake of fulfilling the intentions of all Tathāgatas, for the sake of the attainment of all aims for the entire realm of sentient beings without exception, for the sake of experiencing all happiness and mental well-being, and up to the attainment of the supreme accomplishment of the fulfillment of the aims of all Tathāgatas— having consecrated that Vajramaṇi with the Vajraratnāṅkuśa consecration in the capacity of the Vajraratnacakravartin for that Mahābodhisattva Ākāśagarbha, he bestowed it upon him with both hands.
Then all the Tathāgatas conferred upon him the consecration with the vajra-name, saying: “Vajragarbha! Vajragarbha!
(STT 1,49,68). Then the great bodhisattva Vajragarbha, placing that vajra-jewel in the place of his own consecration, uttered this inspired utterance:
(STT 1,49,69) “This is the consecration of the realm of sentient beings for all the Buddhas. (STT 1,49,69)

"I have placed jewel upon jewel, bestowed by my own hand. (STT 1,49,69) Then the Blessed One again entered the samādhi called the Vajra of the Empowerment of the Jewel Arising from the Samaya of the Mahātejas Mahābodhisattva, and from his own heart he emitted this Heart-mantra of all Tathāgatas, called the Samaya of the Rays of All Tathāgatas:
(STT 1,50,70) "Vajrateja! (STT 1,50,70)

Then, as soon as it had issued forth from the hearts of all the Tathāgatas, that very Blessed One Vajrapāṇi became great solar mandalas; having entered the heart of the Blessed One Vairocana and manifested as a single solid form of the Vajrasūrya, he took his place in the hand of the Blessed One.

Then, from that Vajra-sun mandala, there issued forth Tathāgata-forms as numerous as the atoms of all world-systems. Having performed all the miraculous transformations of the Tathāgatas, such as the emission of immeasurable rays of light from all the Tathāgatas, they coalesced into a single, solid mass of the body of a Great Bodhisattva of immense splendor, due to the great majesty of the Vajrasattva samādhi and its extreme firmness. Abiding in the heart of the Blessed One Vairocana, he uttered this inspired utterance: "Aho! How incomparable is your splendor, illuminating the realm of sentient beings!"
"That which purifies even the pure Buddhas, the Protectors" (STT 1,50,72).

Then that body of the Great Bodhisattva Vimalatejas, having emerged from the heart of the Blessed One and taken its place upon the lunar mandala to the right of all the Tathāgatas, once again sought his command (STT 1,50,73).

Then the Blessed One, having entered the samādhi called the Vajra Empowerment of the Light-Mandalas of All Tathāgatas, bestowed that Vajra-Sun with both hands upon that Great Bodhisattva Mahātejas for the sake of the samaya of the rays of all Tathāgatas—in order that the entire realm of sentient beings, without exception, might experience incomparable splendor and all happiness and mental well-being, up to the attainment of the supreme siddhi of the self-radiance of all Tathāgatas.
Then, he was consecrated by all the Tathāgatas with the vajra-name empowerment, “Vajraprabha, Vajraprabha.
Thereupon, the Great Bodhisattva Vajraprabha, illuminating all the Tathāgatas with that Vajrasūrya, uttered this inspired utterance:
“This is that which destroys the darkness of ignorance of all Buddhas.”

"Having a radiance exceeding that of suns as numerous as the atoms of a world-system. (STT 1,51,74) Then the Blessed One again entered the samādhi called the Vajra of the Jewel-Adhiṣṭhāna Arising from the Samaya of the Bodhisattva Ratnaketu, and from his own heart he emitted this Heart of All Tathāgatas called the Samaya that Fulfills the Hopes of All Tathāgatas:
(STT 1,52,75) "Vajraketu. (STT 1,52,75)

Then, as soon as it had issued forth from the hearts of all the Tathāgatas, that very Blessed One Vajradhara, having become banners possessing various colors, forms, ornaments, and shapes, emerged; he entered the heart of the Blessed One Vairocana and, manifesting as a single solid mass in the form of a Vajradhvaja, became established in the hand of the Blessed One.

Then, from that form of Vajradhvaja, there issued forth as many forms of Tathāgatas as there are atoms in all world-systems. Having performed all the miraculous displays of the Buddhas, such as raising the jeweled banners of all the Tathāgatas, and because of the great jewel-bannered nature of the vajra of all samādhis and its extreme firmness, they merged into a single solid mass—the body of the Great Bodhisattva Ratnaketu—and, remaining in the heart of the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Vairocana, they uttered this inspired utterance: (STT 1,52,77)
"Aho! I am indeed the peerless banner named Sarvārthasiddhi (Accomplisher of All Aims), for I am the fulfillment of all aims for those whose every hope has been perfected.

Then that great bodhisattva body Ratnaketu emerged from the heart of the Blessed One and, having taken his place upon the moon-mandala to the left of all the Tathāgatas, once again awaited further instructions.

Then the Blessed One, having entered the samādhi called the Vajra of the Empowerment of the Elevation of All Tathāgatas, bestowed that same Vajra Banner with both hands upon the Great Bodhisattva Ratnaketu for the sake of the pledge of the elevation of the wish-fulfilling king-jewel banner of all Tathāgatas—in order to fulfill all the hopes of all sentient beings without exception or remainder, to cause them to experience all happiness and mental well-being, and for the purpose of attaining the fruit of the supreme great accomplishment of all Tathāgatas.
Then he was consecrated by all the Tathāgatas with the vajra-name consecration, saying: “Vajrayaṣṭi, Vajrayaṣṭi! (STT 1,53,79).
Then the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrayaṣṭi, employing that Vajradhvaja, exhorted all the Tathāgatas toward the perfection of generosity and uttered this inspired utterance:
(STT 1,53,80) “This is that which fulfills all the hopes of all the Buddhas. (STT 1,53,80)
"The method of the perfection of generosity is called the Banner of the Wish-Fulfilling Jewel.

(STT 1,53,80) Then the Blessed One again entered the samādhi called the Vajra of the Empowerment of the Jewel Arising from the Samaya of the Great Bodhisattva Whose Faculties are Constantly Joyful and Delighted; from his own heart, he emitted this Heart of All Tathāgatas called the Samaya of the Joy of All Tathāgatas:
(STT 1,5354,81) "Vajrahāsa" (The Vajra-Laughter). (STT 1,54,81)

As soon as this had issued forth from the hearts of all the Tathāgatas, that very Blessed One Vajradhara, having become the smiles of all the Tathāgatas, emerged; he entered the heart of the Blessed One Vairocana and, manifesting as a single solid mass in the form of the Vajra-Smile, he came to rest upon [Vairocana’s] hand. (STT 1,54,82) Then, from that form of the Vajra-Smile, Tathāgata-forms as numerous as the atoms of all world-systems emerged, and having performed all the miraculous displays of the Buddhas’ supernatural powers, such as the wonders of all the Tathāgatas, (STT 1,54,83)

Because his faculties were perpetually joyful and delighted through the samādhi of Vajrasattva, and because that samādhi was extremely firm, he became a single, solid mass—the body of a great bodhisattva whose faculties are perpetually joyful and delighted—and remaining in the heart of the Blessed One Vairocana, he uttered this inspired utterance:
"Aho! I am the Great Laughter, the great wonder of all that is most supreme!"
"Whatever they employ for the sake of the Buddhas, always being perfectly concentrated.

(STT 1,54,83) Then that body of the Great Bodhisattva, whose faculties were constantly joyful and delighted, emerged from the heart of the Blessed One; having taken his place upon a moon disc behind all the Tathāgatas, he once again sought their command. (STT 1,54,84)

Then the Blessed One, having entered the samādhi called the Vajra of the Miraculous Empowerment of All Tathāgatas, bestowed that Vajra-Smile with his two hands upon that Great Bodhisattva whose senses were ever-joyful and delighted, for the sake of the pledge of the miraculous origin of all Tathāgatas— which is worthy of being experienced as the complete and total bliss of the faculties of the entire realm of sentient beings without exception— and as the cause for attaining the fruit of the knowledge and supernormal powers that purify the faculties of all Tathāgatas.
Then he was consecrated by all the Tathāgatas with the vajra-name-consecration: “Vajraprīti, Vajraprīti!
Then the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajraprīti, gladdening all the Tathāgatas with that vajra-smile, uttered this inspired utterance:
“This is that which reveals the wondrous manifestation of all the Buddhas.”
"The knowledge that produces great joy is unknown to the teachers who measure others.
(STT 1,55,86) "The great consecration, the circle of light one fathom wide, the purpose of the Great Being, and the great laughter.
(STT 1,55,87) These are the beings of the great consecration of all Tathāgatas. (STT 1,55,87)

Then the Blessed One again entered the samādhi called the Vajra of the Dharma-Adhiṣṭhāna Arising from the Samaya of the Great Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara, and from his own heart he emitted this Heart-Mantra of all Tathāgatas, called the Dharma-Samaya of all Tathāgatas:
"Vajradharma!"

Then, as soon as it had issued forth from the hearts of all the Tathāgatas, that very Blessed One Vajradhara, by virtue of his thorough penetration of the wisdom of the equality of phenomena which are pure by nature through the samādhi of Vajrasattva, emerged as rays of light of the True Dharma.
By those rays of the True Dharma, all the world-systems were illuminated and became composed of the realm of phenomena (dharmadhātu).

And that entire realm of phenomena (dharmadhātu), having entered the heart of the Blessed One Vairocana, became a single mass; appearing as a great lotus-form with a magnitude equal to the convergence of the entire realm of space, it was established in the hand of the Blessed One.
Then, from that vajra-lotus form—

As many forms of the Tathāgata as there are atoms in all world-systems issued forth, and having performed all the miraculous transformations of the Buddhas—such as the samādhis, wisdoms, and superknowledges of all Tathāgatas—in all world-systems, they condensed into a single, solid mass of the body of the Great Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara due to the sovereign power of his own vision and the extreme firmness of the Vajrasattva-samādhi; then, abiding in the heart of the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Vairocana, he uttered this inspired utterance: *(STT 1,56,91)*
"Aho! I am indeed the ultimate reality, the primordially pure among the self-arisen ones, since the purity of phenomena—which are like a raft—is thus perceived.

Then that body of the Great Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara, having descended from the heart of the Blessed One Vairocana, took his place upon a moon disc in front of all the Tathāgatas and once again awaited an instruction.

Then the Blessed One, having entered the meditative absorption named the Vajra of the Samaya of the Wisdom and Samādhi of All Tathāgatas, for the sake of purifying all Tathāgatas— the complete purification of the selves of all sentient beings without exception— and for the purpose of experiencing all happiness and mental well-being, up to the cause of attaining the fruit of the superknowledges of the Dharma-wisdom of all Tathāgatas, consecrated that vajra-lotus with the empowerment of the Dharma-body of all Tathāgatas upon the Great Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara as the Turner of the Wheel of the True Dharma, and bestowed it upon him with his two hands.
Then, all the Tathāgatas conferred upon him the vajra-name initiation, saying: “Vajranetra! Vajranetra! (STT 1,57,93).

Thereupon, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajranetra, gazing at that vajra-lotus by way of its blossoming petals and by way of beholding the nature of passion as pure and stainless, uttered this inspired utterance:
(STT 1,57,94) “This is the awakening to the reality of passion of all the Buddhas. (STT 1,57,94)
"I [have received] the Dharma established in the Dharma, which has been placed into my own hand.

(STT 1,5758,94) Then the Blessed One again entered the samādhi called the Vajra of the Dharma Empowerment Arising from the Samaya of the Great Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī, and from his own heart he emitted this Heart of All Tathāgatas called the Samaya of the Great Wisdom-Knowledge of All Tathāgatas:
(STT 1,58,95) "Vajratīkṣṇa" (STT 1,58,95)

Then, as soon as it had issued forth from the hearts of all the Tathāgatas, that very Blessed One Vajradhara became wisdom-swords and, having issued forth, entered the heart of the Blessed One Vairocana; appearing there as a single mass in the form of a vajra-sheath, he established himself in the hand of the Blessed One.

Then, from that adamantine treasury-form (*vajrakośavigraha*), as many forms of Tathāgatas as there are atoms in all world-systems issued forth. Having performed all the miraculous displays of the supernatural powers of all Buddhas, such as the wisdom and knowledge of all Tathāgatas, they condensed into a single, solid body of the Great Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī—due to his being the most excellent Mañjuśrī and the extreme firmness of the Vajrasattva samādhi—and, remaining in the heart of the Blessed One Vairocana, uttered this inspired utterance (*udāna*):
"Aho! Indeed, I am remembered by all the Buddhas as Mañjughoṣa!"
"Since the nature of sound is perceived within formless wisdom" (STT 1,59,97).

Then that body of the Great Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī, having emerged from the heart of the Blessed One and taken its place upon the lunar mandala to the right of all the Tathāgatas, again requested the command (STT 1,59,98).

Then the Blessed One, having entered the samādhi called the Vajra of the Wisdom-Knowledge of All Tathāgatas, for the sake of the commitment that severs the afflictions of all Tathāgatas, for the sake of severing all suffering of the entire realm of sentient beings without exception and for the sake of experiencing all happiness and mental ease, and up to the sake of the supreme accomplishment consisting in the fulfillment of wisdom that accords with the resonance of all Tathāgatas, bestowed that Vajra-treasury upon the Great Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī with his two hands in that same manner.
Then he was consecrated by all the Tathāgatas with the vajra-name-consecration, "Vajrabuddhi, Vajrabuddhi! (STT 1,60,99).
Thereupon, that Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrabuddhi, striking all the Tathāgatas with that vajra-treasury, uttered this inspired utterance:
(STT 1,60,100) "This is the method of the Perfection of Wisdom of all the Buddhas. (STT 1,60,100)
"The supreme destroyer of all enemies and remover of all sins" (STT 1,60,100).

Then the Blessed One again entered the samādhi called the Vajra of the Dharma-Adhiṣṭhāna arising from the Samaya of the Great Bodhisattva Sahacittotpāditadharmacakrapravartin, and from his own heart he emitted this Heart of All Tathāgatas called the Samaya of the Wheel of All Tathāgatas:

Then, as soon as it had issued forth from the hearts of all the Tathāgatas, that very Blessed One Vajradhara became all the maṇḍalas of all the Tathāgatas, beginning with the Great Maṇḍala of the Vajra Realm; having issued forth and entered the heart of the Blessed One Vairocana, he appeared as a single solid mass in the form of a vajra-wheel and was established in the hand of the Blessed One.

Then, from that form of the Vajra-Wheel, as many forms of Tathāgatas as there are atoms in all world-systems issued forth. Because of the turning of the Wheel of Dharma upon the mere arising of the thought [of awakening], and because of the extreme firmness of the Vajrasattva-samādhi, they became a single solid mass—the body of the Great Bodhisattva who turns the Wheel of Dharma upon the mere arising of the thought [of awakening]. Abiding in the heart of the Blessed One Vairocana, he uttered this inspired utterance: "Aho! I am the vajra-wheel of those who possess the supreme vajra-dharma!"

"By the mere arising of the thought [of awakening], the wheel of Dharma is set in motion. (STT 1,61,103) Then that body of the Great Bodhisattva Sahacittotpāditadharmacakrapravarti, having descended from the heart of the Blessed One and taken his place upon the moon-maṇḍala to the left of all the Tathāgatas, again requested the command. (STT 1,62,104)

Then the Blessed One, having entered the samādhi called Sarvatathāgatacakravajra, for the sake of causing all beings of the entire realm of sentient beings— without exception— to enter the pledge of the great maṇḍala of all Tathāgatas, to become irreversible through the wheel [of Dharma], and to experience all happiness and mental well-being, up to the sign of the supreme accomplishment of setting in motion the wheel of the true Dharma of all Tathāgatas, bestowed that Vajracakra with his own two hands upon that Great Bodhisattva who had simultaneously generated the thought of turning the wheel of Dharma, in that very same manner.
Then he was consecrated by all the Tathāgatas with the vajra-name-consecration, saying, “Vajramaṇḍa, Vajramaṇḍa! (STT 1,62,105).
Then the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajramaṇḍa, establishing all the Tathāgatas in the state of non-retrogression by means of that vajra-wheel, uttered this inspired utterance:
(STT 1,62,106) “This is that which destroys all phenomena of all the Buddhas. (STT 1,62,106)
"The irreversible wheel is known as the seat of awakening (*bodhimaṇḍa*).

(STT 1,6263,106) Then the Blessed One again entered the samādhi called the Vajra of the Dharma-Adhiṣṭhāna Arising from the Samaya of the Silent Great Bodhisattva, and from his own heart he emitted this Heart of All Tathāgatas called the Samaya of the Recitation of All Tathāgatas:
(STT 1,63,107) "Vajrabhāṣa" (STT 1,63,107).

Then, as soon as it had issued forth from the hearts of all the Tathāgatas, that very Blessed One Vajrapāṇi, having become the syllables of the Dharma of all the Tathāgatas, issued forth; having entered the heart of the Blessed One Vairocana, he appeared as a single solid form of vajra-recitation and took his place in the hand of the Blessed One.

Then, from that mastery of vajra-recitation (*vajrajāpa*), as many forms of Tathāgatas as there are atoms in all world-systems emerged. Having performed all the miraculous displays of the Buddhas, beginning with the *dharmatā* of all Tathāgatas, and because of the self-speech of the Vajrasattva-samādhi and its extreme firmness, they coalesced into a single, solid body of the Great Bodhisattva Avāca. Abiding in the heart of the Blessed One Vairocana, he uttered this inspired utterance (*udāna*):
"Aho! I have remembered the secret intentional discourse (*saṃdhābhāṣa*) of the Self-Existent Ones."
"Which they teach as the True Dharma, free from the proliferation of speech.

(STT 1,64,109) Then that body of the Great Bodhisattva Avāca, having emerged from the heart of the Blessed One and taken his place upon a moon disc behind all the Tathāgatas, once again awaited an instruction. (STT 1,65,110)

Then the Blessed One, having entered the samādhi called the Vajra of Speech of All Tathāgatas, for the sake of experiencing the speech-siddhi of the entire realm of sentient beings without exception—the commitment of the wisdom of the speech of all Tathāgatas—and for the attainment of the supreme siddhi of the secret speech of all Tathāgatas, bestowed that vajra-recitation upon the Mahābodhisattva with his two hands in that very same manner.

Then he was consecrated by all the Tathāgatas with the vajra-name consecration, "Vajravāca, Vajravāca! (STT 1,65,111). Thereupon, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajravāca, conversing with all the Tathāgatas through that vajra-recitation, uttered this inspired utterance: (STT 1,65,112) "This is the vajra-recitation proclaimed for all the Buddhas. (STT 1,65,112)

"The swift accomplishment of the mantras of all the Tathāgatas" (STT 1,65,112) refers to the knowledge of the reality-nature (*dharmatā*) of the Vajra, the knowledge of the wisdom of all the Tathāgatas, the knowledge of the turning of the great wheel, and the knowledge of the cessation of the conceptual proliferation of the speech of all the Tathāgatas (STT 1,67,113). These are the Great Wisdom Beings (*mahājñānasattva*) of all the Tathāgatas (STT 1,67,113).

Then the Blessed One entered the samādhi called the Vajra of the Empowerment of Action Arising from the Samaya of the Mahābodhisattva Viśvakarman of All Tathāgatas, and from his own heart he emitted this heart-mantra of all Tathāgatas called the Samaya of the Action of All Tathāgatas:
"Vajrakarma."

Then, as soon as this had issued forth from the hearts of all the Tathāgatas, because of the thorough penetration of the knowledge of the equality of all activities through the samādhi of Vajrasattva, that very Blessed One Vajradhara became rays of light of the activities of all the Tathāgatas and issued forth.

And by those rays of activity of all the Tathāgatas, all world-systems were illuminated and became composed of the activity-realm of all the Tathāgatas. That entire activity-realm of all the Tathāgatas entered the heart of the Blessed One Vairocana; it then became equal in measure to the convergence of the entire space-realm. From that activity-realm of all the Tathāgatas, there emerged a body of the Vajra of Activity, which came to rest upon the hand of the Blessed One.

Then, from that body of Karma-Vajra, there issued forth Tathāgata-forms as numerous as the atoms in all world-systems. Having performed all the activities of the Tathāgatas, such as [the work of] all Buddhas, and all miraculous displays of supernatural power throughout all world-systems, they merged into a single, solid mass—the body of the Great Bodhisattva Sarvatathāgataviśvakarma—due to the infinite activity of all Tathāgatas and the extreme firmness of the Vajrasattva-samādhi. Abiding in the heart of the Blessed One Vairocana, he uttered this inspired utterance: *(STT 1,6768,116)*
"Aho! Truly, the manifold activity of the Buddhas is unfailing; for the sake of the effortless purpose of the Buddhas, vajra-activity proceeds.

Then that body of the Great Bodhisattva Sarvatathāgataviśvakarma emerged from the heart of the Blessed One, took his place upon a moon-maṇḍala in front of all the Tathāgatas, and once again awaited an injunction.

Then the Blessed One, having entered the samādhi called *Sarvatathāgatāmoghavajra*, for the sake of setting in motion the worship of all Tathāgatas and so forth, for the sake of the extensive ritual procedures of all immeasurable and unfailing actions, for the sake of experiencing all success in action and all happiness and mental well-being for the entire realm of sentient beings without exception, and for the sake of the fruit of the supreme accomplishment of the knowledge and superknowledges of the vajra-action of all Tathāgatas—[bestowed] that Action-Vajra upon that Great Bodhisattva Sarvatathāgatavajrakarma.

Having consecrated him for the sovereignty over all activities with the vajra-consecration of all Tathāgatas, [the Buddha] bestowed it upon his two hands. Then, he was consecrated by all the Tathāgatas with the vajra-name-consecration: “Vajraviśva, Vajraviśva!
Then the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajraviśva, placing that vajra at his own heart and enjoining all the Tathāgatas to the state of activity, uttered this inspired utterance:
“This is that supreme performer of all activities for all Buddhas.”

"I have placed the entire universe within my hand; the universe is joined to me. (STT 1,69,119) Then the Blessed One entered the samādhi called the Vajra of the Empowerment of Action Arising from the Samaya of the Mahābodhisattva Duryodhanavīrya, and from his own heart he emitted this Heart-mantra of all Tathāgatas called the Samaya of Protection for all Tathāgatas:
(STT 1,71,120) "Vajrarakṣa" (STT 1,71,120).

Then, as soon as it had issued forth from the hearts of all the Tathāgatas, that very Blessed One Vajrapāṇi, having become firm armors, emerged and entered the heart of the Blessed One Vairocana; appearing there as a single solid mass in the form of a great adamantine armor, he established himself in the hand of the Blessed One.

Then, from that body of the Vajra Armor, as many forms of Tathāgatas as there are atoms in all world-systems issued forth; having performed all the miraculous displays of the Buddhas, such as the extensive rites for the protection of all Tathāgatas and so forth, they merged into a single, solid mass of the form of a Great Bodhisattva of invincible vigor due to the difficulty of conquering through the samādhi of Vajrasattva and its extreme firmness. Abiding in the heart of the Blessed One Vairocana, he uttered this inspired utterance:
"Aho! This armor consisting of vigor is most firm; I am one whose self is firm.
Because of its firmness, it is supreme for producing a vajra-body even for those who are bodiless.

Then that body of the Great Bodhisattva Duryodhanavīrya, having emerged from the heart of the Bhagavat and taken his place upon the lunar disc to the right of all the Tathāgatas, once again sought the [Bhagavat’s] command.

Then the Blessed One, having entered the samādhi called Sarvatathāgatadṛḍhavajra, bestowed with both hands that adamantine armor upon the Mahābodhisattva Duryodhanavīrya for the sake of the commitment (*samaya*) of the Vīryapāramitā of all Tathāgatas—in order to protect the realm of sentient beings without exception or remainder, to cause them to experience all happiness and mental well-being, and as a cause for the supreme accomplishment of attaining the vajra-body of all Tathāgatas.

Then he was consecrated by all the Tathāgatas with the vajra-name-consecration, “Vajramitra, Vajramitra! (STT 1,72,124). Then the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajramitra, arming all the Tathāgatas with that vajra-armour, uttered this inspired utterance: (STT 1,72,125) “This is that supreme armour of loving-kindness belonging to all the Buddhas. (STT 1,72,125)
"The great protection of firm vigor is proclaimed as the great friend.

(STT 1,72,125) Then the Blessed One again entered the samādhi called the Vajra of the Empowerment of the Ritual Actions Arising from the Samaya of the Great Bodhisattva Sarvamārapramardin, and from it he issued this Heart of all Tathāgatas, called the Samaya of the Skillful Means of all Tathāgatas, which is the heart of all hearts:
(STT 1,73,126) "Vajrayakṣa" (STT 1,73,126).

Then, as soon as it had issued forth from the hearts of all the Tathāgatas, that very Blessed One Vajradhara became great fang-weapons; having issued forth and entered the heart of the Blessed One Vairocana, he manifested as a single solid mass in the form of a vajra-fang and was established in [the Buddha's] hand.

Then, from that form of Vajradaṃṣṭra, there issued forth as many forms of Tathāgatas as there are atoms in all world-systems. Having performed all the miraculous displays of the supernatural powers of the Buddhas, such as the fierce subduing of all Tathāgatas, they merged into a single solid mass—the body of the Great Bodhisattva Sarvamārapramardin—due to the utter crushing of all Māras and the extreme firmness of the Vajrasattva samādhi. Abiding in the heart of the Blessed One Vairocana, he uttered this inspired utterance:
"Aho! What a great means of the Buddhas, whose very nature is compassion, that for the sake of sentient beings they even manifest ferocity despite being peaceful!

Then, that body of the Great Bodhisattva Sarvamārapramardi emerged from the heart of the Blessed One and, having taken its place upon the lunar mandala to the left of all the Tathāgatas, once again sought their command.

Then the Blessed One, having entered the samādhi called Sarvatathāgatapracaṇḍavajra, for the sake of subduing the wicked of all Tathāgatas, so that the entire realm of sentient beings without exception might experience fearlessness, all happiness, and mental well-being, and for the purpose of attaining the fruit of the supreme siddhi—the great skillful means, knowledge, and supernormal powers of all Tathāgatas—bestowed that weapon of the vajra-tusk upon that Great Bodhisattva Sarvamārapramardin with his two hands, just as before.
Then he was consecrated by all the Tathāgatas with the vajra-name-consecration, "Vajracaṇḍa, Vajracaṇḍa! (STT 1,74,130).
Then the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajracaṇḍa, having placed that weapon of the vajra-fangs in his own mouth and terrifying all the Tathāgatas, uttered this inspired utterance:
(STT 1,74,131) "This is that [weapon] of all the Buddhas, the supreme subduer of all the wicked. (STT 1,74,131)
"The sharp weapon of the Vajra-fang is the skillful means (*upāya*) of those whose nature is compassion.

(STT 1,74,131) Then the Blessed One again entered the samādhi called the Vajra Empowerment of the Ritual Action Arising from the Samaya of the Great Bodhisattva Sarvatathāgatamuṣṭi, and from his own heart he emitted this heart-essence (*hṛdaya*) of all Tathāgatas, called the Samaya of the Vajra-Bond of the Body, Speech, and Mind of all Tathāgatas:
(STT 1,75,132) *vajrasandhi*. (STT 1,75,132)

Then, as soon as this had been emitted from the hearts of all the Tathāgatas, that very Blessed One Vajradhara, having become the binding of all the seals (mudrā) of all the Tathāgatas, emerged and entered the heart of the Blessed One Vairocana; there he appeared as a single, solid mass in the form of a vajra-binding and settled upon [Vairocana’s] hand.

Then, from that body of the vajra-bind, as many forms of Tathāgatas as there are atoms in all world-systems issued forth; having performed all the miraculous displays of the supernatural powers of all Buddhas, such as the knowledge of the mudrās of all Tathāgatas in all world-systems, they became a single solid mass—the body of the Great Bodhisattva Sarvatathāgatamuṣṭi—due to the state of the Vajrasattva-samādhi being perfectly firm and well-bound by the great fist of all Tathāgatas. Having arisen and stationed themselves in the heart of the Blessed One Vairocana, they uttered this inspired utterance:

"Aho! How firm indeed is the bond of the vow for those of steadfast soul, that even for the liberated there is bondage for the sake of accomplishing all hopes! Then the body of the Great Bodhisattva Sarvatathāgatamuṣṭi emerged from the heart of the Blessed One, took his place upon a moon-maṇḍala behind all the Tathāgatas, and once again awaited an instruction.

Then the Blessed One, having entered the samādhi called the Vajra of the Samaya of All Tathāgatas, for the sake of experiencing the bliss and mental well-being of all accomplishments through the visualization of the presence of the deities of all Tathāgatas—and for the purpose of attaining the fruit of the supreme accomplishment of sovereignty over the mudrās of the omniscient knowledge of all Tathāgatas—bestowed that vajra-binding with his own hands upon that Great Bodhisattva Sarvatathāgatamuṣṭi in the same manner.
Then he was consecrated by all the Tathāgatas with the vajra-name consecration, "Vajramuṣṭi, Vajramuṣṭi.
Thereupon, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajramuṣṭi, binding all the Tathāgatas with that vajra-binding, uttered this inspired utterance:
"This is that great and firm fist-binding of all the Buddhas."
"That which all Buddhas have declared for the sake of accomplishment is the samaya that is difficult to transgress" (STT 1,76,137).
[It is] the extensive ritual procedure for the worship of all Tathāgatas, the firm armor of great heroism, the great skillful means of all Tathāgatas, and the knowledge of all mudrās (STT 1,78,138).
[These are] the great action-beings of all Tathāgatas (STT 1,78,138).

Then indeed, the Tathāgata Akṣobhya, having brought to completion all the gnoses of the Bhagavān Vairocana and for the purpose of sealing all the gnoses of the Tathāgatas, entered the samādhi called "Vajra-Adhiṣṭhāna Arising from the Samaya of the Vajra-Pāramitā. From his own heart, he emitted this seal of all the Tathāgatas called "The Vajra-Samaya of All Tathāgatas":
*Sattvavajri*.
As soon as she had issued forth, vajra-rays streamed out from the hearts of all the Tathāgatas.

And from those vajra-rays, that very Blessed One Vajradhara became as many forms of Tathāgatas as there are atoms in all world-systems; having sealed the gnoses of the vajra-perfection of all Tathāgatas, he once again appeared as a single, solid mass, a great vajra-form equal in measure to the convergence of all world-systems, and resting upon a moon-mandala in front of the Blessed One Vairocana, he uttered this inspired utterance:
"Aho! Indeed, among all Buddhas, I am the firm Vajra of beings (sattvavajra); because of this firmness, though bodiless, I have attained the state of the Vajra-body.

Then the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Ratnasaṃbhava, for the purpose of sealing the gnosis of all Tathāgatas of the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Vairocana, entered the samādhi called "Vajra-empowerment arising from the commitment of the Jewel Perfection" (ratnapāramitāsamayasambhavavajrādhiṣṭhāna), and from his own heart he emitted this self-seal called "Vajra-Jewel Commitment" (vajraratnasamayā).
Ratnavajrī!
(STT 1,80,142) Then, as soon as she had emerged, jewel-rays issued forth from the hearts of all the Tathāgatas. (STT 1,80,143)

From those jewel rays, that very Blessed One Vajradhara became as many forms of Tathāgatas as there are atoms in all world-systems. Having sealed all the gnoses of the Tathāgatas, he once again appeared as a single, solid mass, a great vajra-jewel form equal in extent to the convergence of all world-systems. Taking his place upon a moon disc at the right side of the Blessed One Vairocana, he uttered this inspired utterance:
"Aho! Indeed, I am remembered as the Jewel-Vajra of all Buddhas."
"For indeed, this is the firm method of consecration for all mudrās.

(STT 1,80,144) Then the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Lokeśvararāja, in order to [reveal] the crown-jewel of the knowledge of all Tathāgatas for the Blessed One Vairocana, the Tathāgata, entered the samādhi called "Vajra-Adhiṣṭhāna Arising from the Samaya of the Perfection of Dharma," and from his entire heart he emitted this, his own mudrā called "Dharma-Samaya": (STT 1,81,145) *Dharmavajrī*. (STT 1,81,145)
Then, as soon as this [mudrā] was released, lotus-rays of light issued forth from the hearts of all the Tathāgatas.

From those lotus-rays, that very Blessed One Vajradhara became as many Tathāgata-forms as there are atoms in all world-systems; having sealed all the gnoses of the Tathāgatas, he again appeared as a single, solid mass, a great vajra-lotus form equal in size to the convergence of all world-systems. Resting upon a moon-maṇḍala behind the Blessed One Vairocana, he uttered this inspired utterance:
"Aho! I am the pure Dharma-vajra of all Buddhas."
"For by means of the purity of intrinsic nature, even passion is indeed utterly stainless.

(STT 1,82,147) Then the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Amoghasiddhi, for the purpose of sealing the gnosis of all Tathāgatas belonging to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Vairocana, entered the samādhi called "The Vajra Empowerment Arising from the Assembly of All Pāramitās," and from his own heart issued forth this mudrā of his own called "The Samaya of the Activity of All Tathāgatas":
KARMAVAJRI (STT 1,82,148)
Then, as soon as this had issued forth, rays of light for all ritual actions emerged from the hearts of all the Tathāgatas.

And from all those rays of activity of the Tathāgatas, that Blessed One Vajradhara became as many forms of Tathāgatas as there are atoms in all world-systems; having sealed all the gnoses of the Tathāgatas, he once again manifested as a single, solid mass, equal in extent to the convergence of all world-systems, a great vajra-form of activity facing in every direction. Taking his place upon a moon-maṇḍala at the left side of the Blessed One Vairocana, he uttered this inspired utterance:
"Aho! Indeed, I am the many Vajras of the karma of all Buddhas, since being one, I perform virtuous deeds for the entire realm of sentient beings.
This is the great consecration of the pledge of the wisdom of all Tathāgatas, the vajra-nature of reality, and all worship.
The Great Perfections of All Tathāgatas.

Then the Blessed One Vairocana again entered the samādhi called the Vajra Arising from the Samaya of the Worship of the Delight of All Tathāgatas, and from his own heart he brought forth this Great Goddess of the Family of All Tathāgatas:
Vajralāsye.
Then, as soon as she had issued forth, vajra-mudrās issued forth from the hearts of all the Tathāgatas.

From those [emanations] whose faces were the vajra-mudrā, that very Blessed One Vajradhara became as many forms of Tathāgatas as there are atoms in all world-systems; then, once again, he became the single mass of the Great Goddess Vajralāsyā, whose physical form resembled Vajrasattva, who possessed various colors, forms, marks, and modes of deportment, who was adorned with all ornaments, who embodied the gathering of all Tathāgata families, and who was the beloved of Vajrasattva. Having appeared, she took her place upon a moon disc at the left side of the Blessed One Akṣobhya’s maṇḍala and uttered this inspired utterance: *(STT 1,84,153)*

"Aha! There is indeed no other worship equal to mine for the Self-Existent Ones, since all worship proceeds through the worship of desire and passion. Then the Blessed One again entered the samādhi called the "Vajra Arising from the Samaya of the Empowerment of the Jewel Garland of All Tathāgatas," and from his own heart he brought forth this Great Goddess of the Family of All Tathāgatas: (From *Sarvatathāgatatattvasaṃgraha*, STT 1,84,154; 1,86,155)
"Vajramāle!
(STT 1,86,155) Then, as soon as this [mantra] was uttered, the Great Jewel Mudrās issued forth from the hearts of all the Tathāgatas. (STT 1,86,156)

From those Great Jewel Seals (*mahāratnamudrā*), that very Blessed One Vajradhara became Tathāgata forms as numerous as the atoms in all world-systems; then, once again becoming a single solid mass as the Great Goddess Vajramālā in the same manner, she took her place upon a full moon disc on the left side of the Blessed One’s Ratnasaṃbhava maṇḍala and uttered this inspired utterance (*udāna*):
"Aho! Indeed, I am peerless, proclaimed as the Worship of Jewels (*ratnapūjā*).”
"Because, being fully honored, they govern the supreme sovereignty over the three realms.

(STT 1,86,157) Then the Blessed One again entered the samādhi called the Vajra Arising from the Samaya of the Concert of All Tathāgatas, and from his own heart he issued forth this Great Goddess of the Family of All Tathāgatas:
(STT 1,88,158) "O Vajra Song! (STT 1,88,158)
Then, as soon as she had emerged, the Dharma-mudrās of all the Tathāgatas issued forth from the hearts of all the Tathāgatas.

And from those Dharma-mudrās of all the Tathāgatas, that very Blessed One Vajradhara became Tathāgata-forms as numerous as the atoms in all world-systems; these then once again condensed into a single mass as the Great Goddess Vajragītā. Taking her place upon a moon disc at the left side of the maṇḍala of the Blessed One Lokeśvararāja, she uttered this inspired utterance:
"Aho! This worship consisting of song is for all the All-Seeing Ones;
for they are pleased by such offerings, even though they are like echoes.

Then the Blessed One again entered the samādhi called the Vajra Arising from the Samaya of the Dance-Worship of All Tathāgatas, and from his own heart he emitted this Great Goddess of the Family of All Tathāgatas: *(STT 1,88,160–161)*
In the *Vajranṛtya* (Vajra Dance):

(STT 1,88,161) Then, as soon as this [mantra] had been emitted, there issued forth from the hearts of all the Tathāgatas the detailed ritual procedures for the dance-offerings of all the Tathāgatas. (STT 1,88,162)

And from all those extensive rituals for the worship of dance by all the Tathāgatas, that very Blessed One Vajradhara became as many forms of Tathāgatas as there are atoms in all world-systems; then, once again becoming a single mass as the Great Goddess Vajranṛttā, she took her place upon a full moon disc on the left side of the mandala of the Blessed Tathāgata Amoghasiddhi and uttered this inspired utterance:
"Aho! I am indeed the sublime worship among all who perform acts of worship!"
"That which is performed as an offering to the Buddhas by means of the rite of the Vajra-dance" (STT 1,89,163).

[It is] the commitment (*samaya*) of the unsurpassed bliss and mental well-being of all Tathāgatas; it is the garland of all Tathāgatas, the verse of all Tathāgatas, and the performer of the unsurpassed ritual of worship for all Tathāgatas (STT 1,89,164).
These are the secret offerings of all Tathāgatas (STT 1,89,164).

Then again, the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Akṣobhya, in order to perform a reciprocal worship for the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Vairocana, entered the samādhi called the Vajra Arising from the Samaya that Delights All Tathāgatas, and emitted this Sarvatathāgatagaṇikā from his own heart:
VAJRADHŪPE.

Then, as soon as this [mantra] had issued forth from the hearts of all the Tathāgatas, that very Blessed One Vajradhara became an array of clouds of manifold kinds of incense offerings, which pervaded the entire vajra-realm, and they emerged.

And from those oceans of clouds of incense offerings, the bodies of incense deities as numerous as the atoms of all world-systems arose; they took their place upon a moon disc at the left corner of the Blessed One’s peaked pavilion of vajra-jewel-summits and uttered this inspired utterance: (From STT 1, 90, 166)

"Aho! Indeed, I am the great worship, auspicious and full of joy, because through the yoga of the entry into sentient beings, awakening is swiftly attained. Then the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Ratnasaṃbhava, in order to perform a reciprocal worship for the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Vairocana, entered the samādhi called the "Vajra Arising from the Worship-Samaya of Jewel Ornaments" and emitted this female attendant of all Tathāgatas from his own heart: [The mantra follows] (From *Sarvatathāgatatattvasaṃgraha*, STT 1,90,167–168)
"Vajrapuṣpe!

(STT 1,91,168) Then, as soon as this [mantra] had issued forth from the hearts of all the Tathāgatas, that very Blessed One Vajradhara emerged as arrays of all flower-offerings, pervading the entire realm of space. (STT 1,91,169)

And from all those arrays of flower offerings, as many forms of Tathāgatas as there are atoms in all world-systems emerged; these then merged once more into a single solid body of the deity Vajrapuṣpa, and resting upon a moon disc in the left corner of the Blessed One’s peaked pavilion made of vajra-jewels, she uttered this inspired utterance:
"Oh, how wonderful! I am the Flower Offering, the creator of all ornaments, since by worshipping the jewel-nature of the Tathāgata, it is swiftly attained."

Then the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Lokeśvararāja, for the sake of honoring and being honored by the Blessed One Vairocana, the Tathāgata, entered the samādhi called the Vajra Arising from the Pūjā-samaya of the Light of All Tathāgatas, and emitted this Dhūtī of all Tathāgatas from his own heart: VAJRĀLOKE!

Then, as soon as she had issued forth from the hearts of all the Tathāgatas, that very Blessed One Vajradhara, together with the array of offerings for all the worlds, having become a pervasion of the entire dharmadhātu, emerged.

And from all those arrays of worship honored by all the worlds, there issued forth Tathāgata-forms as numerous as the atoms of all world-systems; these then merged once more into a single, solid body of the deity Vajrāloka, and resting upon a moon-maṇḍala in the left corner of the Blessed One’s peaked pavilion of vajra-jewel-summits, he uttered this inspired utterance:
"Aho! How truly magnificent is this auspicious worship consisting of lamps, By which one may swiftly obtain the vision of all Buddhas, like light!"

Then the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Amoghasiddhi, in order to perform a reciprocal worship for the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Vairocana, entered the samādhi called the "Vajra Arising from the Samaya of the Worship with Incense of All Tathāgatas," and from his own heart he emitted this female servant of all Tathāgatas:
"Vajragandhe!
As soon as she had issued forth, she emerged from the hearts of all Tathāgatas, pervading the entire world-system.

And from those arrays of fragrant offerings, as many forms of Tathāgatas as there are atoms in all world-systems emerged; these then merged once more into a single, solid body of the deity Vajragandhā. Taking her place upon a moon disc in the left corner of the Blessed One’s jeweled gabled palace with its peak of vajra-gems, she uttered this inspired utterance:
“Oh, how delightful I am, this divine offering consisting of fragrance!
For indeed, it bestows the scent of the Tathāgata upon every part of the body.”

[She is] the penetration of the wisdom of all Tathāgatas, the accumulation of the great factors of enlightenment, the illumination of the Dharma of all Tathāgatas, and the fragrance of ethical discipline, concentration, the foremost wisdom, liberation, the analytical knowledge of liberation, and the vision of wisdom.
(STT 1,94,177) She is the executor of the commands of all Tathāgatas.

(STT 1,94,177) Then the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Vairocana, again entered the samādhi called the Vajra Arising from the Samaya-Hook of All Tathāgatas, and from his own heart he emitted this Lord of the Entire Host of Mudrās of All Tathāgatas: (STT 1,94,178)
Vajrāṅkuśa! (STT 1,94,178) Then, as soon as this had issued forth from the hearts of all the Tathāgatas, they emerged having formed into hosts. (STT 1,95,179)

And from all those multitudes of seals (*mudrā*) of all the Tathāgatas, as many forms of Tathāgatas as there are atoms in all world-systems issued forth; these then merged once more into a single, solid body of the Great Bodhisattva Vajrāṅkuśa. Taking his place within the moon disc at the center of the vajra-gate of the Blessed One’s peaked pavilion of vajra-jewels, he drew in the commitments (*samaya*) of all the Tathāgatas and uttered this inspired utterance (*udāna*):
"Aho! I am the firm summoner of all the Buddhas!"
"For indeed, those whom I have drawn forth shall worship the entire maṇḍala.

(STT 1,95,180) Then the Blessed One again entered the samādhi called the Vajra Arising from the Samaya of the Great Being who Enters the Samaya of All Tathāgatas, and from his own heart he emitted this gatekeeper for entering the mudrās of all Tathāgatas: (STT 1,96,181) VAJRAPĀŚA! (STT 1,96,181)

Then, as soon as he had issued forth from the hearts of all the Tathāgatas, that very Blessed One Vajradhara emerged, having become the multitudes of mudrās for entering the samaya of all the Tathāgatas.

And from those multitudes of mudrās for entering the samaya of all Tathāgatas, as many forms of Tathāgatas as there are atoms in all world-systems emerged; these then merged once more into a single, solid mass, the body of the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāśa. Taking his place upon a moon disc in the center of the jeweled door of the Blessed One’s peaked pavilion, which is adorned with a crest of vajra-jewels, he entered all the Tathāgatas and uttered this inspired utterance:
"Aho! I am the firm Vajrapāśa of all Buddhas!"
"Though it has entered all atoms, it shall be made to enter by me once again.

(STT 1,97,183) Then the Blessed One again entered the samādhi called Sarvatathāgatasamayasphoṭamahāsattvasamayodbhavasattvavajra, and from his own heart he emitted this messenger of all the Tathāgatas, named Sarvatathāgatasamayabandha: (STT 1,98,184) Vajrasphoṭa! (STT 1,98,184)

Then, as soon as he had issued forth from the hearts of all the Tathāgatas, that very Blessed One Vajradhara emerged in the form of the multitudes of mudrās for binding the samaya of all the Tathāgatas.

And from all those hosts of mudrās that bind the samaya of all Tathāgatas, there emerged Tathāgata-forms as numerous as the atoms in all world-systems; these then merged once more into a single, solid mass, the body of the Great Bodhisattva Vajrasphoṭa. Taking his place upon a moon disc in the center of the Dharma-door of the Lord’s gabled palace with its peak of vajra-jewels, and binding all the Tathāgatas, he uttered this inspired utterance:
"Aho! Indeed, I am the firm Vajrasphoṭa of all Buddhas!"
That which is desired as bondage for those liberated from the bonds of existence, for the sake of the welfare of sentient beings.

Then the Blessed One again entered the samādhi called *Sarvatathāgatāveśamahāsattvasamayasambhavasattvavajra* (the Vajra-being arising from the pledge of the great being who is the penetration of all Tathāgatas), and from his own heart he emitted this servant of the seals (*mudrāceṭa*) of all Tathāgatas:
*Vajrāveśa*.
As soon as it had been emitted, from the hearts of all the Tathāgatas, that very Blessed One Vajradhara emerged, having become the entire host of seals of all the Tathāgatas.

And from all those hosts of seals (*mudrā*) of all the Tathāgatas, as many forms of Tathāgatas as there are atoms in all world-systems issued forth. Once again, they manifested as a single, solid mass in the form of a Vajra-entrance (*vajrāveśa*), and having taken their place upon a moon disc in the center of the action-door of the Blessed One’s peaked pavilion (*kūṭāgāra*) of precious vajra-jewels, they inspired all the Tathāgatas and uttered this inspired utterance (*udāna*):
"Aho! I am the firm Vajra-entrance of all Buddhas!"

"Since even servants become lords of all," (STT 1,100,189) [there is] the summoning of all Tathāgatas, as well as their entry, binding, and subjugation. (STT 1,100101,190) These are the executors of the commands of the Tathāgatas of sentient beings. (STT 1,101,191)
Then the Blessed One made the gesture of snapping his fingers (*vajrācchaṭikā*) in order to empower the assembly of all Tathāgatas.
And he spoke this heart-mantra (*hṛdaya*) for the empowerment of the assembly of all Tathāgatas:
*Vajrasamāja*.

Then, in that very instant, second, and moment, all the Tathāgatas—equal in number to the atoms within all the world-systems throughout the ocean-like clouds of the expanse of all world-systems—being impelled by the signal of the snapping of fingers from all the Tathāgatas, assembled together with their circles of assemblies of Bodhisattvas. They approached the peaked pavilion with its crest of vajra-jewel, where the Blessed One Vairocana was staying;
having approached, they said: "Oṃ, I perform prostration at the feet of all the Tathāgatas."

Having performed a prostration at the feet of all the Tathāgatas with this mantra, which is established by its very nature and recited according to one’s inclination, they uttered this inspired utterance:
"Oh, how great is the honor paid to the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra! For the Tathāgata shines forth in the midst of the wheel of the Tathāgatas!"

Then, having said this, all those Tathāgatas who had assembled from all the world-systems of the ten directions, through the empowerment (*adhiṣṭhāna*) of all the Tathāgatas, entered the heart of the Blessed One Vairocana together with the circles of their assemblies of Bodhisattvas.

And from the hearts of all those Tathāgatas, their respective circles of assemblies of Bodhisattvas emerged, formed mandalas on every side of the Blessed One’s peaked palace (*kūṭāgāra*) with its pinnacle of vajra-jewel, and remaining there in meditative absorption (*samāpanna*), they uttered this inspired utterance (*udāna*): *(STT 1,102,194)*
Oh, how truly sublime is the primordial majesty of all Buddhas, born of no beginning,
in that all atoms, when enumerated, have indeed attained oneness with the Buddhas!

Then the Blessed Ones, the Tathāgatas of the ten directions, having again assembled, made this request of the Blessed Lord, the Sovereign of all Tathāgatas, the Self-Vajrasattva, the Beginningless and Endless Great Vajra-Holder, for the sake of empowering this Great Maṇḍala of the Vajra Realm, for the protection of the entire realm of sentient beings without exception, for the attainment of all benefit and happiness, and for the supreme accomplishment of the perfect awakening to the wisdom and superknowledges of all Tathāgatas, by means of these one hundred and eight names: [The names follow]... (STT 1,104,196)
Vajrasattva, Mahāsattva, Vajra of all Tathāgatas, Samantabhadra, O primordial Vajra, Vajrapāṇi— homage be to you! Vajrarāja, supreme among those of excellent wisdom, Vajrāṅkuśa Tathāgata!
O Amogharāja, supreme vajra, vajra-attraction, homage be to you! O Vajrarāga, great bliss, vajra-arrow, subduer, O Mārakāma, great vajra, vajra-bow, homage be to you!
O Vajrasādhu, supreme among beings, O Vajratuṣṭi of great delight!
O Prāmodyarāja, foremost of vajras, O Vajraharṣa, homage be to you!
O Vajraratna, you whose aim is the excellent vajra, O Vajrākāśa, great jewel!
