Ākāśagarbha, rich in vajras, Vajragarbha, homage be to you!
Vajra-Tejas, great flame, Vajrasūrya, light of the Jinas,
Vajrarasmi, great brilliance, Vajraprabha, homage be to you!
Vajraketu, you who fulfill all purposes well; Vajradhvaja, you who are easily pleased!
Ratnaketu, Great Vajra, O Vajrayaṣṭi, homage be to you!
Vajrahāsa, Great Laughter, Vajrasmita, Great Wonder!
O supreme vajra of joy and gladness, O Vajraprīti, homage be to you! (STT 1,105,198) O Vajradharma, you who possess the meaning of true reality; O Vajrapadma, you who purify excellently;
O Lokeśvara, O excellent Vajrākṣa, O Vajranetra, homage be to you! (STT 1,105,199)
O Vajratīkṣṇa, Great Vehicle, Vajra-treasury, Great Weapon!
O Mañjuśrī, Vajra-profundity, Vajra-buddhi, homage be to you!
O Vajra-cause, Great Essence, Vajra-wheel, Great Method!
O you who turn [the wheel] well, arisen from the vajra, O Vajramaṇḍa, homage be to you!
O Vajra-speech, supreme among good vidyās, O Vajra-recitation, bestower of excellent accomplishment;
O wordless one, supreme vajra-accomplishment, O Vajra-voice, homage be to you!
O Vajrakarma, O Excellent Vajra-Knowledge, O Vajra-Action, O All-Pervading One!
(STT 1,106,200) O Vajrāmogha, O Great Magnanimity, O Vajraviśva, homage be to you!
(STT 1,106,200) O Vajrarakṣa, O Great Fortitude, O Vajravarman, O Greatly Firm One! (STT 1,106,200)
O Duryodhana, foremost of the very heroic, Vajravīrya, homage be to you! (STT 1,106,200) O Vajrayakṣa, great in skillful means, Vajradaṃṣṭra, source of great terror!
(STT 1,106,200) O crusher of Māra, fierce Vajra, terrible Vajra, homage be to you! (STT 1,106,200)
Whoever should hold these one hundred and eight auspicious names of yours,
he is consecrated with all the supreme [consecrations], such as the vajra-name-consecration and others.
But this [collection] is merely a secondary name for the Great Vajradhara.
Constantly singing and praising, he too shall become equal to the Holder of the Vajra.
Praised by us with these one hundred and eight names,
expand this Great Way, the realization of the Mahāyāna!
"We entreat you, O Protector, speak the supreme method:
the great wheel of all Buddhas, the most excellent great maṇḍala.

Then the Blessed One Vajradhara, having heard the words of entreaty from all the Tathāgatas, entered the samādhi called "The Vajra Empowerment Arising from the Samaya of All Tathāgatas" and proclaimed this great maṇḍala called the Vajradhātu.
Now, therefore, I shall fully explain the supreme great mandala,
which resembles the Vajradhātu and is known as the Vajradhātu.
Having sat down according to the rule in the center of the mandala...

Meditating upon and consecrating the Great Seal (mahāmudrā) of the Mahāsattva, he likewise arises while abiding in the mudrā, gazing in all directions; with a majestic stride and pride, he proclaims Vajrasattva.

The wise one should, according to his ability, outline a beautiful maṇḍala with a new, well-prepared, and perfectly measured thread. It should be square, with four gates and adorned with four archways.
Equipped with four lines and adorned with silk ribbons and flower garlands,
one should mark out the outer maṇḍala, inlaid with vajra-jewels at all corners, at the junctions of the gates and the projections.
Having entered its inner city, which resembles a wheel,
it is encircled by vajra-threads and adorned with eight pillars. It is further embellished by five lunar mandalas situated at the tops of the vajra-pillars.
One should place the image of the Buddha in the center of the middle mandala.
On all sides of the Buddha, in the midst of the mandalas,
one should draw the four supreme pledges in successive order.
Having entered with vajra-velocity into the fourfold mandalas,
one should construct the Akṣobhya-maṇḍala together with Vajradhara and the others;
and the Ratnasambhava-maṇḍala, filled with Vajragarbha and the others.
The mandala of Amitāyus is purified by Vajranetrī and the others;
the mandala of Amoghasiddhi, beginning with Vajraviśva, should be drawn.
One should paint the Vajra goddesses situated in the corners of the wheel.
One should draw the Buddha-worships in the corners of the outer mandala;
in the middle of all the doors, one should place the four door-keepers;
and among those situated within the outer mandala, one should install the Mahāsattvas.

Then, having duly bound the supreme pledge-mudrā (*samayāgrī-mudrā*), the Vajrācārya, having entered, should burst [the seal] and enter [the state]. In this regard, the heart-mantra for all entries is as follows: *Aḥ*.
Having properly sought permission and likewise performed the self-consecration (*svādhiṣṭhāna*) and so forth,
one should then recite one's own name and accomplish it with the vajra.
Then, having bound the Sattvavajrāṅkuśī mudrā, the Vajrācārya [proceeds] further.

By performing the snapping of fingers, one should assemble all the Buddhas. At that very moment, all the Buddhas, accompanied by Vajrasattva and complete with all the maṇḍalas, proceed to the assembly in the maṇḍala.
Then, having swiftly meditated upon the Mahāmudrā of Vajradhara,
one should recite once the supreme eight hundred names.
Thereupon, the Tathāgatas, being satisfied by this assembly, proceed with firm resolve.
Vajrasattva himself, having attained accomplishment, stands present as a friend.
Then, having performed the rites at all the gates with the hook and other implements,
one should establish the pledges by means of the supreme mudrās of great action.

One should accomplish the Great Beings by means of the supreme pledge-mudrās, such as Sattvavajrī and the others, while emitting the syllables JAḤ HŪṂ VAṂ HOḤ. Then all the Buddhas and other Great Beings assemble together.
"Drawn in, well-entered, and bound, they shall go under his control.
Then, having gratified those great-souled ones with secret offerings, he should request:
"For the sake of all sentient beings, grant all accomplishments!"
Thus, in all maṇḍalas, this is the activity of the Vajrācārya.
Now, herein in the Great Maṇḍala of the Vajradhātu, there occurs the detailed procedure for the entry of the vajra-disciples and so forth.

Therein, first of all, the entry takes place for the sake of performing the task of the supreme accomplishment of all benefit and happiness, and for the protection of the entire realm of sentient beings without exception or remainder.
In this entry into the great maṇḍala, no examination of who is a worthy vessel and who is not should be performed.
Why is that?
Because there are certain beings, O Blessed One, who have committed great evils; yet, having seen and entered this great maṇḍala of the Vajra Realm, they shall become free from all states of woe.

Furthermore, there are beings who are greedy for all kinds of food, drink, and sensual pleasures, who are hostile toward the commitments (*samaya*), and who are incapable of performing preliminary practices (*puraścaraṇa*) and so forth;
even for them, once they have entered here, there shall be the fulfillment of all their hopes by virtue of being able to act according to their desires.

Furthermore, Blessed Ones, there are beings who, being preoccupied with the practice of dancing and singing, do not understand the reality (*dharmatā*) of the realization of the Mahāyāna of all Tathāgatas; consequently, they enter the maṇḍalas of other deities, yet—fearing the rules of training (*śikṣāpada*)—they do not enter the maṇḍalas of all the Tathāgata families, which are the means of gathering [beings] through the fulfillment of all aspirations and which produce unsurpassed joy, delight, and gladness.
For those whose faces are situated on the path leading into the mandalas of the states of woe, this very entry into the Great Mandala of the Vajra Realm is appropriate,

for the sake of experiencing all delights, joys, supreme accomplishments, bliss, and mental well-being, and for the purpose of turning back from the path directed toward re-entering all states of woe.

Furthermore, Blessed One, there are righteous beings who, seeking the awakening of a Buddha through the supreme means for achieving the morality, concentration, and wisdom of all Tathāgatas, exert themselves and undergo hardship by means of the stages such as meditative absorption (*dhyāna*) and liberation (*vimokṣa*).
For them, by merely entering this very Great Maṇḍala of the Vajra Realm, even the state of being a Tathāgata is not difficult to attain; how much less so, then, any other accomplishment (*siddhi*)!
In that regard, first of all:
One should perform the fourfold prostration to all the Tathāgatas.
It is as follows:
with the entire body and the vajra-añjali extended, one should prostrate with this mantra: [Mantra] (STT 1,122,214)

Oṃ, I offer myself for the service and worship of all Tathāgatas; O Vajrasattva of all Tathāgatas, empower me! (STT 1,122,214) Remaining in that same position, placing the vajra-añjali at the heart, one should prostrate with the forehead while reciting this mantra:
(STT 1,122,215) Oṃ, I offer myself for the consecration of the worship of all Tathāgatas; O Vajraratna of all Tathāgatas, consecrate me! (STT 1,122,215)
Then, rising right there, one should prostrate with the head and face while forming the *vajrāñjali* mudrā, with this mantra:

*oṃ sarvatathāgatapūjāpravartanāyātmānaṃ niryātayāmi, sarvatathāgatavajradharma pravartaya mām //* Then, remaining in that same position, lowering the *vajrāñjali* from the head and placing it at the heart, one should prostrate with the crown of the head while reciting this mantra: *(STT 1,122,217)*

Oṃ, I offer myself for the ritual of worship of all Tathāgatas; perform for me the vajra-activity of all Tathāgatas! (STT 1,122,217) Then, wearing a red upper garment and having one’s face covered with a red cloth, one should bind the Sattvavajrī mudrā with this heart-mantra: (STT 1,122,218) "You are the Samaya! (STT 1,122,218)
Then, having tied the garland with the two middle fingers, one should cause [the disciple] to enter with this heart-mantra:
*sahama hūṃ*.
Having thus caused [him] to enter, one should speak as follows:

Today you have entered the family of all the Tathāgatas. Therefore, I shall generate in you the vajra-knowledge, by means of which knowledge you will attain even the accomplishment of all the Tathāgatas,
let alone other accomplishments.
"You must not speak [of this] to anyone who has not seen the great maṇḍala, lest your *samaya* be violated.

(STT 1,123,220) Then the Vajrācārya himself, having bound the Sattvavajrī mudrā with its face turned downward and placed it upon the head of the Vajra-disciple, shall say: (STT 1,123,221) "This Samaya-vajra shall split your head if you speak of it to anyone. (STT 1,123,221)
Then, having likewise consecrated the water once with the Samayamudrā while reciting the Śapathahṛdaya mantra, one should have that disciple drink it.
In this regard, the Śapathahṛdaya is as follows:
"Today Vajrasattva himself is established within your heart."
"If he should say this method, one should depart at that very moment after piercing through.
(STT 1,123,222) *Vajrodaka ṭhaḥ*.
(STT 1,123,222) Then, one should speak to the disciple: (STT 1,123,223)
"From this day forward, I am your Vajrapāṇi; whatever I tell you to do, that must be performed.
You must not disregard me, lest by failing to avoid misfortune, you bring about your own death and fall into hell.
Having said this, he should speak as follows:
"Speak! May all the Tathāgatas empower me; may Vajrasattva enter me! Then, the Vajrācārya, acting with haste, should form the Sattvavajrī mudrā and recite this:
"This is that samaya-vajra, known as Vajrasattva."
"May the unsurpassed vajra-wisdom enter you this very day!
(STT 1,125,224) "Vajra-entrance! Aḥ! (STT 1,125,224) Then, having formed the wrathful fist, one should release the Sattvavajrī mudrā. (STT 1,125,225)
And one who desires it should utter the Mahāyāna-abhisamaya with vajra-words. (STT 1,125,225) Thereupon, [the deity] enters; as soon as one has been entered, divine knowledge arises.
(STT 1,125,226) By means of that knowledge, one understands the minds of others. (STT 1,125,226)
He knows all matters— past, future, and present.
His heart becomes firm in the teaching of all the Tathāgatas,
and all his sufferings perish.

He becomes free from all fear and invulnerable among all sentient beings, and all the Tathāgatas empower him. All accomplishments (siddhis) become manifest before him, and unprecedented joys— producing causeless laughter, delight, and gladness— arise within him.

Through those blisses, for some, meditative absorptions (*samādhi*) are accomplished; for some, the dhāraṇīs; for some, the fulfillment of all hopes; and even for some, the state of a Tathāgata is accomplished.
(STT 1,125,226) Then, having bound that mudrā, one should release it at one’s own heart with this heart-mantra:
(STT 1,125,227) “Abide, O Vajra! Be firm for me; be eternal for me. Empower my heart and grant me all accomplishments! HŪṂ HA HA HA HA HOḤ! (STT 1,125,227)
Then, one should cast that garland into the great maṇḍala with this heart-mantra:
"Pratīccha vajra hoḥ.
Then, whatever [deity] it falls upon, that one will be accomplished for him.
Then, having taken that garland, one should bind it upon his very head with this heart-mantra:
*Oṃ, you of great power, accept this being!* By its being bound, he becomes accepted by that Great Being.
And his [mantra] will be accomplished quickly.
Then, for one thus possessed, one should release the binding of the mouth with this heart-mantra:
Oṃ! Vajrasattva himself is now intent upon opening your eyes.
The one with all-seeing eyes opens the unsurpassed vajra-eye: "O Vajra, look! (STT 1,127,230). Thereafter, he should show the great maṇḍala in its proper sequence. (STT 1,128,231)
Upon merely seeing the great maṇḍala, one is empowered by all the Tathāgatas.
Vajrasattva abides in one’s heart.
And one beholds various miracles and transformations, such as the appearance of circles of light and so forth.

Because he is empowered by the Tathāgata Arvata, the Blessed One Mahāvajradhara sometimes grants a vision in his own form, saying, "I am the Tathāgata. From that moment on, all goals, all desired undertakings, and all accomplishments— up to and including the state of Vajradhara or the state of a Tathāgata— are attained.
Then, having shown the great maṇḍala, one should consecrate [the disciple] with scented water from the vase empowered by the vajra, using this heart mantra:
*vajrābhiṣiñca*.
Then, having bound one of the garlands of mudrās and placed his own insignia upon the hand, one should speak thus:
Today you have been consecrated by the Buddhas through the vajra-consecration.
Take this state of all-buddhahood, the vajra, for the sake of perfect accomplishment!
Oṃ, I consecrate you as the Lord of Vajras.
"Abide, O Vajra, you are the Samaya!
Then, one should consecrate [the disciple] with the Vajra-name consecration by means of this mantra:
"Oṃ, Vajrasattva, I consecrate you through the Vajra-name consecration; O, [you whose] Vajra-name is such-and-such!"* (*The specific name is to be inserted here.)
"Whatever name one may give [to a disciple], the word 'he' (he-śabda) should be used for that person. (STT 1,130,234) This concludes the detailed procedure for the entry into all maṇḍalas.
(STT 1,130,234) Then one should say: "Which do you prefer: the knowledge of the accomplishment of the arising of wealth? (STT 1,131,235)

Or the knowledge of the accomplishment of the perfection of supernatural powers (*ṛddhisiddhi*); or the knowledge of the accomplishment of the perfection of the *vidyādhara*s; up to the knowledge of the accomplishment of the supreme perfection of all the Tathāgatas.
Then, whatever is pleasing to each [practitioner], that they should maintain.
Then, one should teach the knowledge of the seal (*mudrā*) for the accomplishment of the attainment of the goal:
"One should visualize the vajra-image situated as a treasure within the heart."
Meditating thus, he beholds treasures situated within the earth.
Having drawn the form of a vajra, one should contemplate it in the sky;
wherever one perceives that [vajra] falling, there one should indicate the treasure.
A wise man should visualize the vajra-image upon his tongue;
in this regard, he himself declares by his own speech that "it exists" from the perspective of ultimate truth.
Visualizing his entire body as consisting of the vajra-image, he should meditate.
"Wherever one who is possessed falls, there one should indicate a treasure. In that very context, the heart-mantras are as follows:
*vajranidhi*.
Treasure of jewels; treasure of Dharma; treasure of karma.
Then, one should teach the knowledge of the seal for the accomplishment of the Vajra-ṛddhiṣīdhinī:
"When the vajra-possession has arisen, one should visualize water consisting of vajra-forms; having quickly attained accomplishment, one may walk upon the surface of that water."

In that very same way, having generated an absorption, whatever form one contemplates as oneself, that indeed becomes even the form of a Buddha for oneself. Likewise, having absorbed oneself, one should think of oneself as "I am space."

Meditating thus, one may become invisible for as long as one desires. Having oneself become possessed by the Vajra and meditating, "I am the Vajra," one shall become a traveler through the sky, reaching whatever place one ascends to.
In this regard, there are these heart-mantras:
Vajrajala,
Vajrarūpa.
"I am Vajra.
(STT 1,133,239) Then, one should teach the knowledge of the mudrā for the accomplishment of the siddhi of the Vajra-Vidyādhara:
(STT 1,136,240) "Having drawn a lunar disc, one should ascend to the sky above the head. (STT 1,136,240)
Manifesting a vajra in his hand, he becomes a Vajra-vidyādhara.
Having ascended the lunar disc, he should manifest a vajra-jewel;
as long as he desires, that pure-souled one flies up in an instant.
Having ascended upon moon discs, one should visualize a vajra-lotus held in the hand;
visualizing thus as Vajranetra, one shall grant the station of the Vidyādharas.
Standing in the center of a moon mandala, one should visualize the Karma-vajra.
"From the Vajraviśvadharā, one shall quickly become a master of all vidyās. (STT 1,136,241) Now, the heart-mantras are as follows: (STT 1,136,2412) Vajradhara! (STT 1,136,2412)
Ratnadhara,
Padmadhara,
Karmadhara.
Then, one should teach the knowledge of the mudrās for accomplishing the supreme siddhi of all Tathāgatas:
"Having fully contemplated the samādhi of all vajras within the realms of space,
the Vajra-Self flies up in an instant for as long as he desires."

By meditating upon the supreme *sarvaśuddhasamādhi*, one who accomplishes gnosis swiftly attains the five superknowledges (*pañcābhijñā*). Recollecting that all space consists of Vajrasattva—(STT 1,137,242; STT 1,137–140,242; STT 1,138,243).
Possessing firm recollection, one will swiftly become Vajradhara himself.
Having resolved that everything within the expanse of space consists of the forms of the Buddhas,
the samādhi of all Buddhas will lead to the state of Buddhahood.
Now, the heart-mantras for this are as follows:
Vajra-vajra!
Śuddha-śuddha! (STT 1,138,244)
Sattvasattva / Buddhabuddha / The accomplishments of all siddhis and the perfection of gnosis.
Then, when he becomes capable of maintaining the secret, one should first speak to him the Heart-mantra of the Oath:
Oṃ! Vajrasattva himself is today established within your heart.

"If he should say, 'I will go there immediately after piercing through,' then one should speak thus: 'You must not transgress this heart-mantra of the oath; otherwise, by failing to avoid calamity, you shall suffer an untimely death and, with this very body, fall into hell.
Thereafter, one should instruct him in the secret mudrā-knowledge."
Having generated the vajra-entrance (*vajrāveśa*), one who is composed should perform the clapping of hands (*tāla*).
By means of the subtle claps of the vajra-añjali, even a mountain may be brought under control.
This is the Vajra-clapping Mudrā (*vajratālamudrā*).
Having applied the ritual procedure for the vajra-entrance (*vajrāveśavidhi*), one should strike with the palms in the vajra-bind (*vajrabandha*) gesture;
by means of the subtle practice of *tāla*, even a mountain may be entered.
Likewise, through the ritual of entrance, when the vajra-bind is extended—

"By snapping the fingertips together, one may destroy a hundred lineages in an instant. Through the application of the subtle method of entry, with all fingers joined together and released from the vajra-bind, it is the supreme remover of all suffering."
Now follows their secret practice:
one should enter the body of a woman or a man through the *bhaga*.
Having entered, one should mentally pervade that entire body evenly.
In this regard, these are the *tālahṛdayas*:
Vajravaśa,
Vajraviśa.
Vajrahana!
Vajrahara!
Then, having bestowed the heart-mantra, one should instruct [the disciple] in the knowledge of the four mudrās of the deity of one’s own family.
It should be spoken according to this procedure:
"You must not show even a single one of these other mudrās to anyone who is unskilled in them.
For what reason?"
For if sentient beings, having not seen the great maṇḍala, should nevertheless employ the binding of mudrās, then they will not achieve success in that manner.
Consequently, overcome by doubt and failing to avoid danger, they will quickly die and fall into the great Avīci hell. Furthermore, you yourself would go to the states of woe.
Now follows the knowledge of the great mudrā for accomplishing the being of all Tathāgatas:
Beginning with the knowledge of the mind, one should accomplish Vajrasūrya;
one should manifest oneself as the image of the Buddha, the Vajradhātu.
"By this alone, once it is accomplished, one attains knowledge, longevity, strength, and youth;
one attains the power to go everywhere, and even Buddhahood is not difficult to obtain.
This is the *Sarvatathāgatābhisaṃbodhimudrā*.
Now follows the binding of the Great Seal (*mahāmudrā*) for the practice of Vajrasattva:
Brandishing the vajra with pride and maintaining the pride of the Vajra,
one shall oneself become Vajrasattva through the vajras of body, speech, and mind.
By this, one becomes all-pervading, the lord of all desires, and happy;

through supernatural power, longevity, strength, and supreme form, one shall become equal to Vajrasattva. According to the sequence of the drawing, [one should practice] with the vajras of body, speech, and mind.

One should accomplish the Mahāsattvas together with their signs and mudrās. Now, herein I shall explain, in due order, the accomplishment and the very success of all ritual manuals (kalpas), as well as the great rites of those who have attained success.
Every day, at the appropriate time before [other activities], one should perform the self-consecration (*svādhiṣṭhāna*) and so forth;
having done so, one should accomplish everything thereafter as one pleases.
In this regard, the detailed procedure for accomplishing the Great Seal (*mahāmudrā*) is as follows:
Having generated the vajra-entrance (*vajrāveśa*) and having bound the great seal (*mahāmudrā*) according to the ritual procedure, one should visualize that Great Being before oneself.
Having seen that Knowledge Being (*jñānasattva*), one should visualize him within one's own body.
"Having drawn [them] forth, caused them to enter, bound them, and brought them under control, one should accomplish [the rite].
In that regard, their heart-mantras are as follows:
Vajrasattva, ĀḤ."
The Heart of the Vajra-Entrance; (STT 1,147,255) O Vajrasattva, you who are visible; (STT 1,147,255) the Heart of the Recollection of Mahāsattva. (STT 1,147,255)
JAḤ HŪṂ VAṂ HOḤ.
This is the heart-mantra for summoning, causing entry, binding, and subjugating the Great Beings (mahāsattva).
When it is proclaimed, "You are the pledge" (samayas tvam), one should enter the moon behind [the deity].
In that regard, one should meditate upon oneself as the *sattva*, saying, "I am the pledge (*samaya*).
One should meditate upon oneself as the very mudrā of whichever *sattva* [is being practiced].
One should accomplish the mastery of all mudrās through the vajra-recitation (*vajrajāpa*).
Jaḥ hūṃ vaṃ hoḥ—one should cause all the Buddhas to enter the body of the *būrva*.
Through the mind and the excellent yoga, this is another great accomplishment (*sādhana*).
Now I shall explain their activity, the unsurpassed Vajra-activity.
One who has attained perfection through the recollection of the Buddha (buddhānusmṛti) shall swiftly attain Buddhahood.
One who has attained perfection through Sattvavajrī shall become the sovereign of all mudrās. Through the Ratnavajrī mudrā, however, one becomes the sovereign of all jewels.
Through the Dharma-vajrī, one indeed becomes a bearer of the Buddha-dharma;
through the Karma-vajrī mudrā, one becomes a performer of vajra-activities.
By binding the Sattva-mudrā, Vajrasattva is accomplished.
One should attract the Vajra-holders through the application of the Vajra-attraction.
The Great Seal of Vajra-passion shall cause all Buddhas to feel passion;
one shall satisfy all Buddhas through the application of the Vajra-excellence.
One should bestow the empowerments of the Buddhas, as well as the ritual for the jewel and the nectar.
Through the application of Vajrateja, one will quickly become Vajrateja.
By serving the holder of the Vajra-banner, one becomes a fulfiller of all hopes.
Applying the procedure for the Vajra-Laughter, one should laugh together with all the Buddhas.
Through the application of the Vajra-Dharma, one shall become a bearer of the Vajra-Dharma;
through the application of the Vajra-Sharp, one becomes the foremost wisdom of all the Buddhas.
Having served the Holder of the Vajra-Wheel, he shall turn the Wheel of Dharma;
through the application of the Vajra-Speech, he attains the accomplishment of the Buddha’s word.
Through the supreme sādhana of Vajra-Action, Vajra-Action will swiftly be accomplished.
Having bound the vajra-armour, one shall attain the state of a vajra-body.
By accomplishing the Vajrayakṣa, one shall become equal to the Vajrayakṣa.
Through the binding of the vajra-fist, all mudrās are successfully accomplished.
By accomplishing Vajralāsyā, one shall indeed obtain great vajra-delight;
by binding the Vajramālā, one bestows the empowerment of all Buddhas;
and one should employ Vajragītā through the application of Vajragītā.
By performing the Vajra Dance, he is honored by all the Buddhas.
Through the application of Vajra Incense, he shall gladden the entire world.
By performing the Vajra Flower, he shall bring the world under his control.
By offering worship, one should bestow the eye of the Great Seal (mahāmudrā) of Vajrāloka;
through the application of Vajragandha, one shall become the remover of all suffering.
Through the drawing-in with the Vajrāṅkuśa, one becomes the supreme performer of all summonings.
"Through the application of the Vajrapāśa, may one become capable of entering all;
by joining the Vajrasphoṭa, one becomes capable of binding all;
and by applying the procedure of the Vajrāveśa, one is a accomplisher of all entrances."

Now follows the knowledge of the vajra-samaya-mudrā of all the Tathāgatas: Having firmly formed the añjali with all the fingers bound together, it is declared to be the Vajra-añjali; when well-bound, it is the Vajra-bandha.
All samaya-mudrās, however, arise from the vajra-bind;
I shall now explain their binding, the unsurpassed vajra-bind:
having made the *sattva-vajrā* firm, with the middle fingers raised and joined like sprouts.
The second [mudrā] described by the Buddha is formed by the contraction of the middle fingers;
the middle finger and thumb are like a jewel, while the middle fingers are contracted like a lotus.
The fifth is the Buddha-mudrā, likewise with the tips well-curved.
Now, therefore, I shall fully explain the binding of the mudrā for taking the pledge, as well as the accomplishment and the ritual activity of the Tathāgata family.
[It is formed] with both hands joined like a moon, with the middle fingers omitted.
Through the non-attachment of the faces of the final fingers, the *vajra* indeed [is joined] with the *sattvavajrī*.
Through the supreme union of the foremost *aṅkuśī*, she bestows the cry of "Excellent!
(*sādhukāra*). This is indeed the host of *siddhi-mudrās* for the fourfold *Vajrasattva*.

The Ratnavajrā [mudrā] is formed by joining the tips of the thumbs and index fingers together; that same [mudrā], with the middle, ring, and little fingers well extended, is the Patākā, provided with the thumbs and little fingers held level.
That very same [mudrā], when rotated, remains positioned at the place of the hand;
with the thumbs extended and level and the index fingers bent,
that same [mudrā] becomes the Vajrakośa when the middle fingers are joined at their tips.
That same [mudrā], however, when the little fingers are equalized and designated as a wheel,
with the thumbs released from their bond and positioned at the opened mouth—
by joining the tips of the little fingers and the thumbs, it becomes the Karmavajrī.
That very same [mudrā], with the tips [of the fingers] joined together and extended straight in the heart,
has its tips bent like fangs, while the little fingers are released from their joint;
one should press the two thumbs within the space of the little fingers using the bent tips.
At the heart, the *mālinī* mudrā has the thumbs joined and the fingers well-extended;
when dancing, it is cupped above the head with the fingertips emerging from the mouth.
The *vajrabandha* is directed downward, while the *svāñjali* is held upward.
With the thumbs pressed together and the palms well extended;
with one index finger contracted and the two thumbs bound in a knot;
with the tips of the thumbs bound in a circle—this is called the "vajra-fist" seal, joined at the tips.
Now I shall explain their accomplishment, the supreme Vajra-accomplishment (vajrasādhana),
by means of one’s own mudrā abiding at the heart through the Sattvavajra-samādhi.
Now I shall explain their activity, the unsurpassed Vajra-activity (vajrakarma).

Through the *Samāja*, the Tathāgatas will, at that very moment, bestow their empowerment upon the mandala master and his disciples by means of the mudrās beginning with Vajradhātu. When the Sattvavajrī mudrā is bound, one becomes equal to the Holder of the Vajra.
As soon as Vajrāṅkuśī is bound, one should summon all the Buddhas.
By means of the application of Rāgavajra, one may inspire passion even in the Perfectly Awakened Ones.
Through Vajratuṣṭi, one is praised with shouts of "Excellent! by all the Victors.
When the Ratnavajrī [mudrā] is bound, he is consecrated by the Buddhas;
when the Vajrasūryā is indeed bound, he becomes like the radiance of a Buddha.
Having become a bearer of the Vajraketu, he shall fulfill all hopes.
By means of the application of the Vajra-laugh, one should laugh together with all the Buddhas.
Having assumed the Dharmavajrī [mudrā], one becomes like Vajradharma.
Having grasped the Vajrakośā [mudrā], one cuts through all afflictions.
Having made the Vajracakra firm, one shall become the lord of the maṇḍala.
Through the application of Vajra-speech, the supreme accomplishment of Vajra-voice is attained.
By concentrating upon Karmavajrā, one becomes equal to Vajra-action.
Having made the adamantine armor firm, the body shall become composed of vajra.
With the seal of the tip of the adamantine fangs, he shatters the wicked Māras.
Having bound the firm adamantine fist, he brings all seals under his control.
Through *lāsya* one obtains divine delights; through *mālā*, ornaments;
through *gīta*, constant eloquent speech; and through *nṛtya*, one receives worship.
Through *dhūpa*, one gladdens the world; through *puṣpa*, one is adorned with beauty.
Through Dīpā, one attains purity of light; through Gandhā, divine fragrance.
(STT 1,165,277) Vajrāṅkuśī shall attract, and Vajrapāśā shall cause entry. Vajrasphoṭā shall bind, and Vajraghaṇṭā shall cause [them] to enter. (STT 1,165,277)
Now follow the Dharma-mudrās:
The Vajra-knowledge of the Buddhas makes the Vajra-realm firm.
Hereafter, I shall explain the Dharma-mudrās according to the ritual procedure.
When "You are the Samaya" is uttered, one becomes the lord of all mudrās. When "Bring them here! is indeed uttered, one will certainly summon the Buddhas.
When "Aho! How blissful! is uttered, one may even cause the Buddhas to experience passion.
Having uttered "Excellent! Excellent! with words of praise, he should satisfy [the deity]. When it is proclaimed, "You are truly great," one shall obtain the consecration of a Buddha.

When "rūpoddyotā" is uttered, one will possess the splendor of the Dharma; (STT 1,171,279) when "arthaprāptiḥ" is uttered, he shall fulfill all hopes. (STT 1,171,280) By laughing "ha ha hūṃ he," one attains the smile of a Buddha. (STT 1,171,280)
When "the doer of all" is proclaimed [by the Buddhas], even that which is not to be done is purified. When "the cutter of suffering" is proclaimed, he cuts through all sufferings.
When "the awakening of the Buddha" is proclaimed, one becomes the sovereign of the maṇḍala.
When "Pratiśabda" (Echo) is uttered, one shall converse with the Buddhas.
When "Suvaśitvam" (Mastery) is uttered, mastery shall arise from all sides. When "Nirbhayas tvam" (You are fearless) is uttered, may one become fearless in an instant.
When "Enemy-devourer" is uttered, he shall devour all enemies. When "All-accomplishment" is uttered, all accomplishments will come to pass.
[He shall attain] great delight, divine pleasure, and likewise the splendor of divine form.

*Śrotrasaukhya* shall grant happiness; *Sarvapūjā*, supreme worshipfulness. *Prahlādini* grants happiness of mind; for *Phalāgāmi* indeed bestows fruits. *Sutejāgri*, O you of great splendor! *Sugandhāṅgi*, grant the state of fragrance!
"Āyāhi jaḥ" is the summoner; "āhi hūṃ hūṃ" is the one that causes entry.
"He sphoṭa vaṃ" is the great binder; "ghaṇṭa aḥ aḥ" is the one that sets [them] in motion.
Now, the auspicious practice for these Dharma-mudrās will be explained.
"One should visualize a vajra upon the tongue while performing all activities. (STT 1,173,284) Now follows the binding of the action-seal (karmamudrā):
(STT 1,185,285) "Having firmly formed the vajra-fist, one who is composed should divide it into two. (STT 1,185,285)
The two vajra-mudrās shall come together; from that, the binding is performed.
The left vajra-finger is to be grasped by the right as it is raised up.
This mudrā, named Bodhāgrī, bestows the awakening of the Buddhas.
For Akṣobhya, however, it is the earth-touching [mudrā]; for Ratnasambhava, likewise, the boon-granting;
for Amitābha, the supreme samādhi; and for Amoghasiddhi, the fear-dispelling.
Hereafter, I shall explain the action-mudrās (karmamudrā) in brief.
These are the activators of vajra-activity for the beings such as Vajrasattva and others.
With pride, she is raised up by the two [hands] while remaining in the posture of grasping a hook;
and through the application of striking with an arrow, she is the one who utters "Well done! (sādhukāra) while abiding in the heart.
In the consecration, however, there is the display of the double-vajra at the heart and the sun;
likewise, the staff-like arm is positioned on the left and rotated toward the mouth.
With the right and left [hands] opened wide, the left hand at the heart holds the edge of a sword.
Whirling like a circle of fire, it emerges from the two mouths of the vajra;
it is situated upon the uṣṇīṣa with cheeks released by the whirling of the vajra-dance;
it is the armor, the foremost tusk of the little finger, pressed by the two fists.
One should bow with the application of vajra-pride, with intentions trembling;
[offerings] issued from the mouth as a bound garland, set in motion by vajra-dance.
Likewise, through the application of the vajra-fist, one should present incense and the other offerings.
Compared to the worship of all Buddhas, these [other] offerings are considered inferior.

(STT 1,186,289) By binding the index fingers like a hook, the little fingers become the Great Hook (Mahāṅkuśī). (STT 1,186,290) By pressing the tips of the arms against the shoulders and the backs of the hands together. (STT 1,186,290)
Now I shall explain their accomplishment, equal to that performed by Vajrakarmakṛt:
"One should visualize a vajra consisting entirely of vajras within the heart.
Now, regarding these action-mudrās (*karmamudrā*), there are manifold vajra-activities.
When the Fist of Knowledge is bound, the wisdom of a Buddha enters [the practitioner].
When Akṣobhya is bound, the mind becomes unshakable.
Through the mudrā of Ratnasaṃbhava, one becomes possessed of supreme grace for others.
In the seal of the Wheel of the True Dharma (*saddharmacakramudrā*), one should turn the wheel of Dharma;
one will swiftly become supreme, bestowing fearlessness upon all sentient beings.
Having made the vajra-pride firm, one shall obtain the bliss of Vajrasattva.
One should attract all the Tathāgatas from the Black [direction] with Vajrāṅkuśī;
one should even personally arouse passion for one’s own Vajra-consort with Vajravāṇa.
Indeed, through Vajratuṣṭi, all the Victors bestow words of praise.
Having bound the great vajra-jewel, he is consecrated by the Teachers.
Having attained the Vajrasūrya [samādhi], he becomes equal to Vajrasūrya.
Having raised the Vajradhvaja, he shall cause a rain of jewels to fall.
By maintaining the Vajrasmitā samādhi, one quickly laughs together with the Buddhas.
(STT 1,194,294) By maintaining the Vajraphullā samādhi, he beholds the Vajradharma.
(STT 1,194,295) Having firmly bound the Vajrakośā, he cuts through all sufferings. (STT 1,194,295)
Having correctly assumed the vajra-wheel, one should turn the wheel of Dharma;
indeed, all the words of the Buddha are accomplished through the vajra dance. By means of the supreme worship of the vajra dance, one may bring even the Vajra-Buddhas under one's control.
With his limbs bound by adamantine armor, he shall attain the essence of a vajra.
Having assumed adamantine fangs, he himself may shatter even vajras.

One shall take away everything with the Vajra-fist and obtain the accomplishment of the mudrās. Vajralāsyā bestows delight; Vajramālā [bestows] beautiful form; Vajragītā [bestows] the state of being a fine singer; and Vajranṛtyā causes one to dance.
With Dhūpā one obtains delight of the mind; with Puṣpā, ornaments. Through the worship of light, one attains great radiance; through Vajragandhā, a fragrant scent.
With Vajrāṅkuśī, one should attract; with Vajrapāśī, one should cause entry.
"One should bind the vajra-shackles, and one should move the vajra-bell. (STT 1,195,298) Now follows the detailed procedure for the general method of binding all mudrās:
(STT 1,199,299) Therein, at the very outset, having performed the snapping of the fingers of the vajra-bind, one should recite this heart-mantra at the heart: (STT 1,199,299)
*vajrabandha traṭ*!
(STT 1,200,299) Thereupon, all mudrā-bindings come under control within the vajras of one’s own body, speech, and mind.
(STT 1,200,300) Then, having bound the samaya-mudrā of vajra-entrance, one should recite this heart-mantra: (STT 1,200,300)
Aḥ!
(STT 1,200,300) Then, having entered [the state], they abide as friends.
(STT 1,200,300) Thereafter, recollecting the Mahāsattva of the Mudrā-samaya, one should utter this heart-mantra: (STT 1,200,301)
"I am the Great Samaya Being.

(STT 1,200,301) By this, all mudrās are accomplished; thus concludes the detailed procedure for the accomplishment of all mudrās. (STT 1,200,301) Now follows the detailed procedure for the general means of accomplishment:
In that regard, having first bound one’s own mudrā, one should visualize oneself as the being of one’s own mudrā with this heart mantra:
*samayo ’ham*.
Then, having visualized oneself as the being of one’s own mudrā, one should consecrate it with this mantra: [mantra].
"Empower me as the Samayasattva! (STT 1,201,303).

Then, one should accomplish [the goal]; this is the detailed procedure for the means of accomplishment (sādhana-vidhi). Now follows the detailed procedure for the attainments (siddhi): (STT 1,202,304).
In that regard, first of all, one who desires the accomplishment of wealth should [use] this heart-mantra for the accomplishment of wealth:
"By this, the mudrā is accomplished; it brings about the arising of great wealth.
(STT 1,202,304) Then, one who desires the accomplishment of the Vajra should [use] this heart-mantra: (STT 1,202,305)
Vajrasiddhi!
By this, one becomes a Vajrasiddha according to one's desire.
Now, if one should desire the accomplishment of a Vidyadhara, [one should use] this heart-mantra: (STT 1,203,306)
"O Vajra-Vidyādhara!
By this [mantra], there is the accomplishment of a Vidyādhara according to one's desire.
Now, if one should desire the supreme accomplishment, [one should do so] with the heart-mantra of one's own mudrā."
The Detailed Procedure for the Accomplishment of Siddhis.
(STT 1,203,306) Now follows the detailed procedure for the general consecration (*vajrīkaraṇa*) of all mudrās within one’s own body, speech, and mind-vajras:
(STT 1,203,307) When the empowerment of the mudrā becomes lax, or when one desires to release it oneself, (STT 1,203,307)
Then, one should stabilize [the commitment] with this heart-mantra:
Oṃ vajrasattva samayam anupālaya vajrasattvatvenopatiṣṭha.

Dṛḍho me bhava, sutoṣyo me bhava, anurakto me bhava, supoṣyo me bhava, sarvasiddhiṃ ca me prayaccha, sarvakarmasu ca me cittaśreyaḥ kuru, hūṃ ha ha ha ha ho bhagavan sarvatathāgatavajra mā me muñca vajrībhava mahāsamayasattva āḥ.

"By this, even those who have committed the immediate transgressions (*ānantarya*), and even those who seek liberation from all Tathāgatas, and those who practice the seals (*mudrā*) of all Tathāgatas, shall—through the firm realization of Vajrasattva—swiftly attain in this very life whatever accomplishment they desire: whether it be the supreme accomplishment (*uttamasiddhi*), the adamantine accomplishment (*vajrasiddhi*), the accomplishment of Vajrasattva, or even the accomplishment of a Tathāgata. Thus spoke the Blessed One, the Vajrasattva of all Tathāgatas. (STT 1,204,308) Now follows the detailed general procedure for liberation regarding all seals (*sarvamudrā*). (STT 1,205,309)
Therein, from the very beginning, one should release each mudrā at the very place from which it arose, using this heart-mantra:
*vajra muḥ*.

Then, with the Ratnavajrī-mudrā arisen from the heart, standing in the position of one’s own consecration, one should consecrate [oneself] and, winding and binding the garland with the tips of the fingers, likewise bind the armor using this heart-mantra: *vajra muḥ*.
Oṃ, consecrate me with the jewel-vajra; make all my mudrās firm with the excellent armor! Vaṃ.
(STT 1,205,310) Then, having again released the binding of the garland ending with the armor, one should satisfy [the deity] with equanimity by means of this heart-mantra:
Vajra tuṣya hoḥ! (STT 1,205,311)
By this rite, the mudrās—both those released and those bound—are satisfied;
they shall attain the state of Vajra, or else that of Vajrasattva.
Vajrasattva, when recited even once, [grants] whatever is desired to those whose nature is bliss.

"It is accomplished by mere recitation, according to the words of Vajrapāṇi," said the Blessed One Samantabhadra regarding all the ritual activities for the accomplishment of the beings such as Vajrasattva and others.
For in this [system], recitation (jāpa) is indeed pleasing and bestows accomplishment in all ritual manuals (kalpa).

By means of the methods as one desires for the heart-seals (hṛnmudrā), mantras, and vidyās— whether according to what is taught in the manuals or even those composed by oneself— the practice (sādhana) here is entirely universal.
Then, proclaiming the secret mudrā of worship, one should perform the fourfold secret worship while singing this vajra hymn of praise:
Oṃ! Through the gathering of Vajrasattva, [you are] the unsurpassed Vajraratna;
through the songs of Vajradharma, become a performer of Vajrakarma.
Then, within the inner mandala as well, worship should be performed with this very song of vajra-praise, with the hand-gesture of vajra-dance, and with secret incense and other offerings.
Then, having performed worship with vajra-incense and so forth in the outer mandala, one should place those offerings in their respective positions.
Then, let everyone perform worship according to their ability.

Having informed all the Tathāgatas and having performed worship with incense and other offerings according to one's desire, one should satisfy those who have entered [the maṇḍala] with all kinds of food, drink, dwellings, and requisites as available, presented from the great maṇḍala; then one should bestow this Vajra-vow of all the Tathāgatas:
"This is that state of all Buddhahood, residing in the hand of Vajrasattva.
You too must always maintain this firm vow of Vajrapāṇi."

Oṃ, O Vajra-samaya of the accomplishment of all Tathāgatas, abide! I cause you to hold this, O Vajrasattva! Hi hi hi hi hūṃ! (STT 1,214,316) Then, it must not be told to anyone by any of them again. (STT 1,214,316) The heart-mantra of the oath should be proclaimed. (STT 1,214,316)
Then, having dismissed all the Tathāgatas as they entered, one should inform them:
having formed the Sarvavajrī mudrā, one should release it upward and recite this heart-mantra:
oṃ kṛto vaḥ sarvasattvārthaḥ siddhir dattā yathānugā //
"Go to the realm of the Buddha, but return again!
Vajrasattva muḥ!
Thus it should be performed in all maṇḍalas, and there is liberation through the supreme samaya-mudrās.
The detailed procedure for the Great Maṇḍala of the Vajra Realm from the *Sarvatathāgata-mahāyānābhisamaya-mahākalparāja* is completed.
(The Detailed Procedure for the Vajra-Guhyamaṇḍala).
Then the Blessed One entered the samādhi called the Vajra Arising from the Samaya of All Tathāgatas’ All-Vajra Dhāraṇīs.

And immediately upon his entering [that state], at that very moment, from the hearts of all the Tathāgatas, that very Blessed One Vajrapāṇi, having become the deities of the Vajradhāraṇī-samaya-mudrās who bear the form of Vajradharas and possess inner universal flames, emerged.

Having perfected the wisdoms of the *vajra-dhāraṇīs* of all the Tathāgatas of all world-systems, and having become the reflected images of the *samaya-mudrās* of all the Tathāgatas, they relied upon moon-discs through the yoga of the arrangement of the Great Maṇḍala of the Vajra Realm of all the Tathāgatas, and uttered this inspired utterance: "Oh,
how great is the desire for the welfare of all beings inherent in the thought of awakening (*bodhicitta*),
that these heroes assume even the form of women according to the needs of those to be trained!"
Then the Blessed One entered the samādhi called the Empowerment of the Vajra Realm of the Samaya of the Wisdom-Mudrās of All Tathāgatas, and spoke this supreme mantra of his own:
Oṃ vajradhātvīśvari hūṃ vajriṇi!

Then indeed, the Tathāgata Akṣobhya entered the samādhi called the Empowerment of the Maṇḍala of the Wisdom-Mudrās of the Samaya of Vajrasattva of All Tathāgatas, and spoke this supreme mantra of his own:
Oṃ vajravajriṇi hūṃ!

(STT 1,219,324) Then the Tathāgata Ratnasaṃbhava entered the samādhi called "The Empowerment of the Maṇḍala of the Knowledge-Seals of the Samaya of the Jewel-Vajra of All Tathāgatas," and uttered this supreme vidyā of himself:
Oṃ ratnavajriṇi hūṃ! (STT 1,219,325)
Then the Tathāgata Amitāyus entered the samādhi called “The Empowerment of the Maṇḍala of the Wisdom-Mudrā of the Vajra-Dharma-Samaya of All Tathāgatas” and spoke this supreme personal vidyā-mantra:
OṂ DHARMAVAJRIṆI HŪṂ.

Then the Tathāgata Amoghasiddhi entered the samādhi called “The Empowerment of the Maṇḍala of the Wisdom-Mudrā of the Vajra-Karma-Samaya of All Tathāgatas” and spoke this supreme personal vidyā-mantra:
Oṃ karmavajriṇi hūṃ!
Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi spoke the fourfold samaya-mudrās of the great dhāraṇīs of all the Tathāgatas:
Oṃ vajrasattvaguhyasamaye hūṃ!
Oṃ guhyavajrāṅkuśi hūṃ.
Oṃ vajraguhyārāge rāgaya hūṃ.
Oṃ guhyavajrasādhvīśvari hūṃ.
Samantabhadrā;
Tathāgatāṅkuśī;
Ratirāgā.
And Sādhumatī. These are the Vajra-dhāraṇīs: Oṃ vajraguhyaratnasamaye hūṃ.
Oṃ vajraguhyaprabhe hūṃ!
Oṃ vajradhvajāgraguhye hūṃ!
Oṃ guhyahāsavajri hūṃ!
Ratnottamā,
Ratnolkā,
Dhvajāgrakeyūrā.
And Hāsavatī. These are the Ratnadhāraṇīs. Oṃ vajradharmaguhyasamaye hūṃ.
Oṃ vajrakośaguhye hūṃ! Oṃ vajraguhyamaṇḍale hūṃ! Oṃ vajraguhyajāpasamaye hūṃ!
Vajrāmbujā,
Ādhāraṇī,
Sarvacakrā.
And the Sahasrāvartā:
Oṃ vajraguhyakarmasamaye hūṃ!
Oṃ vajraguhyakavace hūṃ!
Oṃ, you who bear the secret vajra fangs, hūṃ!
Oṃ, vajra-secret fist, hūṃ!
Siddhottarā!
The protection of all;
the one that withdraws vital energy;
and the seal of the dhāraṇī.

(STT 1,221,336). Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi again proclaimed the four secret samaya-mudrās of all the Tathāgatas:

Oṃ guhyaratnavajri hūṃ. Oṃ guhyadharmavajri hūṃ. Oṃ guhyakarmavajri hūṃ.

(STT 1,223,339) They should be placed within the great maṇḍala of Vajradhātvīśvarī, blazing and resting upon moon-discs.
