Oṃ vajraguhyaratipūjāsamaye sarvapūjāṃ pravartaya hūṃ! (STT 1,224,341) Oṃ vajraguhyābhiṣekapūjāsamaye sarvapūjāṃ pravartaya hūṃ! (STT 1,224,341) Oṃ vajraguhyagītapūjāsamaye sarvapūjāṃ pravartaya hūṃ! (STT 1,224,342)

Oṃ, at the time of the secret vajra dance offering, set forth all offerings! Hūṃ! (STT 1,225,342) Those very goddesses, Vajralāsyā and the others, blazing with flames, holding their own symbols as mudrās, should be placed in the four corners of the wheel-maṇḍala.
(STT 1,225,343) Then Vajrapāṇi again spoke this great vajra-maṇḍala named Vajraguhya: (STT 1,225,344)
Now, therefore, I shall fully explain the supreme Vajra-maṇḍala,
which resembles the Vajra-dhātu and is known as the Vajra-guhya.
By means of the yoga of the Great Maṇḍala, one should draw all the maṇḍalas.
In the centers of all maṇḍalas, one should draw the Buddha-mudrā.
The Caitya seated comfortably in the paryanka posture is known as Vajradhātvīśvarī;
in the paryanka posture, the Vajra-vajra is celebrated as Vajracitta.
The Vajraratna in the cross-legged posture is proclaimed as "Self-Consecration" (svabhiṣeka).
The Vajrapadma in the cross-legged posture is proclaimed as "Weapon" (āyudha).
The Karmavajra in the cross-legged posture is proclaimed as "All-Vajras" (sarvavajra).
Established upon lotuses, they should be drawn, situated within circles of light.
One should draw a vajra in the paryanka posture, as well as two raised goads;
likewise, a vajra embraced by a vajra, and two gestures of "well done" (sādhukāra).
One should draw a jewel blazing with light, and likewise the sun-seal;
the top of a banner with flames, and two rows of teeth upon two vajras. In the center of the vajra, one should draw a lotus and a sword likewise blazing with light.
The vajra-spoke and the vajra-wheel, the tongue blazing with rays of light;
the vajra on all sides of the face, and the armor joined with the vajra;
likewise, one should draw the two vajra-fangs, and the fist-mudrā with both hands.
The Sattvavajrī and others should be drawn according to the rules in the Dhātu-maṇḍala;
the symbolic seals (mudrās) of Vajralāsyā and the others should be drawn in the [Vajra]maṇḍala.
Furthermore, one should draw their respective symbols on the outside in accordance with the proper method.
"One should draw the specific symbols of Maitreya and the others as one desires.
(STT 1,227,355) Now follows the detailed procedure for the entry and other rites into this Vajraguhya-maṇḍala:

(STT 1,229,356) Therein, first of all, the Vajrācārya himself, having bound the Sattvavajrī mudrā, should enter. Having entered, and having performed a circumambulation from left to right, he should offer that mudrā to the Blessed One Vajrapāṇi. (STT 1,229–230,356)

Having properly released [the deity] into one's own heart, and having performed the rites at the four gates according to the rules by means of the *vajrāṅkuśa* and *karmamudrā* and so forth, one should exit.
Having exited, one should cause the disciples to enter by means of the yoga of the Great Maṇḍala of the Vajra Realm (*vajradhātumahāmaṇḍala*).

Then, having caused them to enter and covered them with a fist, and having bestowed the secret vajra-mark of accomplishment (*siddhiguhyavajracihna*), one should instruct them in the knowledge of the secret vajra-mudrās (*vajraguhyamudrājñāna*).
In that regard, first of all, one should teach the knowledge of the secret body-mudrā of Vajra:
Within the center of a moon mandala, with hands and feet joined in añjali at the face, yawning, one should visualize the vajra; thus one should also arouse passion for the Vajriṇī.
One should visualize the goad as the contraction of the arms and the head as the vajra;
summoning her with the hand, one should bring even Aṅkuśī [under control].
By means of the application of discharging an arrow, yawning, one should strike the heart.
"By means of passion and the yoga of slaying, one should oneself [subdue] even Ratnavajrā.
(STT 1,232,362) One should bind one's own heart with the binding of the arms.
(STT 1,232,363) By means of the application of the adamantine armor, one should protect oneself, even from the Buddha. (STT 1,232,363)
In that regard, their heart-mantras are as follows:
(STT 1,232,364) Vajrarāgaya hoḥ! (STT 1,232,364) Vajrāṅkuśa jaḥ! (STT 1,232,364)
Māraya māraya phaṭ!
Bandha rakṣa haṃ!
Then, one should teach the knowledge of the Vajra-secret-gaze mudrā.
The Vajra-gaze has eyes wide open with intense passion and great joy;
a woman gazed upon by it becomes eternally submissive.
Her eyes have trembling lashes that move rapidly as they draw [the gaze] in.

The "blazing gaze" is so called because it can attract the entire world. (STT 1,233,367) Having fixed the "wrathful gaze"—which has its brow furrows and frowns destroyed, yet its eyes narrowed with anger—one may destroy even the three worlds. (STT 1,233,368)
With eyes as firm and unblinking as the stones of Mount Meru and Mandara, she is known as Maitrīdṛṣṭi, the remover of fevers, seizing spirits, and poisons.
Now, their heart-mantras (hṛdayas) follow: [The mantras follow here.]
Vajra-gaze: *maṭ*. Lamp-like gaze and hook: *jaḥ*. Wrathful gaze: *hīḥ*.
"Dṛḍhadṛṣṭi traṭ!
(STT 1,233,370) Then, one should teach the knowledge of the secret speech-mudrā of the Vajra:
"Hoḥ hoḥ hoḥ ho!"—when this is uttered, by means of that which is devoid of speech, in an instant... (STT 1,234,371–372)
One should cause all sentient beings to be impassioned with perfectly clear Vajra-speech. When "jjaḥ jjaḥ jjaḥ jja" is uttered with the speech of a wrathful deity,
one shall summon the entire world, even those equal to the Holder of the Vajra.
HŪṂ HŪṂ HŪṂ HŪṂ— having concentrated [the mind] with this sound and speech that is not fully distinct—
one may slay all sentient beings, even those as massive as Mount Meru or Mandara.
HAṂ HAṂ HAṂ HAṂ— when this is uttered with subtle speech that is not fully distinct...
"One should protect this entire world, even the Victor who is of the nature of the vajra. In that regard, these are the heart-mantras:
*vajra hoḥ*.
Vajra jjaḥ!
Vajra hūṃ!
Vajra haṃ!
Then, one should teach the knowledge of the Vajra-Guhyacitta-mudrā:
"Meditating upon oneself as endowed with the excellence of all aspects, one shall bring all Buddhas under one's control;
meditating upon oneself by means of one's own self as endowed with the excellence of all aspects."

One should attract one’s own self as Vajragarbha; one should attract Vajrapāṇi. Meditating upon oneself by means of one’s own person as endowed with the excellence of all aspects, one should slay all phenomena with one’s own self as Vajranetra.

Meditating upon himself as being endowed with the excellence of all aspects, he protects himself as the Universal Vajra (*vajraviśva*), the embodiment of all vajras. In this regard, these are the heart-mantras: *(STT 1,236,381)* *(STT 1,236,382)*
Vajrapāṇi, bring all Buddhas under control! Hoḥ!
(STT 1,236,382) Vajragarbha, quickly summon Vajrapāṇi! Hūṃ Jjaḥ! (STT 1,236,382) Vajranetra, destroy all phenomena! Hūṃ Phaṭ! (STT 1,236,382)
*vajraviśva rakṣa sarvavajraṃ haṃ //* (STT 1,236,382) Then, one should teach the knowledge of the secret Vajra-mudrā: (STT 1,238,383) Having placed the Sattvavajrī at one’s own heart, (STT 1,238,384)
Indeed, gazing with the vajra-vision, one should pervade the entire world.
Having placed the jewel-vajra within one's own heart,
gazing indeed with a blazing vision, one brings everything under control.
Having established the Dharma-vajrā within his own heart,
and gazing upon the entire world with a wrathful gaze, he shall indeed slay it.
Having established the Karma-vajrā within his own heart...
"Indeed, by gazing with a loving eye, one should protect this entire world.
(STT 1,238,387) Now, these are the heart-mantras of these secret vajra-knowledge-mudrās:
(STT 1,238,388) *vajraguhyasamaya aḥ* (STT 1,238,388).
Vajraguhya-samaya hoḥ!
Vajraguhya-samaya hūṃ! Vajraguhya-samaya haṃ!
Then, one should teach the binding of the Great Mudrā of the Vajra Secret:
"The great secrets arising from the vajra-añjali are proclaimed as the Mahāmudrās; their binding shall now be explained in brief."
With her two big toes forming a cross-legged posture and the tips of her fingers joined together,
with her waist, middle, and head held straight, she is known as Vajradhātvīśvarī.
That same [mudrā], when the middle fingers are formed into a jewel, is Maṇivajrā.
The middle, nameless, and little fingers are extended with the fingertips spread apart.
The *vajrā* is formed by the tips of the two index fingers grasping the two thumbs;
the *ratnāgrā* is formed by the tips of the [middle] fingers, while the *karojjivalā* is formed by the tips of the jewels [the middle fingers]. (STT 1,239,392; STT 1,240,393)
That same [mudrā], when reversed, has its last finger equalized;
with all the fingertips well-extended, it rests between the thumbs.
That same [mudrā], however, when its fingers are extended into a circle and raised toward the face, [is the next].

Covered by the thumb-vajra, it remains with the tips of the fingers joined together within; then, when the two thumbs are opened wide, it becomes the inner Vajrinī. Furthermore, these secret vajras arise from the vajra-binding.
Furthermore, the secrets of the Dharma are [revealed] by means of signs manifested within the *saṃpuṭa*;
the secrets of action are revealed by means of signs situated within the secrets of action.
Hereafter, I shall explain the Dharma-mudrās in brief.

Āḥ jjaḥ hoḥ saḥ oṃ āṃ traṃ haḥ hrīḥ dhaṃ maṃ raṃ kaṃ haṃ hūṃ vaṃ. Having doubled the secret mudrā, one should fashion the action mudrās; and likewise, having doubled as many of the supreme commitments (samaya) as there are.
(1,244,400) Next, I shall explain their method of accomplishment, saying, "You are the pledge" (samaya).
(1,244,401) Having bound them themselves, those whose nature is the bliss of desire and passion attain success. (1,244,401)
However, one should never bind even one of these at all times;
rather, the wise man should employ them in secret or for a great purpose.
For these are the firm consorts of the self-existent ones, abiding within the essence of all.
"Deeply attached to practitioners, may they not abandon their own husband.
(STT 1,244,403) Now, there are the rites such as the binding of all these mudrās:
"Having generated the vajra-entrance for oneself or for another," (STT 1,246,405)
One should bind, or cause [another] to be bound, by means of this heart-mantra:
*vajra hūṃ bandha*. Now, if one is to be released:
From wherever all the mudrās have arisen in brief,
one should release them in those very places with this heart-mantra:
Oṃ vajra muḥ.
Now follows the firming:
having firmly grasped the Jewel-Vajra, it is released from the heart to the crown of the head;
one should bind the armor with the tips of the fingers while reciting this heart-mantra.
Oṃ dṛḍhavajrakavaca dhṛṭ! Now follows the samaya of binding: Just as those who are liberated in their respective places are made firm by means of armor.
One should indeed bind all [the mudrās] with this heart-mantra by means of the clapping of the palms:
OṂ GUHYASAMAYATĀLA SAḤ.
Vajrasattva, when recited according to one’s preference, is [efficacious] in all mandala rites.
"At this time, the supreme [mantra] that accomplishes all siddhis should be employed.
(STT 1,247,416) The detailed procedure for the Vajra-Guhyavajra-maṇḍala from the *Sarvatathāgata-mahāyānābhisamaya-mahākalparāja* is completed.
(STT 1,248,417) The detailed procedure for the Vajrajñāna-dharma-maṇḍala. (STT 1,249,418)

Then the Blessed One again entered the samādhi called the Empowerment of the Maṇḍala of the Samaya-Jñānamudrā of the Subtle Vajra of All Tathāgatas—[alternatively: Then the Blessed One again entered the samādhi called the Vajra of the Being Born from the Samaya of the Great Bodhisattva Amogharāja]—and spoke this supreme vidyā of himself:
OṂ SŪKṢMAVAJRAJÑĀNASAMAYA HŪṂ.
Then, indeed, the Tathāgata Akṣobhya entered the samādhi called "The Empowerment of the Subtle Samaya Maṇḍala of All Tathāgatas Vajrasattva" and spoke this supreme personal vidyā:

OṂ VAJRASATTVA-SŪKṢMA-JÑĀNA-SAMAYA HŪṂ Then, indeed, the Tathāgata Ratnasaṃbhava entered the samādhi called "The Empowerment of the Subtle Wisdom Samaya Maṇḍala of All Tathāgatas Vajraratna" and spoke this supreme personal vidyā:
Oṃ vajraratnasūkṣmajñānasamaya hūṃ!

(STT 1,249,421) Then indeed, the Tathāgata Amitāyus entered the meditative absorption called the Empowerment of the Maṇḍala of the Samaya of the Subtle Wisdom of the Vajra-Dharma of All Tathāgatas, and spoke this supreme mantra of his own wisdom:
Oṃ vajradharmasūkṣmajñānasamaya hūṃ! (STT 1,249,422)

Then, indeed, the Tathāgata Amoghasiddhi entered the meditative absorption called "The Empowerment of the Maṇḍala of the Samaya of Subtle Wisdom of the Vajra-Action of All Tathāgatas" and spoke this supreme mantra of his own knowledge:
OṂ VAJRAKARMASŪKṢMAJÑĀNASAMAYA HŪṂ Then the Blessed One Vairocana entered the meditative absorption called "The Vajra of Subtle Wisdom of All Tathāgatas."

And as soon as the Blessed One had entered [that state], immediately thereafter, subtle vajra-rays of gnosis issued forth from the hearts of all the Tathāgatas, pervading all world-systems. Having stabilized the attainment of the samādhi of the subtle vajra-gnosis of all the Tathāgatas for all sentient beings, they again became one. Taking hold of the nature of the vajra-body of samādhi-gnosis, they coalesced into a single mass of Tathāgata-gnosis and entered the heart of the Blessed One Vairocana.
Then Vajrapāṇi, having entered into the heart-knowledge of all Tathāgatas, spoke this Great Samaya-Vajra of the Subtle Knowledge of All Tathāgatas:
"Subtle Vajra!"

Then, as soon as this was spoken, Vajrapāṇi emerged from the hearts of all the Tathāgatas; having empowered himself as the subtle wisdom-vajra image of all the Tathāgatas, and having empowered himself as the subtle wisdom-vajra image of all the Tathāgatas, he stood at the tips of the noses of all the Tathāgatas and uttered this inspired utterance:
"Oh, how great is my subtle vajra of all the Buddhas!
Because of its greatness, though it is subtle, it can pervade even the triple world!"

Then, having spoken this, the Blessed One, the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, by means of the radiation of the signs of the extremely subtle vajra-wisdom from the tips of the noses of all the Tathāgatas, having radiated [it] from the bodies of all the Tathāgatas, and by way of the yoga of pervading the entire realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*), having completely pervaded the entire realm of space (*ākāśadhātu*) with the signs of the extremely subtle vajra-wisdom, remained established after empowering himself as the vajra-image of the wisdom of all the Tathāgatas expanded throughout the entire realm of space.

Then, at that very moment, having focused upon the vajra-nature within the vajra of the gnosis of all Tathāgatas, he remained absorbed in the samādhi called "The Empowerment of the Vajra of the Subtle Gnosis of All Tathāgatas.
Then, from that vajra of the gnosis of all Tathāgatas, there issued forth the heart-mantra of the samādhi-gnosis of all Tathāgatas:
VAJRA-NĀBHI-TATHĀGATA HŪṂ.

Then, as soon as this had issued forth, the Blessed One Vajrapāṇi again entered the bodies of all the Tathāgatas by means of the yoga of entering subtle gnosis, and remained there, having become vajra-images within their hearts.
Then, from those vajras of the beings of all the Tathāgatas, these four great gnosis-hearts issued forth:
"Vajrātmaka! (The nature of the vajra!)
Heart-vajra-hook!
(STT 1,256,434) Stay, O Rāgavajra; enter the heart!
(STT 1,256,434) Oh, Vajra-delight! (STT 1,256,434)
The wisdom-seal of Vajrasattva;
the wisdom-seal of the empowerment of the assembly of all Tathāgatas;
the wisdom-seal of the passion of all Tathāgatas.
And [the seal of] the knowledge of great satisfaction.
These are the great samādhis of all the Tathāgatas.

Then Vajrapāṇi, the heart of all the Tathāgatas, again entering his own heart by means of the yoga of entry into subtle knowledge, remained abiding after empowering himself as a vajra-form within the heart.
Then, from that vajra-form, this fourfold heart-mantra issued forth:
*Vajraratnātmake* (O you whose nature is the vajra-jewel),
*Hṛdayavajrasūrya* (Heart-vajra-sun).
"Stay, O Vajradhvajāgra vaṃ!
Heart-Vajra-Laughter!
[This is] the wisdom-seal of the vajra-consecration of all Tathāgatas."
The wisdom-seal of the array of the great circle of light;
(STT 1,257,438) the wisdom-seal that fulfills the aspirations of all Tathāgatas;
(STT 1,257,438) the wisdom-seal of the great laughter of all Tathāgatas. (STT 1,257,438)
The Samādhis of the Jewels of All Tathāgatas.
(STT 1,257,438) Then Vajrapāṇi, again through the yoga of entering the subtle vajra-knowledge, entered his own heart, the vajra-heart; having empowered himself as the vajra-form, he remained there.
(STT 1,258,439) Then, from that vajra-form, this tetrad of hearts issued forth: (STT 1,258,440)
Consisting of the vajra-lotus!
O Vajra-treasury of the heart!
Abide, O Vajra-wheel; enter the heart!
Vajra-jihvāgra-hṛdaya!
(The Seal of the Knowledge of the Equality of All Dharmas;
the Seal of the Wisdom-Knowledge of All Tathāgatas.)
The seal of the knowledge of entering the great wheel;
(STT 1,258,441) the seal of the non-conceptual knowledge of the speech of the Dharma of all Tathāgatas.
(STT 1,258,442) These are the samādhis of the Dharma of all Tathāgatas. (STT 1,258,442)

Then Vajrapāṇi once again, through the yoga of entering the extremely subtle gnosis, entered that Vajrahṛdaya from the vajra-heart within his own heart. (STT 1,259,443) Furthermore, he remained there, having empowered himself as a subtle vajra-form.
(STT 1,259,443) Then, from that subtle vajra-form, this fourfold heart-mantra issued forth: (STT 1,259,444)
Consisting of all vajras!
Vajra-armour of the heart!
Stay, O vajra-yakṣa-heart!
The Heart of the Vajra Fist (vajramuṣṭihṛdaya) is the wisdom-seal of the all-encompassing creative activity of all Tathāgatas;
it is the wisdom-seal of the invincible heroic vigor.
The Wisdom-Seal that shatters the entire mandala of Māra;
the Wisdom-Seal of the binding of all Tathāgatas;
and the Samādhis of the activities of all Tathāgatas.

Then the Blessed One Vajrapāṇi, once again, through the yoga of the radiation of the signs of extremely subtle gnosis, emerged from the bodies of all the Tathāgatas; having manifested as the body of the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, and further assuming the forms of the Great Bodhisattvas beginning with Vajrasattva, he established his respective emblems within their hearts.
Then, by means of the arrangement of the great maṇḍala of the Vajradhātu, resting upon moon-discs, they remained absorbed in the meditative concentrations of their own hearts.

Then Vajrapāṇi, once again, for the sake of accomplishing the samādhis, gnoses, and supernormal knowledges of all the Tathāgatas, spoke this Vajra-Sūkṣma-Jñāna-Maṇḍala: "Now, therefore, I shall fully explain the supreme Dharma-maṇḍala,
which resembles the Vajra-dhātu and is known as the Vajra-Sūkṣma."
One should cause the Great Beings (mahāsattva) to enter by means of the yoga of the great maṇḍala;
one should draw the Buddha in the center of the vajra, and also within the Buddha-maṇḍalas.
The Great Beings are to be painted along with their own mudrās and likewise their heart-mantras.
"Seated in meditative absorption, with both hands in the vajra-binding gesture.
(STT 1,260,451) Now, herein follows the detailed procedure for the rites of summoning and so forth in this Vajra-Sūkṣmadharma Maṇḍala.
(STT 1,261,452) Having performed the detailed procedure for entry and so forth through the yoga of the Great Maṇḍala, one bestows the symbol of gnosis upon the two hands. (STT 1,261,452)
One should teach the knowledge of the Great Seal (*mahāmudrā*) regarding the nature of one’s own mind:
having placed the tongue against the palate, one should focus on the tip of the nose;
through the touch of the bliss of the subtle vajra, the mind becomes absorbed in meditative concentration (*samādhi*).

When the sign of the subtle vajra-sensation of bliss arises, one should expand that sign; indeed, that mind should be made to radiate everywhere. Through such expansion according to one's wish, the mind may even pervade the three realms.
Then one should withdraw that [light] until it reaches the tip of the nose.
From that point onward, being well-composed, whatever one should visualize,
one should make all of this firm, as it is fashioned by the wisdom of meditative concentration.
Now, their heart-mantras are as follows:
*sūkṣmavajra*, *sphara vajra*.
Withdraw, O Vajra!
O Vajra, remain firm!
May great and very firm loving-kindness arise for whichever sentient being [is present].
By means of the yoga of the pervasion of the mind, one should pervade all sentient beings with that [loving-kindness].

By means of the yoga of the pervasion of loving-kindness, one should extend compassion toward anyone whatsoever. Indeed, being intent upon the welfare of all sentient beings, one should pervade them through actual practice.

All are naturally luminous, primordially pure, and equal to space. Whether they are non-dharmas or dharmas, they rejoice through the nature of pervasive radiance. Those who resemble the most stubborn of beings are not vessels for the awakening of a Buddha.
For the sake of awakening them, one should cultivate great equanimity.
In this regard, these are the heart-mantras:
"Pervade with great loving-kindness! (mahāmaitryā sphara).
Pervade with great compassion! Pervade with all-pure joy! Awaken all sentient beings!
Then, one should train in the knowledge that recollects all the Tathāgatas:
"Whether in space or in another place, through the application of the subtle vajra,
whether standing or sitting, one should meditate upon the vajra-form."
Then, in all places, through the application of the subtle vajra,
one should meditate upon the Bodhisattva Heart-Vajra with perfect concentration.
One should meditate upon the great image of Vajrapāṇi in all places.
By means of the subtle vajra-application, according to the rule and in successive order, one should,
being well-composed, meditate in due sequence and according to the rule upon the form of the Buddha, endowed in every way with the excellence of all aspects.
In this regard, there are these heart-mantras:
"O you who possess a vajra face, become so! O Great Bodhisattva, enter!"
O Vajrapāṇi, reveal your own form!
Enter through the recollection of the Buddha!
One should meditate by oneself through the application of the subtle vajra.
The meditation on oneself as the lunar disc is the meditation on Bodhicitta.
One should meditate upon oneself within the center of the moon-maṇḍala.
The meditation on oneself as the vajra-disc is the meditation on Sattvavajra.
Applying the subtle vajra method, one should meditate upon oneself by means of one's own self.
Meditating on oneself as the heart of Sattvavajra is the meditation on Vajrasattva.
One should meditate upon oneself by means of one's own self, endowed with the excellence of all forms.

"One's own self as the image of the Buddha is indeed the meditation on the awakening of a Buddha. (STT 1,267,473) In this regard, these are the heart-mantras: (STT 1,267,474) "O Samantabhadra, enter! (STT 1,267,474)
Enter the Sattvavajra! (STT 1,268,474) Enter the wisdom-samādhi of Vajrasattva! (STT 1,268,474) I am the Tathāgata! (STT 1,268,474)
Then, one should teach the knowledge of the secret mudrā of the *dharmatā* of all Tathāgatas:
"By speaking once with vajra-words, 'I am indeed equal to the Tathāgata,' one shall certainly attract the world through the union of the two organs."
For I am indeed equal to the Great Vajra; by speaking once with vajra-words, one shall certainly attract the world through the union of the two organs.
For I am indeed equal to Vajradharma; by speaking once with vajra-words...
"By means of the union of the two organs, he shall destroy the entire world.
For by speaking once with the vajra-speech, I am indeed equal to the Viśvavajra. By means of the union of the two organs, he shall accomplish all activities."
Then, one should teach the knowledge of the samādhi-mudrā of the empowerment of the vajra of the wisdom of all Tathāgatas:
"By means of the application of the subtle vajra, one should meditate on the form of a Buddha within the center of the vajra as one's own self; for in this way, one shall attain Buddhahood."
Then, one should teach the knowledge of the samādhi-mudrā of Vajrasattva:
"By applying the subtle vajra method, the hosts such as Vajra and the rest are placed in the heart;
by meditating upon Vajrasattva and the others, they bestow their respective siddhis."
Then, one should teach the knowledge of the samaya-mudrās of the samādhi of the family of all the Tathāgatas:
"Those arising from the vajra-bind are proclaimed to be sixteen. Now, their binding, which is the supreme samādhi-samaya, shall be explained."
Seated in the paryanka posture, fully reclined, and likewise with limbs folded and unfolded...
(STT 1,272,486) The fourth is situated at the heart in the mandala of Vajrasattva and the others.
(STT 1,272,486) Situated on the forehead, at the back of the head, and on the shoulder, she is employed with laughter. (STT 1,273,487)
The *mukhadhātrī* is in the heart, the *khaḍgā* is in the heart, and the *hṛdvikāsā* is situated in the mouth. The *mūrdhavakṣe* is in the mouth, while the *jyeṣṭhasthā* is likewise in front.
Hereafter, one should teach the *dharmamudrās* in brief.
Ṭakki!
Gra gra!
Maṭaḥ!
Agra / Traṃ traṃ / Aṃ aṃ.
caṃ caṃ / tṛṭaḥ / dhṛṭaḥ /
bhṛtaḥ / kraśaḥ / ha haḥ /
va va / vaṃ vaṃ / phaṭaḥ /
Then, however, the foremost of those whose activity is Dharma should instruct the subtle Vajra-holders:
"One should apply the Knowledge-Fist Samaya by dividing it into two."
The detailed ritual procedure for the Dharma-maṇḍala of Vajra-gnosis from the *Mahākalparāja*, the Great Sūtra of the Realization of the Mahāyāna of all Tathāgatas, is completed.
(STT 1,276,492) The detailed ritual procedure for the Action-maṇḍala of Vajra-activity.

(STT 1,277,493) Then the Blessed One again entered the samādhi called the "Vajra Empowerment of the Samaya of the Activity that Pervades the Detailed Ritual Procedure for the Supreme Worship of all Tathāgatas," and spoke this supreme personal vidyā-mantra: (STT 1,277,494)
Oṃ, at the time of the pervasive supreme worship of the vajra-realm of all Tathāgatas, hūṃ!

(STT 1,277,494) Then, the Tathāgata Akṣobhya entered the samādhi called "The Vajra Empowerment of the Ritual Procedure for the Pervasive Supreme Worship of All Tathāgatas as Vajrasattva," and spoke this supreme personal vidyā-mantra:
(STT 1,277,495) Oṃ, at the time of the pervasive supreme worship of all Tathāgatas as Vajrasattva, hūṃ! (STT 1,277,495)

Then the Tathāgata Ratnasaṃbhava entered the samādhi called the Vajra Empowerment of the Ritual Procedure for the Extensive Pervasion of the Supreme Vajra-Jewel Worship of All Tathāgatas, and spoke this supreme mantra of his own knowledge:
OṂ SARVATATHĀGATAVAJRARATNĀNUTTARAPŪJĀSPHARAṆASAMAYE HŪṂ.

Then indeed, the Tathāgata Amitāyus entered the samādhi called "The Vajra Empowerment of the Samaya of the Activity of the Pervasive Expansion of the Extensive Ritual Procedures for the Unsurpassed Worship of the Vajra-Dharma of All Tathāgatas," and spoke this supreme personal vidyā-mantra:
Oṃ sarvatathāgatavajradharmānuttarapūjāspharaṇasamaye hūṃ.

Then, indeed, the Tathāgata Amoghasiddhi entered the samādhi called "The Vajra Empowerment of the Samaya of the Activity of Pervasive Expansion of the Ritual for the Unsurpassed Worship of the Vajra-Activity of All Tathāgatas," and spoke this supreme mantra of his own knowledge:
OṂ SARVATATHĀGATAVAJRAKARMĀNUTTARAPŪJĀSPHARAṆASAMAYE HŪṂ!

Then the Blessed One Vairocana again entered the samādhi called the Vajra of the Samaya of the Ritual for the Extensive Worship of All Tathāgatas, which Pervades the Entire Dharmadhātu. As soon as he had entered that state, from the hearts of all the Tathāgatas, that very Blessed One Vajradhara emerged as deities who pervade the entire dharmadhātu, who converge within the entire expanse of space, and who form oceans of clouds of the extensive rituals for the manifestation of all kinds of worship. Having thus come forth, they issued out.

In all the ocean-like clouds of the expanse of world-systems, within the circles of the assemblies of all Tathāgatas, there is the generation of the unsurpassed great mind of enlightenment by all Tathāgatas, the delighting in the families of all Tathāgatas, the accomplishment of the conduct of Samantabhadra, the approach to the seat of great enlightenment, and the subduing of all Māras.

They remained there, manifesting all the miraculous transformations of the Buddhas, such as the realization of the equality of all Tathāgatas, the generation of the great maṇḍalas of all Tathāgatas, the conquest of the entire triple world, the turning of the wheel of the true Dharma, and the accomplishment of the welfare of the realms of sentient beings without exception or remainder.

And those deities of the ocean-like clouds of offerings, their two hands occupied with their respective mudrās, having worshipped all the Tathāgatas according to the ritual, and having become established upon moon-maṇḍalas through the yoga of the Great Maṇḍala of the Vajradhātu, uttered this inspired utterance:
"Aho! Truly, I am the worship of the Buddhas, the initiator of all worship;
for all the Buddhas bestow that which is Buddhahood, the state of greatness."
Then Vajrapāṇi again proclaimed the extensive ritual procedure for the activities of worship and so forth of all the Tathāgatas, the activity maṇḍala named Vajrakārya:
Oṃ sarvatathāgatasarvātmaniryātanapūjāspharaṇakarmavajri āḥ!
Oṃ sarvatathāgatasarvātmaniryātanapūjāspharaṇakarmāgri jjaḥ!
Oṃ, O arrow of the ritual action that radiates the offering of affectionate surrender of the self of all Tathāgatas, hūṃ hoḥ!
(STT 1,282,507) Oṃ, O satisfaction of the ritual action that radiates the offering of "well done" for the surrender of the self of all Tathāgatas, aḥ!
(STT 1,282,507) The supreme bliss of all Tathāgatas. (STT 1,282,508)
The attractor of all Tathāgatas; the one who possesses unsurpassed passion for all Tathāgatas;
and the one who brings satisfaction to all Tathāgatas.

The Great Worship of All Tathāgatas. Oṃ, homage to the jewels of the empowerment of the bodies of all Tathāgatas; Vajramaṇi, oṃ! Oṃ, homage to the suns of all Tathāgatas; Vajratejini, blaze forth, hrīḥ!
Oṃ, homage to those who are like wish-fulfilling jewels upon the tips of the victory banners that fulfill the aspirations of all Tathāgatas; O Vajradhvajāgra, traṃ!
(STT 1,283,510) Oṃ, homage to those who produce great joy and rapture for all Tathāgatas; O Vajrahāsa, haḥ!
(STT 1,283,510) The Great Sovereign Lady. (STT 1,283,511)
Mahoddyotā,
Mahāratnavarṣā,
and Mahāprītiharṣā.
The offerings for the consecration of all Tathāgatas:
Oṃ, with the samādhis of the vajra-nature of all Tathāgatas, I praise you, O supreme great Dharma! Hrīḥ!
Oṃ, with the accomplishments of the Prajñāpāramitā of all Tathāgatas, I praise you, O follower of the great sound! Dhaṃ!
Oṃ! I praise with all the methods of the sūtras, beginning with the transformation of the syllables of the wheel of all Tathāgatas; HŪṂ in all maṇḍalas! Oṃ!
I praise by singing with the concordant speech of all Tathāgatas and the communal chanting of the Buddhas; VAṂ to Vajravāc!
This is the Song of Great Gnosis.
Following the great sound;
entering all mandalas; and the practice of mantra.
The Dharma-offerings to all Tathāgatas:
Oṃ, for the rite of offering the pervading cloud of incense of all Tathāgatas: *kara kara*. Oṃ, for the rite of offering the pervading expansion of flowers of all Tathāgatas: *kiri kiri*.

Oṃ, for the rite of worship consisting of the radiation of the blazing light of all Tathāgatas: bhara bhara! (STT 1,285,516) Oṃ, for the rite of worship consisting of the radiation of the ocean of perfumes of all Tathāgatas: kuru kuru!
(STT 1,285,516) Sattvavatī. (STT 1,286,517)
Possessing the factors of great enlightenment;
possessing vision;
and possessing fragrance.
The Offerings of the Ritual Activities of All Tathāgatas. Now, herein is the Vajra-Action Maṇḍala, which initiates the worship of all Tathāgatas without exception or remainder.
Therefore, I shall now fully explain the supreme Action Maṇḍala.
The Vajra-activity is known as that which awaits the Vajradhātu.
(STT 1,287,519) One should arrange the images of the Buddhas by means of the Mahāmaṇḍala-yoga;
one should depict the deities together with their mudrās by means of the yoga of Vajrasattva and the others. (STT 1,287,520)
Herein follows the detailed procedure for entering the maṇḍala of vajra-activities and so forth.
Therein, from the very beginning, one should cause [the disciple] to enter by means of the yoga of entry into the Vajradhātu.
Having caused him to enter in this manner, one should say:
This is the *samaya* for the worship of all Tathāgatas.
Therefore, you must perform these sixteen types of worship every day according to your ability.
Then, having released the blindfold and shown the *karmamaṇḍala*, one should place the universal insignia (*viśvacihna*) into both hands.
Then he is honored even by all the Tathāgatas, let alone by others.
Thereafter, one should teach the knowledge of the seal (*mudrā*) for the worship that accomplishes the Great Bodhicitta:
"By generating the firm resolve for enlightenment, thinking 'I am a Buddha'..."
By worshipping with Rati, one attains even the bliss of a Buddha.

(STT 1,288,526) Through the firm generation of the thought of awakening (*bodhicitta*), thinking "I am a Buddha," and having fully worshipped oneself with offerings such as garlands, one is consecrated. (STT 1,288,527)
By generating the firm resolve for awakening (*bodhicitta*), thinking "I am a Buddha," and honoring oneself with songs, pleasures, and offerings, one should arouse passion.
By generating the firm resolve for awakening, thinking "I am a Buddha," [one should worship].

"One who honors oneself while dancing is honored even by the Buddhas. (STT 1,289,529) In this regard, these are the heart-mantras: (STT 1,289,530) "I am the Buddha-self" (buddhātmāham). (STT 1,289,530)
I consecrate the Buddha;
I offer praise to the Buddha;
I perform worship of the Buddha.
Then, one should teach the knowledge of the mudrās for the worship of all Buddhas:
by means of the supreme applications of the vajras of body, speech, and mind,
bowing and worshipping all Buddhas, one will certainly become worthy of veneration.

Born from the vajra of the body, speech, and mind of all Buddhas’ great merit, one whose self consists of the worship of rejoicing shall swiftly attain Buddhahood; through the offering of oneself from the divine vajras of body, speech, and mind.

"One worships by thinking, 'I worship the Perfect Buddhas with all offerings. (STT 1,290,534) "Through the offerings of dedication, one becomes equal to all Buddhas by means of the vajra of body, speech, and mind, which is the entire accumulation of merit. (STT 1,290,535)
In this regard, there are these heart-mantras:
(STT 1,290,536) "I prostrate; (STT 1,290,536) I rejoice. (STT 1,290,536)
Buddha-worship. Dedication. Then, one should teach the knowledge of the mudrā of Dharma-worship.
All phenomena are luminous by nature, for they are pure from the very beginning by their own essence.

By means of this Dharma-seal, he cuts through all sufferings.

All-pure / Samantabhadra / Dharmacakra.

By meditating on the forms of vajras, one who is of the nature of vajra shall quickly become so.

Meditating upon one's own atoms within the vajras of body, speech, and mind as Vajrasattvas, one shall become equal to Vajrasattva. (STT 1,294,546) One's own atoms within the vajras of body, speech, and mind... (STT 1,294,547)

"By constantly performing the worship of the bliss of embracing the bodies of all the Self-Existent Ones,
he shall quickly become equal to Vajrasattva."

By bestowing the pleasures of seizing the hair [of the consort] through the union of firm passion upon the Buddhas, one becomes equal to a vajra-jewel. By bestowing the supreme pleasures of kissing, which are attached to the bliss of firm joy, one likewise attains such a state.

By offering these to the Buddhas, one becomes equal to Vajradharma. (STT 1,295,552) By offering everywhere the blisses of the yoga of the union of the two organs, one becomes equal to Vajrakarma through such worship. (STT 1,295,553)
In this regard, these are the heart-mantras of the secret mudrās:
Rativajra,
Rāgavajra.
Prītivajra!
Kāmavajra!

Through yoga, [the mudrās] are situated on the heart, the sides, the back, and likewise on the forehead and so forth;
they are located on the face, the ears, the head, the back, the crown, the shoulders, the mouth, and the waist.
Then, one should teach the knowledge of the *sarvatathāgata-pūjākarmasamayamudrā*.
Having made the vajra-binding firm through the application of the mahāmudrā, one should worship the Jinas by means of placing [the mudrās] at the heart and other locations. Then,
one should teach the knowledge of the Dharma-mudrās for the worship of all the Tathāgatas.

"In brief, those who are difficult to discipline through karma are governed by the *karmamudrā*.
(STT 1,300,560) The detailed procedure for the *karmamaṇḍala* of Vajrakārya from the *Sarvatathāgatamahāyānābhisamaya-mahākalparāja* is completed.

Then the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Vairocana, having generated the family of all Tathāgatas through the empowerment of all Tathāgatas, spoke this Heart of the Tathāgata Mudrā for the sake of encompassing all accomplishments within this extensive ritual procedure of the Great Kalpa of the Family of All Tathāgatas:
Oṃ sarvatathāgatamuṣṭi vaṃ.

Then indeed, the Tathāgata Akṣobhya, having generated the family of all Tathāgatas through the empowerment of all Tathāgatas, spoke this seal of all Tathāgatas for the sake of gathering all accomplishments within this extensive ritual procedure of the Great Kalpa of the Family of All Tathāgatas:
Oṃ vajrasattvamuṣṭi aḥ.

Then the Tathāgata Ratnasaṃbhava, having generated the family of all Tathāgatas through the empowerment of all Tathāgatas, spoke this seal of all Tathāgatas for the purpose of gathering all accomplishments within this extensive ritual procedure of the Great Kalpa of the Family of All Tathāgatas:
Oṃ vajraratnamuṣṭi traṃ.

The Tathāgata Amitāyus, having generated the family of all Tathāgatas through the empowerment of all Tathāgatas, spoke this seal of all Tathāgatas for the purpose of gathering all accomplishments within this extensive ritual procedure of the Great Kalpa of the Family of All Tathāgatas:
Oṃ vajradharmamuṣṭi khaṃ.

Then the Tathāgata Amoghasiddhi, having generated the family of all Tathāgatas through the empowerment of all Tathāgatas, spoke this seal of all Tathāgatas for the purpose of gathering all accomplishments from this extensive ritual procedure of the Great Kalpa of the Family of All Tathāgatas:
Oṃ vajradharmamuṣṭi hāṃ!

Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, through his own empowerment, having generated the family of all Tathāgatas for the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Vairocana, spoke this maṇḍala of the four mudrās called Vajrasiddhi, for the sake of gathering all accomplishments from this extensive ritual procedure of the Great Kalpa of the Family of All Tathāgatas:
"Now, therefore, I shall fully explain the supreme maṇḍala of mudrās,
which resembles the Vajradhātu and is known as Vajrasiddhi."
The skillful one should trace the lines by means of the yoga of the great maṇḍala. Having first established the image of the Buddha, one should draw the four mudrās.
One should draw the vajra-mudrā and the others within the centers of the moon-maṇḍalas.
Then, having performed the detailed ritual for summoning and so forth in this Vajrasiddhi-mudrā-maṇḍala, and having caused [the disciple] to enter in that same manner, one should say:
"You must not reveal this secret chapter to anyone. For what reason?"

There are beings who possess wrong views, who perform evil deeds, who are indeed deficient in vigor and devoid of ritual knowledge, and who are unacquainted with the arts of painting; considering the great maṇḍalas of all the Tathāgata families, such as the Vajradhātu and others, they do not enter them because of their lack of vigor. (STT 1,303,573)

For their sake, this Vajrasiddhi-mudrā-maṇḍala—which is the very essence of the samaya of the maṇḍalas of all the Tathāgata families, which protects the realm of sentient beings without exception or remainder, and which is empowered for the purpose of experiencing all benefit, happiness, and mental well-being, up to the sign of the supreme siddhi of all the Tathāgatas’ vajras—has been established.

Therefore, you must not lack faith in these secrets of the samaya-mudrās of all the Tathāgata families; otherwise, there may be rebirth for you among hell-beings, animals, or pretas, or there may be an untimely death through the failure to avoid calamities.
Having said this, one should release the binding of the mouth and show the maṇḍala.
Then, one should proclaim the samaya of the seals (mudrā) of all the Tathāgatas: "Whichever seal one should bind for whichever great being..."
While reciting, one should meditate upon that [deity] with one's own self through the meaning of the heart-mantra.
By this yoga of gnosis, the great-souled ones attain accomplishment;
indeed, for all [practitioners], all mudrās are as Vajrapāṇi has spoken.
Then one should explain the secret of all mudrās:
"Having opened one's own faculty, one should grasp the vajra in the 'vajra-fist' hold.
Whichever mudrā one touches with that, it comes under one's control at that very moment."
Then one should proclaim all the dharmas of the mudrās:
"Having applied the subtle vajra procedure, one should bind the jñānamudrā;
by means of this application of the procedure, one shall bring the jñānamudrā under control."
Then one should explain all the ritual actions of the mudrās:
"By offering songs, dances, flavors, food, recreation,
and other pleasures to the Buddhas, one brings the karma-mudrās under control."

Then, one should teach the secret knowledge of the mudrās that govern all maṇḍalas: "Having made one's own *liṅga* rigid, one should sit upon a white cloth, presiding over the *liṅga* as a shrine, [thinking]: 'I myself am Vajradhātu.'"

Having made the vajra-bind firm, with the middle fingers raised like sprouts and the little and index fingers extended from the mouth, this is the *samaya* of those who possess the foremost *samaya*. With the application of the subtle vajra, one should meditate with well-composed concentration.
One should bring the subtle vajra-maṇḍala under the mastery of meditative concentration (samādhi).
Having bound the pair of vajra-mudrās, one should firmly grasp the vajra between them. By binding the tips of the little fingers, this is called the "Supreme Maṇḍala for Vajra-Activities."

Then, having instructed [the disciple] in the fourfold binding of the great mudrās of Vajrasattva according to the rule, [one should proceed] with the detailed procedure for the great maṇḍala of the Vajradhātu according to the rule.
Just as the maṇḍala of the four mudrās of Vajrasiddhi, so too should all maṇḍalas, beginning with Akṣobhya, be drawn by means of the yoga of the four-mudrā maṇḍala.
For it is through their respective individual mudrās that all accomplishments (*siddhi*) are bestowed.
Thus, when painted upon cloth, walls, space, or any location, they grant all accomplishments (*siddhi*).
From the time of the construction of the maṇḍala, for some, accomplishment is attained according to their desire at that very entry into the maṇḍala;
for some, it begins from that point after one day; for some, after four days; and for some, after sixteen days.

For some, even those who have committed the five acts of immediate retribution (*pañcānantarya*), the Blessed One has declared that supreme accomplishment is attained within a year, provided they perform all their activities according to their desire, experiencing the pleasures of all-encompassing affection, all flavors, all food, and all modes of conduct.

Then the Blessed One Vairocana again entered the samādhi called the Vajra of the Samaya of the Supreme Accomplishment of All Tathāgatas, and from his own heart he emitted this Heart of All Tathāgatas called the Realization of the Mahāyāna of All Tathāgatas: VAJRASATTVA.

Then the Blessed One, the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, for the sake of protecting the entire realm of sentient beings without exception and for them to experience all benefit, happiness, and mental well-being, and so forth, up to the attainment of the supreme siddhi of all Tathāgatas, spoke this Mahāyāna Abhisamaya Maṇḍala: "Now, therefore, I shall fully explain the supreme great maṇḍala,
which resembles the Vajradhātu and is known as Vajrasattva."
One should delineate the outer maṇḍala by means of the yoga of the great maṇḍala.
One should place Vajrasattva in the center of the moon-maṇḍala.
Then, having performed the summoning, entry, and so forth according to the rules, one should generate the gnoses of the accomplishments of all the Tathāgatas.
In this regard, first of all, it must be said:
"You must not speak of these secrets to anyone who has not seen the samaya or who is unskilled in them.
Lest you be reborn in any of the miserable states, or suffer an untimely death through the avoidance of what is dangerous."
Then, one should train in the knowledge that accomplishes the supreme siddhi of Vajrasattva:
"Mounted upon a full moon mandala and embracing the Mahāmudrā,
by meditating on oneself as Vajrasattva, one quickly attains accomplishment."
Then, one should teach the secret samaya-knowledge of all mandalas:
"There is no other evil in the three realms equal to dispassion;
therefore, you must never again practice dispassion toward desire."

likewise, the accomplishments [are attained].

Thus ends the detailed procedure for the Great Maṇḍala of the Vajradhātu.

Then all the Tathāgatas, having gathered together once more, offered words of praise with this heart-mantra of Vajratuṣṭi to the Blessed One, the Lord of all Tathāgatas, the Great Bodhicitta, Vajrasattva, Mahāvajrapāṇi: *(STT 1,313,611–612)*
Oṃ! Well done to you, Vajrasattva; well done to you, Vajraratna.

The secret of all Tathāgatas, which is the compendium of the Mahāyāna; even the name of Vajrasattva is supreme for accomplishing all siddhis. When practiced with purity, one shall indeed attain Buddhahood through bliss.

Then all the Blessed Tathāgatas, having gathered together once more, entreated the Blessed One, the Great Universal Monarch of all Tathāgatas, with these eight hundred names: (STT 1,315,619).

Buddha-huṃkāra, Huṃkāra, Vajra-huṃkāra, Dāmaka;
O Viśvavajrāṅga, Vajrogra, Vajrapāṇi, homage be to you!
You are to be saluted, worshipped, honored, and revered by the Tathāgatas.
Because your mind is as firm as a vajra, you are called Vajrasattva.
Indeed, perfect enlightenment depends upon you; you are the father of all who see.
Having relied upon you, the Tathāgatas have arisen and will arise.
One should indeed praise with this king of hymns with true devotion;
whoever praises while singing shall become equal to the Holder of the Vajra.
We entreat you, O Protector, who brings joy to all Buddhas.
