(STT 1,318,639) Then Vajrapāṇi, the lord of all Tathāgatas, having heard the words of the exhortation from all the Tathāgatas, established that vajra in his own heart, summoned all those Tathāgatas, and spoke thus:
(STT 1,323-324,640) "O Blessed Ones, all Tathāgatas, I do not proceed [to act]. (STT 1,324,641)
All the Tathāgatas asked:
"What is the cause? Vajradhara replied:
"Venerable ones, there are wicked beings such as Maheśvara and others who cannot be led even by you or by all the Tathāgatas; how should I deal with them?

(STT 1,324,644) Then the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Vairocana, through the empowerment of all the Tathāgatas, entered the meditative absorption named "The Vajra of the Great Skillful Means Wisdom of All Tathāgatas. (STT 1,325,645)

Immediately upon entering [the meditative absorption], all the Tathāgatas, by means of an emanation as vast as the convergence of atoms within the entire realm of space, returned once more to the assembly atop Mount Sumeru in the gabled pavilion of the peak of the *vajra* jewel-mountain.
Having focused their minds on the equality of all Tathāgatas, they entered the heart of the Blessed One Vairocana at the Śrīvatsa mark.

Then the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Vairocana, having empowered himself as the heart of all Tathāgatas, for the sake of the supreme accomplishment of all benefit and happiness that protects the entire realm of sentient beings without exception through the equality of all vajras, and for the sake of subduing all who are wicked,
relied upon the knowledge of the samādhi of skillful means and great compassion of all Tathāgatas,
and entered the samādhi called the Vajra of the Commitment of the Wrath of Skillful Means and Great Compassion of All Tathāgatas.

And immediately upon his entering [that state], at that very moment, from the hearts of all the Tathāgatas, there issued forth the heart-mantra of all the Tathāgatas called the "Vajra-Samaya of All Tathāgatas":
HŪṂ.

As soon as this had issued forth, from the Vajra of the Heart of Vajrapāṇi, that very Blessed One, the Holder of the Vajra, appeared, filled with flames on all sides, with a frowning brow, knitted forehead, and a mouth made terrifying by fierce fangs.

With hands busily occupied by weapons such as the vajra-hook, the sheath, and the noose, blazing with vajra-flames and fire, wearing various garments and ornaments of manifold colors, and having assumed the forms of Vajrapāṇi, they roamed through the [ten] directions;

having subdued all the wicked ones in all world-systems, they took their places upon moon-maṇḍalas through the yoga of the great maṇḍala of the Vajradhātu surrounding the Blessed One Vairocana, and uttered this inspired utterance:
"Aho! How wonderful is the discipline of skillful means for those who possess the great skillful means!"
"Because they discipline sentient beings through skillful means, the stainless ones manifest as wrathful.

(STT 1,326,654) Then the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Vairocana, relying upon the non-conceptual nature of all phenomena of all Tathāgatas, entered the samādhi called "The Vajra Empowerment of the Great Wrathful Vajra-Samaya of All Tathāgatas," and spoke this supreme vidyā, the heart-essence of all Tathāgatas, called "The Vajra Hūṃkāra of All Tathāgatas": (STT 1,328,655)

Oṃ śumbha niśumbha hūṃ gṛhṇa gṛhṇa hūṃ gṛhṇāpaya hūṃ ānaya ho bhagavan vajra hūṃ phaṭ! (STT 1,328,656) Then, as soon as this [mantra] had issued forth, Vajrapāṇi emerged from the hearts of all the Tathāgatas. Having empowered and drawn in all the Tathāgatas, together with their assemblies of Bodhisattvas and maṇḍalas, from as many oceans of clouds throughout the expanse of all world-systems, he caused them to enter the great maṇḍala of the Vajra-samaya, bound them by the samayas, (STT 1,328–329,657)
Once again, having become a single massive body of the Great Vajra Wrath, he stood in the heart of the Blessed One Vairocana and uttered this inspired utterance:
"Oh, how truly auspicious in every respect is the thought of awakening (bodhicitta), free from all fault! For even wrath, through its capacity to discipline all, attains a state of delight."
Then that body of the Great Vajra-Wrathful One, having emerged from the heart of the Blessed One and taken his place upon a moon-maṇḍala in front of all the Tathāgatas, again sought the command.

(STT 1,329,660) Then the Blessed One, entering the samādhi called the "Vajra for Attracting the Samayas of All Tathāgatas," emitted from his own heart this heart-mantra of all the Tathāgatas called the "Goad of the Samayas of All Tathāgatas":
(STT 1,330,661) HŪṂ ṬAKKI JJAḤ! (STT 1,330,662)

Then, as soon as this [mantra] had issued forth, all the lords of the triple world, Maheśvara and the rest, as many as there were in the ocean-like clouds of the expanse of all world-systems—each surrounded by their hosts of worldly inhabitants—were drawn in their entirety and without exception by the vajra-hook of the samaya of all Tathāgatas.

Having approached the summit of Mount Sumeru and the gabled pavilion of the vajra-jewel-peak, they stood surrounding the Blessed One on all sides from within that gabled pavilion of the vajra-jewel-peak.
Then Vajrapāṇi, taking that vajra from his own heart and brandishing it, surveyed the entire wheel of the three worlds within the whole triple realm and spoke thus:
"Enter, O sirs, into the teaching of all the Tathāgatas and obey my command!
Then they spoke as follows:
"How should we practice?
The Blessed One Vajrapāṇi replied:
"By practicing the taking of refuge in the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Saṅgha."
"O friends, practice for the sake of attaining the wisdom of the omniscient one! (STT 1,331,668).
Then, Mahādeva—who is the sovereign of the entire triple world in this world-system, and who is proud of his sovereignty over all the three worlds—displaying great wrath, spoke thus: (STT 1,331,669).

"O Yakṣa, I am the sovereign of the triple world, the Lord, the creator, the ordainer, the lord of all beings, the god beyond gods, Mahādeva; so how could I carry out the command of a Yakṣa? (STT 1,332,670).
Then Vajrapāṇi, brandishing his vajra once more, commanded:
"O wicked being, enter the maṇḍala quickly!
Abide in my samaya!"
Then the god Mahādeva said this to the Blessed One:
"Blessed One, who is this being who issues such a command to Īśvara?
Then the Blessed One, having summoned the entire host of the three worlds beginning with Maheśvara, spoke thus:

"Follow along, friends! If you do not observe the vow of taking refuge in the Three Jewels, this yakṣa Vajrapāṇi—cruel, wrathful, fierce, and a great bodhisattva—will destroy the entire triple world with his blazing vajra!"

Then Maheśvara, by virtue of his sovereignty over the entire triple world and his mastery of his own gnosis, in order to manifest himself before the Blessed One Vajrapāṇi, displayed the state of a great fierce wrathful deity, the form of a great terrifier, the emission of great blazing flames, and a great, terrible, boisterous laugh, together with fire; and while displaying these, he spoke thus:
"O sir, I am the sovereign of the entire triple world; I give you my command!
Then Vajrapāṇi, brandishing that vajra with pride and laughing, spoke thus:
"O *kaṭapūtana*, eater of human flesh, you who subsist on funeral-pyre ashes as food, drink, bedding, seat, and clothing, carry out my command!

(STT 1,332,678) Then Maheśvara Mahādeva, having empowered the entire triple world so that it was possessed by great wrath, spoke thus: (STT 1,332,679) "You too must observe my command and abide by the pledge! (STT 1,332,680)
Then Vajrapāṇi, the great king of wrath, said this to the Blessed One:

"Blessed One, this god Mahādeva, out of pride in the power of his own knowledge and because of his great sovereignty and lordship, does not bow before the teaching of all the Tathāgatas. How, then, should he be dealt with?"
Then the Blessed One caused [the practitioners] to recollect the Great Vajra Samaya, which arises from the hearts of all Tathāgatas:
*oṃ niśumbha vajra hūṃ phaṭ*.
Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi uttered his own Vajra Heart-mantra: *oṃ niśumbha vajra hūṃ phaṭ*.
HŪṂ!

(STT 1,336,684) Now, as soon as this was spoken, the great gods and others, the lords of the entire triple world who had assembled from all the three realms, fell face down and went for refuge to Vajrapāṇi.
(STT 1,336,685) And that great god, the deity, fell upon the ground, became motionless, and died. (STT 1,336,685)
Then the Blessed One, although already knowing [the situation], spoke thus to Vajrapāṇi:
"Act, Vajrapāṇi, for the sake of the safety of this entire wheel of the three worlds; do not cause them to meet their death!
Then Vajrapāṇi, the Great King of Wrath, having heard the words of the Blessed One, summoned all those gods and others and spoke thus:
"Go for refuge to the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Saṅgha; and if you desire your own lives, act according to my command. Then they spoke thus:
“We take refuge in the oceans of the Buddha, Dharma, and Saṅgha;
we do not know the command of your teaching.
Then the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Vairocana, addressed them and said:

"O gods, this Blessed One, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Samantabhadra, is our sovereign of all Tathāgatas, the father of all Tathāgatas, the executor of the commands of all Tathāgatas, and the eldest son of all Tathāgatas; he has been consecrated into the state of the Great Wrathful King for the purpose of performing the work of disciplining all sentient beings.
Why is that? Because—"

"Among you there are wicked hosts such as Mahādeva and others, who cannot be turned away from their evils even by all the Tathāgatas through peaceful means. I have empowered [this rite] for the sake of subduing those evil beings; therefore, you must abide by this pledge (samaya). This is my command.
They replied thus:
“O Blessed One, protect us from this destruction of our lives!
We shall do whatever command you give.
The Blessed One said:
"O worthy ones, go for refuge to him alone; he alone will protect you, and no other!

(STT 1,338,695) Then those lords of the three worlds, who had assembled from the entirety of the triple realm of the three worlds, turned toward the Blessed One Vajradhara and, with one voice, emitting cries of great distress, spoke thus:
(STT 1,340,696) "Protect us, O Blessed One! Protect us, O Sugata, from this suffering of death! (STT 1,340,697)
Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, having summoned those gods and others, spoke thus:
"Ho! You wicked ones, conduct yourselves according to my teaching; lest I, by means of this vajra, reduce you all to a single blaze and turn you entirely to ashes!
They replied as follows:

“O Blessed One, you are Samantabhadra; you are the arising of the mind of all Tathāgatas, peaceful and well-disciplined, seeking the welfare of all sentient beings, and bestowing fearlessness upon all sentient beings.
Therefore, O Blessed One, how is it that you would burn us?
Then Vajrapāṇi, the Great Wrathful King, spoke to them thus:

"Therefore, O worthy ones, I am Samantabhadra; because I carry out the commands of all the Tathāgatas, I shall destroy you—those of a wicked nature and evil intent like yourselves—for the sake of purifying you, provided that you do not abide by my samaya.
They replied, "So be it.
Then Vajrapāṇi, the Great Wrathful King, having released Maheśvara and comforted the other gods for the purpose of raising them up, spoke this Heart of All Tathāgatas called "Vajra Arising":
"Vajra! Arise! (STT 1,342,704).

As soon as this was spoken, with the exception of Maheśvara, all those lords of the three worlds assembled in the triple realm, together with their retinues, having been unconscious, became comforted in heart.
Experiencing divine pleasures, free from fear, trembling, and horripilation, they looked toward the Blessed One Vajrapāṇi and rose up. (STT 1,342,705–706)
Then the Blessed One addressed the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi:
"O Mahāsattva, this Mahādeva, the lord of the gods, has not been raised up.
What is the use of taking his life?"
"Bring this man back to life; he shall become a virtuous person.
Then Vajrapāṇi, having said "So be it," recited this Heart-mantra for Reviving the Dead:
*Vajrāyuḥ*.
Then, as soon as this was spoken, the god Mahādeva, having died, wished to revive and rise up, but he was unable to rise.
Thereupon, he said this to the Blessed One:
"How am I to be instructed by the Blessed One?"
The Blessed One said:
"You do not intend to carry out the command of this Great Being;
he alone instructs you, not I."
Maheśvara said:
"O Blessed One, why have you not been told to protect us from this wicked being?
The Blessed One replied: [as follows].
"I am not capable of protecting him from this.
Maheśvara said:
"For what reason?"
The Blessed One said:
"Because he is the sovereign of all Tathāgatas.
Maheśvara said:

“Blessed One, I do not understand the meaning of what the Blessed One has said. However, since there is indeed another sovereign even over the Tathāgatas, the lords of the entire triple world—I do not know who this is.
Then the Blessed One, the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, again addressed Mahādeva, saying: “You do not comply with my command, you wicked being!”
Then Mahādeva, having heard the words of Vajrasattva, became enraged and fierce; remaining in that very state of collapse, he displayed an even more extremely terrible form and spoke thus:
"I would even venture death, but I will not carry out your command!
Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, manifesting great wrath, caused this Vajra-attendant to issue forth from the sole of his own foot.

Oṃ ed. Oṃ pādākarṣaṇavajra hūṃ! (STT 1,345,720) Then, from the soles of the Blessed One’s feet, a Vajra-attendant emerged, possessing a great mouth made terrifying by fangs and a frown, with a core of flames blazing on all sides. Having issued forth and gone out, he stood before Vajrapāṇi and awaited his command. (STT 1,345,721) Then Vajrapāṇi spoke thus for the purpose of purifying Maheśvara: (STT 1,345,722)

Oṃ pādākarṣākarṣaya sarvavajradharānucarākaḍḍhākaḍḍha-vajra hūṃ jaḥ! (STT 1,345,722) Now, when this had been said, Mahādeva, together with the goddess Umā, standing on his head, naked, and being mocked by all the world, was placed at the soles of the feet before the Blessed One Vajrapāṇi by the foot-drawing Vajra-attendant. (STT 1,345,723) Then the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi addressed the Blessed One as follows: (STT 1,347,724)
“Blessed One, this wicked being is accompanied by his wife; what shall I do?
The Blessed One said:
“Oṃ vajrākrama hoḥ!”
Then, when this had been said, the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, having trampled Mahādeva with his left foot and causing him to be trampled by Umādevī with his right, uttered this heart-mantra:
*Oṃ vajrāviśa hana pātraṃ traṭ*.
As soon as it was recited, Mahādeva was possessed, and with his own thousand hands he struck his own thousand faces while they were lifeless.
Then, from the exterior of the peaked pavilion with its crest of vajra-jewels, a great roar was uttered by all the inhabitants of the three worlds:
"This is our sovereign! He has been entered by this Great Being!
Then the Blessed One, having generated great compassion for Mahādeva, spoke this *Sarvabuddhamaitrīhṛdaya*:
Oṃ buddhamaitrīvajra rakṣa hūṃ!
(STT 1,349,729) As soon as this was spoken, Mahādeva’s suffering of possession was pacified.

(STT 1,349,730) And that touch of Vajrapāṇi’s palm became the means for attaining the supreme accomplishment, the empowerment, the meditative absorption, the liberation, the dhāraṇīs, the knowledge, and the superknowledges, up to the state of a Tathāgata. (STT 1,349,730)

Then Mahādeva, experiencing the bliss of the samādhis, dhāraṇīs, and liberations of all the Tathāgatas through the touch of the Blessed One’s foot, offered that Mahādeva-body at the feet of Vajrapāṇi.

Passing downward through world-systems as numerous as the atoms in thirty-two world-systems, each equal to the sands of the river Gaṅgā, there is a world-system named Bhasmācchanna; therein, a Tathāgata named Bhasmeśvaranirghoṣa appeared.
Then, from that body of Mahādeva, this inspired utterance (*udāna*) issued forth:
"Oh, indeed, the unsurpassed Buddha-knowledge of all Buddhas! Having caused [beings] to fall away from the state of syllables and words, they establish them in *nirvṛti* (cessation)."
Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi spoke thus to those others, Nārāyaṇa and the rest, the lords of all the three worlds:
"Enter, O worthy ones, into this great maṇḍala of the vajra-samaya of all the Tathāgatas; having entered, maintain the samaya of all the Tathāgatas.
They replied as follows:
“As you command, so shall we do.
Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi addressed those inhabitants of the three worlds, saying:
“Ho there, friends! Receive once more the vow of the training in the observance of taking refuge in the Three Jewels.”
"And abide in my teaching.
They replied,
"So be it."
"However, we do not yet understand the time for the Blessed One’s command.
Then Vajrapāṇi bestowed his own commitment (*samaya*):
"Having generated the thought of awakening (*bodhicitta*)," [he said].
Then, in due order,
one should [strive] for great enlightenment according to one's ability.
"Exert yourselves with perfect composure!
Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, having said, "I shall bind the entry-seal (*praveśasamayamudrā*) for those gods and others," he bound it, using this heart-mantra of the Great Samaya-seal:
Oṃ vajrasamaya gṛhṇa bandha samayaṃ vajrasattva samayam anusmara sarvatathāgatasamayas tvam.

"Be firm for me! Be steady for me! Be unassailable for me! Be irresistible for me! And bring about the excellence of my mind in all activities! Ha ha ha ha hūṃ! (STT 1,353,742) Then, as soon as this was uttered, the Vajra-Krodha-Terittiri mudrā entered the hands of the entire assembly of beings throughout the three worlds of the triple realm, and by being bound, it became firm. (STT 1,353,743)

Then Vajrapāṇi, having caused them to enter in the proper manner, having shown them the entire great maṇḍala in successive order, having consecrated them with the consecrations of vajra-jewels, having given the vajra symbols into their hands, and having consecrated them with the consecrations of vajra-names, established them in the state of being the all-purpose of all Tathāgatas. Then follows the ritual activity of the lords of the entire triple world, as follows:
To Maheśvara, Krodhavajra;
to Nārāyaṇa, Māyāvajra;
to Sanat-umāra, Vajraghaṇṭa.
To Brahmā, Maunavajra;
to Indra, Vajrāyudha. Thus they were consecrated as the Vidyārājas.
Then he bestowed [the empowerment] upon all the lords of the gods who move through the intermediate space (*antarīkṣa*).
Namely:
Vajrakuṇḍali to Amṛtakuṇḍali.
To Indu, Vajraprabha;
to Mahādaṇḍāgrīya, Vajradaṇḍa;
to Piṅgala, Vajrapiṅgala.

Thus were they consecrated as the Vajra-krodhas (Vajra Wrathful Ones). Then he bestowed [the rank] upon all the lords of the gods who move through space (*ākāśacara*), as follows: Namely: [The names follow].
To Madhumatta, Vajraśauṇḍa;
to Madhukara, Vajramāla;
to Jaya, Vajravaśī.
"Vijayavajra [is for] Jayāvaha. Thus were the Gaṇapatis consecrated.
Then he bestowed [the office] upon all the terrestrial lords of the gods.
They are as follows:
for Kośapāla, the Vajra-mace;
for Vāyu, the Vajra-wind.
Vajrānala for Agni;
Vajrabhairava for Kuvera—
these and others were thus consecrated as messengers.
Then he bestowed [these] upon all the gods who are lords of Pātāla.
Namely:
to Varāha, the vajra-goad.
To Yama, Vajrakāla;
to Pṛthivīcūlika, Vajravināyaka;
to Varuṇa, Nāgavajra.
Thus, these and others were consecrated as *ceṭakas*.

Then, having consecrated the sovereigns of the three worlds and all the goddesses with the vajra-jewel consecration, having empowered their own emblems—the vajras—and having consecrated them with the vajra-name consecration, he established them in the welfare of the sentient beings of all the Tathāgatas.
It was as follows:
To Umā, Krodhavajrāgni;
to Rukmiṇī, Vajrahemā;
to Ṣaṣṭhī, Vajrakaumārī.
"Vajramuṣṭi for Brahmāṇī"—
thus they were consecrated as the Vajrarājñīs.
Then he bestowed [the consecrations] upon all the Mothers who move through the atmosphere.
Namely:
for Amṛtā, Vajrāmṛtā;
for Rohiṇī, Vajrakānti.
To Daṇḍadhāriṇī, Vajradaṇḍāgrī, and Vajrāgrī; to Jātahāriṇī, Vajramekhalā—
thus were these and others consecrated as the Vajra-krodhinīs.
Then he bestowed [the teachings] upon all the Mothers who move through the sky (*khecarī*).
Namely:
Vajravilayā to Māraṇyā.
To eating, Vajrāśanā;
to clothing, Vajravasanā;
to pleasure, Vajravaśā.
Thus were the *gaṇikās* consecrated with these and other [names].
Then he bestowed [the consecration] upon all the Mothers who roam the earth (*bhūcarīs*).
It was as follows:
To Śivā, Vajradūtī; to Vāyavī, Vegavajriṇī; to Āgneyī, Vajrajvālā.
"To Kauveryā, Vajravikaṭā"—
thus were they consecrated as the Vajra-messengers (vajradūtīs).
Then he bestowed [the consecration] upon all the Mothers (mātṛs) who dwell in the netherworld (pātāla).
Namely: to Vārāhī, Vajramukhī;
to Cāmuṇḍā, Vajrakālī.
To Chinnanāsā, Vajrapūtanā;
to Vāruṇī, Vajramakarā—
thus were these and others consecrated as the Vajraceṭīs.

Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, having brought about the realization of the Buddha-knowledges for all those who had entered, and having instructed them in the binding of all mudrās, bestowed the Vajra Samayas with this heart-mantra of oath:
"This vajra is the great vajra, empowered by all the Buddhas. Through the transgression of the samaya, it shall swiftly reduce one's entire family to ashes."
Oṃ hanasamaya hūṃ phaṭ!
Then he bestowed the heart-seizing mudrā:
having formed the double vajra-mudrā, the two index fingers are bound like hooks.
"Whoever intends to accomplish a task should perform the *valita-udvalita* [gesture].
You must stand before him for the sake of accomplishing that task;
for this is the command, lest it lead to the destruction of your lives."

Having made the vajra-bind firm and well-restrained with the tips of the fingers bent, one should join the pair of thumbs and press them against the pair of middle fingers. This is your pledge (samaya); it shall destroy anyone who should transgress it.
The binding of the Samayamudrā belongs to the Vajra-vidyādhara.
As for the two Vajramudrās, they consist of the binding of the little fingers;
having turned them so that the tips of the fingers grasp each other from behind, they remain positioned at the head.
The binding of the Vajra-Vidyādhara is this commitment (*samaya*) of the Great-Souled One.
One who looks upon [the practitioner] while enraged should likewise remain before him.
Having firmly bound the Vajra-Rakṣā, one should then press the Vajra-Bandha.
For this is the convention of the terrestrial [deities], which protects all sentient beings.
Whoever, filled with wrath, should bind [the mantra] for the sake of protection,
he must stand behind that being who is to be protected.
Having bound the pair of vajra-mudrās, with the left [hand] pressing upon the tips of the vajras,
one should perform the turning and un-turning and then extend the little fingers.
Whoever, being composed yet wrathful, should employ this— this indeed is the *samaya*.
"You must stand before him for the sake of the supreme accomplishment of sentient beings.
Having bound it firmly with the vajra-bind, one should join the two index fingers;
one should encircle the vajra-mudrā at the tips of the middle fingers and the thumbs.
Having turned [the hand] over and placed it upon the forehead, whoever should summon [an opponent], that person must always stand before him if they wish to live.
Now, these are the heart-mantras for seizing the pledge of these mudrās which seize the hearts of the entire triple world: [Mantras follow]
Oṃ valitodvalita-vajra ākarṣaya hūṃ jjaḥ!
(STT 1,371,789) This is the heart-mantra for summoning the gods with the *vajravalita* mudrā.
(STT 1,371,789) Hūṃ vajrāgra pīḍaya samaya hūṃ! (STT 1,371,790)
For those who move through the atmosphere:
Oṃ vajramālāgra vaṃ.
For those who wear garlands: Oṃ vajramālāgra vaṃ.
Oṃ vajrabandha haṃ! (For those who move upon the earth. Oṃ vajrapātāla bhañja bhañja hūṃ phaṭ!
[This is] for those dwelling in Pātāla: Oṃ herukavajrasamayasarvaduṣṭasamayamudrāprabhañjaka hūṃ phaṭ! [This is] for all the Mothers.
Then the Blessed One Vajrapāṇi said this to the Blessed One:
"Blessed One, I have been consecrated by all the Tathāgatas as the 'Tamer of the Wicked'."
"Therefore, please command how I should proceed against all these bonds of evil maṇḍalas.
Then the Blessed One, having heard this, spoke as follows:
"Oṃ vajraśumbha niśumbha hūṃ phaṭ!"
Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, for the sake of protecting all sentient beings, spoke this heart-mantra for summoning all maṇḍalas:
Oṃ vajrasamayākarṣaya sarvamaṇḍalān vajradharasatyaṃ mātikrama huṃ phaṭ!
Having formed the two vajra-hooks, one should rotate them at the heart.
"The two *agrāṅkuśī*s [are for] the supreme drawing in of the outer maṇḍala.
(STT 1,373,800) Then, as soon as this was spoken, all the maṇḍalas stood surrounding the summit of Mount Sumeru from all sides on the outside.
(STT 1,373,801) Then the Blessed One Vajrapāṇi, having summoned all those arrangements of maṇḍalas, spoke thus: (STT 1,373,802)
"Engage yourselves, sirs, in the undertaking of the commitment to abstain from taking life!
(STT 1,373,802) Then those outer maṇḍala beings of the commitment addressed the Blessed One:

"Blessed One, we are meat-eaters; because we are wicked beings, we maintain our livelihood by consuming living creatures. Therefore, may the Blessed One command us: how are we to live? (STT 1,373,803)
Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi spoke this Malicious Vajra Wrath:
OṂ DUṢṬAVAJRAKRODHA HANA DAHA PACA VIDHVAṂSAYA VIKIRA SARVADUṢṬASAMAYAMUDRĀMAṆḌALĀN BHAÑJA BHAÑJA MARDĀ MARDĀ KHĀDA KHĀDA PARAMANTRĀN VAJRASAMAYAHŪṂ PHAṬ!
The fingers of the Vajra Wrath are correctly joined, with the nails interlaced and encircled.

One should join [the hands] firmly at the mouth; this is the *mudrā* for the destruction of the wicked. (STT 1,373–374,805) As soon as this was spoken, all the mandalas of the wicked gathered together and were destroyed and scattered in great numbers. (STT 1,374,806) The binding of the *samaya-mudrās* was shattered. (STT 1,374,806)

And those wicked beings of the *samaya*, being burned and cooked, uttering great cries of distress like those of the Great Hell of Wailing (*Mahāraurava*), joined their palms toward where the Blessed One Mahāvajradhara was and spoke thus:
"Protect us, Blessed One, so that we may not lose our lives!
Then Vajrapāṇi again addressed the Blessed One in this way:
"Command me, Blessed One, how I am to proceed against these wicked maṇḍalas.
Then the Blessed One spoke this:
"Oṃ niśumbha hana daha paca gṛhṇa bandha huṃ phaṭ!"
Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi spoke this Vajra-Cruel-Anger mantra:

Oṃ, O Great Vajra-Cruel-Anger! Strike down all evil maṇḍalas! Destroy all evil samayas! Scatter, shatter, and explode! Break all evil samaya-seals and bonds! Seize, slay, burn, and cook all evil samaya-beings! Vajrasamaya hūṃ phaṭ!
Then, as soon as this had been spoken, all those mandalas of the seals of the wicked samayas once again became one and fell into the great ocean.
Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi spoke thus again to the Blessed One:
"I have been requested by the Blessed One to subdue all the wicked."
"Therefore, how should I proceed against these and all other seizing spirits, such as the *ḍākinīs*?
Then the Blessed One spoke this:
"Oṃ hana hana vajra huṃ phaṭ!"
Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi again spoke the heart-mantra for summoning all the wicked grahas, such as the ḍākinīs:
OṂ VAJRĀKARṢAYA ŚĪGHRAṂ SARVADUṢṬAGRAHĀN VAJRADHARASATYENA HŪṂ JAḤ.
As soon as this was spoken, all the wicked grahas, such as the ḍākinīs, gathered on the summit of Mount Sumeru and stood surrounding it in a circle.
Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi summoned those ḍākinīs and all the wicked grahas and spoke thus:
"Commit yourselves, friends, to the training and the vow of the pledge of abstaining from taking life; otherwise, I shall consume your families with my blazing, flaming, single-mass vajra!
Then those ḍākinīs and all the wicked grahas, toward where the Blessed One was, joined their palms in reverence and made this request to the Blessed One:
"O Blessed One, we are meat-eaters. Therefore, please command us: how should we proceed? Then the Blessed One spoke thus to Vajrapāṇi:

"Proceed, Vajrapāṇi, having generated great compassion for these beings, to grant them the means [of deliverance]. (STT 1,377,819) Then Vajrapāṇi, the Great Compassionate One, spoke this heart-mantra of the seal of knowledge regarding the signs of death for all beings: (STT 1,377,820) Oṃ vajra, receive this heart; draw it forth! If this being dies within half a month, then let his heart emerge! Samaya hūṃ jaḥ! (STT 1,377,820)
Now follows the formation of its mudrā:
Having firmly applied the vajra-bind with both arms at the heart,
one should scratch one's own armpits with the tips of the vajra-fingers.

"By means of this mudrā, you must extract the hearts of all sentient beings and consume them. (STT 1,377,822) Then those ḍākinīs and all the malevolent grahas, uttering "hulu hulu" and letting out shrill cries, departed for their own abodes.
(STT 1,377,823) Then the Blessed One Vajrapāṇi again addressed the Blessed One as follows: (STT 1,379,824)
"I have been requested by all the Blessed Tathāgatas to be the subduer of all malevolent beings.
Therefore, may the Blessed One command me: what shall I do regarding diseases such as fever and the like?
Then the Blessed One said:
Oṃ hūṃ phaṭ!
Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi uttered the heart-mantra for summoning all fevers and the like:
Oṃ vajrasamayānaya sarvaduṣṭajvarādīn nāśaya hūṃ phaṭ!
Then, as soon as this was spoken, all the fevers and other afflictions surrounded Mount Sumeru on its summit from the outside and remained there.
Then Vajrapāṇi, having summoned those fevers and others, spoke to them thus:
"Friends, enter into the restraint of undertaking the training in abstaining from harming sentient beings."
Then they said this:
"Blessed One, we sustain our livelihood by taking away the vital energy (*ojas*) of sentient beings. Therefore, may the Blessed One please grant us permission."
"How shall we proceed?
Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi uttered this Heart-Mantra for the Purification of One's Own Karma:
Oṃ vajrakarma viśodhaya sarvāvaraṇāni buddhasatyena samaya hūṃ!
Now follows the binding of its mudrā: Having made the vajrāñjali firm, with the two index fingers bent and the thumbs tightly bound and constrained, it is the "remover of evil."
If this mudrā is shown through ritual action to anyone afflicted by all diseases such as fever,
you must depart from that place;
lest there be the loss of your lives.
Then, having said, "So be it," they departed.
(STT 1,380,833) Then the great bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi spoke thus to all the Tathāgatas:
(STT 1,382,834) "I have been emitted from the hearts of the Blessed Ones for the sake of purifying all obscurations, hindrances, and karmic obstructions. (STT 1,382,835)
"Therefore, may the Blessed Ones command me: how should one practice regarding these lower realms, such as the hells and so forth?
The Blessed One said:
"Oṃ kṣapaya vajra svāhā."
Then Vajrapāṇi, the Great Pure Being, spoke this heart-mantra for drawing forth all those in the wheel of rebirths in the lower realms, beginning with Raurava:
OṂ SARVĀPĀYĀKARṢAṆAVIŚODHANAVAJRASAMAYA HŪṂ PHAṬ!
(STT 1,382,837) As soon as this was spoken, all the abodes of the lower realms, beginning with Raurava and Mahāraurava, stood surrounding the summit of Mount Sumeru from the outside. (STT 1,382,838)
Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, having summoned all those beings dwelling in the realms of misfortune, spoke thus:
"O Blessed One, protect us from this calamity and distress!
We here go for refuge to the Buddha, the Dharma, the Saṅgha, and to you."
Then they spoke with one voice:
"Protect us, Blessed One, from this calamity and distress!
We go for refuge to the Buddha, the Dharma, the Saṅgha, and to you."
Then Vajrapāṇi uttered the heart-mantra for shattering all evils:
Oṃ vajrapāṇi visphoṭaya sarvāpāyabandhanāni pramokṣaya sarvāpāyagatibhyaḥ sarvasattvān sarvatathāgatavajrasamaya traṭ! Then follows the binding of its mudrā:

Having firmly established the vajra-bind, with the two middle fingers joined at their tips and the four remaining fingers touching the mouth [of the hand], it is proclaimed as "Pāpasphoṭā. Then, all those sentient beings dwelling within the wheel of the three miserable destinies, having seen this mudrā from Vajrapāṇi, fell away from all evil states of existence and were reborn at the feet of the Blessed One Vairocana.
"And those [weapons] fell into the great ocean.
(STT 1,383,843) Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi again addressed the Blessed One as follows:

(STT 1,385,844) "O Blessed One, for the sake of protecting the realm of all sentient beings without exception or remainder, and for the purpose of experiencing all benefit and happiness, up until the attainment of the fruit of the supreme siddhi of the state of all Tathāgatas, I have bestowed the Vajra of the Siddhi of All Tathāgatas, and I have been exhorted by all the Tathāgatas. (STT 1,385,844)
"Therefore, may the Blessed Ones, all the Tathāgatas, graciously command me: what shall I do for these humans?
Then all the Tathāgatas, having gathered together once more, spoke this:

"Oṃ! Vajrapāṇi, cause them to enter the great maṇḍala; ward off all the wicked and fierce ones; liberate them from their sins; purify those who have fallen into wrong views; destroy, utterly annihilate—ha ha ha ha hūṃ!"

Then Vajrapāṇi, having heard the command of all the Tathāgatas, for the sake of protecting the realm of sentient beings without exception or remainder, for the sake of the supreme accomplishment of all benefit and happiness, and for the cause of attaining the fruit of the knowledge and super-knowledges of all the Tathāgatas, spoke this great maṇḍala named Trilokavijaya, which is the great vajra-samaya of all the Tathāgatas:
"Now, therefore, I shall fully explain the supreme great maṇḍala."
Resembling the Vajradhātu, it is the supreme bringer of all accomplishments;
it is the pledge (samaya) born of the Vajra named Trilokavijaya,
which sets in motion the awakening of the Buddhas and destroys all that is evil.
There, one should mark out the lines with this mantra:
*Oṃ vajrasamaya sūtraṃ mātikrama*.
[It should be] four-cornered, with four gates, and adorned with four archways.
Equipped with four threads and beautifully adorned with silk garlands,
one should mark out the outer maṇḍala, inlaid with vajra-jewels at all the corners of the maṇḍala and at the junctions of the doors and projections.
Within that, the wise one [should construct] a square [mandala] adorned with vajra-jewels, having four doors and protected by eight pillars;
it is adorned with five lunar mandalas situated at the tops of the vajra-pillars.
One should draw the mandala there and fill the lines with colors.
Regarding this, the mantra for the colors is:
Oṃ vajracitrasamaya hūṃ.
Then, standing in the center and being composed, the Vajrācārya should mentally open the four vajra doors. Herein is the mantra for opening the doors:
Oṃ, open the vajra! Enter the samaya! Hūṃ!
Whether in gold or silver, or even in well-painted clay, or upon a square brick, one should place the image of the Buddha.
Next, this is the heart-mantra for summoning all Tathāgatas:
Oṃ vajrajvālāgnipradīptākarṣaya sarvatathāgatān mahāvajrasamaya hūṃ jaḥ!
One should place the vajra in front of the Buddha within the midst of the flames.
One should draw a jewel, a lotus, and likewise the universal weapon (viśvāyudha) in the midst of the flames.
Now, here are the heart-mantras for the placement of these Vajra-samaya-mudrās:
HŪṂ SATTVA-VAJRA-JVĀLĀMĀLA HŪṂ PHAṬ!
Oṃ ratnavajrajvālāmāla hūṃ traḥ. Oṃ dharmavajrajvālāmāla hūṃ hrīḥ.
Hūṃ karmavajrajvālāmāla hūṃ aḥ.
Having emerged with vajra-velocity in that manner before the Buddha,
the wise one should duly draw the Vajra-hūṃkāra maṇḍala.
In this regard, the heart-mantra of Vajravega is as follows:
Oṃ vajravegākrama hūṃ!
Thus, having stepped upon the thread in all mandalas, such as the Vajradhātu and others, one should proceed everywhere.
Now follows its mudrā.
Having mentally raised the line or even the vajra-thread,
whether entering or exiting, he does not tremble from the *samaya*.
Therein, in the center, one should draw the Great Being Vajrapāṇi.
Having the luster of a great blue lotus, he embodies the Vajra-hūṃkāra;
his face is slightly terrifying with bared fangs, and his countenance is grinning with wrath.
He stands firmly in the pratyālīḍha posture, blazing with a mass of flaming garlands.
Maheśvara should be depicted with his left foot stepped upon by him;
his right foot, however, should be drawn resting upon the full breasts of Umā.
In this regard, his heart-mantra is as follows:
HŪṂ!
On all his sides, one should station the Vajra-wrath deities,
who have terrifying fangs of anger and whose splendor consists of a mass of blazing garlands.
Now, their heart mantras are as follows:
Oṃ vajrasattvakrodha hūṃ phaṭ!
Oṃ vajrakrodhākarṣaya hūṃ phaṭ!
Oṃ vajrakāmakrodha rāgaya hūṃ phaṭ!
Oṃ vajratuṣṭikrodha sādhu sādhu hūṃ phaṭ!
Having advanced with vajra-velocity, one reaches the second supreme maṇḍala.
Therein, one should draw the Vajra-initiation surrounded by the Mistress of Wrath (Krodheśvarī).
Now, their heart-mantras are as follows:
TRAḤ.
Oṃ vajrabhṛkuṭikrodha hara hara hūṃ phaṭ! (STT 1,391,873) Oṃ vajrasūryamahājvālāmālakrodha jvālaya sarvaṃ hūṃ phaṭ! (STT 1,391,873) Oṃ vajrakrodhaketu dehi hūṃ phaṭ! (STT 1,391,874)
Oṃ vajrāṭṭahāsakrodha haḥ haḥ haḥ haḥ hūṃ phaṭ!
(STT 1,391,874) Having entered with vajra-velocity into the third supreme maṇḍala, one should draw Vajrasena, surrounded by the great-souled wrathful deities. (STT 1,392,875)
Now, their heart-mantras are as follows:
HRĪḤ; OṂ VAJRADHARMAKRODHA VINĀŚAYA VIŚODHAYA HŪṂ PHAṬ.
Oṃ vajratīkṣṇakrodha cchinda cchinda hūṃ phaṭ!
Oṃ vajrahetukrodha praviśa praveśaya maṇḍalaṃ sarvān hūṃ phaṭ!
Oṃ vajrakrodhabhāṣa vada vada hūṃ phaṭ!

Having entered by means of the vajra-impulse into the fourth, most excellent mandala, one should depict the Vajra-possessing [deity] surrounded by the hosts of Vajra-wrathful ones. Their heart-mantras are as follows:
Aḥ! Hūṃ, Vajrakarmakrodha, perform [it], perform! Hūṃ phaṭ! Oṃ, Vajrakavacakrodha, protect, protect! Hūṃ phaṭ!
Oṃ vajrayakṣakrodha khāda khāda hūṃ phaṭ!
(STT 1,393,880) Oṃ vajrakrodhamuṣṭi sādhaya samaya hūṃ phaṭ! (STT 1,393,880) In the corners of this maṇḍala, however, they should be placed correctly and in successive order. (STT 1,394,881)
One should depict the secret worship by means of the Vajradhātu application.
(STT 1,394,881) Now, their heart-seals (*hṛdayamudrā*) are as follows:
(STT 1,394,882) Oṃ vajralāsye rāgaya hūṃ phaṭ! (STT 1,394,882)
Oṃ vajramāle abhiṣiñca hūṃ phaṭ!
Oṃ vajragīte gāda gāda hūṃ phaṭ!
Oṃ vajranṛtye vaśīkuru hūṃ phaṭ!
Having emerged with the force of a vajra into the supreme outer maṇḍala,
one should place the four offering goddesses there in the corners.
Now, their heart-seals (hṛdayamudrā) are as follows:
Oṃ vajra-dhūpa-pūjā-spharaṇa-samaye hūṃ phaṭ! (STT 1,394,885) Oṃ vajra-puṣpa-pūjā-spharaṇa-samaye hūṃ phaṭ!
(STT 1,394,885) Oṃ vajra-āloka-pūjā-spharaṇa-samaye hūṃ phaṭ! (STT 1,394,886)
Oṃ vajragandhapūjāspharaṇasamaye hūṃ phaṭ!
(STT 1,394,886) The [deities] beginning with Aṅkuśā should be placed in the four centers of the gates;
as for the outer Vajra families, they are situated within the outer maṇḍala. (STT 1,395,887)
Now, their heart-seals (*hṛdaya-mudrā*) are as follows:
Oṃ vajrāṅkuśakrodha ākarṣaya sarvasamayān hūṃ jjaḥ! Oṃ vajrapāśakrodha praveśaya sarvasamayān hūṃ hūṃ!

Oṃ vajrasphoṭa-mahākrodha bandha bandha sarvasamayān hūṃ vaṃ! (STT 1,395,889) Oṃ vajrāveśa-krodha āveśaya sarvasamayān hūṃ aḥ! (STT 1,395,889) Now follows the detailed procedure for entry into this Great Maṇḍala of the Conqueror of the Three Worlds: (STT 1,395,890)

In that regard, first of all, the Vajrācārya himself shall enter after binding the mudrā of Vajrakrodhaterittiri. Having entered, he should inform all the Tathāgatas: "O Blessed Tathāgatas, I shall come under the power of wrath; I shall subdue those who are to be subdued, and I shall gather in those who are to be gathered in."

Having thought, "May the Blessed Ones grant me their command as to how I should proceed," one should place the Vajrakrodha-terittiri-mudrā upon one's own heart according to the ritual rule, perform the rites with the vajra-hook and other implements, and then bind the seal of all commitments (*sarvasamayamudrā*).
Thereupon, they all manifest their presence.
Then, having performed the fourfold secret worship as well as with incense and other offerings,
one should cause the vajra-disciples to enter according to this rite.
The Vajra-Ācārya himself, having bound the mudrā of Vajrakrodha-Terittiri, should cause them to enter with this mantra.
"Oṃ, I enter the vajra-samaya. With this heart-mantra, one should bind the disciple.
"Oṃ, grasp the vajra-samaya, hūṃ vaṃ!

Then, having donned a blue upper garment and a blue turban bound upon the head, and having covered the face with a blue veil, one should cause [the disciple] to enter with this mantra: (STT 1,397,895)
Oṃ, I enter the vajra-samaya.
Then, having caused [the disciple] to enter, one should produce possession within him by means of the Vajrāveśa-samaya-mudrā and this heart-mantra:
Vajrāveśa aḥ!
Then he enters [into that state].
By that entry, he is empowered by all the Tathāgatas.
And he knows everything—past, future, and present—in the mere twinkling of an eye.
He becomes invulnerable to all sentient beings and unassailable;
by the syllable *huṃ*, he becomes capable of both subduing and favoring all sentient beings;
and Vajrapāṇi constantly accomplishes all his undertakings.
Then one should administer the heart-mantra of the oath.
Then, having properly released the binding of the face, one should show the great mandala.
Merely by seeing the mandala, one is liberated from all sins.
One becomes capable of conquering the entire triple world.
By means of the syllable *huṃ*, one becomes able to attract, cause to enter, bind, subjugate, and strike down all the gods, beginning with Mahādeva.
Furthermore, through the empowerment (*adhiṣṭhāna*) of all the Tathāgatas, the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi remains constantly by one's side and bestows his own accomplishments (*siddhi*).
Then, having consecrated him with the vajra-consecration, one should duly place the sharp insignia of his own vajra into his two hands with this mantra:
*oṃ vajrapāṇi vajrakarmakaro bhava*.
Then, one should bestow the vajra-name consecration with this mantra: [om vajranāma abhiṣiñca].
"Oṃ, Vajrakrodha, I consecrate you with the vajra-name-consecration; O [Vajra-]Name! (STT 1,398,903).
Then, whatever name one should give to someone, the word "he" (*he*) should be employed before it (STT 1,398,904).
Thereafter, one should generate the gnoses. (STT 1,399,905)
Having drawn the Vajra-image, which has the radiance of a mass of flames, upon the heart;
through the meditative absorption (*samāpatti*) of the Vajra-wrathful one, one should cause the entire world to enter [into it].
Likewise, having drawn the Vajra-jewel upon the forehead; STT 1,399,906.
By means of the meditative absorption of Vajrakrodha, one should bring all sentient beings under control.
Placing the vajra-lotus at the throat, with its radiance consisting of a mass of blazing flames,
he shall destroy all sentient beings through the meditative absorption of Vajrakrodha.
Having established the universal vajra upon the head, blazing with a mass of light,
one should protect this entire world through the meditative absorption (*samāpatti*) of the Vajra Wrathful One (*vajrakrodha*).
Now, here are the heart-mantras (*hṛdaya*) of these wisdom-mudrās (*jñānamudrā*):
Hūṃ! O Sattvavajra-krodha, enter! Aḥ! Ho!
O Ratnavajra-krodha, bring [them] under control! Traṃ! Hūṃ! O Vajradharma-krodha, phaṭ!
"Haṃ! O Karmavajra-krodha, protect! (STT 1,399,909).
Then, one should teach the knowledge of the mudrā for summoning the gods and others:
(STT 1,400,910) having drawn a vajrāṅkuśa on the surface, marked with the syllable *huṃ*. (STT 1,400,910)
Moving one's finger while enraged is the supreme method for summoning the gods.
Having drawn a vajra-hook from the center of the sole of one's own foot,
and having stepped upon the *liṅga* with that very [foot], one will certainly summon the gods.
Having drawn the vajra-hook, when one’s own penis has arisen, by moving it,
one shall summon Umā and all other women.
Likewise, having drawn the vajra-hook upon the secret *trikakuda*, [one shall do the same].
With that, one should step upon whichever deity [one wishes]; this is the supreme summoning of them.
In this regard, their heart-mantras are as follows:
Oṃ vajrakrodhāgrākarṣaya hūṃ phaṭ!

Oṃ vajrakarmāṅkuśakrodha ākarṣaya hūṃ phaṭ! (STT 1,401,914) Oṃ vajrakrodhadaṇḍāgra ākarṣaya hūṃ phaṭ! (STT 1,401,915) Oṃ vajrakrodhāsana āgaccha ākarṣayāmi te vajrasamayam anusmara hūṃ phaṭ! (STT 1,401,915)
Then, one should teach the knowledge of the fourfold mudrās:
"Standing firmly in the *pratyālīḍha* posture through the application of the *vajrāveśa*,
one may cause the entire world to be possessed in an instant by means of the mere syllable *hūṃ*."
With adamantine speech, one should correctly utter [the mantra] conjoined with four *huṃ*s;
this heart-mantra of all the Buddhas will certainly bring everything under control.
Through the meditative absorption (*samāpatti*) of Vajrakrodha, there is the supreme gaze of Vajrakrodha.
One may slay the entire world through the yoga of Vajra-hūṃkāra.
(STT 1,403,918) One should armor one’s own body or that of another with the mind;
by means of the yoga of the Great Armor, one should protect this entire world. (STT 1,403,919)
Now, their heart-mantras are as follows:
Oṃ vajrakrodhakāyāveśaya huṃ aḥ.
Oṃ vajravidyottamamahākrodhānaya ho bhagavan vajra huṃ phaṭ.
Oṃ vajrakrodhadṛṣṭi hana daha paca vināśaya huṃkāreṇa pātaya vajrasamaya huṃ phaṭ!
Oṃ manodṛḍhavajrakavacakrodha rakṣa huṃ phaṭ!
Then, one should teach the knowledge of the seal that seals all sentient beings.
Through the meditative absorption of Vajrakrodha, whomever one should embrace,
that person becomes sealed by the recitation of the Vajra-hūṃkāra mantra.
Speaking with a loud voice, one should say "Ṭakki hūṃ phaṭ" once.
Whomever he strikes with his blazing thunderbolt while enraged— whichever sentient being he gazes upon with the Vajra-vision through the Vajra-wrath samādhi— that very person shall meet their death.
Thinking "I shall slay with the mind," one should visualize the vajra at the heart;
by the syllable *huṃ* alone, one personally seals all [beings] on every side.
Whichever sentient being one seals with whichever mind, that [being is sealed].
"By means of these mudrās, one should accomplish all rites exceedingly well.
Now, their heart-mantras are as follows:
*Ṭakki aḥ*.
Ṭakki jjaḥ! (STT 1,405,927) Ṭakki huṃ! (STT 1,405,927) Ṭakki haṃ! (STT 1,405,927)
"One should employ the four heart-mantras of the mudrās for the four activities with each individual mudrā. (STT 1,405,928) Then, one should teach the knowledge of the secret wrathful mudrās:
"Having encircled [the disciple] with all limbs, one should apply the syllable *huṃ* to whichever [mudrā] is appropriate. (STT 1,405,929)

Through the union of the two organs, his life would perish. (STT 1,405,929) But by kissing, seizing the lip with the teeth, and through the application of the syllable *huṃ*, (STT 1,405,930) the mouth of whosoever [performs] the union of the two organs shall fall down. (STT 1,405,930)
He who employs the syllable *huṃ* while experiencing pleasure,
yet through the union of the two organs, he shall encounter suffering. He who employs the syllable *huṃ* while pressing with his entire body...
"By the union of the two organs, his entire body shall fall.
(STT 1,405–406,932) Then, here are the heart-mantras:
Hūṃ jjaḥ!
Hūṃ hoḥ!
Hūṃ haṃ!
Then, one should teach the knowledge of the mudrās of the reality of the samaya of the great maṇḍala of the Conqueror of the Three Worlds:
"By means of the application of the Vajradhātu, one becomes possessed of the recollection of the Buddhas;
whoever acts for the benefit of sentient beings shall attain Buddhahood."

Having drawn Maheśvara and Umā upon the ground, one should likewise proceed; according to the drawing, one should accomplish the *sattva-mudrā*. By merely binding this [mudrā], one becomes a conqueror of the three worlds.
One shall quickly become a possessor of accomplished knowledge, resembling Vajrahuṃkāra.
Standing in the midst of a circle of flames according to the instructions of the drawing,
one should bind the *sattva-mudrās* with the vajras of body, speech, and mind.
Now I shall explain their activity, the unsurpassed Vajra-activity:
"One who has attained perfection through the recollection of the Buddha shall quickly attain Buddhahood.
Having bound the Trilokavijayā [mudrā], one becomes a conqueror of the three worlds.
Vajrāyus is all-pervading, resembling Vajrahuṃkāra.
Vajrābhiṣekā is sovereignty; Sudharmiṇī is lordship over the worlds. Karmavajramahākrodhā shall be the performer of vajra-activities.
Through *Sattvakrodhā*, there is great firmness; through *Krodhāṅkuśī*, one summons [the deity].
Through *Krodharāgā*, one should arouse passion; through *Sādhukrodhā*, satisfaction is granted. Through *Bhṛkuṭī*, everything is destroyed; through *Krodhasūryā*, there is great brilliance.
Through *Hetukrodhā*, one should seize wealth; through *Aṭṭahāsā*, however, one should cause death.
Through *Dharmakrodhā*, one should seize the teachings (*dharma*); indeed, one should cut [them] with *Krodhavajrā*.
Through *Hetukrodhā*, one should seize away sufferings; one should utter speech with the *Krodhabhāṣā*.
One should perform virtuous deeds through Karmakrodha, and provide protection through Rakṣā.
One should devour the enemy, the Yakṣa of Wrath; indeed, Krodhamuṣṭi brings about accomplishment.
Now follows the binding of the Vajrasamaya-mudrā: [The text continues with the mudrā-bindings.]
Those born from the pair of Vajras are proclaimed as the supreme commitments (*samaya*).
I shall now explain their binding, the unsurpassed binding of the Wrathful Ones (*krodha*):
having joined the arm-vajras, the little fingers are bound in the form of hooks.

The mudrā named Trilokavijayā consists of the two index fingers threatening [the enemy]. Likewise, the Maṇi [mudrā] is formed by joining the tips of the two index fingers while slightly curling them inward.
The Padma [mudrā] has its middle fingers raised level, with the tips of the two middle fingers threatening [the enemy].
The two index fingers as vajras, with the right one bent into a hook;
likewise, it is that very same [mudrā] which utters the *huṃ* sound while devouring, and similarly performs the gesture of approval (*sādhukāra*).
With its two tips joined at the brow, it forms a solar disc at the heart.
With the index finger extending over the top of the outstretched arm and pointing toward the mouth;
the right hand forms a fist with the thumb tucked inside, while the index finger is pressed against the nail [of the middle finger],
and the tips of the middle and index fingers are raised to form a wheel that emerges from the mouth.
The *tarjanīmadhyavajrā* and the *grīvāveṣṭitatarjanī*;
the *agryādvikamahādaṃṣṭrā* with the tips grasped by the *vajramuṣṭi*.
These are the mudrās of the female deities (*sattvī*) such as Vajralāsyā and the others; they are the same [mudrās] when uttered with the syllable *huṃ*.
Furthermore, those very same *dharmamudrās* are accompanied by the syllable *huṃ*.
(STT 1,410,953) Now, the *vajrasamayadharmamudrās* are as follows:
(STT 1,412,954) The syllable *huṃ* belongs to the Buddha and Vajrin; the syllable *traḥ* belongs to Vajragarbha. (STT 1,412,954)
The syllable *hrīḥ* is that of Vajrasena; the syllable *aḥ* is that of Vajraviśvata. *Huṃ heḥ*.
*Trāṃ taṃ*.
