HŪṂ GRAṂ / KṚ VAṂ / DṚ AḤ //
Then there are the Vajra-samaya-karma-mudrās:
Having formed the wrathful fist in two ways through the yoga of Vajra-arrogance and so forth,
the karma-mudrās are briefly taught in the Great Vajra Family.

Whichever mudrā belongs to whichever [deity], and whichever side it occupies according to its function, one should indeed employ that specific mudrā by encircling it in those respective places. This is the procedure for all mudrās.
Now, herein follows the binding of the seals common to the great maṇḍala of Trilokavijaya:
The seal of Trilokavijaya belongs to the Vajrāgra-samaya;
it bestows all accomplishments in an instant for the mantra of Vajra-hūṃkāra.

One should bind the two vajras, upper and lower, with the tips of the little fingers acting as hooks; this is the Samayāṅkuśa mudrā, which instantly draws in everything. Among all the supreme vidyās, it is known as Trilokavijayā.
It is the one that causes all to fall, and likewise the performer of all rites.
Having properly joined the two foremost fingers of the double-vajra while well-composed, one should raise up everyone who has died; this is known as the Vajrottiṣṭha [mudrā].

One should properly bind the two foremost fingers of the two vajras with the vajra-bind; having turned it, one should place it upon the head, for it increases longevity and health. The vajra-bind is formed by inserting the two thumbs together.

With the index fingers firmly clenched and the [feet] rotated, it draws the feet [toward oneself]. Having bound the Trilokavijayā mudrā, if one should step upon the image of a being with the left foot, that being will achieve accomplishment within half a month.
Having bound the pair of Vajra-mudrās, one should strike them against each other;
indeed, one should strike whichever being’s body has been entered [by the mantra].
Having bound the pair of Vajra-mudrās, you are the armor of another.
By joining [the hands] with the two index fingers, protection becomes eternal.
(STT 1,415,968) Having formed the vajra-bind at the palms, one with a wrathful mind should cover [them];
by firmly pressing with the thumb-vajras, the great Vajra family is accomplished. (STT 1,415,969)
Having made the *sattvavajra* firm, with the two middle fingers grasped by the thumbs,
the sharp [edges] from the tips of the little fingers constitute the *samayagrāhā*.
Having bound the pair of *vajra-mudrās*, the tips [of the index fingers] are joined in a curved shape.
Performing the supreme drawing-in of the deities by alternating the contraction and expansion [of the fingers],

one should firmly establish the *vajrabandha* with the tips of the fingers curled and well-restrained. Pressing the pair of thumbs together at the junction, one should direct them toward the midst of those who dwell in the intermediate space (*antarīkṣa*).
The middle of the little fingers belongs to the pair of Vajra-mudrās;
having turned them back so that the tips of the fingers grasp from behind, this is for those who move through the sky.
Having made the Vajra-protection firm, one should press the Vajra-bind.
For this is the convention of the terrestrial [spirits], which accomplishes all things and is difficult to transgress.
Having bound the pair of vajra-mudrās, with the tips of the left vajra-fingers pressed together and the final fingers snapped, this is the summoner of the netherworld (pātāla).

The two index fingers are firmly knotted with the vajra-bind; the middle fingers and thumbs form a vajra, which shatters evil mudrās. Having bound the two vajra-mudrās and placed them at the heart, one should remain in meditative composure.

One should press the Krodhamuṣṭi; it destroys the outer maṇḍala. Grasping the left vajra-finger with the tip of the right [hand] bent, one who is well-enraged, clapping [the hands], could even cause Sumeru to fall.
Grasping the left vajra-finger with the tip of the right hook,
one who is well-enraged shall draw them in and bring all the planetary spirits (grahas) under control.
Having firmly formed the vajra-bind with both arms at the heart, (one should act as follows).
One should seize the two armpits with the two supreme vajras and draw the heart [of the enemy] with the kuśa [fingers].
(STT 1,418,980) With the tips of the index fingers, one whose mind is filled with wrath should press;
this is the supreme method for summoning fever by means of the base of the two thumbs. (STT 1,418,981)

Having made the vajra-añjali firm, with the two index fingers bent and the two thumbs well-joined and constrained, it removes all evil. Having bound the two foremost fingers from between the two vajra-mudrās...
One should lift [the hands] upward in an instant; this is the supreme "Raising the Fallen.
Having made the vajra-bind firm, with the middle fingers joined at their tips and the fourth and little fingers not touching, one shatters all evils in an instant.
Now follows the binding of the mudrās for the conceptualization of the mandala of all Tathāgatas:
Having first laid out the mandala by means of assuming the Vajra-mudrā, one should subsequently hold the thread; this is remembered as the proper method for laying the thread.
Having properly joined the two tips of the two vajra-fingers,
one should summon all the limbs with a blazing gaze.
Having correctly and firmly joined the two vajra-tip fingers with their palms facing upward, (one should perform the rite).
"Enraged, one should tear it open; this is the supreme method for opening the door.

(STT 1,420,987) Now follows the accomplishment of all the mudrās of the entire Vajra family: (STT 1,420,988) Having assumed the pratyālīḍha posture, one should proclaim [the mantra] with the speech of a wrathful deity. (STT 1,420,988)
"By means of a wrathful gaze, being thoroughly enraged, one shall accomplish all rites.
Thus ends the detailed procedure for the Great Maṇḍala of Trilokavijaya from the *Sarvatathāgata-vajrasamaya-mahākalparāja* (STT 1,420,988).
[Now follows] the detailed procedure for the Maṇḍala of the Secret Mudrās of the Wrathful Deities (STT 1,422,990).
Then the Blessed One again entered the samādhi called the Vajra Empowerment Arising from the Samaya of the Vajradhāraṇī, and spoke this supreme personal vidyā:
Oṃ sarvavajriṇi vajramāte ānaya sarvaṃ vajrasatyena hūṃ jjaḥ!

Then, as soon as this had been spoken, from the heart of Vajrapāṇi, that very Blessed One Vajrapāṇi—having become the deities of the Vajra-Wrath Samaya-mudrās, whose entire bodies resembled Vajrapāṇi and who were filled with flames on all sides—emerged and [accomplished] the purposes of all the Tathāgatas in all world-systems.

Having thus accomplished it, and in order to conceal their status as the secret consorts of the Blessed One Vajrasattva, they became the reflected images of the seals (*mudrā*) of the body, speech, and mind of vajra; then, through the yoga of the great maṇḍala of Trailokyavijaya of the Blessed One Vairocana, they came to rest upon a moon disc and uttered this inspired utterance (*udāna*):
"Aho! How supreme is the secret gnosis of all Buddhas, In that for the sake of the bliss of the Tathāgatas, they even assume the state of being consorts!"
Hrīḥ! (STT 1,422,994) Then Vajrapāṇi again spoke the maṇḍala of the samaya-mudrās of his own family, named the Secret Vajra Samaya:
(STT 1,423,995) Now, therefore, I shall fully explain the supreme Vajra Maṇḍala. (STT 1,423,996)
Resembling the Vajradhātu, it is known as the Secret Wrath.
(STT 1,423,996) By means of the yoga of the Great Maṇḍala, one should delineate the entire maṇḍala.
(STT 1,423,997) Within those situated in the five maṇḍalas, one should establish the secret mudrā. (STT 1,423,997)
Within this Vajra-maṇḍala, one should place the image of the Buddha;
the Buddha himself should duly draw the wrathful samayas of the Buddha.
Having emerged with vajra-impetus, [one enters] the maṇḍala of Vajrapāṇi.
Therein, in the center, one should draw a vajra established upon horizontal spikes.
Within the midst of the flames, one should duly draw them in proper sequence:
a vajra, a vajra-hook, an arrow, and likewise satisfaction (tuṣṭi).
Having entered with the force of a vajra into the second supreme mandala,
one should indeed draw the Vajraratna [symbol] established in the center of the circle. Furthermore,
one should place a vajra in the middle of Bhr̥kuṭī, a vajra in the sun, and likewise a banner.

Likewise, one should draw rows of teeth upon the sides of that [mandala] with a vajra. Having entered with the force of a vajra, one should draw a divine vajra-lotus established in the center of the third supreme mandala.
One should draw a lotus, a sword, and likewise a wheel in the midst of the flames;
and always, on its sides, one should properly draw Vajrajihvā. Then, having entered with vajra-velocity, one reaches the fourth, most excellent maṇḍala.
One should draw a triple-pronged vajra, surrounded by vajras of great radiance. On all its sides, there are those possessing a brilliance filled with all manner of flames:
Sarvavajra, Sukavaca, Vajradaṃṣṭrā, and Sumuṣṭi.
One should correctly draw the rule in the outer corners;
hereafter, I shall briefly explain the vidyās of the mudrās.
JHĪḤ.
Oṃ vajrakrodhasamaye jhiḥ!
Oṃ vajraroṣāṅkuśy ānaya sarvaṃ jhiḥ!
Oṃ vajraroṣe kāmavajriṇi vaśaṃ mām ānaya jhiḥ!
Oṃ vajratuṣṭikrodhe toṣaya sarvān jhiḥ! (In the Vajra-jhiḥkāra-maṇḍala) jiḥ!

Oṃ vajrabhṛkuṭikrodhe hara sarvārthān jiḥ! (STT 1,426,1010) Oṃ vajrajvālāmālāprabhe mahākrodhāgni jvālaya sarvaṃ raviroṣe jiḥ! (STT 1,426,1010) Oṃ vajradhvajāgrakeyūramahākrodhe dehi me sarvārthaṃ jiḥ! (STT 1,426,1011)
Oṃ vajrāṭṭahāsini hasa hasāṭṭāṭṭahāsena māraya jiḥ! (In the Vajra-jikāra-maṇḍala) diḥ!
Oṃ vajraśuddhakrodhe, strike, slay the wicked!
(Twice) Oṃ tīkṣṇakrodhe, sever all with the vajra-sheath! (Twice) Oṃ vajrahetumahākrodhe, enter the wheel, cause all to enter! (Twice)
Oṃ vajrajihve mahākrodhabhāṣe, release speech twice! (In the maṇḍala of the syllable *vajra-diḥ*!
Hniḥ!
Oṃ, O you who are at the face of all, O Vajra of Action, O Great Wrathful One, perform everything! Hniḥ!
Oṃ, O Vajra Armor Wrathful One, protect me! Hniḥ! Oṃ, O Vajra Fierce Wrathful One, O Great Yakṣiṇī, O you with terrifying fangs like those of a Vetāla, cause [them] to be terrified! Hniḥ!

Oṃ vajrakrodhamuṣṭi bandha hniḥ! (STT 1,427,1017) Oṃ vajrahniḥkāra maṇḍale! (STT 1,427,1018) Then, in the corner maṇḍalas, there are the heart-mantras of the secret worship vidyās of Vajranṛtya: (STT 1,429,1019)
Vajra hūṃ khnaṃ!
Vajra hūṃ ghuṃ!
Vajra hūṃ teṃ!
Vajra hūṃ steṃ.
(STT 1,429,1019) In the outer corners are the heart-mantras for the musical instrument offerings:
Vajra tī te. (STT 1,429,1020)
Vajra ṭaṃ ṭaḥ!
Vajra dhā dhū! Vajra dho dhaḥ!
The heart-mantras for the worship of the gatekeepers are as follows:
Vajra jaḥ jjaḥ;
Vajra hūṃ hūṃ.
Vajra vaṃ vaṃ! (STT 1,429,1021) Vajra aḥ aḥ!
(STT 1,429,10201) Now follows the detailed procedure for entry into this secret maṇḍala of the Vajra family: (STT 1,430,1022)

In that regard, first of all, having entered by means of the procedure for entering the great maṇḍala of Trilokavijaya, and having taken up the vajra, one should perform an offering of dance (*nṛtyopahāra*) for the purpose of worshipping Vajradhara with the *samaya-mudrā*, *pratimudrā*, *upamudrā*, and *jñāna-mudrā* of the Vajra family.
Herein lies the knowledge of the mudrās for the offering of dance, counter-dance, secondary dance, and wisdom-dance: *(STT 1,430,1023–1024)*

There, at the very beginning, while singing the *Vajradhātusaṃgraha-hṛdaya* with a vajra-song and making an offering of a thread to all the Tathāgatas, the Vajrācārya should cause the *sattvavajrī-mudrā* to burst open.
Then, they enter by means of the mudrās according to how they entered. Through the application of the vajra-dance, the two fingers of the vajra-anger [mudrā]—
One should bind the Vajra-hūṃkāra mudrā at the heart;
then, according to the ritual for dancing, with that wrathful hook,
while summoning all the Buddhas, one should cast forth the vajra-arrows.
By encircling with the vajra-arrow, one should accomplish [the rite] through vajra-joy;
having released the mudrā according to the ritual, one should likewise bind it with the clapping of hands.
By this method of worship, one shall satisfy Vajrapāṇi.
Being satisfied and pleased, he shall accomplish all tasks in an instant.
In this regard, these are the *nṛtyahṛdayas* (Heart-mantras of Dance):
*sidhya vajra*.
Bring it, O Vajra!
Enflame it, O Vajra!
Excellent, O Vajra!
Then, one should perform the offerings accompanied by counter-dancing.
Dancing in that very manner, one should grasp the left [hand] with the right fist,
turn it around, and place it upon the forehead with the tip of the face.
Dancing in that very manner, one should summon the Sun to revolve;
raising Vajraketu, one should laugh with the great vajra-laughter.
By this ritual of worship, [one subdues] kings and all human beings.
And through mastery, great splendor, giving, and laughter, one should satisfy [the deity].
In this regard, these are the counter-seals and heart-mantras:
*ĀHI VAJRA*.
Blaze, O Vajra!
Give, O Vajra!
Laugh, laugh, O Vajra!
In the same manner, having released the dance, with the fingers joined like closed buds, one should place the fingertips at the heart and bow with the body trembling from inner devotion.
Likewise, while dancing, one should indeed sever the leaders with the Vajra-sheath.
One should cause the circle of the wheel to revolve with the whirling of a firebrand;
indeed, singing with the vajra-voice, one should worship Vajrapāṇi.
By this method of worship, everything becomes eternal.
In the same way, these become the hearts of the *upanṛtyas*:
"O Vajra, desire!
"O Vajra, cut! (STT 1,433,1038).
"Whirl the vajra!
"Speak, O Vajra!
The fingers of the Vajra-krodha mudrā are properly joined with their palms facing upward.
Having turned it thus toward the *uṣṇīṣa*, with the index finger positioned at the mouth,
one should display the supreme maṇḍala of the entire body through the application of Vajra-activity; then, by means of the ritual of dance, one should dissolve it into the heart.
In the same manner, one should perform the Vajra-protection by means of the dance ritual.
Having formed the Vajra-fangs, one should press [them] with the Vajra-fist.
By this method of worship, one shall become capable of all rites.
Having performed the fourfold worship, one should release the mudrā according to the ritual procedure. In this regard, these are the heart-mantras: "Nṛtya Vajra! (Dance, O Vajra!)
Protect, O Vajra! (STT 1,435,1043) Consume, O Vajra! (STT 1,435,1043) Bind, O Vajra! (STT 1,435,1043)
Then, one should teach the knowledge of the Secret Mudrā of Wrath:
Taking hold of a vajra with both hands, one should snap it with a mind full of wrath;
by the name of whichever person [it is directed toward], that person’s heart shall indeed burst asunder.
Biting the lower lip with one's teeth, one should cause [the victim] to suffer by means of their name;
his head shall quickly burst asunder if he transgresses the command.
One should then close the eyes with the great gaze of the Vajra-Wrathful One.
"By merely gazing at whom [the practitioner] intends, that person's eyes shall burst open.

Through the meditative absorption (*samāpatti*) of the Vajra Wrath, one should oneself personally press upon the heart with the vajra-bind; thus, that person's consciousness shall be completely shattered."
In this regard, there are these heart-mantras:
HŪṂ VAJRASPHOṬA ṬHAḤ;
HŪṂ MUKHAVAJRA ṬHAḤ.
HŪṂ VAJRANETRA ṬHAḤ // HŪṂ MANOVAJRA ṬHAḤ // Then, one should teach the knowledge of the secret mudrās of the Great Vajra Family.

Then, first of all, there is the binding of the Mahāmudrā: by forming the hook with the little fingers, one should place the Vajra-krodhas; on the back of the left [hand], which is like a trident, Trilokavijayā is prescribed.
With the left forefinger well-extended and likewise with the upturned lotus,
and having turned it in that same manner, it is established as the left-vajra.
Having placed the vajra-bind at the palm, one with an enraged mind should cover [the face].
Firmly [pressed] with the vajra of the thumb, it is known as the *krodhaterittiri*. With the tips bent into a hook, it is the *tarjanīmukhavajriṇī*;
likewise, it is the *sādhukārā* when positioned at the tip of the vajra-face with both index fingers.
With the tips of the fingers joined at the heart, it is established at the crown of the head;
having turned [the hands], the tips of the fingers are likewise joined in a bud-like [mudrā] while remaining in a smile.
With both hands, one grasps the hilt of a sword, and the tips of the fingers are bound together like a wheel.
With the tips of the fingers joined at the mouth, the index finger is extended;
with the index fingers bound at the throat, they are positioned at the mouth like fangs.
Through the firm binding of the fist, these are designated as the Great Mudrās.

Now follows the binding of the secret samaya-mudrās of the Vajra family: The supreme samayas are proclaimed to arise from the secret fist. I shall now explain their binding, the unsurpassed Vajra-binding.
Situated in the heart, it is coiled at the side; the drawing of the arrow is from the left.
Emerging from the heart, the frown indeed turns around.
Displaying the solar disc, the arm is extended over the head.
Having turned back and remaining with a smile, she is well-situated in the center of the face;
having the form of the tip of a sheath or a cluster [of petals], she demonstrates the casting of the wheel.
Emerging from the mouth, she is the circle of the supreme body upon the head.
Likewise, one should form the vajra-protection gesture at the two shoulders, the heart, and the two sides;
and by means of the application of the fang-shape, it is firmly pressed with the tight fist.
One should bind the mudrās of the outer maṇḍala according to their respective insignia.
The pledge is by means of the vajra-bind, and likewise others by means of the vajra-fist.
(STT 1,440,1063) Now follow the secret dharma-mudrās of the Vajra family:
(STT 1,441,1064) PHAṬṬAḤ.
Śaṭṭaḥ / Maṭṭaḥ / (STT 1,441,1064)
saṭṭaḥ / raṭṭaḥ / taṭṭaḥ /
Dhṛṭṭaḥ / Haṭṭaḥ / Paṭṭaḥ.
Traṭṭaḥ / Kaṭṭaḥ / Dhaṭṭaḥ.
Kuṭṭaḥ / Riṭṭaḥ / Khaṭṭaḥ.
"Circle.
(STT 1,441,1064) Thus it is said.
Now follows the binding of the secret action-mudrā of the Vajra family: (STT 1,442,1065)
In brief, the *karmamudrā* is the vajra-fist formed in two ways. It should be placed in its respective positions with a wrathful gaze by one who is intensely enraged.
The detailed ritual procedure for the mandala of the secret wrathful *mudrās*, from the *Sarvatathāgatavajrasamayamahākalparāja*, is hereby completed.

(The Detailed Ritual for the Maṇḍala of the Vow of the Dharma-Wisdom of the Vajra Family) (STT 1,444,1067) Then the Blessed One again entered the samādhi called "The Empowerment of the Mudrās of the Wisdom of the Samādhi of the Vajra Family of All Tathāgatas," and spoke this supreme mantra of his own knowledge:
(STT 1,444,1068) Oṃ sarvatathāgatasūkṣmavajrakrodha hūṃ phaṭ! (STT 1,444,1068)
Then Vajrapāṇi, the Great Wrathful King, spoke this supreme subtle-vajra vidyā of the Conqueror of the Three Worlds:
Oṃ sūkṣmavajrakrodhākrama hūṃ phaṭ!
Then the Bodhisattva Vajragarbha spoke this supreme subtle-vajra vidyā of the Conqueror of the Three Worlds: [Oṃ sūkṣmavajrakrodhākrama hūṃ phaṭ!]
Oṃ sūkṣmavajrakrodhākrama hūṃ phaṭ!
Then the Bodhisattva Vajranetra spoke this supreme vidyā-mantra of the Subtle Vajra for Conquering the Three Worlds:
Oṃ sūkṣmavajrapadmakrodhākrama hūṃ phaṭ!
Then the Bodhisattva Vajraviśva spoke this supreme subtle-vajra vidyā for the Victory over the Three Worlds:
OṂ SŪKṢMAVAJRRAKARMARODHĀKRAMA HŪṂ PHAṬ.
Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, having again generated his own family and established it through the yoga of the great maṇḍala of the Vajradhātu, spoke these heart-mantras:
Oṃ vajrasattvasūkṣmajñānakrodha hūṃ phaṭ!
Oṃ sūkṣmavajrāṅkuśākarṣaya mahākrodha hūṃ phaṭ!
Oṃ vajrasūkṣmarāgakrodhānurāgaya tīvraṃ hūṃ phaṭ!
Oṃ sūkṣmavajratuṣṭikrodha hūṃ phaṭ! (STT 1,445,1075) Oṃ sūkṣmavajrabhṛkuṭikrodha hara hara hūṃ phaṭ! (STT 1,445,1076) Oṃ vajrasūkṣmajvālāmaṇḍalakrodhasūrya jvālaya hūṃ phaṭ! (STT 1,446,1076)
Oṃ, O Subtle Vajra Banner-tip Wrathful One, bestow upon me all goals quickly! Hūṃ Phaṭ! Oṃ, O Vajra Subtle Wrathful One, ha ha ha ha hūṃ phaṭ!
Oṃ, O Subtle Vajra Dharma Wrathful One, purify! Hūṃ Phaṭ!

Oṃ, subtle vajra-cutting wrathful one, cut! Pierce! Hūṃ phaṭ! (STT 1,446,1078) Oṃ, subtle vajra-wrath great wheel, cut! Strike down! Having entered the head, pierce the heart! Hūṃ phaṭ! (STT 1,446,1079) Oṃ, subtle vajra-hūṃkāra wrathful one, slay! Strike down with a mere word! Hūṃ phaṭ! (STT 1,446,1079)

Oṃ, subtle Vajra-karma-krodha, become the performer of all actions; accomplish all tasks! Hūṃ phaṭ! Oṃ, Vajra-sūkṣma-kavaca-krodha, protect, protect! Hūṃ phaṭ! Oṃ, subtle Vajra-yakṣa-krodha, slay and devour all the wicked by mere thought, O Vajra-tusked one! Hūṃ phaṭ!
Oṃ, subtle-vajra-fist-anger, bind, bind! Hūṃ phaṭ! (STT 1,447,1081) Then Vajrapāṇi again proclaimed this *vajrakula-sūkṣmajñāna-samayamaṇḍala*:
(STT 1,448,1082) Now, therefore, I shall fully explain the supreme Dharma-maṇḍala. (STT 1,448,1083)
That which resembles the Vajradhātu is known as the Wisdom of Wrath (krodhajñāna).
By means of the yoga of the Great Maṇḍala, one should delineate the entire maṇḍala;
in its center, one should depict the Buddha situated within the Wisdom-Vajra.
One should draw those very same mudrās on all sides of the Buddha.
Having emerged from the four mandalas with vajra-velocity,
one should duly install Trilokavijaya and the others.
From all sides of them, however, one should [emanate] the Vajra-krodhas according to the ritual procedure.
Now, herein, the detailed ritual procedure for the subtle wisdom maṇḍala of the Vajra family occurs as follows: first of all, having caused [the disciples] to enter, one should say:
"Today you are consecrated by the Blessed One Vajrapāṇi into the state of the Vajra-wrath of all the Tathāgatas.

Therefore, act well for the sake of protecting the entire realm of sentient beings without exception, and for the purpose of attaining the fruit of the supreme accomplishment of the welfare and happiness of all the Tathāgatas. As the Vajra-wrath, you must purify even all sentient beings; what need is there to mention all the wicked?
Having said this, he should release the binding of the face.
Then, having shown the entire maṇḍala and having placed the vajra— or that vajra— properly into the hand,
one should then teach the subtle gnoses of the Vajrakrodha.
Having made the subtle vajra firm through the yoga of the Vajra-hūṃkāra.
To whomsoever one applies the syllable *huṃ*, that person’s life perishes.
Having made the subtle vajra firm, one should cause it to radiate according to the ritual rule;
for as far as it radiates, so far does that enemy perish.
Applying the subtle vajra procedure through the yoga of Vajra-hūṃkāra,
the wrathful one should radiate [emanations] until all [obstacles] are destroyed.
In the same way, the practitioner of yoga may withdraw them as long as he desires.
"For one may indeed give back everything without remainder, even life itself.
(STT 1,450,1093) In this regard, their heart-mantras are as follows:
HŪṂ! Destroy, O Vajra!
HŪṂ! Annihilate all, O Vajra!
OṂ! Subtle Vajra, bring [them] back quickly, HŪṂ!
If a sentient being possesses a very firm enmity that has existed since beginningless time,

one should destroy that enmity by means of pervading it with loving-kindness through the yoga of the pervasion of loving-kindness. Through the yoga of the pervasion of the Vajra, one [should destroy] the enmity of anyone whatsoever by means of compassion.
Through that application of compassion, he shall destroy all malevolent beings.
Whether they be non-dharmas or dharmas, they are luminous by nature;
meditating thus upon sentient beings, one should destroy them with the syllable HŪṂ.
For those beings who are stubborn and unruly, and who are unfit vessels for the awakening of a Buddha—
one should destroy them with the syllable *HŪṂ* for the sake of purifying them.
In this regard, their heart-mantras are as follows:
Vairavajra-krodha hūṃ phaṭ! Karuṇāvajra-krodha hūṃ phaṭ! Hūṃ Viśuddhakrodhavajra hūṃ phaṭ!
HŪṂ! O Vajra-wrath of purification, HŪṂ PHAṬ!
(STT 1,451,1099) Having mentally drawn the Vajra-image of anyone at all, if one causes it to fall into the middle of that person’s house, their entire family shall perish. (STT 1,453,1100)
In that very same way, one should contemplate the heart-vajra through subtle procedures;
[otherwise], by causing the great image of the Bodhisattva to fall, one will destroy one's family.
Wherever one causes the great image of Vajrapāṇi to fall while practicing its accomplishment, [therein lies the consequence].
That kingdom, along with the king himself, perishes through various calamities.
However, one should meditate upon the image of the Buddha, endowed with the excellence of all forms;
in whichever kingdom one causes that [image] to fall, that kingdom will certainly perish.
In this regard, there are these heart-mantras:
HŪṂ VAJRAPRAPĀTA;
HŪṂ BODHISATTVAPRAPĀTA.
HŪṂ, the descent of Vajradhara!
HŪṂ, the descent of the Buddha!
By means of the application of the subtle vajra, one should [visualize] the lunar disk as oneself.
Visualizing himself as his own self, wherever he may fall, there he shall indeed fall.
(STT 1,454,1105) Visualizing himself as a vajra within the moon by means of his own self, wherever he falls while intensely enraged, that family perishes in an instant. (STT 1,454,1106)
Meditating upon oneself as Vajrapāṇi by means of one’s own self,
wherever one falls, that place will soon be utterly destroyed.
Meditating upon oneself as the form of a Buddha by means of one’s own self...
"Wherever that kingdom falls [into such a state], it will perish in no time at all.
In this regard, there are these heart-mantras:
*bodhyagra prapātaya hūṃ*.
Sattvavajra, cause to fall! Hūṃ! Vajrasattva, cause to fall! Hūṃ!
Buddha, cause to fall! Hūṃ!
Then, one should teach the knowledge of the secret mudrā of the Dharma of the Vajra Family:
"Through the meditative absorption of Vajrakrodha, one should envelop one's own body;
by means of the Vajra-hūṃkāra, while enveloping it, [one should act] with the name of whomever is to die."
Having entered into the subtle vajra through the subtle nose once,
by means of the yoga of the breath and the syllable *huṃ*, one may even cause the three worlds to fall.
Applying the procedure of the subtle vajra while being wrathful, one should do so with the vajra-gaze.
If one gazes [at her], one goes blind or meets with death.
But whoever has entered her vulva with the mind,
by drawing out her heart, she comes under his control— whether she is his own or belongs to another.
In this regard, their heart-mantras are as follows:
HŪṂ VAJRAVALITAKRODHA MĀRAYA HŪṂ PHAṬ! OṂ VAJRASŪKṢMAVAJRAŚVĀSA VIṢAṂ PĀTAYA HŪṂ PHAṬ!
Oṃ vajradṛṣṭi viṣaṃ nāśaya hūṃ phaṭ!
Hūṃ, O Wrathful One who draws forth the heart, enter the body, cut the heart, pierce it, drag it out, drag it out, phaṭ!
Then, one should teach the knowledge of the Dharma-mudrā of the Vajra family.
In that regard, first, there is the binding of the Mahāmudrā:
"By means of the application of Vajra-jñāna, visualizing oneself as the Vajra-krodhas, whose radiance is filled with garlands of flames, one attains accomplishment in an instant."
Then, one should teach the knowledge of the Dharma-samaya-mudrā of the Vajra family:

it should be established in its proper places as the supreme bestower of all accomplishments."
Then, one should teach the knowledge of the Dharma-mudrā of the Vajra-family Dharma-samaya:
*phaṭ śaṭ maṭ saṭ raṭ raṭ dhṛt haṭ paṭ traṭ kaṭ bhaṭ kṛṭ riṭ khaṭ vaṭ ca iti*. These are the Dharma-mudrās in brief.
Then one should teach the knowledge of the action seals (*karmamudrā*) of the Dharma-samaya of the Vajra family:
"Having formed the 'Dharma-fist' in two ways according to their proper placement,
the action seals attain accomplishment in brief, according to the prescribed ritual."
The detailed ritual procedure for the Maṇḍala of the Vow of the Dharma-Wisdom of the Vajra Family from the *Sarvatathāgatavajrasamayamahākalparāja* is completed.
(STT 1,461,1120) [The Detailed Ritual Procedure for the Karma-Maṇḍala of the Vajra Family] (STT 1,462,1121).

Then the Blessed One entered the meditative absorption named "The Empowerment Arising from the Vow of the Vajra-Activity of All Tathāgatas" and spoke this supreme personal vidyā-mantra: (STT 1,462,1122)
Oṃ, O Sovereign of the Activity of all Tathāgatas, Hūṃ!

(STT 1,462,1122) Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi again spoke this supreme rite of his own: (STT 1,462,1123) Oṃ, at the time of the extensive ritual procedure for the great act of worship that pervades the Dharma-realm of all Tathāgatas, O Conqueror of the Three Worlds, subdue all the wicked, O Wielder of the Vajra, Hūṃ! (STT 1,462,1123)
Then the Bodhisattva Vajragarbha again spoke this supreme mantra of his own knowledge:
Oṃ sarvatathāgatākāśadhātusamavasaraṇamahāpūjākarmavidhivistarasamaye hūṃ.
Then the Bodhisattva Vajranetra again spoke this supreme mantra of his own knowledge:
Oṃ, at the time of the extensive ritual procedure for the great worship that pervades the dharma-realm of all Tathāgatas, hūṃ!
(STT 1,462,1125) Then the Bodhisattva Vajraviśva again spoke this supreme mantra of his own knowledge:
Oṃ, at the time of the extensive ritual procedure for the various great acts of worship in all the world-systems of all Tathāgatas, hūṃ! (STT 1,462,1126)

Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, once again generating from his own heart the deities of the extensive ritual for worship of his own family, performed all the miraculous transformations of the supernatural powers of all the Tathāgatas— such as summoning all the Tathāgatas in all world-systems, subjugating them, causing them to feel affection, and enjoining them to perform the activities that accomplish all rites— and then once more, by means of the yoga of the great maṇḍala of the Vajra Realm, he remained stationed upon moon-maṇḍalas before the Blessed One Vairocana.
Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi spoke this extensive ritual procedure for the *karmamaṇḍala* of the Vajra-Action Samaya:
"Now, therefore, I shall fully explain the supreme *karmamaṇḍala*,
which resembles the Vajradhātu and is known as the Karmavajra."
One should delineate the entire maṇḍala by means of the yoga of the great maṇḍala.
One should place the image of the Buddha within the central maṇḍala.
On all sides of the Buddha, one should place the foremost of the samayas.
Having ascended by means of the Vajra-impulses (vajravega) into the fourfold mandalas,
one should duly install the four Vajra-lords and so forth;
and on all their sides, one should install the Great Beings (mahāsattva).
Now, in this ritual mandala, there are the Vajra Action Mudrās:
Oṃ vajrasattvasiddhijñānasamaye hūṃ jjaḥ.
Oṃ vajrākarṣaṇakarmajñānasamaye hūṃ jjaḥ.
Oṃ vajrarati rāgakarmajñānasamaye hūṃ jjaḥ! (STT 1,465,1134) Oṃ vajrasādhukarmajñānasamaye hūṃ jjaḥ! (STT 1,465,1134) Oṃ vajrabhṛkuṭi vaśīkuru hūṃ! (STT 1,465,1135)
Oṃ vajrasūryamaṇḍale vaśīkuru hūṃ! Oṃ vajradhvajāgrakeyūre vaśīkuru hūṃ! Oṃ vajrāṭṭahāse vaśīkuru hūṃ!
Oṃ vajrapadmarāge rāgaya hūṃ! (STT 1,465,1136) Oṃ vajratīkṣṇarāge rāgaya hūṃ! (STT 1,465,1136) Oṃ vajramaṇḍalarāge rāgaya hūṃ! (STT 1,465,1136)
Oṃ vajravāgrāge rāgaya hūṃ! (STT 1,465,1136) Oṃ vajrakarmasamaye pūjaya hūṃ! (STT 1,465,1137) Oṃ vajrakavacabandhe rakṣaya hūṃ! (STT 1,465,1137)
Oṃ vajrayakṣiṇi māraya vajradaṃṣṭrayā bhinda hṛdayam amukasya huṃ phaṭ!

(STT 1,465,1137) Oṃ vajrakarmamuṣṭi sidhya sidhya huṃ phaṭ! (STT 1,465,1137) Then, having performed the detailed ritual procedure here in this karma-maṇḍala according to the rules, one should generate the action-wisdoms of the Vajra family. (STT 1,466,1138)
In that regard, from the very beginning, one should teach the knowledge of rites for pacification (*śāntika*) and so forth:
having kindled the fire with sweet-smelling sacrificial wood (*samidh*), being well-composed,
and through the meditative absorption (*samāpatti*) of Vajrakrodha, one should burn away misdeeds by offering sesame seeds as oblations.
Having kindled the sacrificial fire with those very same fuel-sticks,
by constantly offering oblations of rice grains, one will certainly attain the prosperity of the household.
Having likewise kindled the fire with sweet-smelling fuel-sticks, the wise man [should proceed].
By offering sprouts of *dūrvā* grass with clarified butter, one’s lifespan increases.
Having kindled the sacrificial fire with those very same fuel-sticks,
by offering sprouts of *kuśa* grass with oil, there is eternal protection.
Now, their heart-mantras are as follows:
(STT 1,466,1144) Oṃ sarvapāpadahanavajrāya svāhā. (STT 1,467,1144) Oṃ vajrapuṣṭaye svāhā. (STT 1,467,1144)
Oṃ vajrāyuṣe svāhā!
Oṃ apratihatavajrāya svāhā!
First, with pungent sacrificial fuel sticks (samidh), one should perform [the rite] through the Vajrakrodha-samādhi.
Having kindled the fire with *kuñja* thorns, he proceeds, though afflicted by them; yet,
having kindled the fire with those very same sticks as fuel, the one possessed of great wrath,
offering red flowers or fruits, brings the world under his passion.
Enraged by those very fuel-sticks, the practitioner of yoga, having kindled the fire,
shall become bound as firm as a thunderbolt by offering iron filings into it.
Having kindled the fire with those same fuel-sticks, he should remain composed.
One should offer bitter fruit; through anger, one shall produce pestilence in an instant.
In this regard, their heart-mantras are as follows:
HŪṂ VAJRĀKARṢAYA SVĀHĀ.
Hūṃ vajrarāgaya svāhā! Hūṃ vajrabandhāya svāhā! Hūṃ vajramāraṇāya svāhā!

Having kindled the fire with sour fuel-wood, the wise one, being wrathful, performs a burnt offering with sour fruits and flowers; this is the supreme rite of subjugation. Having likewise kindled the fire with those same fuel-woods, he should remain composed.
If one who is angry performs oblations with fruits that grant desires, he shall attain the power to assume any form at will.
Having kindled the sacrificial fire with such very same fuel-sticks (*samidh*),
one who offers oblations of the stalks of invisible flowers will, by virtue of that splendor, become invisible.

Having kindled the fire with those very fuel-sticks, one who is composed, offering flowers from the sky-vine (*ākāśavallī*), shall become a traveler through the sky. In this regard, their heart-mantras (*hṛdaya*) are as follows:
Oṃ vajravaśaṃkarāya svāhā! (STT 1,472,1154) Oṃ kāmarūpavajrāya svāhā! (STT 1,472,1154) Oṃ adṛśyavajrāya svāhā! (STT 1,472,1154)

Oṃ vajrakhacarine svāhā! (STT 1,472,1154) Having kindled the fire with fuel-sticks of bitter potency, one who is composed should, while enraged, offer vajra-flowers; thus the Vajra shall become an executor of commands. (STT 1,473,1155)
Having kindled the fire with those very fuel-sticks, the one full of great wrath— O Śauri, he for whom one offers a garland shall even become a servant at his command.
With those fuel-sticks, being highly incensed and composed, one should kindle the fire.
One should offer a garland to Vajrapāṇi; he too will quickly attain the state of being an obedient servant.
Having kindled the fire with those very same fuel-sticks, one who is intensely wrathful should offer robes to the Buddha; in an instant, [the Buddha] goes to the state of being an obedient servant.
In this regard, their heart-mantras are as follows: HŪṂ VAJRAVAŚAṂKARĀYA SVĀHĀ HŪṂ ŚAURIVAŚAṂKARAVAJRĀYA SVĀHĀ
HŪṂ VAJRAPĀṆIVAŚAṂKARĀYA SVĀHĀ.
HŪṂ BUDDHAVAŚAṂKARAVAJRĀYA SVĀHĀ.
Then, one should teach the knowledge of the secret action-mudrā.
While dwelling together with his beloved woman, he should place collyrium in her vulva and rub it there; by means of that, he should apply the collyrium to his eye and bring her under his control.
Having pierced realgar into her vulva, he should seal it with the vajra-bandha.
Through four kinds of signs, there are likewise four kinds of accomplishment:
Having placed the *rocanā* within the vulva, one should press it with the secret fist.
Once placed there, it blazes forth; one becomes equal to the Holder of the Vajra.
Having pierced the vulva with saffron and that vulva with a true vajra, it blazes when covered; indeed, it becomes like the Holder of the Vajra.
In this regard, their heart-mantras are as follows:
Oṃ vajraguhyarati vaśaṃkara sidhya huṃ!
Oṃ vajraguhya sidhya huṃ!
Oṃ guhyavajra sidhya huṃ!
Oṃ vajradharaguhya sidhya hūṃ.
Then, one should teach the knowledge of the great mudrā of the activity of the Vajra family:
"In brief, the great mudrās are [accomplished] through the application of vajra-activities."
Through the meditative absorption of Vajrakrodha and by means of the application of the Vajramuṣṭi mudrā,
the Supreme Samaya [mudrās] are likewise formed here through the union of the syllable *huṃ* with the fingers.
Likewise, the Dharma-mudrās are formed here by means of the syllables beginning with *oṃ*.
In brief, the *karmamudrās* are formed by making two *karmamuṣṭis*.
They are pure and bring about all accomplishments through the application of *vajrakarma*.
The detailed procedure for the *karmamaṇḍala* of the *Vajrakula*, from the *Sarvatathāgatavajrasamayamahākalparāja*, is completed.

(STT 1,480,1169) Then the Blessed One again entered the samādhi called "The Empowerment of the Vajra-Samaya-Mudrā of All Tathāgatas" and spoke this supreme personal vidyā:

HŪṂ BHR̥KUTI-VAJRI RAṬ!
(STT 1,480,1172) Then the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajranetra spoke this self-dharma-samaya-mudrā:

Then the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajraviśva spoke this *svakarmasamayamudrā*: *Hūṃ vajrakarmāgri kṛṭ!* Then the great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi again spoke this *trilokavijaya-caturmudrā-maṇḍala*.
Now, therefore, I shall fully explain the supreme maṇḍala of mudrās,
which resembles the Vajradhātu and is known as Krodhavajra.
One should delineate the entire maṇḍala by means of the yoga of the Great Maṇḍala.

Then, having performed the detailed ritual for summoning and so forth by means of the yoga of the great maṇḍala within this four-seal maṇḍala, and having caused [the disciples] to enter, one should instruct them in the secret seal knowledge of the four-seal maṇḍala (STT 1,481,1178; STT 1,482,11782).
Having personally drawn the maṇḍala of the four mudrās, which is the pure nature of phenomena (śuddhadharmatā),
one attains accomplishment while dwelling together with a woman while reciting [the mantra].
Having personally drawn the maṇḍala of the four mudrās, which is the pure nature of phenomena...
By reciting [the mantra] while gazing with passion, accomplishment is attained.
(STT 1,482,1180) Having personally drawn the maṇḍala of the four mudrās, which is the pure nature of phenomena, one succeeds by setting it in motion and kissing a beloved woman. (STT 1,482,1181)

Having personally drawn the maṇḍala of the four mudrās, which is the pure reality (*śuddhadharmatā*), one should embrace [the consort] while reciting [the mantra]; thus all accomplishments (*sarvasiddhi*) are attained.
In this regard, these are the mudrās of pure reality: *(STT 1,482,1182–1183)*
Oṃ, the pure nature of all Tathāgatas, hoḥ!
Oṃ, vajra-pure vision, jjaḥ!
Oṃ, face of intrinsic purity, hūṃ!
Oṃ sarvaviśuddhakāyavāṅmanaḥkarmavajri phaṭ!
Then, one should train in the secret and most secret mudrās of the four-mudrā maṇḍala:
having entered this maṇḍala with the five excellent objects of desire.
Delighting in the wives of others, he attains supreme accomplishment.
Then his heart becomes:
"O Vajrakāma!"

Then, having duly taught the four samaya-mudrās, beginning with the Vajrakrānti and Triśūla, along with their detailed rituals, one should offer vajra-instruments, musical instruments, and cymbals by means of this application of the four mudrās. Singing the heart-verse of the *Vajrasattvasaṃgraha*, one should perform the worship of dance-offerings (*nṛtyopahāra*) with the mudrās, counter-mudrās (*pratimudrā*), near-mudrās (*upamudrā*), and knowledge-mudrās (*jñānamudrā*). In this regard, the worship of dance-offerings is as follows:
By means of the application of the Vajra-dance, the two fingers of the Vajra-wrath [mudrā]...
One should bind the Vajra-hūṃkāra mudrā at the heart;
likewise, while dancing, one should grasp the left [hand] with the right fist, turn it over,
and place it upon the forehead with the tips of the fingers facing forward.
In the same way, having released the dance, with the fingers joined like closed buds,
one should place the fingertips at the heart and bow with the body trembling from devotion.
The fingers of the Vajra-Krodha [mudrā] are properly joined with their faces turned upward.
Having turned it upward in that same way, [it is] positioned with the tip of the index finger.
(STT 1,485,1190) Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi again spoke this own Vajra-Samaya-Krodha:
Now follows its mandala:
(STT 1,486,1192) Now, therefore, I shall fully explain the supreme secret mandala, which resembles the Vajradhātu and is known as Vajra-hūṃkāra. (STT 1,486,1192)
One should draw the outer maṇḍala by means of the yoga of the great maṇḍala. In its center, one should correctly draw the Vajrin upon a moon-maṇḍala,
holding in his hands the great mudrās of the vajra and the *vajra-huṃkāra*.
"Having the excellent posture of *pratyālīḍha*, with color and form as they truly are.

(STT 1,486,1194) Then, having performed the detailed procedure for all accomplishments (*siddhi*) here in the secret maṇḍala, one should proclaim the knowledge of the secret mudrā of Vajrahuṃkāra: (STT 1,487,1195–1196)

Having entered this mandala, one should accomplish the *trilokavijayāṅgulī* by piercing the *bhaga*; thus one succeeds in all rites. Now follows its heart-mantra for accomplishment: [Mantra: OṂ TRILOKAVIJAYĀ ĀVEŚAYA HŪṂ PHAṬ SVĀHĀ.
HŪṂ VAJRASAMAYA KṚTAḤ!
Then, one should teach the knowledge of the secret *sādhana* mudrā of Vajrahuṃkāra:
"Having properly entered the maṇḍala, one should remain established in the supreme Great Mudrā."
"By dwelling together [with her], one becomes Vajrahuṃkāra, the performer of all rites.
In this regard, the heart-mantra for her practice is as follows:
*Hūṃ vajrasamaya hūṃ*.
Then, one should teach the fourfold binding of the mudrās according to the proper method; for in that very way, the accomplishments (siddhis) arise.
Just as it is with the mandala, so too is the accomplishment common to all images drawn on cloth and other media.
Then Vajrapāṇi, having summoned all the Tathāgatas, spoke thus:
"O Blessed Ones, all Tathāgatas, please consecrate this family of mine, so that all sentient beings may attain all siddhis by acting according to their desires.
Then all the Tathāgatas of the Blessed One, having gathered together once more, spoke these words for the sake of consecrating this *Trilokavijaya-kalpa*:
Excellent for you, O Vajrasattva; excellent for you, O Vajrarati!
Excellent for you, O Vajradharma; excellent for you, O Vajrakarman!
This well-spoken sūtra is the unsurpassed Vajrayāna.
The Secret of All Tathāgatas, the Compendium of the Mahāyāna.
(STT 1,490,1204) The Great Ritual Manual of the Vajra-Samayas of All Tathāgatas, the Great King of Kalpas; the detailed exposition of the Great Vajra-Kalpa is completed.
(STT 1,490,1205) The Detailed Exposition of the Ritual for the Great Maṇḍala of the Wheel of the Three Worlds. (STT 1,491,1206)
Then all the Blessed Tathāgatas, having again assembled, knowing full well, spoke thus to the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi:
"O child, comply with the command of all the Tathāgatas by releasing this body of Maheśvara from the sole of your own foot.
Then the Blessed Vajrapāṇi spoke thus to those Tathāgatas:
“I have been consecrated by the Blessed Ones as Wrath, the subduer of all evil ones; therefore, this one has been slain by me. How then shall I release him?

Then, for the sake of restoring life to the body of Maheśvara, the sovereign of the entire triple world, the heart-mantra for summoning back the consciousness of the deceased issued forth from the hearts of all the Tathāgatas.
Oṃ vajrasattva hūṃ jjaḥ. Now follows the binding of its mudrā:
Having firmly formed the secret hook (guhyāṅkuśī), with the little fingers fully extended and joined together.
By placing it upon the head of the deceased, one shall attain the restoration of life through bliss.

(STT 1,492,1210) As soon as this was accomplished, the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Bhasmeśvaranirghoṣa, came from the world-system Bhasmacchanna, entered the body of Maheśvara, and uttered this inspired utterance:
(STT 1,492,1211) "Aho! Indeed, the supreme Buddha-knowledge of all Buddhas! (STT 1,492,1212)
"For even this body, though dead, has attained the state of being devoid of life.
Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi uttered this heart-mantra called "Lifting the Foot":
Oṃ vajra muḥ.
Now follows the binding of its mudrā:
"The Vajra-krodha finger-samaya, joyful and unimpeded at the mouth;
having turned those two vajras, one should raise them upward from below."

Forming the *samaya* gesture with the fingers of the Vajra-Wrath deity, and binding the faces together in meditative absorption, while whirling the vajra in joy (or moving it in the hand), one should raise the Vajra-Downward-Directing [mudrā] (or raise the earth from beneath the head). As soon as this was spoken, Mahādeva was released from the presence of the Great Vajradhara and recognized it for himself. Then, this body of Maheśvara was empowered by that Tathāgata through the act of reviving him.

While he was still in the state of crown prince (*yuvarāja*), right here in this world-system, he established [himself] for the sake of all sentient beings and for the sake of subduing all the wicked.
(STT 1,504,1216) Then, from the palm of Vajrapāṇi’s foot, there issued forth this mudrā of the bodhicitta of all Tathāgatas, named Candrapadā:
(STT 1,505,1217) Oṃ candrottare samantabhadrakiraṇe mahāvajriṇi hūṃ! (STT 1,505,1217)
Now follows the binding of its mudrā:
having made the *vajrabandha* firm, with the little fingers and thumbs joined together and extended, it is known by the name *candrapāda*.

Then, as soon as she had emerged from that very foot-drum, the Tathāgata Candrottara himself emerged; with his feet treading upon the head of Maheśvara and the hand of Vajrapāṇi, and being mounted upon the crescent moon, he stood on the left side.

Then, all the Tathāgatas, having bound the Vajra-knowledge in the hands [or: having given the vajra-spear] of Vajrapāṇi as a friend, consecrated him with the vajra-name-consecration: "Vajravidyottama, Vajravidyottama!"
Then the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajravidyottama, performing a dance-offering with that vajra-spear by whirling it like a circle of fire, uttered this inspired utterance:
"Oh, how supreme is the bodhicitta of all the Buddhas!
For by merely touching the tips of their feet, I have attained Buddhahood!"
Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, having emerged from that Vajra-Wrath Samādhi, addressed the Blessed One as follows:
"Blessed One, all the Tathāgatas have placed a vajra in my hands and consecrated me as Vajrapāṇi.

Therefore, I shall assign the positions for these external vajra families of gods and others within this Great Maṇḍala of Victory over the Three Worlds, so that those beings will become irreversible from unexcelled, perfect enlightenment."
Then the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Vairocana, the Arhat, the Samyaksambuddha, uttered this Tathāgata-Uṣṇīṣa:

OṂ VAJRASATTVOṢṆĪṢA HŪṂ PHAṬ! As soon as this was spoken, from all the uṣṇīṣas of the Tathāgatas, that very Blessed One Vajrapāṇi became multicolored rays of light. Having illuminated all the world-systems, they returned and settled within the crown of the Blessed One Vajrapāṇi through the union with the uṣṇīṣas of all the Tathāgatas.
Then, from that mass of splendor, this Sarvatathāgatoṣṇīṣa issued forth:
Oṃ namaḥ sarvatathāgatoṣṇīṣatejorāśe anavalokitamūrdhe hūṃ dhaka vidhaka dara vidara hūṃ phaṭ!
Then the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi uttered this supreme mantra of his own knowledge:
Oṃ niśumbha vajra hūṃ phaṭ!
Then again, Vajrapāṇi uttered this heart-mantra from his own heart:
Oṃ ṭakki jjaḥ!
Then the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajragarbha spoke this supreme vidyā of his own:
Oṃ vajraratnottama jvālya hūṃ phaṭ!
Then the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajranetra spoke this supreme vidyā of his own:
Oṃ, purify all with the naturally pure vajra-lotus, O supreme vidyā, hūṃ phaṭ! (STT 1,516,1231) Then the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajravośva spoke this supreme vidyā of his own:

(STT 1,516,1232) Oṃ, supreme vajra-action, vajra-holder, remember the samaya! Subdue, utterly subdue, attract, cause to enter, cause to possess, bind, cause to accept the samaya! Perform all actions for me, O Mahāsattva, hūṃ phaṭ! (STT 1,516,1232)
Then the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajravidyottama offered this, his own heart-mantra, as a salutation at the feet of the Blessed One Vajrapāṇi:
OṂ ŚUMBHA NIŚUMBHA VAJRIVIDYOTTAMA HŪṂ PHAṬ!
Then the Wrathful Vajra, the King of Knowledge (Vidyārāja), prostrated at the feet of the Blessed One and gave this, his own heart-mantra:
HŪṂ VAJRAŚŪLA!
Then the Vidyārāja Māyāvajra spoke this own heart-mantra:
OṂ VAJRAMĀYA VIDARŚAYA SARVAṂ HŪṂ PHAṬ!
Then the Vidyārāja Vajraghaṇṭa gave his own heart-mantra:
OṂ VAJRAGAṆṬA RAṆA RAṆA HŪṂ PHAṬ.
Then Maunavajra gave his own heart-mantra: OṂ MAUNAVAJRA SVĀHĀ.
Oṃ vajramauna mahāvrata hūṃ phaṭ! (STT 1,518,1237) Then Vajrāyudha gave his own heart-mantra: (STT 1,518,1238) Oṃ vajrāyudha dāmaka hūṃ phaṭ! (STT 1,518,1238)
The Vidyārājas.
Then the Vajra-wrath Vajrakuṇḍali offered this, his own heart-mantra, which is to be honored by prostration at the feet, to the Blessed One Vajrapāṇi:
Oṃ vajrakuṇḍali mahāvajrakrodha! Seize! Burn! Cook! Destroy! Split the head with the vajra! Break the heart! Vajrakrodha! Hūṃ phaṭ!
Then Vajraprabha, the Vajra Wrathful One, gave this heart-mantra:
OṂ VAJRAPRABHA MĀRAYA SAUMYAKRODHA HŪṂ PHAṬ.
Then Vajradaṇḍa, the Vajra Wrathful One, gave his own heart-mantra: (STT 1,519,1242)

Oṃ vajradaṇḍa tāḍaya sarvaduṣṭān mahākrodha hūṃ phaṭ! (STT 1,519,1242) Then the Vajra-krodha Vajrapiṅgala gave this heart-mantra: (STT 1,519,1243) Oṃ vajrapiṅgala bhīṣaya sarvaduṣṭān bhīmakrodha hūṃ phaṭ! (STT 1,519,1243)
The Vajra Wrathful Ones.
(STT 1,520,1243) Then Vajraśauṇḍa Gaṇapati offered this heart-mantra to the Blessed One Vajrapāṇi:
(STT 1,520,1244) Oṃ vajraśauṇḍa mahāgaṇapati! Protect [me] from all evil ones; uphold the command of the Vajra-holder! Hūṃ phaṭ! (STT 1,520,1244)
Then Vajramāla gave this heart-mantra:
Oṃ vajramālagaṇapate, by means of the garland, attract, cause to enter, cause to possess, bind, subjugate, slay! Hūṃ phaṭ! Then Vajravaśī gave his own heart-mantra: [Oṃ vajravaśī hūṃ phaṭ].

Oṃ vajravaśī mahāgaṇapate vaśīkuru hūṃ phaṭ! (STT 1,520,1246) Then Vijayavajra, the lord of the Gaṇas, gave his own heart-mantra: (STT 1,520,1247) Oṃ vajravijaya vijayaṃ kuru mahāgaṇapati hūṃ phaṭ! (STT 1,520,1247)
The Gaṇapatis. (STT 1,520,1247) Then Vajramusala, the Vajra-messenger, offered this heart-mantra to Vajrapāṇi:
(STT 1,521,1248) Oṃ vajramusala, crush, crush all the wicked ones! Vajradūta hūṃ phaṭ! (STT 1,521,1248)
Then the messenger Vajrānila gave his own heart-mantra:
OṂ VAJRĀNILA MAHĀVEGA ĀNAYA SARVADUṢṬĀN HŪṂ PHAṬ.
Then the messenger Vajrānala gave his own heart-mantra: [OṂ VAJRĀNALA MAHĀTEJA ĀNAYA SARVADUṢṬĀN HŪṂ PHAṬ].
Oṃ, O great messenger Vajrānala, set everything ablaze! Reduce all malevolent beings to ashes! Hūṃ Phaṭ! (STT 1,522,1250) Then the messenger Vajrabhairava gave his own heart-mantra:
(STT 1,522,1251) Oṃ, O Vajra-messenger Vajrabhairava, devour all malevolent beings, O Great Yakṣa! Hūṃ Phaṭ! (STT 1,522,1251)
The Messengers.
(STT 1,522,1251) Then Vajrāṅkuśa, the Vajra-servant, offered this heart-mantra to the Blessed One Vajrapāṇi:
(STT 1,523,1252) Oṃ vajrāṅkuśākarṣaya sarvaṃ mahāceṭa hūṃ phaṭ! (STT 1,523,1252)
Then Vajrakāla gave his own heart-mantra:
Oṃ vajrakāla mahāmṛtyum utpādaya hūṃ phaṭ. Then Vajravināyaka gave his own heart-mantra: [Oṃ vajravināyaka mahāgaṇapati sarvavighnān nāśaya hūṃ phaṭ].
Oṃ, O Vajra-Vināyaka, create an obstacle! Huṃ Phaṭ! (STT 1,523,1254) Then Nāgavajra offered this, his own heart-mantra, as a salutation at the feet of the Blessed One Vajrapāṇi:

(STT 1,523,1255) Oṃ, O Nāgavajra, bring forth all wealth, grain, silver, gold, jewels, pearls, ornaments, and all such requisites! O Vajradhara, remember the pledge! Summon! Seize! Bind! Take away, take away their lives! O Great Servant, Huṃ Phaṭ! (STT 1,523,1256)
The Servants.
(STT 1,523,1256) Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi proclaimed this samaya for summoning all the vajra families:
(STT 1,524,1257) Oṃ vajrāṅkuśākarṣaya hūṃ! (STT 1,524,1257)
Then he uttered the formula for the entry:
*HŪṂ Vajrapāśākaḍḍha HŪṂ*. Then he uttered the binding of the pledge (*samayabandha*): [formula].
HŪṂ VAJRASPHOṬA VAṂ. Then he uttered the heart-mantra of action: OṂ VAJRAKARMA SĀDHAYA KṚT.
Then Vajrapāṇi spoke this great maṇḍala of the entire Vajra family:
"Now, therefore, I shall fully explain the supreme great maṇḍala;
one should delineate the entire maṇḍala resembling the Wheel of Dharma."
In this regard, the heart-mantra for the thread is as follows: OṂ VAJRASŪTRĀKARṢAYA SARVAMAṆḌALĀN HŪṂ. Having indeed pierced a kīla made of khadira wood into the very center of the maṇḍala...
Then, having doubled the thread, one should mark out [the area] with it.
In this regard, this is the heart-mantra of the stake:
OṂ VAJRAKĪLA KĪLAYA SARVAVIGHNĀN BANDHA HŪṂ PHAṬ.
One should draw the wheel-maṇḍala joined with four lines;
having gone out from its exterior, one should likewise do so twice [the distance],
and for that as well, one should perform the drawing of the outer maṇḍala three times [the distance].
"By means of the application of the intermediate directions, one should draw the diagonal lines.
This is the procedure for the drawing.
Then, as for that drawing, one should fill it with pure colors.
With the great left vajra-fist, one should first [draw] the line; thereafter, as is convenient. In this regard, the heart-mantra for the colors is as follows: Oṃ vajraraṅgasamaya hūṃ.
Then, standing in the center, the Vajrācārya, composed in meditation,
shall mentally open the four vajra-doors. In this regard, the heart-mantra for opening the doors is as follows:
Oṃ, O Vajra-Opening Samaya, enter quickly! Remember the Vajra-Samaya! Hūṃ Phaṭ!
Whether in gold or silver, or even in well-painted clay, one should place an image of the Buddha upon a square brick.
In this regard, this is the heart-mantra of all Buddhas:
Oṃ sarvavit.
One should perform the four great beings for the Buddha from all sides.
While conquering the three worlds, Vajrapāṇi stands before him.
In this regard, these are the heart-mantras of the four Great Beings:
Oṃ śumbha niśumbha hūṃ gṛhṇa gṛhṇa hūṃ gṛhṇāpaya hūṃ ānaya ho bhagavan vajra hūṃ phaṭ.
Oṃ vajrabhṛkuṭikrodha ānaya sarvaratnān hīḥ phaṭ!
Oṃ vajradṛṣṭikrodha dṛṣṭyā māraya huṃ phaṭ!
Oṃ vajraviśvakrodha kuru sarvaṃ viśvarūpatayā sādhaya hūṃ phaṭ!
One should enter or even exit while keeping the mantra present in the mind;
thus known as Vajravega, one should thereby traverse the lines.
In this regard, this is the heart-mantra (hṛdaya) of Vajravega: [Mantra follows]
With the Vajravega [mantra], having emerged, one should likewise draw the first mandala; then,
in due order and according to the rules, one should draw Vajramāyā and the others.
In this regard, their heart-pledges (samaya-hṛdaya) are as follows:
Oṃ vajracakra hūṃ.
Oṃ vajraghaṇṭa hūṃ.
Oṃ vajradaṇḍakāṇṭha hūṃ!
Oṃ vajrāyudha hūṃ!
Having advanced with the speed of a thunderbolt, one likewise [enters] the second maṇḍala.
One should then station the Vajra-krodhas, beginning with Vajrakuṇḍalin.
Their heart-mantras are as follows:
Oṃ prajvalitapradīptavajra hūṃ.
Oṃ vajrasaumya hūṃ.
Oṃ vajradaṇḍa hūṃ.
Oṃ vajravikṛta hūṃ.
Then, however, one should draw [the deities] at the four gates with Vajravega;
all [deities] beginning with Vajraśauṇḍa are to be drawn according to the rules in their proper sequence.

Having advanced with vajra-velocity, one should proceed to the third maṇḍala;
there, in due order and according to the rule, [one should place] the vajra-musala and the others.
In this regard, their heart-mantras are as follows:
Oṃ vajramusala hūṃ;
Oṃ vajrapaṭa hūṃ.
Oṃ vajrajvāla hūṃ!
Oṃ vajragraha hūṃ!

Oṃ vajradaṃṣṭra hūṃ.

At all the vajra-gates, those very ones are the gatekeepers.
"Hereafter, I shall explain the detailed ritual procedure exactly as it is.

(STT 1,536,1290) Now, having performed the rites of summoning and so forth in this great maṇḍala of the Wheel of the Three Worlds (*trilokacakra*), the Vajrācārya himself, having bound the mudrā of Vajrakrodhaterittiri, should speak thus:
(STT 1,537,1291) "I shall generate for you the wisdom of the Vajra-samaya. (STT 1,537,1292)
"This must not be told by you to anyone;
lest, through failure to avoid danger, you should meet your end by falling from a mountain peak.
Having said this, he should give him this Heart-mantra of the Oath.
Having bound the Vajrakrodha-terittiri-mudrā, one should display it:
"This is your Vajrakrodha-samaya; it shall burn your family and destroy your body from the head down if you should transgress it. Bind the samaya!
Then, one should bind the Vajradhāri-karma-mudrā with this heart-mantra:
Oṃ! O Vajradhara of all Tathāgatas, seize, bind, samaya! Hūṃ! (STT 1,538–539,1295) Now follows the binding of this mudrā:
(STT 1,539,1296) Both hands, with the little fingers and thumbs bound together, are placed one above the other. (STT 1,539,1296)

This mudrā is known as the *karmasamayā*, and it is also celebrated as the *vajrabandhā* (or *vajrabandheti*). [It is] proclaimed as the holder of the vajra (*vajradhārī*) who performs all supreme activities.
Then, one should consecrate [the disciple] with vajra-water while reciting this heart-mantra:
OṂ VAJRĀBHISEKĀBHISIÑCA VAJRADHARATVE SAMAYA GRA GRA //
Then, having bound their faces with a cloth, one should cause the disciples to enter with this heart-mantra:
