Then Vajramukhī, the Vajra-maid, spoke her own ritual pledge: (1, 1433) Oṃ! O Vajramukhī, bring them forth! O Vajra-fanged one, O terrifying one, you who dwell in the netherworld! Dig, dig! Eat, eat! Cause everything to enter your mouth! Shatter the vital points of all the wicked ones, O bearer of the sharp vajra-sword! Hūṃ Phaṭ! (1, 1433) Then Vajrakālī spoke her own ritual pledge: (1, 1434)

Oṃ Vajrakāli! You who have the form of a great *preta*, you who delight in human flesh and blood, come, come! Seize, seize! Devour, O Vajra-Ḍākinī! O Vajra-Śaṅkalā, you who are the mother of all the hosts of gods and *bhūtas*! Take away, take away the life-breaths of [Name]! Your entire body is adorned with a garland of skulls; why do you delay? You who wield the vajra-khaṭvāṅga, upon the corpse of a *preta* and a human, quickly cause [him] to enter, cause [him] to descend, bind [him], and slay [him]! O Vajra-Rākṣasī, hūṃ hūṃ hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ! Then Vajrapūtanā spoke her own *karmasamaya*:

Oṃ! O Vajrapūtani, you who consume human flesh, blood, urine, feces, phlegm, snot, semen, and the fetus—come quickly! Perform this for him! O bearer of the Vajra-purifier, perform all my rites! Hūṃ phaṭ! (1, 1436) Then she spoke the Vajramakari-svakarmasamayā:
Oṃ! O Vajramakari, swallow, swallow! Quickly, quickly, cause [him] to enter! Devour Pātāla! O bearer of the Vajra-maraka, hūṃ phaṭ! (1, 1437)
The Vajra Servants.
(1, 1437) Then Vajrapāṇi again spoke this mandala of the activities of the entire Vajra family: (1, 1438) Now, therefore, I shall fully explain the supreme activity mandala. (1, 1439)

One should delineate the entire mandala by means of the yoga of the vajra-maṇḍala. All the foremost points of the mandala have the Buddha situated in their center; one should indeed arrange the Great Beings (mahāsattvas) in rows along their sides.
In its center, he himself, together with his consort, [should worship] Vajravidyottama;
he should worship him with the secret dance offerings beginning with Vajralāsya.
Here, the goddesses follow in succession according to the yoga of the wheel-maṇḍala.
One should depict them dancing with their own mudrās and counter-mudrās (1, 1443).
For the sake of worship, one should perform the application of the Vajra-dance for the Buddha and the Vajrin (1, 1444).
In the corners and at the door-sections, one should arrange the incense and other offerings in successive order (1, 1444).

Then, having performed the rites of summoning and so forth in this ritual mandala, and having duly bound the Vajradhāri-karmasamayamudrā, one should speak as follows: "You must not disclose this secret rite to anyone who has not seen the sequence of deities or who does not understand the ritual; lest your samaya be violated."
Having spoken thus, one should bind the samaya-mudrā of the Vajradhārin of one's own activity. Gazing with a wrathful look, one should utter this:
Oṃ vajradhāri āveśaya praveśaya nṛtyāpaya sarvakarmasiddhiṃ me prayaccha hūṃ aḥ hūṃ a la la la la vajri!
Then, having entered himself, he enters [the mandala].
With hand gestures (*mudrā*) and counter-gestures (*pratimudrā*), he performs worship with dance and offerings.
From that time forward, he accomplishes all rites as desired by means of the vajra-gestures of body, speech, vision, and mind (*kāyavāgdṛṣṭimanovajramudrā*).
Then, having released the binding of the face, one should teach the knowledge of the mudrās for the dance offering:
"The supreme commitments of the Buddhas, Vajradhara, and the others are manifested in two ways;
indeed, [one performs] the worship with Vajralāsyā and the others for the Supreme Vidyā of the Vajra."
And having worshipped the ritual maṇḍala with all the vidyās in their proper order and sequence through dances, offerings,
and worship, one should condense the great mudrās by means of the application of the vajra dance.
Having divided the supreme samayas into two, one should visualize the counter-mudrās.
By worshipping all the leaders with these offerings of dance,
as well as Mahāvajradhara and the others, the accomplishment of the activity will certainly be attained.
The detailed procedure for the ritual maṇḍala of all the activities of the Vajra Family from the *Sarvatathāgatavajrasamayamahākalparāja* is completed.

(1, 1455) Then Vajrapāṇi, having enjoined all the Vajra Families to the welfare of all sentient beings and established them on the stage of non-retrogression, knowing [the intent] of the Blessed One, addressed him as follows:
(1, 1456) "I have been consecrated by the Blessed Ones, the All-Tathāgatas, into the office of the holder of all secrets. (1, 1457)
"Therefore, command what that secret of the Tathāgatas is.
Then the Blessed One entered the samādhi called the Vajra Secret of All Tathāgatas and spoke this secret of all Tathāgatas:
"In whatever way all beings to be trained [are guided] according to their own kind..."
For in such and such a way, one who is pure through passion and the other [afflictions] should act for the sake of sentient beings.
Then Vajrapāṇi spoke this secret of his own:
"For the benefit of all sentient beings, and for the sake of the Buddha's teaching."
Even if one were to kill all sentient beings, one would not be defiled by sin.
(1, 1460) Then the Bodhisattva Vajragarbha spoke this secret of his own jewel:
(1, 1461) "For the sake of the welfare of all sentient beings, through the application of the purpose of the Perfectly Awakened One... (1, 1461)
But one who takes away all forms of wealth is not defiled by sin.
Then the Bodhisattva Vajranetra spoke this secret of all dharmas:
"There is no pleasure equal to passion; therefore, bestowing that [passion] upon the Victors..."
"By serving the wives of others for the sake of sentient beings, one attains merit.
Then the Bodhisattva Vajraviśva spoke this secret of his own activity:
"For the benefit and welfare of all sentient beings, and for the sake of the Buddha's teaching,"
"He shall indeed perform all rites and obtain great merit.
(1, 1463) Then the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Vairocana, praised the Blessed Guhyadhara Vajradhara with words of "Well done!":
(1, 1464) "Well done to you, O Vajrasattva; well done to you, O Vajraratna! (1, 1465)
"Excellent for you, O Vajradharma! Excellent for you, O Vajrakarman!
This well-spoken sūtra is the unsurpassed Vajrayāna, the secret of all Tathāgatas, the compendium of the Mahāyāna."
The Great Ritual King named *Sarvatathāgatavajrasamaya*, from the *Sarvatathāgatatattvasaṃgraha*, is completed. (1, 1467) The Great Ritual King named *Sarvatathāgatadharmasamaya*.
(2, 1468) Then all the Tathāgatas, having again assembled, requested the Blessed One Vajrapāṇi, the Lord of All Dharmas Avalokiteśvara, with these eight hundred names: (2, 1469)
Padmasattva, Mahāpadma, Lokeśvara, Maheśvara; Avalokiteśvara, foremost of the steadfast, Vajradharma—homage be to you! Dharmarāja, Greatly Pure One, King of Beings, Great-Minded One.
O you whose nature is the lotus, Great Lotus, Lord of the Lotus, homage be to you! (2, 1471) Born from the lotus, with the splendor of a beautiful lotus, pure as a lotus, O purifier;
Lotus-vajra, whose limbs are adorned with beautiful lotuses, Lotus-lotus, homage be to you! (2, 1472)
O Great Universe, O Great World, O Great Task, O Great Paragon!
(2, 1473) O Great Steadfast One, O Great Hero, O Great Śauri, homage be to you!
(2, 1473) O Intent upon Beings, O Mahāyāna, O Great Yoga, O Grandfather! (2, 1474)
O Śaṃkara, pure in essence, O Buddha Padma, homage be to you!
(2, 1474) O true reality of phenomena, True Dharma, Pure Dharma, Maker of the Excellent Dharma, (2, 1475) Great Dharma, Supreme Excellent Dharma, Wheel of Dharma, homage be to you! (2, 1475)
Buddha-being, supreme among excellent beings, Dharma-being, upholder of the excellent being;
Supreme being, knower of the excellent being, being of beings—homage be to you! O Avalokiteśvara, foremost protector, great protector, who beholds all!
O Light of the world, for the sake of the world, Lord of the world, homage be to you!
(2, 1477) Great among the syllables of the world, the supreme syllable, comparable to the syllable; O syllable beyond syllables, all-seeing one, the syllable of the wheel, homage be to you! (2, 1478)
O Lotus-handed One, Great-handed One, Consoler, Bestower! (2, 1479) O Buddha-dharma, Great Buddha, Buddha-essence, homage be to you!
(2, 1479) O Buddha-form, Great-form, Vajra-form, Possessor of beautiful form! (2, 1480)
O Dharma-light, of supreme and most brilliant splendor, O Illuminator of the World, homage be to you!
(2, 1480) O Lord Padmaśrī, foremost of lords, O Lord Dharmaśrī, you who possess all lords;
O Lord Brahmā, Great Brahmā, Son of Brahmā, homage be to you! (2, 1481)
O Lamp, foremost of lamps, supreme lamp, light of lamps, excellent illuminator!
(2, 1482) O Lord of Lamps, Great Lamp, Lamp of the Buddhas, homage be to you!
(2, 1482) Consecrated by the Buddhas, foremost of Buddhas, Son of the Buddha, Great Buddha! (2, 1483)
O Buddha, consecrated at the crown of the head; O Buddha of Buddhas, homage be to you!
(2, 1483) O Buddha-eye, Great Eye, Dharma-eye, of great vision;
O you whose entire essence is the wisdom of meditative concentration, Vajra-eye, homage be to you! (2, 1484)

Whoever should contemplate or praise this hundred and eight names of yours, which are entirely figurative, shall attain sovereignty over the world. We entreat you, O Hero, O Great Sage: reveal [them].
"Having produced one's own family, [one attains] the supreme mandala of Dharma.

(2, 1486) Then the noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, having heard the words of exhortation from all the Tathāgatas, stood facing the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Śākyamuni, and placing that vajra-lotus upon his own heart, uttered this inspired utterance:
(2, 1487) "Aho! How truly supreme and pure is this vajra-lotus of mine! (2, 1488)
"I am his father and he is my son; please preside over this family.

Then the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Vairocana, entered the samādhi called "The Lotus Arising from the Empowerment of the Samaya of the Vajra-Dharma of All Tathāgatas," and from his own heart issued forth this Heart-Mantra of All Tathāgatas, known as the "Dharma-Samaya of All Tathāgatas": HRĪḤ.
Then, as soon as this had issued forth from the hearts of all the Tathāgatas, rays of light in the form of lotuses—possessing various colors, forms, marks, and modes of conduct—issued forth.

Having purified the knowledge of the nature of the perfectly awakened Dharma regarding passion and other afflictions throughout all world-systems, they returned once more and entered the heart of Noble Avalokiteśvara.
Then the Blessed One spoke the supreme vidyā-mantra named Sarvatathāgatadharmasamaya:
Oṃ vajrapadmottama hrīḥ!
(2, 1493) Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi spoke this supreme mantra of his own knowledge:
Oṃ vajra hūṃ phaṭ! (2, 1494)
Then the Bodhisattva Vajragarbha spoke this supreme vidyā of his own: OṂ VAJRARATNOTTAMA TRAḤ. Then the Bodhisattva Vajranetra spoke this supreme vidyā of his own: [OṂ VAJRANETRA TRAḤ].
Oṃ vajravidyottama hrīḥ!
(2, 1496) Then the Bodhisattva Vajraviśva spoke this supreme mantra of his own knowledge:
Oṃ vajraviśvottama aḥ! (2, 1497)

Then indeed, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara entered the samādhi called "Manifestation of All Forms" and uttered this own heart-mantra named "The Commitment for the Discipline of the Entire World":
Oṃ huṃ hrīḥ hoḥ.

Then, as soon as this had been spoken, from the heart of the noble Avalokiteśvara, that very Lord Vajradhara emerged, having assumed the forms of great Bodhisattvas who bore the likeness of the noble Avalokiteśvara, were established upon lotuses, bore the insignia of the lotus mudrā, and possessed diverse colors, forms, attire, and ornaments; they manifested the bodies of all beings, beginning with the Tathāgatas. (2, 1499)

Having manifested their own forms in all world-systems according to the needs of those to be trained, and having brought about the discipline of the entire realm of sentient beings without exception, they returned once more. Abiding upon moon-discs on all sides through the yoga of the great maṇḍala of the Vajradhātu, they uttered this inspired utterance (udāna) to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Śākyamuni:
"Oh, how marvelous is the skillful means of all the Buddhas whose very nature is compassion! For through the guidance of such skillful means, even the gods [are brought to maturity]."

Then the Blessed One, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, having generated his own family and having offered it to all the Tathāgatas for the sake of attaining the supreme siddhi that grants fearlessness and all aims to all sentient beings, as well as the fruit of obtaining the knowledge and supernormal powers of the Vajra-dharmatā, proclaimed the great maṇḍala named Sarvajagadvinaya (The Subduer of the Entire World):
"Now, therefore, I shall fully explain the supreme great maṇḍala,
which resembles the Vajradhātu and is known as Jagadvinaya."
It is square, with four gates, adorned with four archways,
provided with four [boundary] lines, and decorated with silk ribbons, garlands, and festoons.
At all the corners of the maṇḍala and at the junctions of the gates and projections, [it is thus adorned].

One should trace the outer maṇḍala, inlaid with vajra-jewels; within that, one should draw a square line. One should then fashion the second [section], the corners of the gates, in the shape of lotuses.
By means of the application of eight pillars, one should draw an eight-petaled lotus;
in the midst of its filaments, one should place the image of the Buddha.
In this regard, this is the heart-mantra for the entry of the Buddha:
Buddha hūṃ!
(2, 1508) The Buddhas are to be depicted everywhere, established in the centers of lotuses;
likewise, the vajra, the jewel, the lotus, and the double lotus. (2, 1509)
In this regard, their heart-mantras are as follows:
*Dhiḥ* / *Kṛḥ* // Having emerged with the speed of a thunderbolt, [he enters] the maṇḍala for the discipline of the world. (2, 1510–1511)
There, Lokeśvara is to be depicted, manifesting all forms.
On all his sides, through the yoga of Vajragarva and the others,
one should draw the Buddhas and other Great Beings bearing the lotus insignia.
In this regard, their heart-mantras are as follows:
ĀḤ!
OṂ TATHĀGATADHARMA HŪṂ! (2, 1513)

Oṃ, holder of the vajra-lotus hook and sheath, Vajrasattva, hūṃ phaṭ! (2, 1513) Oṃ, slay, slay! Holder of the lotus-flower weapon, unerring arrow, hoḥ! (2, 1514) Oṃ, born from the lotus, lotus-in-hand, well done, hūṃ! (2, 1514)
Having entered the second maṇḍala with vajra-velocity,
one should likewise paint the Tathāgata in the midst of matted locks at its center.
On all his sides, [the deities] such as Bhṛkuṭī and others should be depicted according to their respective applications.
They should be depicted in due order, bearing the lotus insignia.
Their heart-mantras are as follows:
Oṃ padmabhṛkuṭi taṭi traḥ // (2, 1517) Oṃ padmasūryajvāla hūṃ // (2,
1517) Oṃ padmamaṇiketudhara candraprahlādaya avalokiteśvara, grant me the welfare of sentient beings quickly; samaya hūṃ // (2, 1518)
Oṃ, Padmāṭṭahāsa, eleven-faced one, haḥ haḥ haḥ hūṃ!
(2, 1518) Having entered by means of Vajravega, likewise the third maṇḍala, one should depict the Great Being who has attained [samādhi], established upon a lotus. (2, 1519)
On all its sides, in due order and according to rule, one should establish the Mahāsattvas through their connection with Padmāloka and the others. Their heart-mantras therein are as follows:
Dha! Oṃ Tārāpadmāvalokaya māṃ samayasattva hūṃ!
Oṃ Padmakumāra padmaśaktidhara, cut through, cut through with the sword! Hūṃ phaṭ!

Oṃ! O you who possess the playful lotus-throat, holding a conch, discus, mace, and lotus in your hands; clothed in a tiger skin; with a black serpent serving as a sacred thread and a deerskin as an upper garment over your left shoulder; assuming the form of Nārāyaṇa; three-eyed one; let out a loud laugh and cause [them] to enter! Grant me the pledges and bestow upon me accomplishment, O Avalokiteśvara!
Hūṃ! (2, 1522) Oṃ! Born from the lotus of Brahmā, recite, recite! O Lotus-Speaker! Hūṃ!
(2, 1523) And having stepped forth with vajra-velocity, likewise [entering] the fourth maṇḍala. (2, 1524)

There, one should draw a four-faced Padma, holding a lotus and a trident. On all his sides, according to the ritual procedure, the Mahāsattvas bearing the lotus emblem should be drawn, through their connection with Vajranṛtyā and the others.
In this regard, their heart-mantras are as follows:
(2, 1526) *Trīḥ* //(2, 1526) *Oṃ padmanarteśvara naṭa naṭa pūjaya sarvatathāgatān vajrakarmasamayākarṣaya praveśaya bandhayāveśaya sarvakarmasiddhiṃ me prayacchāvalokiteśvara hūṃ //* (2, 1526)
Oṃ abhayandadāvalokite vara rakṣa bandha padmakavacaṃ samaya haṃ // (2,
1527) Oṃ mahāpracaṇḍaviśvarūpavikaṭapadmadaṃṣṭrākarālabhīṣaṇavaktra trāsaya sarvān padmayakṣa khāda khāda dhik dhik dhik // (2, 1527) Oṃ padmamuṣṭisamayas tvaṃ bandha hūṃ phaṭ // (2, 1527)
Having approached with the force of a vajra, one should draw [the deities] in all the corners.
By means of the yoga of Vajralāsyā and the others, one should [draw] the deities Padmalāsyā and the rest.
In this regard, these are the mudrās:
Oṃ padmalāsye, arouse passion, O Great Goddess, at the time of the offering of passion, hūṃ! (2, 1529) Oṃ padmamāle, consecrate me, at the time of the offering of consecration, hūṃ!
(2, 1529) Oṃ padmagīte, sing, at the time of the offering of song, hūṃ! (2, 1530)
Oṃ padmanṛtye nṛtya sarvapūjāpravartanasamaye hūṃ!
(2, 1530) Having emerged with vajra-velocity, in the vicinity of the outer maṇḍala, one should draw the four goddesses of worship, Padma, Dhūpā, and the others. (2, 1531)
In this regard, these are the offering mudrās:

Oṃ, at the time of the lotus incense offering, gladden [me], O beloved of the Lotus family, O great gaṇī, O delight of the lotus, hūṃ! Oṃ, at the time of the lotus flower offering, O dweller in the lotus, O great glory, O female doorkeeper of the Lotus family, accomplish all aims, hūṃ!

Oṃ! At the time of the lamp offering, O beautiful one of the Lotus family, O great messenger, produce light! Padma Sarasvatī, hūṃ! (2, 1533) Oṃ! At the time of the incense offering, O servant of the Great Lotus family, perform all my activities! Padmasiddhi, hūṃ!
(2, 1533) Then all the attendants and others [are stationed] at the four lotus gates. (2, 1534)
They should be depicted exactly according to their essential heart-mantras (*hṛdaya*).
In this regard, their heart-mantras are as follows:
Oṃ! Hayagrīva, great lotus-hook, draw [them] forth quickly! All those belonging to the Lotus Family and the pledge (*samaya*), O wielder of the lotus-hook, hūṃ jaḥ! (2, 1535)

Oṃ! Amoghapadmapāśakrodha, attract and cause to enter the great Paśupati, Yama, Varuṇa, Kubera, and Brahmā; O you who wear their guises, [bind] the samayas of the Padmakula! Hūṃ hūṃ! Oṃ! Padmasphoṭa, bind all the samayas of the Padmakula quickly! Hūṃ vaṃ! Oṃ! Ṣaṇmukha, you who wear the guise of Sanatkumāra, cause the entry by means of the lotus-bell; bind all the samayas of the Padmakula, bind all the mudrās, and grant me all siddhis! O Padmāveśa, aḥ aḥ aḥ aḥ!
Now, herein follows the detailed ritual procedure for the Padmamaṇḍala that subdues all worlds.

Therein, at the very outset, the Lotus Master (Padmācārya), having bound the Vajrapadmasamayamudrā and entered [the maṇḍala] according to the rule, should perform the rites by means of the yoga of the Great Maṇḍala of the Vajradhātu, using these heart-mantras:
Oṃ padmasphoṭādhitiṣṭha aḥ.

Then, having likewise requested permission and likewise consecrated himself with the *samayamudrā*, having taken up the lotus-form, having uttered his own lotus-name, and having performed the ritual action with the lotus-hook and so forth, he should then accomplish the Great Beings (*mahāsattva*) by means of those very same *dharmamudrās*.
Then, in that same manner, success (*siddhi*) is attained. Thereafter, he should cause the lotus-disciples to enter.
Therein, first of all, one should give the Heart of the Oath to the lotus-disciple:
"The Lotus-being himself now resides within your heart;
it would burst asunder and depart at that very moment if you were to speak this method."
This is what must be done. Then he should say:
"You must not disclose this detailed ritual procedure for the secret [teachings] to anyone."
"May you not fall into hell;
for by failing to avoid danger and thus meeting your death, there would be a falling into hell.
Then, one should bind the Samaya-mudrā with this heart-mantra:
Oṃ, you are the vajra-lotus samaya! (2, 1544) Then, wearing a white upper garment and having his face bound with a white cloth, he should be made to enter with this heart-mantra:
(2, 1545) Oṃ padmasamaya hūṃ! (2, 1545)
Then, having performed the ritual action as prescribed, one should place a lotus-form in the hand [of the disciple], saying:
"Oṃ! O Lotus-Handed One, protect the vajra-nature!
Thereupon, he should be asked: "Of what nature is that vajra-nature?"
Then it should be said:
"Just as this red lotus is not stained by defects of its lineage,
so too one who cultivates total purity is not stained by sins."
This is the *dharmatā* in this regard:
(2, 15489) Then, one should teach the knowledge of the mudrās of the Lotus Family.
(2, 1549) Having drawn a lotus in the heart, one should meditate on the lotus within the heart. (2, 1549)
One would bring even Padmaśrī under one's control, let alone women who are inferior;
moreover, having drawn the image of the Buddha upon one's forehead, one should meditate upon it constantly.
Through that meditation, one quickly attains consecration.
Having placed the lotus within the crown of the head while remaining in meditative equipoise,
by meditating on the lotus in the crown, one becomes a sky-walker and shall bring others under one's control.
In this regard, there are these heart-mantras.
Bring Padmaśrī under control, Hoḥ!
Bestow the lotus empowerment, vaṃ.
Padmasarasvatī, purify! Hūṃ!
Subjugate those who go above the lotus: *jjaḥ*.
Whether visualizing an excellent lotus on a wall or in open space,
one achieves the supreme subjugation of all sentient beings by means of this [mantra].
Visualizing an excellent lotus either in the sky or in another place, when one sees it, then one should take it; through this desire-meditation, one shall attain invisibility.
Whether on a wall or in open space, one should meditate upon the Viśvapadma;
seeing it and grasping it as a gift, one then becomes the one whose form is the universe.
One should visualize a vajra-lotus either in the sky or in another place;
by grasping it, one becomes a Lotus Vidyādhara in an instant.
In this regard, these are their heart-mantras:
Oṃ, enter the lotus of the wisdom that brings all the world under control! Aḥ.
Oṃ, O Wisdom Lotus, remain; make it visible, vaṃ!
Oṃ, rest upon the universal lotus of meditative concentration; O Blessed One, display your universal form: dhaḥ!
Oṃ, O Samādhivajrapadma, stay! Arise quickly! Hrīḥ!
(2, 1558) Having inscribed "Lokevara" everywhere upon the mandala and other [supports], one should summon him before it using the supreme Hayagrīva mudrā.
Having painted an image of Lokeśvara in mandalas and other such settings,
he shall indeed bring the world under his control by means of the Amoghapāśa mudrā.
Having painted an image of Lokeśvara within mandalas and other such settings,
he shall indeed subjugate the world by means of the Amoghapāśa mudrā.
Having observed the best in the world everywhere within the mandalas and other [sacred sites],
one should then bind [the protection] before him with the Padmasphoṭāgra mudrā.
"Having painted Lokeśvara in mandalas and other such settings,
the supreme possession of all occurs before him by means of the lotus and bell."
In this regard, these are their heart-mantras:
Oṃ, O Lotus Hook, draw in all great beings! Hūṃ Jjaḥ!
Oṃ Amoghapāśakrodha hūṃ hoḥ!
Oṃ padmasphoṭa vaṃ.
Oṃ, Padmaghaṇṭā, enter everything! Aḥ.
(2, 1563) Visualizing himself as a being with four lotus-faces, he himself, as his own self, shall then become an accomplished one of manifold forms in an instant.
Meditating upon himself as a lotus within a lotus by means of his own self,
and abiding in the samādhi of Vajradharma, he attains the imperishable state.
Visualizing himself by means of his own self within the matted locks of Lokeśvara,
one’s own person becomes like Amitāyus.
Meditating by himself through the *viśvarūpa-samādhi*,
one who abides in the *viśvarūpa-samādhi* shall become equal to Lokeśvara.
In this regard, these are their heart-mantras:
Padmaviśva / Dharmakāyapadma / Buddhābhiṣeka /
Lokeśvara! (2, 1568) Then one should teach the knowledge of all the mudrās of the great maṇḍala.
In that regard, first of all, there is the knowledge of Mahāmudrā.

Having fashioned the great image of the lotus within the lotus through meditative absorption,
one should sit and mentally slay oneself.
Having fashioned a four-faced lotus with his hand and grasping it, he performs the rites of possession and so forth while rotating it.
Now, their heart-mantras are as follows: (1811)
Oṃ, accomplish the supreme offering of fragrance, hrīḥ!
Oṃ, O Tathāgata Padmamukuṭa, bring all under control!
Oṃ, O Lotus-Lotus, destroy all adversaries! Samādhi-jñāna, dhik! (1812)
Oṃ viśvapadma, perform all activities! Lalilvali lali hūṃ phaṭ! (1813) Then, one should teach the secret knowledge of the mudrās:
"One who is red shall accomplish all tasks; for this is the samaya."

"For even a mudrā that is difficult to accomplish is indeed accomplished in an instant through yoga. (1814) In this regard, his pledge-mantra (*samaya*) is as follows: *Oṃ sādhaya padmarāgasamaya aḥ*. (1815)
Then, one should teach the binding of all mudrās, beginning with the Mahāmudrā.
[The detailed ritual procedure for the mandala of the four mudrās is completed.
(1816) Then the noble Great Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara spoke this heart-mantra named "The Subduer of All Worlds. (1817)
Oṃ, O Great Being who tames the entire world, come! Swiftly manifest your manifold forms and bestow upon me all accomplishments, Hrīḥ! (1818)
Then the noble Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara spoke this maṇḍala called the "Discipline of All Worlds":
"Now, therefore, I shall fully explain the maṇḍala of the Discipline of the World.
One should draw the outer maṇḍala by means of the yoga of the great maṇḍala."
Within that [mandala], one should likewise draw a lotus;
therein, one should draw the Universal Form (*viśvarūpa*) expanded from all lotuses.
(1821) Then, having duly entered this great mandala according to the detailed ritual procedure,
Having spoken thus,
one should teach the knowledge for disciplining all worlds;
having drawn the mandala known as "Disciplining the World."
"By meditating upon Mahāmudrā, one becomes like the Holder of All.
(1824) Then, one should teach the secret knowledge of the mudrā for the discipline of the world:
"Meditating with a well-composed mind upon the samādhi of the Universal Form,"
Through the union of the two organs within the mandala, he attains accomplishment.
Thereafter, one should teach the binding of the seals, beginning with the Mahāmudrā; in that very way, the accomplishments are attained.
In the same way, [this applies] to cloth and so forth.
Even with respect to the mudrās, the accomplishments (*siddhi*) are attained in the same way through the yoga of the single-mudrā maṇḍala.
(1826) Then all the Tathāgatas, having gathered together once more, bestowed words of praise upon the Great Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara:
(1827) "Excellent for you, O Vajrasattva! Excellent for you, O Vajraratna!"
“Excellent for you, O Vajradharma! Excellent for you, O Vajrakarman!
This well-spoken sūtra is the unsurpassed Vajrayāna, the secret of all Tathāgatas, and the compendium of the Mahāyāna. (1828–1829)

The *Sarvatathāgatadharmasamaya*, the great king of rituals (*mahākalparāja*) from the *Sarvatathāgatatattvasaṃgraha*, is hereby completed. (1830) The *Sarvatathāgatakarmasamaya*, the great king of rituals (1831),
[containing] the detailed procedure for the great maṇḍala of the accomplishment of all aims (*sarvārthasiddhi*).

Then indeed, all the Tathāgatas, having gathered together once more, entreated that very Vajradhara, the noble Mahābodhisattva Āryākāśagarbha—the Jewel of the Empowerment of All Tathāgatas—with these eight hundred names:
"O Ākāśagarbha! O Being for the sake of sentient beings! O Great Being! O Great Splendor!"
Great jewel, supreme among excellent jewels, Vajra-jewel, homage be to you!
(1833) Consecration, great jewel, utterly pure, most auspicious, Buddha-jewel of purified limbs, jewel among jewels, homage be to you! (1834)
O you who have arisen from the space of space, the great sky of all space;
O realm of space, all-hoping one, foremost among all hopes, homage be to you!
(1835) O Ratnasaṃbhava, jewel-eyebrowed one, Buddha-eyebrowed one, well-gone Tathāgata!
O you who are the most excellent of all jewels, the jewel-activity, homage be to you!
(1836) O Jewel, foremost of jewels, fierce jewel, jewel of all Tathāgatas, supreme jewel, great space, equal to space, homage be to you! (1837)

O Ornament of great splendor, maker of beauty, most beautiful one; pure in all purposes, pure in aim, O you whose conduct is giving, homage be to you! (1838) O Tathāgata, jewel of the Dharma, supreme and stainless, jewel of the Saṅgha!
Homage to you, the Great Consecration, for the sake of the world and for the sake of joy! (1839) O Giver, Bestower, Supreme Giver, Renouncer, Noble Renouncer, Bestower of gifts;
O You who exist for the sake of all beings, for the sake of reality, and for the sake of the Great Purpose—homage be to you! (1840)
O King of Thought, of great majesty, the method of the perfection of generosity!
O Tathāgata, Great Being, homage be to you, the embodiment of all Buddhas! (1841) O Great Jewel of the Tathāgata, O Great Radiance of the Tathāgata!
O Great Banner of the Tathāgata, O Great Laughter, homage be to you!

(1842) O Foremost Consecration of the Tathāgatas, O Great Consecration, O Great All-pervading Lord, O Protector of the World, O Best of the Well-favored World, O Sun of the World, homage be to you! (1843)
O you who are more excellent than the most excellent jewels, O jewel-adornment, O bearer of jewels! O light of jewels, O great light, O light of jewels, homage be to you!
(1844) O mass of jewels, arisen from supreme jewels, O gem, O diamond-gem, O virtue!
O Ratnākara, whose limbs are brilliantly radiant, O you who consist of all jewels, homage be to you!
(1845) O Great-Souled One, Lord of the Staff, Lord of Jewels, fulfiller of all hopes; O you who grant the attainment of all intentions, O Radiance of Jewels, homage be to you! (1846)
O Sovereign of Light, all-pervading, the Self of All, Bestower of Boons, Great Boon!
O Manifestation of all prosperity, Vajragarbha, homage be to you!
(1847) Whoever should hold these one hundred and eight auspicious names of yours—
That faultless one obtains the consecration of all Buddhas in an instant.
We entreat you, O Jewel: speak of the accumulation of wealth;
produce the supreme consecration of all Buddhas and manifest your own family. Thus it is said. (1848–1849)
Then the Bodhisattva Ākāśagarbha, having heard these words of all the Tathāgatas, uttered his own heart-mantra called "The Commitment of the Empowerment of All Tathāgatas":
Oṃ vajraratna hūṃ. (1850)
Then the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Vairocana, spoke this supreme vidyā called the "Pledge of the Jewel of All Tathāgatas":
*oṃ sarvatathāgatāśāparipūraṇamahāratna hūṃ*.
(1851) Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi spoke this supreme vidyā arising from his own family:
Oṃ vajra hūṃ traḥ.
(1852) Then the Bodhisattva Vajragarbha spoke this supreme vidyā of his own:
Oṃ maṇi hūṃ. (1853)
Then the Bodhisattva Vajranetra spoke this supreme vidyā born from his own family: Oṃ padma hrīḥ. Then the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajraviśva spoke this supreme vidyā of his own: [Oṃ vajra viśva hūṃ].

Oṃ viśvaratna hūṃ. (1855) Then the noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Ākāśagarbha entered the samādhi called "The Jewel of the Empowerment of All Tathāgatas. (1856) As soon as he had entered it, at that very moment, rays of light from diamond-jewels issued forth from the hearts of all the Tathāgatas. (1857)

Having illuminated all those world-systems and having consecrated all sentient beings with the consecrations of all the Tathāgatas, they once again became one and entered the heart of the Blessed One, the Great Bodhisattva Ākāśagarbha.

(1858) Then, from that heart of Ākāśagarbha, the Blessed One Vajrapāṇi himself emerged, having become the bodies of Great Bodhisattvas whose interiors were filled with the blazing flames of simultaneous rays of light, whose bodies were adorned with various ornaments such as the consecration-jewels of variegated vajras and gems, and whose hands were busily engaged with the seals (*mudrā*) of the great vajra-gem-jewel insignia. (1859)

Having satisfied all world-systems through the production of jewels, such as rains of great jewels, and having returned once more, they took their places upon moon-maṇḍalas by means of the yoga of the Great Maṇḍala of the Vajra Realm surrounding the Blessed One Vairocana, and uttered this inspired utterance:
"Aho! This Vajra Jewel Family, which is the collection of all jewels of all Buddhas, has arisen for the sake of the world. (1861)
Then the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Ākāśagarbha, having generated his own family,
offered it to all the Tathāgatas for the fulfillment of all hopes, and proclaimed this great maṇḍala named Sarvārthasiddhi.
(1862) Now, therefore, I shall fully explain the supreme great maṇḍala.
Resembling the Vajradhātu, it is known as the "Accomplishment of All.
It is square, with four doors, adorned with four archways,
provided with four [boundary] lines, and decorated with silk ribbons, garlands, and festoons.
In all the corners of the mandala, at the junctions of the gates and projections,
one should mark out the outer mandala, inlaid with vajra-jewels.
Inside that, one should construct a city equal to the vajra-jewels.
There, one should have the layout marked out using the method of eight hundred excellent pillars.
Adorned with five mandalas and blazing with various jewels,
one should place the Buddha there together with his retinue of personal mudrās.
In this regard, their heart-mantras are as follows:
Oṃ buddharatna hūṃ.
Oṃ vajramaṇi hūṃ.
Oṃ vajraratāṅkura hūṃ.
Oṃ vajra-ratna-padma hūṃ.
Oṃ vajraratnavarṣa hūṃ.
(1868) Having entered with vajra-velocity into the maṇḍala of the accomplishment of all aspirations, one should draw Vajragarbha, who resides therein and bestows the supreme jewel. (1869)
On all his sides, great beings endowed with jewel-seals should be painted in due order and according to the rules. Now, their heart-mantras are as follows:
Oṃ, bestower of the accomplishment of all aims, hūṃ!
Oṃ vajramaṇicihnākāśagarbha bhagavan sidhya sidhya hūṃ. (1871) Oṃ ratnāṅkuśākarṣaya sarvārthān ānaya śīghraṃ sarvatathāgatasatyam anusmara hūṃ.
Oṃ maṇirāga, bring all goals under control; O Ākāśagarbha, summon them! Hūṃ!
Oṃ ratnatuṣṭi hūṃ.
Having entered the maṇḍala of the Ratnamāla with vajra-impetus,
one should correctly draw there in the center the supreme wearer of the jewel garland.
On all his sides, in due order and as prescribed,
the Mahāsattvas should be painted, with jewels as the marks on their hands.
Their heart-mantras are as follows:
Oṃ ratnadṛṣṭi traḥ.
Oṃ, jewel garland of the empowerment of all Tathāgatas, hūṃ!
Oṃ maṇisūrya hūṃ. (1875) Oṃ cintāmaṇidhvajasarvāśāprapūrakākāśagarbha hūṃ.
Oṃ ratnāṭṭahāsa hasa hasa hūṃ.
(1876) Having stepped forward with vajra-velocity, one should draw the maṇḍala of the jewel-lotus;
therein, one should depict the Lord holding a jewel-lotus, established upon a jewel. (1877)
On all his sides, one should paint the great beings,
with the jewel as their emblem, in brief, according to the rules and in proper sequence.
Herein are their heart-mantras:
Oṃ ratnapadma hūṃ.
Oṃ, you whose womb is the renunciation, meditative concentration, and wisdom, hūṃ!
Oṃ, supreme treasury of jewels, hūṃ!
Oṃ, turn the jewel-wheel, hūṃ!
Oṃ ratnabhāṣa hūṃ.
(1880) Having entered with vajra-velocity into the maṇḍala of the rain of jewels, one should there draw the Great Being raining down a shower of jewels. (1881)
On all his sides, one should briefly place the great beings according to the ritual rules, endowed with jewel insignia and having their hands in the [appropriate] mudrās.
Their heart-mantras are as follows:
Oṃ, rain down a shower of jewels! O Blessed One, with jewels in hand, bring about the fulfillment of all aims! Hūṃ!
Oṃ maṇipūjāsamaya hūṃ.
Oṃ maṇibandhakavaca hūṃ.
Oṃ, O Great Yakṣa with terrifying jewel-fangs, take away, take away all [obstacles] to our aims; strike fear into them! Hūṃ!
Oṃ maṇiratnabandhasamaya hūṃ.
(1884) Having stepped forth with vajra-impetus, one should draw Ratnalāsyā and the others in all the corner sections, in due order and according to the rules. (1885)
In that regard, their mudrās are as follows:
Oṃ ratnarati hūṃ.
Oṃ ratnamāle hūṃ.
Oṃ, O jewel-song, hūṃ!
Oṃ ratnanṛtye hūṃ.
(1886) Having emerged with vajra-velocity, one should draw the supreme outer maṇḍala;
in the corners of the outer maṇḍala, one should depict the offerings of incense and so forth. (1887)
In this regard, their mudrās are as follows:
Oṃ dhūparatne.
Oṃ Puṣpamaṇi.
Oṃ Ratnāloke!
Oṃ maṇigandhe. (1888) The gatekeepers are to be placed in the four centers of the gates. Hereafter, I shall explain in detail the ritual procedure for the maṇḍala. (1889)
Now, here are the heart-formulas.
Oṃ! Attract all jewels! Noble Aruṇamahāsattva, impel the Blessed One Ākāśagarbha; summon him quickly! Ho! Jaḥ!
Oṃ, O pledge of entry into all jewels, cause [them] to enter the family of the Great Jewel King; O jewel-noose, hūṃ!
Oṃ maṇibandha hūṃ vaḥ.
Oṃ maṇiratāveśa aḥ.

(1890) Then, having himself entered this great maṇḍala according to the rule and performed the detailed ritual for himself, the Maṇiratna-ācārya then consecrated the maṇi-disciples with the water from the flask empowered by the jewel.
One should bind the Vajramaṇi-samaya-mudrā with this heart-mantra:
Oṃ vajramaṇisamaya vaṃ. Then, having arranged the upper garment (uttarāsaṅga) according to the appropriate color, [one should proceed].
Having bound the eyes with that very [cord], one should cause [the disciple] to enter with this heart-mantra:
*oṃ hūṃ praviśa maṇirājakulam*.
Then, having caused him to enter, it should be said:
"You must not tell this to anyone;
otherwise, may you never be liberated from the suffering of poverty throughout all your future births,
and may your dwelling in hell be firm."
Having spoken thus, one should burst the seal and recite the realization of the Mahāyāna.
Then, once [the disciple] has been possessed by the vajra-speech, one should ask:
"Where is the great treasure?
Or how is it obtained? (1894)
Then, as soon as it was said, "The Blessed One, the Bodhisattva Ākāśagarbha, causes all to speak," he released the binding of the mouth and displayed the great maṇḍala;
and he should proclaim the pledge of the empowerment of all the Tathāgatas.
Until the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, has arrived. Then, having performed worship according to one’s means, one should accomplish all tasks.
Now, in this regard, there are the knowledge-mudrās (*jñānamudrā*).

Having bound the great mudrā of Vajragarbha while well-composed, one digs for treasure; wherever the treasure is, there one beholds it. Having indeed bound the supreme samaya-mudrā, wherever treasure exists, [one finds it].
If one presses that mudrā there, it then rises up by itself.
By meditating with a well-concentrated mind upon the Vajragarbha-samādhi,
one knows by means of the mind alone where a treasure-trove is located.

Having bound the mudrā consisting of karma through the vajragarbha-samādhi, one should enter that mudrā and observe where the treasure is located. In this regard, these are their heart-mantras: (1901) The heart-mantras for them are as follows: [followed by the mantras].
Oṃ, enter the great jewel-treasure! Hūṃ.
Oṃ maṇipīḍa, reveal!
Oṃ, Jewel Samādhi, speak!
Oṃ ratnāveśa darśaya!
(1902) Having assumed the mahāmudrā, wherever one should wrap the body, there a treasure of jewels is to be known by those who have realized the samaya. (1903)
Having indeed bound the supreme *samaya* mudrā, wherever one enters and becomes clearly manifest, a treasure-trove should be recognized there; it shall consist of great jewels.
Having indeed bound the *samādhi* mudrā, if one enters once again by oneself...
One should speak where there may be a treasure consisting of great jewels.
Having indeed bound the *karmamudrā* and having entered into one another, when the hands are joined in the *samaya*, one should point out the treasure there. Thus it is said. (1905–1906)
In this regard, their heart-mantras are as follows: Oṃ mahāratnakāya darśaya ratnam.
Oṃ Ākāśagarbha! O jewel-gem! Manifest, manifest wherever there is a treasure!
Oṃ Maṇiratnajñāna, speak yourself!
Oṃ! Again, show the binding of the samaya.
(1907) Having indeed bound the mahāmudrā, wherever there may be apprehension, there one should recognize by means of gnosis a treasure-trove arising from jewels. (1908)
Wherever doubt may arise, one should bind the *samayāgrī* [mudrā];
when it releases itself, one should indicate that there is a treasure-trove (*nidhi*) there.
Having indeed bound the *samādhimudrā*, wherever doubt becomes certain, [one should know the treasure is there]. (1909)
Having relied upon gnosis, that which is to be known is a treasure that exists there eternally.
Wherever doubt should arise again, one should indeed bind the action-seal (*karmamudrā*) there according to the ritual; then the treasure to be known will manifest once more. (1910–1911)
In this regard, their heart-mantras are as follows:
Oṃ, enter with the knowledge of the treasure!
Oṃ! Jewel-samaya, release the bonds of the treasure!
Oṃ, Jewel of the Dharma, speak the treasure!
Oṃ, shatter all karmas! Reveal [the treasure]! Lift up the bond of the treasure-store!
(1912) Having assumed the Great Seal (mahāmudrā), one should search for the treasure-store; wherever the absorption occurs, there one should point it out. (1913)
Having indeed bound the supreme pledge-mudrā, one should search for the treasure;
wherever it attains firmness, there one should indicate the treasure.
Having assumed the samādhi-mudrā, one should search for the storehouse.
One should indicate that a treasure is located wherever a wise person becomes possessed of knowledge. Having bound the mudrā consisting of action, one should search for the treasure;
wherever the action-mudrā revolves, there one should indicate it.
In this regard, their heart-mantras are as follows:
Oṃ mahāratnaparīkṣāviśa.
Oṃ, firm one of the jewel-samaya, reveal yourself!
Oṃ, enter with the wisdom that examines jewels!
Oṃ maṇikarma bhrāmaya. (1917) Thereafter, one should teach the knowledge of the secret mudrā of the jewel:
"By means of the union of the two organs, one should search for the treasure."

By meditating upon the Mahāmudrā, one shall obtain the treasure through [spiritual] immersion. Having bound the supreme Samaya-mudrā and likewise delighting the woman, wherever the mudrā becomes firm, there one should point out the treasure. (1918–1919)
Through the union of the two organs, one should seek out the treasure;

by cultivating the knowledge-seal (*jñānamudrā*), the knowledge of the treasure arises. Indeed, by binding the action-seal (*karmamudrā*) through the meditative absorption of the two organs, [the treasure is found]. (1920)
Wherever that mudrā bursts open, there one should indicate a treasure-trove.
Regarding this, their heart-mantras are as follows:
Oṃ mahāmaṇisaṃyogāviśa.
Oṃ! Through the union of the samaya, may you be firm for me.
Oṃ, enter, enter the treasury of knowledge, [into] the union!
Oṃ sarvakarmasphoṭasaṃyoga. (1922) Then, one should teach the knowledge of all the mudrās of the Great Jewel Family. Now, the great mudrās are as follows: (1923)
Abiding in the center of the moon-maṇḍala according to the manner of the drawing,
one should meditate upon the great mudrās, which are the supreme accomplishments for all aims. (1924)
Then follow the activities of the great mudrās:
the Buddha-mudrā brings about Buddhahood and the excellent accomplishment for Vajragarbha;
Ratnāṅkuśā performs summoning; Maṇirāgā brings about passion. (1925)
Through the Jewel-Quadruple (or Jewel-Fourfold), there is contentment;
through the Jewel-Vision, it accomplishes one's aims.
Through the Jewel-Garland Empowerment, there is the Jewel-Sun, which bestows great splendor. (1926)

Just as a wish-fulfilling gem grants desires, and a jewel-smile brings wealth, so too the acquisition of the Jewel of Dharma is the supreme gain, the highest form of renunciation. It is a treasury of jewels, a great storehouse, and the sovereignty over the wheel of gems. (1927)
Speech, the path, attainment, the rain of jewels, and great wealth;
(1928) the worship of jewels, being highly venerable, the jewel-army, and that which makes firm;
the jewel-tusk takes away riches, but through the jewel-fist, one succeeds. (1929)
Now, herein is the knowledge of the pledge-mudrās (*samayamudrā*) in this great maṇḍala:
The mudrā consisting of the vajra-jewel bestows the consecration of all Buddhas;
by binding the great vajra-jewel, the vajra-jewel is accomplished. (1930)
Having formed the two vajras into a jewel, one shall obtain wealth from the Vajra-holder;
with that very [mudrā] and the thumb-vajra, one should present the jewel situated at the heart.
Having bound the jewel with the tips of the closed [fingers], one becomes Lokeśvara, the giver of wealth.
One should bestow the Vajra-karma-maṇi, the great Viśva-maṇi-dhvaja.
By means of the Vajra-dhātu-agra-maṇi, one attains the state of a Buddha-jewel.
[The mudrā is formed] by bringing the palms together, contracting them, and binding the thumbs like a vajra. (1932–1933)
This is declared to be the Vajramaṇi, belonging to the hand of Vajragarbha.
Merely by binding this, one obtains the Great Vajramaṇi.
Having placed the Ratnavajra, with its sprout arising from the center, one should hold it level.
By merely binding this [mudrā], one shall obtain one's own consecrations.
That same [mudrā], with the middle and little fingers folded into a bud, is called Avalokita; by it, one should bestow wealth.
By means of the application of the Vajra-jewel [mudrā], the index, thumb, and little fingers [are joined];
with the two middle fingers, the nails are pressed together, and the ring fingers arise like sprouts.
Having made the Vajra-binding firm, the two index fingers are formed into jewels.

With the tips of the thumbs extended toward the heart, this [mudrā] bestows the accomplishment of all aims. Having formed the vajra-bind, with the middle fingers joined like jewels, this is the mudrā of the jewel-sign; it bestows the precious gem.
That same [mudrā], joined with a hook and accompanied by two index fingers,
is the *sarvārthakārṣaṇī* mudrā, known as the *maṇiratnāṅkuśī*. That same [mudrā], when bent and with one index finger grasping the other index finger, [is the *vajrāṅkuśī*].
By means of the yoga of drawing the arrow, one should attract and color the world.
That same [mudrā] is the "Sādhukāra" when the index finger and thumb are joined;
likewise, it is the same when the tips of the fingers are concealed by the joining of the thumb.

Furthermore, when the tips [of the fingers] are directed toward the mouth from between the thumbs and the [other] fingers, that is known as the "Jewel Gaze" (*maṇidṛṣṭi*); it destroys all obstacles once one has beheld them. (1943) The "Garland of the Accomplishment of All Aims" (*sarvārthasiddhimālā*), however, bestows self-consecration. (1944)
That very [mudrā], when applied by joining the tips of the thumbs at the heart,
is the "Jewel-Sun" (maṇisūryā) at the heart, bestowing great splendor.
And when situated at the crown of the head, with the tips of the banners separated, it is the Samānā.

The Great Vajra-Jewel was formerly the fulfiller of all hopes. That very same [jewel], when transformed through playful movement into the form of laughter, is indeed known by the name Ratnāṭṭahāsā; through her laughter, she accomplishes all purposes. (1946–1947)
The supreme jewel-lotus of all, she is the remover of poverty through meditative absorption;
she alone, by bestowing the gift of the end and the beginning, is the giver of the great gift. (1948) She is established as the jewel upon the thumb and forefinger positioned below.

The Maṇikośā [mudrā] seizes the wealth of the worlds through its prowess. The Vajrabandhāgracakrā, with the thumbs joined together and the index fingers positioned like jewels, bestows the status of a universal monarch (cakravartin).
That same [mudrā], when raised from the mouth with the application of the añjali gesture,
and having indeed joined it with speech, takes away wealth by one’s own command.
Having bound the great vajra-gem, one causes a rain of jewels to fall.
But when all the fingers are pressed together, it rains down wealth fourfold.
(1952) Having bound the great vajra-gem and dancing from the midst of the uṣṇīṣa, having worshipped according to the ritual, one is worshipped by all with all kinds of jewels. (1953)
One should embrace the *sarvārthasiddhi-mudrā* at the region of the throat;
it is renowned as the *maṇibandha*, remembered as a protective armor.
That same [mudrā], when positioned at the mouth for the sake of all accomplishments, is the *yakṣayoga*.
Known as Maṇidaṃṣṭrā, she robs all wealth out of fear.

Having made the vajra-bind firm, with the tips [of the fingers] bent and well-restrained, and having properly grasped it between the two thumbs, this "Jewel Fist" (maṇimuṣṭi) bestows accomplishment. (1955–1956)

However, for those who have attained the supreme commitments (*samaya*), through the application of the Vajradhātu and by means of the jewel-yoga (*maṇiyoga*) as it truly is, the foremost commitments are here conceived. But by means of the middle jewel-yoga, those very same [commitments] are conceptualized.
"By means of the yoga of Ekāṅkuśī and the others, all activities are accomplished. (1958) Now follows the knowledge of the Dharma-mudrā of the Mahāmaṇi family:

"Having stabilized the Vajraratna through the Vajraratna-samādhi."

"Whether it be a painting, or a beloved woman, or a woman, or even a man—by joining the two foreheads, both will achieve success as a Buddha. (2120)

Oṃ vajramaṇidhara, grant me the accomplishment of all aims!
Ho! Blessed One Vajraratna Hūṃ!
(2123) Now, here is the mandala: Now, therefore, I shall fully explain the supreme great mandala.
"The mandala for the attainment of all siddhis should be drawn exactly as described.

"One who is not detached from the pleasures of form and so forth,"
"By offering [these] to the Buddhas, one attains the accomplishment of the eon. Thus (2125), one should then teach the fourfold knowledge of mudrās.
Thus, having drawn a sentient being or a mudrā upon cloth and so forth, or within mandalas, one should accomplish [the practice].
(2126) Then all the Tathāgatas, having gathered together once more, covered the Great Bodhisattva Ākāśagarbha with this gift of accomplishment:
"Excellent for you, O Vajrasattva! Excellent for you, O Vajraratna! (2127)
Excellent for you, O Vajradharma; excellent for you, O Vajrakarman!
(2128) Well-spoken is this sūtra, the unsurpassed Vajrayāna, the secret of all Tathāgatas, the compendium of the Mahāyāna. (2129) Thus it is said.

The Great King of Ritual Manuals named *Sarvatathāgatakarmasamaya* from the *Sarvatathāgatatattvasaṃgraha* is completed. (2130) (2131: no text) The Extensive Tantra of the Methods for Accomplishing All Ritual Manuals. (2132)
Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi proclaimed this extensive tantra of the ritual procedures for the great reality of all Tathāgatas.
In that regard, first of all, there is the tantra of the supreme accomplishment of the Great Mudrā of the Tathāgata.
Having bound the Great Seal of the Tathāgata throughout all the realms of space,
and having empowered the forms of the Buddhas, one should cause them to enter into one's own heart. If one desires the supreme, auspicious boon in this very life, [one should do so].
Therefore, this Buddhahood is the task; otherwise, there would be no accomplishment as described above.
(2137) [Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi proclaimed the *Tathāgatakulottamasiddhitantra*: (2138) [In that regard, first of all, there is the *Mahāmudrottamasiddhitantra*: (2139)
Having attained the Mahāmudrā and proclaiming the Great Reality,
I shall meditate upon everything word by word through the yoga of the sentient being.
(2140) If one desires the auspicious state of the Sun in this very life, [one should practice thus].
Therefore, one should perform this for oneself; otherwise, there will be no accomplishment as described above.
(2141) Now follows the *Samayamudrottamasiddhi-tantra*:
(2142) "Visualizing that 'I am just like Vajradhara in terms of accomplishment'..."
"One attains the state of a Buddha-hero; otherwise, there is no accomplishment as described above.
(2143) Now follows the *Dharmamudrottamasiddhitantra*:
(2144) "By means of speech that is pure by nature, one should indeed say: 'All phenomena [are thus].'"
"One attains the state of a Buddha-hero; otherwise, there is no accomplishment as described above.
(2145) Now follows the *Karmamudrā-uttamasiddhi-tantra*:
"Since everything is entirely pure, purifying all actions... (2146)
"One attains the state of a Buddha-hero; otherwise, there is no accomplishment as described above.
(2147) Thus [end] the supreme accomplishments of the Tathāgata family. (2148) Then Vajrapāṇi proclaimed the tantra of the supreme accomplishment of his own family. (2149)

((In that regard, first of all, there is the Mahāmudrā-uttamasiddhi-tantra)): (2150) "By the command of the Buddha, for the sake of all sentient beings, and through the application of all accomplishments, one who accomplishes Mahāmudrā attains Buddhahood in this very life. (2151)
Now follows the *Samayamudrottamasiddhitantra*:
"Meditating, 'Just as Vajradhara is accomplished, so am I,' one attains the state of a hero in an instant through the application of Mahāmudrā. (2152)
Now follows the *Dharmamudrottamasiddhitantra*:
"In phenomena that are beyond syllables, conceptual proliferation does not exist. By speaking thus and meditating upon the supreme phenomenon, one shall attain the state of the Hero. (2153)
Now follows the *Karmamudrottamasiddhitantṛ*:
"For whatever action one performs, whether auspicious or inauspicious, by offering it to the Victors, one attains the state of a hero in an instant. (2154)
Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi proclaimed the *Siddhi-tantra of the Supreme Lotus Family*.
Therein, first of all, is the *Siddhi-tantra of the Supreme Mahāmudrā*:
"Passion is pure by its very nature; it is disregarded by the non-Buddhists."
"In this Mahāyāna, however, the quality of non-attachment is accomplished. (2156) Now follows the *Samayamudrottamasiddhitantra*:
"One should practice great loving-kindness through the firm yoga of meditative concentration."
"By expanding [the visualization] according to the rule through yoga, one attains the state of a sun-god in an instant. Thus [ends the section]. Now follows the *Dharmamudrotamasiddhitantra*:
"One should declare this principle: 'Passionate attachment is pure by its very nature.'"
"Having attained the perfection of passion, one shall obtain the state of a hero in an instant. (2158) Now follows the *Karmamudrā-uttamasiddhi-tantra*:
"By seeing, touching, hearing, or even remembering [the mudrā],"
"May I be the accomplishment that brings an end to all the sufferings of all sentient beings.
(2159) Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi proclaimed the *Maṇikulottamasiddhitantra*.
(2160) In that regard, there is the *Mahāmudrottamasiddhitantra*:
"May I become one who receives the consecration of all Buddhas, like Vajragarbha.
By cultivating this meditation, one indeed attains the state of a Sun-like Lord (*sauritva*) in an instant. Thus [ends the section].
Now follows the *Samayamudrottamasiddhitantra*.

"May I become the fulfiller of all the hopes of all sentient beings; like Ākāśagarbha, may I attain the state of a hero in an instant. Thus [ends the section]. Now follows the *Dharmamudrottamasiddhitantra*.

"Having completely renounced his own wealth, one who is well-joyful and speaks the seal consisting of Dharma attains the state of a hero in this world. Thus [ends the section]. Now follows the *Karmamudrottamasiddhitantra*.

"Devoted to the production of wealth for the benefit of the poor, one attains the state of a hero through exertion, even if success is not achieved as described above. (2164) This concludes the detailed procedure for attaining the supreme accomplishment of the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas regarding all family mudrās. (2165)
Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi again proclaimed the *Sarvatathāgatasamayasiddhi-tantra*.
In this regard, this is the *Tathāgatasamayasiddhi-tantra*:
"One who has the meditative absorption of passion should purify by means of passion;
this is known as the commitment (*samaya*) of the Buddha’s Great Seal (*mahāmudrā*) wisdom.
(2167) In this regard, there is this *Tathāgata-samayasiddhi-tantra*:
Non-detachment from sensual pleasures is this very great commitment (*samaya*);
it is pure within the Tathāgata family and cannot be transgressed even by the Victors. (2168) Now follows the *Vajrakula-samayasiddhi-tantra*.
Even though he is free from anger, he manifests as a great wrathful deity for the sake of sentient beings;
this is the samaya of the Great Vajra Family, which is difficult to transgress.
In this regard, there is this *Padmakula-samayasiddhi-tantra*:
One should act as one desires by means of the wisdom that is pure by its very nature;
this is the samaya of the Great Lotus Family, which is difficult to transgress.
In this regard, there is this *Maṇikulasamayasiddhitantra*:
Whether it be small or great, according to one's preference, one should ensure that each day is not spent in vain by means of giving; for this is the rule.
Thus [ends] the *Sarvakulasamayasiddhividhivistaratantra*. // (2172)
Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi proclaimed the *Sarvatathāgatadharmamudrājñānasiddhitantra*.
In this regard, this is the *Tathāgatadharmasiddhitantra*:
having spoken the syllable of the true nature (*dharmatākṣara*) thus, "The Buddha is known as the Dharma."
This is the supreme method for the wisdom of the Mahāmudrā of the Buddha-dharma.
In this regard, here is the *Tathāgatakula-dharmasiddhi-tantra*:
There is no dharma more pure than passion that bestows all happiness;
even within the Tathāgata family, this dharma is the supreme means for attaining accomplishment.
In this regard, there is this *Vajrakula-dharmasiddhi-tantra*:
Whether by the command of the Buddha, for the purpose of purification, or likewise for the sake of protecting sentient beings,
even one who is not angry attains purity by slaying those who are thoroughly corrupt.
In this regard, there is this *Tantra of the Accomplishment of the Dharma of the Lotus Family*:
"Just as a lotus is unsullied by water, so too passion does not defile.
Speaking thus, one who performs improper acts is not stained by sins.
In this regard, there is this *Maṇikuladharmasiddhitantra*:

"There is no dharma equal to generosity; for it is said that through practice, one attains the dharma of the Great Jewel Family, provided there is no lack of success as described above. Thus ends the *Sarvakuladharmasiddhividhivistaratantra* (The Extensive Tantra on the Ritual Procedures for the Attainment of the Dharmas of All Families).
Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi proclaimed the *Sarvatathāgatakarmasiddhi-tantra*.
In this regard, this is the *Tathāgatakarmasiddhi-tantra*:
"The state of Buddhahood for all sentient beings, as well as the state of a Bodhisattva,"
And by properly disciplining [the mind], one bestows the supreme accomplishment of the action-seal (*karmamudrā*).
In this regard, there is this *Tathāgatakula-karmasiddhi-tantra*:
through the fourfold worship and constant yoga, the fourfold [result] is attained.
By performing [the rites] through application at the four times, one shall accomplish the activities.
In this regard, here is the *Vajrakula-karmasiddhi-tantra*:
Whatever action he performs for the sake of destroying wicked beings,
even within the Karma-vajra family, he is the bestower of all accomplishments.
In this regard, here is the *Padmakula-karmasiddhi-tantra*:
Bestowing fearlessness upon those who are fearful, he disciplines them according to their needs;
this is the bestower of the accomplishments of the Buddha through the activities of the Lotus Family. (2184) Now follows the Tantra of the Accomplishment of Activities for the Jewel Family.
Consecration as well as giving, which fulfills all hopes—
the activity of the Buddhas and of embodied beings indeed accomplishes all aims.
Thus [ends] the *Sarvakulakarmasiddhividhivistaratantra*.
Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi proclaimed the *Sarvatathāgatadharmatāmudrājñānasiddhi-tantra*.
In this regard, this is the *Tathāgatadharmatājñānasiddhi-tantra*:
"The meditative absorption of Vajrasattva is known as the *dharmatā* of the Buddhas."
This is the Buddhahood of the Buddha; the Buddha does not exist apart from this.
In this regard, there is this *Tathāgatakuladharmatājñānasiddhi-tantra*:
By meditating upon Mahāmudrā, one shall accomplish all siddhis;
even within the Tathāgata family, this bestows the supreme accomplishment of the nature of phenomena (dharmatā).
In this regard, there is this *Vajrakula-dharmatā-jñāna-siddhi-tantra*:
One should accomplish all activities by means of the bound [mudrās] of the supreme commitments;
through the application of the Mahāmudrā, one shall attain the Vajra-siddhi.
In this regard, there is this *Tantra of the Accomplishment of Knowledge of the Dharmatā of the Lotus Family*:
By means of the application of the Dharma-seal, one should set forth the Dharma-seal;
by accomplishing all phenomena through this, one realizes the true nature (*dharmatā*) of the Vajra-holder.
In this regard, there is this *Tantra of the Accomplishment of Wisdom regarding the True Nature of the Jewel Family*:

By means of the application of the *karmamudrā*, one meditates on the *karmavajra* abiding in the heart; by contemplating this very *dharmatā*, one attains the state of one's own activity. Thus ends the *Sarvakuladharmatājñānasiddhitantra*.
Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi proclaimed the *Sarvatathāgatajñānasiddhi-tantra*.
In this regard, this is the *Tathāgatajñānasiddhi-tantra*:
"Abiding in the samādhi of Vajrasattva through the application of the moon and the vajra,"
Just as he knows those two according to their color, so does he know the world.
It should be known that when [the mind] is pure, it is pure; when pale, it is luminous;
when red, it is red; and when agitated or angry, it is of the nature of whatever its color may be. (2195–2196)
In this regard, here is the *Tathāgatakulajñānasiddhi-tantra*.
Having established the Mahāmudrā, which possesses the radiance of a moon-maṇḍala,
one should know that the mind of the world is to be experienced just as one experiences one's own body.
In this regard, there is this *Vajrakula-jñānasiddhi-tantra*:
Whether in the sky or in another place, whatever mandalas one sees while being angry, such indeed is the great power (*mahaḥ*) to be understood.
In this regard, there is this *Padmakula-jñānasiddhi-tantra*:
Whether perceiving a subtle line of syllables upon the planes of space,
one knows the mind to be of whatever color [or nature] it possesses in brief.
In this regard, there is this *Maṇikulajñānasiddhi-tantra*:

"Indeed, observing the entire world, whatever kind of appearance it has, one sees the world exactly as such; yet one should perceive it as nothing but mind. (2200) These indeed are the meditative attainments (*samāpatti*), as well as the goings and comings.
Whether they are acting or wandering about, he proceeds in whatever manner he might perceive them. And by means of meditative absorption (*samāpatti*), whatever sentient being he may contemplate,
he understands all their thoughts in that very same way.
Thus spoke the Blessed One Vajragarbha. [This concludes] the Extensive Tantra of the Ritual for the Accomplishment of the Wisdom of All Families.
Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi proclaimed the Tantra of the Wisdom of the Accomplishments of All Tathāgatas.
In this regard, here is the *Tathāgata-siddhi-jñāna-tantra*: "Through the yoga of empowering sentient beings, one should meditate on the body as the image of the Buddha;
by means of this yoga of gnosis, one shall attain the accomplishment of a Buddha. (2206)
In this regard, here is the *Tathāgatakula-siddhijñāna-tantra*:
Whether in the sky or in another place, he perceives himself as his own mudrā-sattva within white and yellow luminous maṇḍalas, as if it were directly before him. (2207)
In this regard, here is the Vajra Family Siddhi-knowledge Tantra:
Within such very same images, one fixes upon a dark-blue [form];
the supreme siddhi of the Vajra Family shall quickly come to pass, whatever one desires. (2208)
In this regard, here is the Knowledge Tantra for the Accomplishment of the Lotus Family:
One sees those very [spaces] as blue like the sky and shaped like lotuses; indeed, the accomplishments of the vidyās arise within the Great Lotus Family. (2209)
In this regard, here is the *Maṇikulasiddhijñānatantra*:
"Whether in the sky or in another place, seeing those very same [deities], pure as the sky, flashing forth circles of light rays, one shall swiftly attain accomplishment. (2210)
Beings such as Vajrasattva and others, possessing the radiance of a moon-maṇḍala,
first manifest themselves in their own true forms at the time of accomplishment.
The Extensive Tantra of the Knowledge of Accomplishment for All Families.
Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi proclaimed the Tantra of the Knowledge-Seals for the Accomplishment of the Superknowledges of All Tathāgatas.
In this regard, here is the Tantra of the Accomplishment of the Superknowledges of the Tathāgatas:
Abiding in the samādhi of Vajrasattva, [one should visualize] the Tathāgatas within the entire body.
And while meditating, one should likewise manifest Bodhisattvas through the body.
In this regard, here is the tantra for the accomplishment of the supernormal knowledges of the Tathāgata family:
Having bound the great mudrā of Vajrasattva while well-composed,
the practitioner attains the five superknowledges through that method.
In this regard, this is the knowledge of the divine eye:
"By maintaining the Mahāmudrā, one should bring forth the visual consciousness;
whatever one then contemplates, one sees even from a great distance.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajrasattva. (2216–2217)
Having stabilized the Mahāmudrā, one should bring forth the auditory consciousness;
by means of that, whatever task one contemplates, even if situated at a great distance, one hears it.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajradhara. (2218–2219)
Having established the Mahāmudrā, one should bring forth the mental consciousness (*manovijñāna*). By means of that, whichever sentient being one gazes upon, he knows their mind.
Having established the Mahāmudrā, [one knows] either one's own or another's [mind].
"One perceives form with the mind; from that, one brings about birth.
Thus spoke the Blessed One Vajrapāṇi.
Then, the accomplishment of the knowledge of the methods of supernatural power occurs.
"Having attained the Mahāmudrā, whatever supernatural power one desires,
or wherever it may be, that indeed shall be manifested through meditative absorption.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, the Great Bodhicitta.
In this regard, here is the *Vajrakulābhijñāsiddhi-tantra*:
Having firmly bound the supreme *Trilokavijaya* mudrā with a well-concentrated mind, the practitioner attains the five supernormal knowledges (*pañcābhijñā*) by means of that ritual procedure. (2226)
"Being joyful, one should perform all activities correctly and in due order;
through the yoga of the divine eye and so forth, one attains all superknowledges (*abhijñā*) in an instant.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajrasattva. (2227–2228)
In this regard, here is the *Padmakula-abhijñāsiddhi-tantra*:
"By forming the *jagadvinaya-mudrā* with the syllable *grīṃ* while remaining well-composed, the practitioner attains the five superknowledges (*pañcābhijñā*) through that ritual procedure. (2229)
"But one who is agitated by passion, by following the ritual according to the proper sequence and through the yoga of the divine eye and so forth, shall become possessed of all superknowledges.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Lokeśvara.
In this regard, here is the *Maṇikula-abhijñā-siddhi-tantra*:
"Having bound the excellent mudrā of the accomplishment of all aims while well-composed, the practitioner attains the five superknowledges (*pañcābhijñā*) by means of that ritual procedure. (2232)
"Indeed, by performing the worship of the Buddha in due sequence,
he perceives the five superknowledges through the application of the divine eye and so forth.
Thus spoke the Blessed One Ākāśagarbha.
The Extensive Tantra of the Rites for the Knowledge and Accomplishment of the Superknowledges of All Families.
(2235) Then the Blessed One, the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, proclaimed the Tantra of the Accomplishment of the Truth of All Tathāgatas:
(2236) In this regard, this is the Tantra of the Accomplishment of the Truth of the Tathāgatas:
"By means of speech that follows the truth, one performs an act of oath;
by upholding the great truth, one shall swiftly attain Buddhahood.
Thus spoke the Blessed Buddha.
In this regard, here is the *Tathāgatakula-satyasiddhi-tantra*: An oath of commitment should be made by one arisen from the Tathāgata family;
by upholding the Vajra-truth, one attains the supreme accomplishment. (2239)
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajradhara.
In this regard, here is the *Vajrakula-satyasiddhi-tantra*:
Having made an oath difficult to transgress regarding the Vajradhārī, [one should proceed].
"One should protect the truth, for this indeed leads to the highest accomplishment," said the Blessed One Vajradhara. This is the *Padmakula-satyasiddhi-tantra*.
"Having established the True Dharma as the supreme of the Great Lotus family,
one should protect the samaya of truth if one desires the highest accomplishment.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajradharma.
In this regard, here is the Maṇikulasatyasiddhitantra:
Having made an inviolable oath regarding the worship of the Buddhas, one should maintain the supreme truth; thus, one shall obtain empowerment. (2245)
Thus spoke the Blessed One regarding the worship of the Buddha.
The Tantra of the Accomplishment of the Oaths of All Families.
(2247) Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi proclaimed the Tantra of the Accomplishment of the Reality of the Samaya of All Tathāgatas:
(2248) In this regard, this is the Tantra of the Accomplishment of the Reality of the Tathāgata Samaya:

"When 'You are the Samaya' is proclaimed, even among all the families of mudrās, they become firmly bound by one's own self; thereafter, they are no longer unaccomplished. Thus spoke the Blessed One, the Great Reality of the Samaya.
In this regard, there is this *Tathāgatasamayatatvasiddhi-tantra*:
When addressed with "O you who are in bliss," all mudrās that have not been previously accomplished will themselves be perfected when bound by the Great Being through the impelling of reality. (2251)
Thus spoke the Blessed One, the Reality of the Great Samaya.
In this regard, here is the *Vajrakula-samayatattvasiddhi-tantra*:
"By means of the single syllable HŪṂ alone, all mudrās are [accomplished] in brief."
"One should bind oneself, or cause another to be bound, or likewise cause oneself or another to be bound.
Regarding this, there is the *Padmakula-samayatattvasiddhi-tantra*:
"When 'all-pure' is proclaimed, whether for oneself or for another..."
"However, those unions resulting from attachment to women do not lead to liberation in any way whatsoever.
(2254) In this regard, there is this *Maṇikulasaṃmayatattvasiddhitantra*:
"In brief, all mudrās are accomplished by the syllable Oṃ alone."
"And they shall be the foremost in all worlds, and the objects of worship for the Self-Existent Ones.
Thus [ends] the *Sarvakulasamayatattvasiddhimudrāvidhivistaratantra*.
(2255) Then the Blessed One, the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, proclaimed the *Sarvatathāgatasiddhimudrātantra*: (2257)
In this regard, there is this *Tathāgata-siddhi-tantra*:
"By focusing upon the Buddha-mudrā while recollecting the Tathāgata, one who practices will swiftly achieve accomplishment, even the stable awakening of a Buddha. (2258)
In this regard, here is the *Tathāgatakula-siddhi-tantra*:
"Having bound the great mudrā of Vajrasattva and meditating upon it, with Vajrasattva before one, accomplishment will become even swifter. (2259)

In this regard, here is the *Vajrakula-siddhi-tantra*: "Having bound the supreme pledge (*samaya*) through the meditative absorption (*samādhi*) of Vajrasattva, and while visualizing Vajrasattva, one's accomplishment (*siddhi*) shall become twofold. (2260)

In this regard, here is the *Padmakula-siddhi-tantra*: "Having bound the mudrā consisting of the Dharma through the meditative absorption (*samādhi*) of Lokeśvara, and while visualizing the Lord of the World, one's accomplishment (*siddhi*) shall become twofold. (2261)

In this regard, here is the *Maṇikulāsiddhitantra*: "Having taken hold of the action-seal (*karmamudrā*) through the *vajragarbha* concentration and meditating upon *Vajragarbha*, accomplishment (*siddhi*) shall become twofold. (2262)
The Extensive Tantra of the Ritual Procedures for the Accomplishment of All Families.
(2263) Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi proclaimed the Tantra of the Means for Achieving All Siddhis of All Tathāgatas:
(2264) In this regard, this is the Tantra of the Means for Achieving All Siddhis of the Tathāgatas:
"Or else, one who practices mindfulness should visualize the Buddhas before oneself;
by binding all the mudrās, they will be accomplished at that very moment.
Thus spoke the Blessed Buddha.
In this regard, here is the *Tathāgatakulasarvasiddhisādhanatantra*:
One should accomplish all mudrās while contemplating, "I am Desire. Through the application of the vajra-recitation, this is the supreme accomplishment of all siddhis. (2267)
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajrasattva.
In this regard, here is the tantra for accomplishing all siddhis of the Vajra family:
Meditating with perfect concentration upon oneself as the Vajra-form, one’s own self...
"One should bind all the mudrās, for they indeed attain accomplishment at that very moment.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, the Vajra of All Tathāgatas.
In this regard, here is the tantra for the means of accomplishing the siddhi of the Lotus Family:
"Meditating upon oneself as a lotus-image by means of one's own self,
the accomplishment consisting of all-knowledge is attained in the Great Lotus Family," thus said the Blessed Lord Avalokiteśvara. (2271–2272)
In this regard, here is the *Maṇikulasarvasiddhisādhanatantra*:
One should visualize oneself as a jewel-gem (*maṇiratna*) blazing with light;
the accomplishment consisting of all worship is taught in the Great Jewel Family. (2273)
Thus spoke the Blessed One Ākāśagarbha. [End of] the Extensive Tantra of the Ritual Procedures for the Accomplishment of the Supreme of All Families.
Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi proclaimed the Tantra of the Accomplishment of the Mudrās Empowered by All Tathāgatas.
In this regard, here is the *Tathāgatādhiṣṭhānasiddhi-tantra*:
Having bound the mudrā of Vajradhātvīśvarī while remaining in meditative equipoise, and having placed it upon the heart, the *ūrṇā*, the throat, and the head, one is empowered by the Buddhas. (2277)
Thus spoke the Blessed One, the Buddha.
In this regard, there is this *Tathāgatakulādhiṣṭhānasiddhitantra*:
"Having made the Sattvavajrī firm through the *vajrasattva* samādhi,"
By placing [the hand] on the heart, the *ūrṇā* [between the eyebrows], the throat, and the head, one is empowered.
In this regard, there is this *siddhi-tantra* for the empowerment of the Vajra family:

"Having indeed bound the Vajra-hūṃkāra mudrā while being well-composed, [the practitioner] abides in meditative absorption at the heart, the ūrṇā, the throat, and the crown of the head at that very moment. Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajranātha.
In this regard, there is the *Padmakulādhiṣṭhānasiddhitant*ra:
Having made the vajra-lotus firm through the samādhi of Lokeśvara, [the mudrās] situated at the heart, the ūrṇā, the throat, and the head are suitable for one’s own empowerment. (2282)
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Avalokiteśvara.
In this regard, here is the *Maṇikula-adhiṣṭhāna-siddhi-tantra*:
Having bound the great vajra-jewel with the *Vajragarbha-samādhi*,...
"Residing in the heart, the *ūrṇā*, the throat, and the head, one should empower [them] for the sake of self-consecration.
Thus spoke the Blessed One Vajragarbha.
This concludes the extensive tantra of the ritual procedures for the accomplishment of the consecration of all families.
Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi proclaimed the *Sarvatathāgatābhiṣekamudrāsiddhitantra*.
In this regard, here is the *Tathāgatābhiṣekasiddhitantra*:
"Having placed the *vajraratna* [mudrā] so that it rests upon the forehead,"
"Having performed [the rite] with 'Vajraratna,' one shall be consecrated by the Victors.
Thus spoke the Blessed Buddha.
In this regard, here is the tantra for the accomplishment of the consecration of the Tathāgata family:
"Beginning with Vajradhātvīśvarī and the other Buddha-mudrās in front,
one is consecrated with a garland on the four sides. Thus,
herein is the *Vajrakula-abhiṣeka-siddhi-tantra*.
"Placing the vajra initiation garland upon the forehead, by means of that garland initiation, he is consecrated as a wielder of the vajra. Thus [ends the section].
Herein is this *Padmakula-abhiṣeka-siddhi-tantra*: (2291) (2292)

"Having visualized Dharmavajrī established before him at the crown of his head, he is consecrated by the Buddhas through her; thus, O excellent Lokeśvara, he is consecrated. (2293) Thus spoke the Blessed One Avalokiteśvara. (2294)
In this regard, here is the *Maṇikulābhiṣekasiddhitant*ra:
(2295) Having formed the Vajraratnāṅkurā mudrā and established it upon the forehead, one who is consecrated by that [mudrā] by the Buddhas is consecrated in the sovereignty of worship. (2296)
Thus spoke the Blessed One Ākāśagarbha.
(2297) This is the *Sarvakulābhiṣekasiddhitanttra*.
(2298) Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi proclaimed the *Sarvatathāgatasamādhisiddhitanttra*: (2299)
In this regard, here is the *Tathāgatasamādhisiddhi-tantra*:
Having bound the mudrā of all the Buddhas according to their forms and being composed in meditative absorption, one who recites the mantra-vidyās indeed swiftly attains accomplishment. (2300)
Thus spoke the Blessed Buddha.
Herein is this *Tathāgatakulasamādhisiddhi-tantra*.
"Through the yoga of the empowerment of sentient beings by means of the Vajradharma Samādhi,
the heart-mudrās, mantras, and vidyās are swiftly accomplished through recitation.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, the Buddha-Samādhi.
