In this regard, here is the *Vajrakula-samādhi-siddhi-tantra*:
"By contemplating, 'You have arisen from passion; I am Wrath,' one will achieve swift accomplishment of the heart-seals, mantras, and vidyās. (2204)
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajradhara.
In this regard, here is the *Samādhisiddhi-tantra* of the Lotus Family:
"Through the yoga of the mantra-practitioner’s emanation, one should accomplish the heart-mantra and the others."
"In the family of Lokeśvara, recitation quickly attains accomplishment.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, the Noble Avalokiteśvara.
In this regard, here is the tantra of the accomplishment of the samādhi of the Jewel Family:

"By cultivating the Sarvākāśa-samādhi while well-composed, and by means of the heart-seals, mantras, and vidyās, as well as the meditative absorptions, one shall become all-pervading. Thus spoke Ākāśagarbha.
The Extensive Tantra of the Rituals for the Accomplishment of the Samādhis of All Families.
(2310) Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi proclaimed the Tantra of the Accomplishment of the Mudrās for Worshipping All Tathāgatas:
(2311) In this regard, here is the Tantra of the Accomplishment of the Worship of the Tathāgatas:

"Having first performed worship with incense and other offerings while being well-composed, one who desires accomplishment, practicing accordingly, shall attain accomplishment. (2312) In this regard, here is the *Tathāgatakulapūjāsiddhitantra*:
"By means of the fourfold secret worship, proclaiming the secret of worship,
or performing worship through the offering of oneself and so forth, one attains accomplishment.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajrasattva.
In this regard, here is the *Vajrakulapūjāsiddhitant*ra:
"By proclaiming the great worship of the Wrathful Vajra and the secret of the Wrathful One, and by forming the wrathful fist, one will indeed swiftly attain accomplishment in my family. (2315)
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajradhara.
In this regard, here is the *Tantra of the Accomplishment of Worship for the Lotus Family*:
"Those [practices] proclaimed through the application of profound and sublime sūtras..."
By offering [this] with mind and speech, one shall swiftly attain accomplishment.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, the Noble Avalokiteśvara.
In this regard, there is this ritual manual for the accomplishment of the worship of the Jewel Family.
By honoring with parasols, banners, and flags, and by royal offerings, the entire family of jewels is accomplished; by giving gifts, one achieves success. Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajragarbha.
Endowed with self-consecration and the other [practices], one becomes equal to Vajrasattva;
through the four miraculous displays, one shall accomplish the universal vajra.
"All accomplishments," said the Blessed One Vajrasattva.
This concludes the extensive tantra concerning the ritual procedures for the accomplishment of empowerments, meditative absorptions, and worship through the empowerment of all families.
Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi proclaimed the *Sarvatathāgatābhijñājñānasiddhi-tantra*.
In this regard, this is the *Tathāgatābhijñājñānasiddhi-tantra*:
"The Buddha-samādhi in the body is indeed this self-mastery belonging to the Sugata."
"Because it is easily penetrated, one shall attain the accomplishment of a Buddha.
Thus [ends the section]. Herein is this *Tathāgatakulābhijñājñānasiddhitantra*:
"One who is well-composed, meditating upon the superknowledges (*abhijñā*) such as the divine eye and so forth..."
"Having personally attained the five superknowledges (*pañcābhijñā*), one shall attain the state of Vajrasattva.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajrasattva.
In this regard, here is the tantra for the accomplishment of the knowledge of the superknowledges of the Vajra family:
"Having generated the superknowledge of wrath and accomplishing [it] with a well-concentrated mind,
one becomes oneself possessed of the five superknowledges and shall attain supreme accomplishment.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajradhara.
In this regard, here is the *Padmakula-abhijñā-jñāna-siddhi-tantra*:

"Having generated the superknowledge of passion (*rāga-abhijñā*) and meditating with well-concentrated mind, one becomes oneself possessed of the five superknowledges and shall attain pure accomplishment. (2330)
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajranetra.
In this regard, here is the tantra for the accomplishment of the supernormal knowledge of the Jewel family:
Having generated the supernormal knowledge of worship, one should meditate with a well-composed mind.
"Having personally attained the five superknowledges (*pañcābhijñā*), one shall possess the supreme of all accomplishments.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajradhara.
This concludes the extensive tantra of the ritual procedures for the accomplishment of the knowledge of the superknowledges of all families.
Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi proclaimed the *Sarvatathāgata-mahābodhi-jñāna-siddhi-tantra*.
In this regard, this is the *Tathāgata-mahābodhi-jñāna-siddhi-tantra*:
Abiding in the samādhi of Vajrasattva and personally possessing the recollection of the Buddhas...
"This is the awakening of the Buddha; by cultivating this knowledge, one shall attain accomplishment.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, the Buddha.
In this regard, there is this *Tathāgatakulamahābodhijñānasiddhi-tantra*:

"Abiding in the samādhi of Vajrasattva and meditating upon Mahāmudrā, one who meditates upon this gnosis, which is Great Awakening, shall attain accomplishment. Thus spoke the Blessed One, the Mahābodhisattva.
In this regard, here is the Vajra Family Tantra for the Accomplishment of the Wisdom of Great Enlightenment.
"Abiding in the samādhi of the Wrathful King, grasping the foremost pledge-finger-seal,
one who meditates on this gnosis of great awakening shall attain accomplishment.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajradhara.
In this regard, here is the *Padmakula-mahābodhi-jñāna-siddhi-tantra*:
Abiding in the samādhi of Lokeśvara and likewise reciting the Dharma-mudrā, one who cultivates this great awakening as gnosis shall attain accomplishment. (2342)
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Avalokiteśvara.
In this regard, there is this Maṇikula-mahābodhi-jñāna-siddhi-tantra.
Abiding in the vajragarbha-samādhi and performing the virtuous deeds of the karmamudrā,
one who cultivates this gnosis of great awakening shall attain accomplishment.
Thus spoke the Blessed One Ākāśagarbha.
The Extensive Tantra of the Ritual Procedures for the Accomplishment of the Wisdom of Great Enlightenment of All Families.
(2346) Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi proclaimed the Tantra of the Accomplishment of the Pleasing of All Tathāgatas:
(2347) In this regard, this is the Tantra of the Accomplishment of the Pleasing of the Tathāgatas:

"Indeed, while performing the welfare of sentient beings, one who seeks the awakening of a Buddha oneself should possess the recollection of the Buddhas (*buddhānusmṛti*) in order to please all the Buddhas. Thus spoke Vajrarāga. (2348–2349)
In this regard, here is the Tantra of the Accomplishment of Delighting the Tathāgata Family.
"Having become as extensive as the object [of practice], one should accomplish Vajrasattva;
through the impelling of reality, being devoted, he quickly attains accomplishment.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajrasattva. (2350–2351)
In this regard, here is the *Vajrakulānurāgaṇasiddhi-tantra*.

"Indeed, for the sake of carrying out the Buddha's command against the wicked through sorcery, and for the sake of purifying sentient beings out of wrath, this is the Vajra-attachment. Thus spoke the Blessed One, Trailokyavijaya. (2352–2353)
In this regard, here is the *Siddhi-tantra* for the enchantment of the Lotus Family:
Beholding with passion, loving-kindness, compassion, preaching the Dharma, and granting fearlessness to all—this is the enchantment of all Buddhas. (2354)
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajranetra.
In this regard, this is the tantra for the accomplishment of the affection of the Jewel Family:
the bestowing of empowerment, and the giving of a collection of wealth.
"And that should be applied according to the meaning of the Buddha; this is the propitiation of the Buddha.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, the Noble Ākāśagarbha.
This concludes the extensive tantra of the ritual procedures for the accomplishment of the propitiation of all families.
Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi proclaimed the *Sarvatathāgatavaśīkaraṇasiddhitantra*.
In this regard, here is the *Tathāgatavaśīkaraṇasiddhitantra*:
"Passion indeed is not to be despised; it is pure and likewise very joyful."
"This yoga for the sake of all sentient beings brings about the subjugation of the Buddhas," said the Blessed One, the Buddha. In this regard, here is the *Tathāgatakulavaśīkaraṇasiddhitantra*:
"Having indulged in desire, you, whose nature is bliss, should speak thus:
'May I accomplish Vajrasattva, who is brought under control by the impulsion of reality.
Thus spoke the Blessed One Samantabhadra. (2362–2363)
In this regard, here is the Vajra Family Tantra for the accomplishment of subjugation.

"For the sake of purifying sentient beings through the Buddha’s command, for the sake of granting fearlessness to embodied beings, and for the sake of protecting the Buddha’s teaching, one should bring [the enemy] under control by slaying him. Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajrahūṃkāra.
In this regard, here is the *Padmakula-vaśīkaraṇasiddhitantra*:
Examining the purification of passion through the blossoming of a lotus petal, one should either delight or cause [the disciple] to be impassioned for the sake of discipline and subjugation. (2366)
Thus spoke the Blessed One, the Noble Avalokiteśvara.
In this regard, here is the tantra for the accomplishment of the subjugation of the Jewel Family:
For the sake of the consecration of all Buddhas, one should [offer] the Vajra-jewel day after day.
"Placing [the mantra] upon the head, one should be consecrated; thus one shall bring all Buddhas under control.
Thus spoke the Blessed One Ākāśagarbha.
This is the extensive tantra of the ritual procedure for the accomplishment of bringing all families under control.
Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi proclaimed the tantra of the accomplishment of the slaying of all Tathāgatas.
In this regard, this is the tantra of the accomplishment of the slaying of the Tathāgatas:
"Without perceiving the welfare of all sentient beings and without purifying the reality of the Buddha, one may attain accomplishment by killing [the enemy] through mind, body, or speech.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, the Tathāgata. (2372–2373)
In this regard, here is the *Tathāgatakulamāraṇasiddhitantra*:
"Due to the non-attainment of all accomplishments and the lack of exertion toward one's family, by striking with the vajra, one who kills achieves accomplishment swiftly. (2374)
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajrapāṇi.
In this regard, here is the tantra for the accomplishment of the slaying of the Vajra family:
"Because of wrath that subdues the undisciplined, and likewise because of the taming of non-beings..."
"And by inflicting suffering upon oneself, one should slay with the syllable *hūṃ*.
(2376) (Thus spoke the Blessed One Vajradhara. (Thus spoke the Blessed One Vajrahūṃkāra.
(2377) In this regard, here is the *tantra* for the accomplishment of slaying within the Lotus Family:
"Through lack of compassion, through lack of loving-kindness, through failing to purify wicked beings,
and through deceiving oneself, one may attain accomplishment while killing," so said the Blessed One Avalokiteśvara. (2378–2379)
In this regard, here is the *Maṇikula-māraṇasiddhi-tantra*:

"By killing [those who] cause harm to oneself through their failure to give, who steal one's wealth, and who bring suffering to sentient beings through poverty, one shall attain accomplishment. (2380)
Thus spoke the Blessed One, the Fulfilled One who fulfills all hopes:
"There are some who, through the application of non-attainment, act as Māras toward the Buddhas;
for the sake of uplifting them, we swiftly bestow accomplishment."
Thus spoke the Blessed One, the Noble Samantabhadra.
(2383) This is the extensive tantra of the ritual procedures for the accomplishment of the slaying of all families.
(2384) Then the Blessed One, the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, proclaimed the tantra of the accomplishment of the protection mudrās of all Tathāgatas. (2385)

In this regard, here is the *Tathāgatarakṣāsiddhitantra*: "Never abandoning any sentient being, always having the nature of making offerings to the Buddhas, and constantly attending to the mind of the Buddha—this is my most wondrous protection. (2386)
Thus spoke the Blessed Buddha.
In this regard, here is the *Tathāgatakularakṣāsiddhi-tantra*:
"The mere grasping of the name of Vajrasattva even once."
"This is the great, eternal protection that bestows accomplishment in an instant," said the Blessed One Vajradhara.
In this regard, there is this *Vajrakularakṣāsiddhitant*ra:

"Contentment within the vidyā-tantras, the nature of the Conqueror of the Three Worlds, and devotion to Vajrahūṃkāra— this is the protection of oneself or others," thus said the Blessed One Vajrahūṃkāra. (2390–2391)
In this regard, here is the *Padmakula-rakṣāsiddhi-tantra*:
"Purity from passion, great loving-kindness, the granting of fearlessness to sentient beings, and the recitation of the name of Lokeśvara—this is the supreme, most wonderful protection. (2392)
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajradharma.
In this regard, here is the *Maṇikularakṣāsiddhi-tantra*:
"One should make the divine service fruitful through practice according to one's capacity."
"Through renunciation and through the two—Buddha and Sattva—I shall protect [them] most wonderfully.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajrarakṣa. This is the extensive tantra for the ritual procedure of the accomplishment of protection for all families.
Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi said this to the Blessed One:
"Accept, O Blessed One, this tantra of the family of all Tathāgatas, by which all sentient beings, having attained mastery over all ritual procedures (*kalpa*), [shall achieve their goal]."
"They shall swiftly awaken to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
Thus [he spoke].
Then the Blessed One gave his approval to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi.

"Excellent, excellent, Vajrapāṇi! This well-spoken [teaching] has been accepted and empowered by us. (2399) Then all the Tathāgatas, having come together once more, bestowed words of praise upon the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi:
"Excellent to you, O Vajradatta; excellent to you, O Vajraratna! (2400)
"Excellent, excellent is it for you, O Vajradharma! Excellent is it for you, O Vajrakarman!
This sutra is well-spoken; it is the unsurpassed Vajrayāna, the secret of all Tathāgatas, and the great compendium of the Mahāyāna. Thus [it was said]. (2401–2402)
The *Sarvakalpopāyasiddhividhivistaratantra* from the *Sarvatathāgatatattvasaṃgraha* is completed.
(2403) The *Sarvakulakalpaguhyavidhivistaratantra*.
(2404) Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi proclaimed the *Sarvatathāgataguhyasiddhitantra*: (2405)
Therein, at the very beginning, is the *Tathāgatottamasiddhiguhyatantra*.
"By cultivating the samādhi of the Buddha's enlightenment while well-composed,
one realizes that enlightenment is attained with ease"—
thus spoke the Blessed One, the Tathāgata of all Tathāgatas. (2406–2407)
In this regard, here is the *Guhyatantra* for the supreme accomplishment of the Tathāgata family:
Having bound the Sattvavajrī at the heart and said, "You are my most beloved wife;
become firm," one shall accomplish all mudrās. (2408)

"By means of this application of ritual, even one who has not attained accomplishment through his own actions will attain accomplishment all the more once it is proclaimed that she is a secret consort.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Sattvavajra.
In this regard, here is the Secret Tantra of the Supreme Accomplishment of the Vajra Family:
"For in whatever way one is provoked to anger, by means of the Vajra-hūṃkāra mudrā, even while slaying all the Buddhas, they indeed grant accomplishment out of fear. (2411)
Thus spoke the Blessed One, the *Hūṃkāra* of all Tathāgatas.
In this regard, here is the secret tantra of the supreme accomplishment of the Lotus family:
Having assumed the samādhi-mudrā and gazing with the vajra-vision, [one should practice].
"Whether with one's own wife or another's wife, one attains the desired accomplishment.
Thus spoke the Blessed One Padmarāga.
In this regard, here is the Secret Tantra of the Accomplishment of the Supreme Family of Jewels:
"By the union of the two organs, bliss is supreme;
by offering one's own organ to all the Buddhas, one quickly attains accomplishment.
Thus spoke the Blessed One Maṇirāga. (2415–2416)
The Secret Tantra of the Accomplishment of the Supreme of All Families.
(2417) Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi proclaimed the Secret Tantra of the Accomplishment of the Samaya of All Tathāgatas:
(2418) In this regard, this is the Secret Tantra of the Accomplishment of the Samaya of the Tathāgatas:
"Having said, 'You are the Samaya,' one should cause all women to rejoice;
by saying, 'Do not cause beings to lose their passion,' one should cause the Buddhas to rejoice.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Mahāvairocana.
In this regard, here is the Secret Tantra of the Accomplishment of the Samaya of the Tathāgata Family:
"Passion indeed is not to be despised; one should delight all women.
By guarding this secret samaya of the Vajra-holder, one attains accomplishment. (2421)
Thus spoke the Blessed One Vairocana.
In this regard, here is the secret tantra of the accomplishment of the samaya of the Vajra family:
"One should slay the world by slaying it through the virtuous performance of the actions of body and speech."
"By means of the syllable *hūṃ*, for the sake of purification, the pledge (*samaya*) indeed bestows the accomplishment of one's aims. Thus spoke the Blessed One, Trailokyavijaya.
In this regard, there is this secret tantra of the accomplishment of the pledge of the Lotus Family (*padmakula*):
"The passion of those with pure souls is indeed pure, whereas that of the practitioners of other paths is impure;
by observing the commitment of those with pure souls, one shall attain accomplishment.
Thus spoke the Blessed Lord Avalokiteśvara. (2425–2426)
In this regard, here is the Secret Tantra of the Accomplishment of the Samaya of the Jewel Family:
Having first bound the Vajra-jewel through the *vajragarbha* concentration, one who takes away the wealth of the wicked becomes a bestower of the accomplishment of the samaya. (2427)
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajraratna.
(2428) This concludes the *Extensive Tantra of the Secret Ritual for the Accomplishment of the Samaya of All Families*.
(2429) Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi proclaimed the *Secret Tantra of the Dharma-Accomplishment of All Tathāgatas*: (2430)
In this regard, here is the *Tathāgatadharmasiddhiguhyatantra*:
"Meditating with a well-composed mind upon the intrinsic purity of all phenomena, one who performs all activities indeed attains the accomplishment of a Buddha. (2431)
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajradhātu.
In this regard, here is the Secret Tantra of the Accomplishment of the Dharma of the Tathāgata Family:
"The passion for all sentient beings and the lack of detachment toward sense objects."
"Purity through passion and the passionless is the secret dharma that bestows perfect accomplishment.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajraguhya.
In this regard, here is the Secret Tantra of the Accomplishment of the Dharma of the Vajra Family:

"By means of the yoga of the *hūṃ* syllable at the nose, slaying all malevolent beings while abiding in the subtle-vajra samādhi, one shall attain supreme accomplishment. Thus spoke the Blessed One, Dharmahūṃkāra.
In this regard, here is the *Guhyatantra* for the attainment of the Dharma of the Lotus Family:
"By means of the application of the subtle vajra, one should delight all women;
through the samādhi of Vajradharma, one attains the attainment of Dharma. (2437)
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Avalokiteśvara.
In this regard, there is this Secret Tantra of the Attainment of the Dharma of the Jewel Family:
"By means of the union of the two organs, fulfilling all hopes..."

"One attains unsurpassed accomplishment regarding women or those who are beloved," so said the Blessed One Vajraratna. This concludes the *Extensive Tantra of the Secret Ritual for the Accomplishment of the Dharmas of All Families*.
Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi proclaimed the Secret Tantra of the Accomplishment of the Activities of All Tathāgatas.
In this regard, here is the Tantra of the Accomplishment of the Activities of the Tathāgatas:
Abiding in the samādhi of Vajrasattva and cultivating the recollection of the Buddha, [one should practice].
"By entering the female organ for the sake of the woman's task, one shall bring women under control.
Thus spoke the Blessed Vairocana.
In this regard, there is this Secret Tantra of the Accomplishment of Ritual Actions in the Tathāgata Family:

"Abiding in the samādhi of Vajrasattva, entering through the vulva in that manner, one should cause the pledge to pervade the body of the woman; even she who is motionless shall be made to feel passion. Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajrarāga.
In this regard, here is the Secret Tantra of the Ritual Accomplishment of the Vajra Family:
Having firmly bound the Vajra-Hūṃkāra mudrā while well-composed, he should enter the bhaga in a state of wrath and cause it to fall by means of his mind. (2447)
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajrasamaya.
In this regard, here is the secret tantra for the accomplishment of the activities of the Lotus family:
Having bound the mudrā consisting of the activity of Dharma through the lotus samādhi,
"By entering through the *bhaga*, one should protect all women," so said the Blessed One, Vajrapadma.
In this regard, here is the Secret Tantra of the Accomplishment of Ritual Actions for the Jewel Family:
"Having bound the *karmavajramaṇi* through the *vajraratna-samādhi*, entering the vulva of women, one enters them instantly and dances.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajraratna. (2451–2452)
The Extensive Tantra of the Secret Ritual for the Accomplishment of the Activities of All Families.
(2453) Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi proclaimed the Secret Tantra of the Accomplishment of the Purity of the Maṇḍalas of All Tathāgatas:
(2454) In this regard, there is this Secret Tantra of the Accomplishment of the Purity of the Tathāgata Wheel:
One should fashion the secret maṇḍala in the form of the wheel of Dharma;
there, one should place the Buddha surrounded by his mudrā-consorts.
Having entered that very secret [maṇḍala], one should immediately address the Buddha.
"For these are indeed your wives, O Lord; grant them all to me.
By speaking thus regarding all the families and mudrās, one attains the secret accomplishment of the Buddhas, who possess incomparable splendor.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, the Buddha.
In this regard, here is the Secret Tantra of the Accomplishment of All Mandalas of the Tathāgata Family:
"One should draw a mandala resembling the Vajradhātu."
This is the supreme method for all the Tathāgata families.
One who desires accomplishment should enter the ritual maṇḍala and speak with haste:
"O Surata, you are the pledge! Hoḥ! Today, through Vajrasattva, may we attain accomplishment!"
Reciting this heart-mantra, one shall accomplish all siddhis; being satisfied through the yoga of the exhortation of reality, one attains success swiftly. Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajrasattva.
Now, this is the *Vajrakula-sarvamaṇḍala-guhyasiddhi-tantra*:
"The wise one should indeed draw the yoga of all maṇḍalas in the form of Trilokavijaya, for it belongs to the entire Vajra family. (2463)
"Having entered that very place, one should quickly speak while requesting success:
'Through passion you have arisen; thus it is accomplished for all.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajrahūṃkāra. (2464–2465)

In this regard, here is the *Padmakula-maṇḍala-guhya-siddhi-tantra*: "By means of the yoga for subduing the world, the wise one should indeed draw the maṇḍalas within all the Padma families; having entered it, he should speak. (2466)
"O Great Lotus of the Passion-nature, O All-pervading Lord, grant me swift accomplishment!
Having spoken thus, he attains success in all mandalas.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Avalokiteśvara.
In this regard, here is the *Maṇikulamaṇḍalaguhyasiddhitantra*:
"One should draw the mandalas through the yoga of the accomplishment of all aims. Having established that [mandala] of the great jewels, one should then speak. (2469)
Among all the accomplishments of one's intentions, the accomplishment of desire and aspiration is supreme.
"Accomplish! Accomplish! O Great Being, Blessed One, for the sake of all accomplishment!
Speaking thus, one should enter into all mandalas.
One attains the supreme secret worship, which is the great accomplishment (mahāsiddhi). From that time forward, the self-perfected one constantly accomplishes the various attainments;
when an attainment is not easily achieved, it is perfected through the impelling of reality (tattva).
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajrasattva.
(2473) This is the *Sarvakulamaṇḍalaguhyasiddhividhivistaratantra*.
(2474) Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi proclaimed the *Sarvatathāgatasarvamudrāguhyasiddhitantra*: (2475)
In this regard, here is the *Tathāgatamudrāguhyasiddhi-tantra*:
"The great goddesses of the Tathāgatas are beloved and bestow all happiness;
by the truth that follows after them, and by the truth of their speech, they swear that there is nothing that cannot be accomplished."
"By means of truthful and consistent words, that which is not accomplished will be accomplished.
Thus spoke the Buddha, the Blessed One.
In this regard, there is this *Guhyasiddhi-tantra* of the Great Seal (*mahāmudrā*) of the Tathāgata family:
Having properly bound the mahāmudrā in its successive stages, one should speak this reality and secret according to the method with vajra-words:
"I am Vajrasattva himself; you are my consort, dwelling within my heart. (2478)
Embracing the entire body, raise it up with vajra-pride.
(2479) The Great Goddess Vajragarvā, impassioned by the exhortation of reality, having become firm throughout the entire body, quickly attains accomplishment as prescribed. (2480)
Thus spoke the Blessed One, the Lord of Vajragarvā.
In this regard, here is the *Guhyasiddhi-tantra* of the Samaya-mudrā of the Vajra Family: "Be accomplished, be accomplished! O you who abide in the pledge, I am the pledge; you are my beloved."
"By such an exhortation, she who is quickly enamored attains accomplishment.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajrasamaya.
In this regard, here is the *Guhyasiddhi-tantra* concerning the Dharma-mudrā of the Lotus Family:
"Awake, awake, O Great Being! You are my most beloved wife.
By this exhortation, she quickly becomes devoted and attains accomplishment.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajradharma.
In this regard, here is the *Guhyasiddhitant*ra of the Action Seal (*karmamudrā*) of the Jewel Family (*maṇikula*):
"O Vajriṇī, you who perform all activities, may you be my wife; may you be accomplished for me today.
By such an exhortation, she who is quickly impassioned indeed attains accomplishment. (2486)
Thus spoke the Blessed One Ākāśagarbha.
(2487) This is the extensive tantra of the ritual procedures for the secret accomplishments of all mudrās of all families.
(2488) Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi proclaimed the tantra of the secret accomplishment of the samaya of all Tathāgatas. (2489)
In this regard, there is this *Tathāgata-samayaguhya-siddhi-tantra*:
"For the sake of benefiting the non-Buddhists (*tīrthika*), the Buddhas' consorts have been kept secret;
by understanding that they are to be depicted through the application of mudrās, one attains accomplishment. (2490)
Thus spoke the Blessed One, the pledge of all Tathāgatas.
In this regard, there is this *Tathāgatakula-samayaguhyasiddhi-tantra*:
"Pervading the minds of all sentient beings, bestowing happiness upon all sentient beings."
"He is the father of all sentient beings and the supreme desire of those who hold the foremost commitments.
Thus spoke the Blessed Ones, the Tathāgatas of all [times].
This is that most wondrous secret of all the Buddhas.
Having understood this and possessing faith, even one who is difficult to discipline shall indeed achieve success.
In this regard, there is this *Vajrakula-samayaguhyasiddhi-tantra*.
"For those who are detached for the sake of purifying passion, yet whose selves are fashioned by the views of non-Buddhist outsiders,
success is achieved upon understanding this supreme *samaya* of slaying.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajradhara.
In this regard, here is the *Padmakula-samayaguhya-siddhi-tantra*:
"How can everything that arises from the great elements be called impure?
For the destruction of the heretics, one will certainly attain accomplishment. (2499)
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajranetra.
In this regard, here is the *Maṇikulasamayaguhyasiddhi-tantra*.
"When a collection of jewels is made through attachment to women,
he succeeds by thinking, 'Women are indeed the unsurpassed jewel.
Thus spoke the Blessed One Ājñākara.
The *Viṣataratantra*, the ritual procedure for the secret accomplishment of the commitments (*samaya*) of all families.
Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi proclaimed the *Guhyasiddhitantra* of the worship of all Tathāgatas.
In this regard, this is the *Guhyasiddhitantra* of the worship of the Tathāgatas:

"Having surrounded himself with women and surrendered the pleasure of playful dalliance for the sake of worshipping the Buddha, he shall attain the perfection of worship. Thus spoke the Blessed Buddha.

In this regard, here is the *Guhyasiddhitantro* for the worship of the Tathāgata family: "One who is exhausted by the fatigue of sexual union, having offered that bliss born of sexual union through the fourfold prostration-worship, quickly attains accomplishment. (2506)
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajradhara.
In this regard, here is the *Vajrakulapūjāguhyasiddhitant*ra:
Having bound the *hūṃ*-syllable pledge (*samaya*) and embraced a woman, a person...
"Indeed, by offering that bliss of embrace, he attains accomplishment.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajrahūṃkāra.
In this regard, here is the secret tantra for the accomplishment of worship in the Lotus Family:
"Having visualized himself as Lokeśvara and gazing indeed at the face of his beloved,
he attains accomplishment by offering up that very bliss of gazing.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Padmanetra.
In this regard, here is the Secret Tantra of the Accomplishment of Worship for the Jewel Family:
Having assumed the form of a karma-mudrā and being adorned with all ornaments, one embraces a woman and, having offered her as an embellishment in worship, attains accomplishment. (2512)

Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajraratna. (2513) This is the Extensive Tantra of the Secret Ritual for the Accomplishment of Worship for All Families. (2514) Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi brought forth the Tantra of the Accomplishment of the Secret Worship of All Tathāgatas. (2515)
In this regard, here is the *Tathāgataguhyasiddhipūjāsiddhi-tantra*:
"Delighting in the wives of others so that no one may know, and meditating on oneself as the Buddha, one shall attain accomplishment through worship. (2516)
Thus spoke the Blessed One, the Buddha.
In this regard, here is the *Tathāgatakulaguhyapūjāsiddhitantra*:
Having entered the meditative absorption (*samādhi*) of Vajralāsyā, one should bind the Vajramālā [mudrā].
Then, having performed the Vajra-song, one should worship with the Vajra-dance.
Through the bliss of dance and song, there is a bliss superior to the consecration of sensual delight;
for there is nothing else [superior], and thus this secret worship is unsurpassed. (2518–2519)

In this regard, here is the *Vajrakulaguhyapūjāsiddhitant*ra: By worshipping according to the prescribed application of ritual through secret worship, and meditating upon Trilokavijaya, one shall attain the accomplishment of worship. (2520)
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajraguhya.
In this regard, here is the *Padmakula-guhyapūjāsiddhi-tantra*:
"Worshipping with the secret yoga in accordance with the ritual manual upon the action seals (*karmamudrā*)."
"Abiding in the mudrā of the world’s discipline, one attains the accomplishment of worship.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Avalokiteśvara.
Herein lies the Maṇikula-guhyapūjāsiddhi-tantra.
"One should accomplish [the goal] through the secret yoga with respect to the action seals (*karmamudrā*) according to the rule;
through the yoga of the accomplishment of all aims, one attains the perfection of worship.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajragarbha. (2524–2525)
The Extensive Tantra of the Ritual Procedures for the Accomplishment of Secret Worship of All Families.
(2526) Then the Blessed One, the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, proclaimed the Tantra of the Secret Accomplishment that Reveals the Families of All Tathāgatas.
(2527) In this regard, here is the Secret Tantra of the Accomplishment of the Arising of the Reality of the Tathāgata:
"Buddhahood indeed arises from the knowledge of meditative concentration; in brief, through the application of the multitude of sentient beings, one swiftly attains the unsurpassed.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, the Tathāgata. (2528–2529)
In this regard, here is the Secret Tantra of the Accomplishment of Revealing the Great Reality of the Tathāgata Family.
The sentient being (*sattva*) is without beginning or end, characterized by arising from space;
he is Samantabhadra, the self of all, desire, and the lord of the entire world.
That mind which belongs to all sentient beings is called "sentient being" because of its firmness.
Through meditative absorption, one becomes equal to a vajra; through certainties, one attains the state of a vajra.
(2531) By means of the yoga of the empowerment of sentient beings, one further becomes Vajrasattva.
That very Blessed One, the Being, is the Tathāgata Vajrakāma. (2532)
"The awakening of a Buddha arises from the penetration of one's own mind according to the prescribed method;
that very Blessed One becomes the entire family of all Tathāgatas.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, the Being without beginning or end.
"That very [family] is the Tathāgata family; that very one is known as the Vajra family;
that very pure one is the Padma family; and that very one is said to be the excellent Maṇi family.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, the Wheel of All Tathāgatas.
The Extensive Tantra of the Secret Siddhi for Producing All Families.
(2537) Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi proclaimed the Secret Tantra of the Siddhi for Designating the Mudrās of All Tathāgatas:
(2538) In this regard, there is this Secret Tantra of the Siddhi for Designating the Emblems of the Tathāgatas.
"That very Blessed One, the being Vajrasattva, abides in the heart;
through meditative absorption, he is indeed the samādhi that accomplishes the awakening of the Buddhas.
Thus spoke the Blessed Buddha.
In this regard, here is the *Guhyatantra* concerning the accomplishment of the designations for the emblems of the Tathāgata family:

The vajra is so called because of its excellent penetration; the hook (*aṅkuśa*) is that which releases those who are seized; the arrow is so called because of its subtle piercing; and the bell is the form of the practitioner, [bestowed] out of joy. (2541)

The jewel is so called because of its arrangement; the sun is so called because of its bestowal of brilliance; the banner is declared to be the upward elevation; and the smile is celebrated as laughter.
The lotus is [so called] due to the purity of passion; the sheath is [so called] from the cutting down of the enemy that is the afflictions.
The wheel [is so called] through its union with the mandala; recitation is said to arise from vocal discourse.
(2543) The "all-vajra" is due to its universal nature; armor is due to the yoga of being impenetrable.
Fangs are due to the yoga of being terrifying; binding is due to the application of mudrās. (2544)
"Just as the Blessed One Vajrasattva is eternally all-pervading,
so too one succeeds by meditating upon the vajra, the insignia, and so forth.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, the insignia of all the Tathāgatas.
The Secret Tantra of the Accomplishment of the Designations of the Emblems of All Families.
(2547) Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi proclaimed the Secret Tantra of the Accomplishment of the Arising of the Binding of the Mudrās of All Tathāgatas.
(2548) In this regard, this is the Secret Tantra of the Accomplishment of the Arising of the Binding of the Mudrās of the Tathāgatas.
"Having bound the vajraparyaṅka with both hands through the vajrabandha,
and abiding in the samādhi of Vajrasattva, one shall swiftly attain Buddhahood.
Thus spoke the Blessed Buddha.

In this regard, here is the *Guhyatantra* on the arising and accomplishment of the binding of mudrās for the Tathāgata family: Just as a royal edict is sealed with the king’s own seals, so too are people sealed by the seals of those of great soul. (2551)
"Through the application of the reflections of the vajras of body, speech, and mind,
one succeeds by realizing that this is the Mahāmudrā of the Great Beings.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Mudra.
In this regard, here is the Secret Tantra on the Arising and Accomplishment of the Binding of Mudrās of the Vajra Family:
"Just as a person might be bound by intense commitments (*samaya*) that cannot be transgressed, so too are all the Tathāgatas. (2554)

"For those who are bound by the supreme mudrā of the vajra-bind and by the bonds of the samaya, they do not transgress [the vow] until death; knowing this, one attains accomplishment. Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajrasamaya.
In this regard, here is the *Guhyatantra* on the arising and accomplishment of the binding of the Dharma-family mudrās:
"Indeed, the vajra-speech is in no way to be transgressed by the Victors;
knowing that 'this is the binding,' one's Dharma will be accomplished. (2557)
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajradharma.
In this regard, here is the secret tantra for the accomplishment of the arising of the binding of mudrās in the Action Family:
"For the command of Vajra and its extensive activity are indeed not to be transgressed;
however, by one who possesses the command, that activity, once understood, is swiftly accomplished.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajra.
The Extensive Secret Tantra on the Arising and Accomplishment of the Binding of Mudrās for All Families. (2561) Then the Blessed One spoke thus to the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi:
"Blessed One, this too has been accepted and empowered by me. (2562)
Then all the Tathāgatas, having come together once more, offered words of praise to Vajrapāṇi, the sovereign of all Tathāgatas:
“Excellent, O Vajrasattva! Excellent, O Vajraratna!
Excellent, O Vajradharma! Excellent, O Vajrakarman!”
This well-spoken sūtra is the unsurpassed Vajrayāna, the secret of all Tathāgatas, the compendium of the Mahāyāna.
Thus [ends the section]. From the *Sarvatathāgatatattvasaṃgraha*, the extensive tantra of the secret ritual procedures for the kalpas of all families is completed.
(The Detailed Ritual of the Supreme Secret Tantra of All Kalpas) (2567) Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi proclaimed the *Sarvatathāgatadharmottamasiddhitantra*.
(2568) In this regard, this is the *Tathāgatadharmottamasiddhitantra*:
"By cultivating the meditative absorption on the qualities of a Buddha while well-composed,
one indeed attains the supreme accomplishment through the yoga of the recollection of the Buddha.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, the Tathāgata.
In this regard, here is the *Tathāgatakuladharmottamasiddhi-tantra*:

Abiding in the meditative absorption of all sentient beings and visualizing with a well-composed mind, one shall attain the supreme accomplishment through the yoga of the recollection of passion. (2571)
Thus spoke the Blessed One, the Samādhi of all Tathāgatas.
In this regard, here is the *Vajrakula-dharmottama-siddhi-tantra*:
"Meditating likewise before oneself on the form of Trilokavijaya..."
"Having become possessed of the power of Vajrapāṇi, one shall be a conqueror of the three worlds.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajrasattva.
In this regard, here is the *Padmakula-dharmottama-siddhi-tantra*:
"Meditating thus upon the Dharma of the world's discipline before him,
he effects the discipline endowed with the excellence of all aspects.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajradharma.
In this regard, here is the *Maṇikuladharmottamasiddhitantra*:
By meditating thus before him upon the form of the accomplishment of all aims, endowed with the excellence of all aspects, one shall obtain every prosperity. (2577)
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajrapāṇi. This is the extensive tantra of the ritual procedures for the supreme accomplishment of the dharmas of all families.
Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi proclaimed the tantra of the accomplishment of the samaya of the dharmas of all Tathāgatas.
In this regard, here is the *Tathāgata-dharma-samaya-siddhi-tantra*:

Having become possessed of the recollection of the Buddha (*buddhānusmṛti*), and uttering "Vajra, Vajra," one attains the accomplishment of a Buddha through the application of the subtle vajra. (2581)
Thus spoke the Blessed One, the Buddha.
In this regard, here is the *Tathāgatakuladharmasamayasiddhi-tantra*.
"Meditating upon the samādhi of Vajrasattva through the subtle vajra, one attains the state of Vajrasattva while reciting 'Vajrasattva,'" said the Blessed One, Vajrasattva. (2583–2584)
In this regard, here is the *Vajrakula-dharmasamaya-siddhi-tantra*:
While recollecting the form of Trilokavijaya in that manner before him, and uttering "HŪM HŪM HŪM HŪM," one attains unsurpassed accomplishment. (2585)
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajrahūṃkāra.
In this regard, here is the *Tantra of the Accomplishment of the Dharma-Samaya of the Lotus Family*:
"Meditating upon the form that disciplines the world from the subtle vajra,"
"By uttering 'Purify! Purify!', one shall indeed attain the supreme accomplishment.
Thus spoke the Blessed One Vajradharma.
In this regard, there is this *Tantra of the Accomplishment of the Dharma-Samaya of the Jewel Family*:
"Meditating on the form of the accomplishment of all aims from the subtle vajra,
and uttering 'Siddhya Siddhya,' the supreme accomplishment of aims shall indeed occur.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Maṇidharma.
The Extensive Tantra of the Rituals for the Accomplishment of the Samaya of the Dharmas of All Families.
(2591) Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi proclaimed the Tantra of the Accomplishment of the Wisdom of the True Dharma of All Tathāgatas:
(2592) In this regard, this is the Tantra of the Accomplishment of the Wisdom of the True Dharma of the Tathāgatas.
The true Dharma, which arises from meditative concentration and primordial wisdom, follows each syllable;
therefore, the letter *a* is traditionally understood as the non-arising (*anutpāda*) of all phenomena.
Then, by cultivating through wisdom this application of the seal, one proceeds.
"The gnosis consisting of all syllables, which belongs to the Sugata, is accomplished in an instant.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, the Noble Mañjuśrī, who is all the Tathāgatas.
In this regard, there is this *Tathāgatakula-saddharmajñānasiddhi-tantra*.
"O Śaradadhan, by upholding and reciting this sūtra, which is the reality of all Tathāgatas, one attains unsurpassed accomplishment.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajrasattva.
In this regard, here is the *Vajrakula-saddharmajñānasiddhi-tantra*:
"For the sake of benefiting beings who are evil, for carrying out the commands of the Buddha, and for the sake of disciplining the wicked, one achieves success through killing. (2598)
Thus spoke the Blessed One, the Vajra Family.
In this regard, here is the *Padmakula-saddharmajñānasiddhi-tantra*:
"Having realized intrinsic purity, it is known as the ultimate reality (*paramārtha*)."
"By meditating upon this primordial [mantra], one quickly attains accomplishment through the Dharma.
Thus spoke the Blessed Lord Avalokiteśvara.
In this regard, there is this *Maṇikulasa-ddharmajñānasiddhi-tantra*:
"By practicing this Dharma of the Jewel Family for the sake of giving to all sentient beings and for the fulfillment of all hopes, one quickly attains accomplishment.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Dharmaratna.
The Extensive Tantra of the Rites for Attaining the Knowledge of the Dharmas of All Families.
(2604) Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi proclaimed the Tantra of the Accomplishment of the Ritual Actions of the Samādhis of All Tathāgatas.
(2605) In this regard, here is the Tantra of the Accomplishment of the Ritual Actions of the Samādhis of the Tathāgatas:
"The activity of the meditative absorption of the Buddhas accomplishes the awakening of the Buddhas;
by cultivating this, one shall attain supreme accomplishment.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajradhātu. (2606) (Tib.)
Thus spoke the Blessed One, the Buddha.
(2607) In this regard, here is the *Tathāgatakulasamādhikarmasiddhitantra*:
"The activity of the Vajrasattva samādhis is supreme and vast."
"It is accomplished through the realization that the universal [form] is the hand of all sentient beings.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajra.
In this regard, there is this *Vajrakula-samādhi-karma-siddhi-tantra*:
"For the purpose of purifying evil, the slaying of all beings—which subdues all sins—is accomplished for those who possess faith. Thus spoke the Blessed One, the Vajrī. (2610–2611)

In this regard, here is the *Padmakula-samādhi-karmasiddhi-tantra*: "With his self purified of all evils through universal purification, he performs all activities; by the realization that 'this is action,' he attains accomplishment. (2612)
Thus spoke the Blessed One Padma.
In this regard, here is the tantra for the accomplishment of the activities of the Maṇi-family samādhi.
"Fulfilling all the hopes of the poor who eat all things, the All-Self, Sarvārthasiddhi, is accomplished; there is no doubt about this. Thus spoke the Blessed One Ratnadhvaja.
The Extensive Tantra of the Ritual Procedures for the Accomplishment of the Samādhi and Activities of All Families.
(2616) Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi proclaimed the Tantra of the Accomplishment of the Subtle Wisdom of All Tathāgatas.
(2617) In this regard, this is the Tantra of the Accomplishment of Subtle Wisdom:
"By constantly applying the subtle vajra method in every respect,
one shall attain the five superknowledges endowed with the excellence of all forms.
Thus spoke the Blessed Buddha.
In this regard, here is the *Tathāgatakula-sūkṣmajñāna-siddhi-tantra*.

"One should not reveal these mudrās before anyone other than an Ācārya, nor before one who is not a disciple, nor before one who has no son; for their accomplishment is attained through extreme secrecy. Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajradhara.
In this regard, here is the *Vajrakula-sūkṣmajñāna-siddhi-tantra*:
"By means of the application of the subtle vajra, through the yoga of the syllable *HŪṂ* at the nose, and abiding in the samādhi of Vajrakrodha, one shall accomplish all activities. (2622)
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajra.
In this regard, here is the *Padmakula-sūkṣmajñāna-siddhi-tantra*.
"By maintaining the vajra-gaze through the application of the subtle vajra,
one who abides in the great lotus-samādhi shall attain the siddhi of passion.
Thus spoke the Blessed One Padmarāga.
In this regard, here is the *Maṇikulasūkṣmajñānasiddhitantra*:
With a blazing gaze and through the extremely subtle *vajraratna-samādhi*, by means of the application of the subtle *vajra*, one shall become an attractor of all objects. (2626)
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajrapāṇi.
(2627) This is the *Sarvakulasūkṣmajñānasiddhi-tantra*.
(2628) Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi proclaimed the *Sarvatathāgatacakṣurjñānasiddhi-tantra*: (2629)
In this regard, here is the *Tathāgatacakṣurjñānasiddhi-tantra*:
"When a mudrā or a meditative absorption (*samādhi*) is employed for the sake of accomplishment, then he sees auspicious forms there as they rush through the sky. (2630)
"Then, O wise one, know this to be my Buddha-eye;
from that time forth, one shall accomplish all the rites of the Buddhas.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, the Buddha.
In this regard, here is the *Tathāgatakulacakṣurjñānasiddhi-tantra*:
"Whatever entities exist, whether stationary or moving, one sees their reflections racing through the sky. (2633)
"Whether they are coming or going, by knowing the purity of the vajra-eye and indeed honoring them, one attains unsurpassed accomplishment.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajrasattva.
In this regard, here is the *Vajrakula-cakṣur-jñāna-siddhi-tantra*:
With his eyes, he sees those [visions] revolving to the right and left in the sky—realms of space rapidly whirling, resembling clouds. (2636)
"Indeed, upon seeing those mudrās born of the Vajra, one should not pierce them;
through the grasping of those [mudrās], the mudrās are accomplished for one who has the eye of mudrā.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajra.
In this regard, here is the *Padmakulacakṣurjñānasiddhi-tantra*:
"When they see mandalas that are white, red, white, or yellow, then, by means of focused contemplation, those with the vajra-eye proceed toward and attain accomplishment. (2639)
Thus spoke the Blessed One Vajrapadma.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Avalokiteśvara.
In this regard, here is the *Maṇikula-cakṣur-jñāna-siddhi-tantra*:
"In the sky, [it is] like a jewel; in gold and other such things, it is similar."
"But when one with the eye of space sees within the sky, one always attains accomplishment.
Thus spoke the Blessed One Vajragarbha.
This concludes the extensive tantra of the ritual for the accomplishment of the knowledge of the eyes of all families.
Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi proclaimed the *Sarvatathāgatakarmottamasiddhitantra*.
In this regard, this is the *Sarvatathāgatakarmottamasiddhitantra*:
"By means of the yoga of the karma-maṇḍala, one should worship all the Leaders."
"For the sake of the ripening of the bliss of passion, one shall attain the accomplishment of Buddhahood.
Thus spoke the Blessed Buddha.
In this regard, there is this *Tathāgatakarmottamasiddhi-tantra*:
"Performing the secret worship while contemplating, 'I am passion,' one shall attain the supreme accomplishment, possessing a splendor equal to Vajrarāga. Thus spoke the Blessed One, Kāma.
In this regard, here is the Tantra of the Supreme Accomplishment of Vajra Action:
"Performing the secret worship while contemplating, 'I am the Wrathful One,' one shall attain the supreme accomplishment, the most excellent victory over the three worlds. (2649)
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajrapāṇi.
In this regard, here is the *Tantra of the Supreme Accomplishment of the Rituals of the Family of Words*:
"Meditating on the purity of desire with a mind directed inwardly..."
"By worshipping the Buddhas with drops of one's own semen, one shall attain accomplishment.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Avalokiteśvara.
In this regard, here is the *Maṇikula-karmottama-siddhi-tantra*:
Maintaining the pride of the Vajra, one should bow with a heart shaken by devotion;
being constantly supreme in prostration, one shall attain consecration.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, the Jewel of Vajra Consecration.
The Extensive Tantra of the Ritual Procedures for the Supreme Accomplishment of the Activities of All Families.
(2655) Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi proclaimed the Secret Accomplishment Tantra of the Samaya of the Activities of All Tathāgatas:
(2656) In this regard, this is the Secret Accomplishment Tantra of the Samaya of the Activities of the Tathāgatas:
All pleasures, beginning with desire, always abide within my heart.
Oh, how marvelous is that which is called "the welfare of sentient beings," wherein detachment is taught!
For this is the ritual of action through the samādhi of the Tathāgata.
"Meditating thus, one should worship the Buddhas and attain the supreme accomplishment.
(2658) Thus spoke the Blessed Buddha.
(2659) In this regard, there is this *Tathāgatakarmasamayaguhyasiddhi-tantra*:
"I am Samantabhadra, the one who bestows happiness upon all sentient beings; abiding in the samādhi of Vajrasattva, one shall attain accomplishment through worship. Thus spoke the Blessed One, Kāma.
In this regard, here is the *Vajrakula-karmasamayaguhyasiddhi-tantra*:
"I am Samantabhadra-Krodha, the benefactor of all sentient beings.
By worshipping through the yoga of Vajra-Hūṃkāra, one shall attain accomplishment. (2662)
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajrapāṇi.
In this regard, there is this *Guhyasiddhi-tantra* of the Action Samaya of the Lotus Family:
"I am Samantabhadra-rāga, the self-bestower of all bliss."
"Abiding in the form of the discipline of the world, one who worships shall attain accomplishment.
Thus spoke the Blessed One Padmarāga.
In this regard, there is this *Maṇikulakarmasamayaguhyasiddhi-tantra*.
"I am King Samantabhadra, the bestower of the great benefit upon all sentient beings.
By worshipping in the form of Sarvārthasiddhi, one shall attain accomplishment.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Sarvārthasiddhi.
The Extensive Tantra of the Secret Accomplishment of the Rituals and Samayas of All Families.
(2668) Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi proclaimed the Tantra of the Supreme Accomplishment of the Dharmatā of the Activity of All Tathāgatas.
(2669) O Vajra! In this regard, here is the Tantra of the Supreme Accomplishment of the Dharmatā of the Activity of the Tathāgatas:
"Facing south, with the foremost [deity] in front, one should bind the armor by means of one's own meditative absorption;
established thus in the uṣṇīṣa, it will provide ultimate protection.
Thus spoke the Blessed Buddha.

In this regard, here is the *Tathāgatakula-karmadharmatottama-siddhi-tantra*: Having drawn the form of a vulva upon a wall with a protruding phallus, whichever woman one contemplates, even if she be old, she shall be brought under his control. (2672)
Thus spoke the Blessed One, the Noble Vajrapāṇi.
In this regard, here is the Tantra of the Supreme Accomplishment of the Dharma-nature of the Rituals of the Vajra Family:
Having drawn the face of a yakṣa upon the ground, one should [draw] the nail from the tip of whichever finger is foremost.
"Having struck [the target] at the location of the eyes, one should draw [it] forth; these are the excellent women," so said the Blessed One, Vajrasattva.
In this regard, here is the *Padmakula-karmadharmatottama-siddhi-tantra*:
Holding a lotus with both hands and contemplating the purity of passion,
he should likewise lead the women to their ultimate goal by means of the vajra-gaze.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajradhara.
In this regard, here is the *Maṇikula-karmadharmanottama-siddhi-tantra*:
Abiding in the *vajraratna* samādhi and holding a jewel in his hand, through the yoga of the *ratna-hūṃkāra*, he may subjugate all women. (2678)

Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajrahūṃkāra. (2679) This is the extensive tantra of the ritual procedures for the supreme accomplishment of the dharmatā of the activities of all families. (2680) Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi proclaimed the tantra of the accomplishment of the ritual activities of all Tathāgatas. (2681)
In this regard, here is the *Tathāgatakarmakāryasiddhitant*ra:
Having applied the ritual procedure for the act of worship, whatever task one intends to perform, the wise practitioner, having made that known, should accomplish the mudrā. (2682)
"Thus spoke the Blessed One Vajradhātu;
thus spoke the Blessed One Buddha.
(2683) In this regard, there is this *Tantra of the Accomplishment of the Ritual Activities of the Tathāgata Family*.
"By applying the procedure for the secret worship through the samādhi of Vajrasattva,
whatever task one declares, one shall swiftly attain its accomplishment.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajradhara.
In this regard, here is the *Vajrakula-karmakārya-dīpikā-tantra*:

Having performed the great secret worship of the family (*kulaguhyamahāpūjā*) with the meditative absorption of wrath (*krodhasamādhi*), whatever the wise one contemplates, that shall swiftly attain accomplishment. (2686)
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajrakrodha.
In this regard, here is the tantra for the accomplishment of the ritual activities of the Lotus Family:
Having performed the worship of Mānuṣī with the meditative absorption of Lokeśvara, ...
"Whatever task a wise person contemplates, they shall quickly attain all of it.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, the Holder of the Lotus.
In this regard, here is the Tantra for the accomplishment of the ritual activities of the Jewel Family:
Having performed worship with incense and other offerings through the Vajragarbha-samādhi,
whatever task the wise one contemplates, all that is accomplished in an instant.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajragarbha.
The Extensive Tantra of the Ritual Procedures for Accomplishing the Activities and Rites of All Families.

(2692) Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi proclaimed the Tantra of the Accomplishment of the Meditation on the Mudrās of All Tathāgatas: (2693) In this regard, there is the Tantra of the Accomplishment of the Yoga of the Tathāgata’s Empowerment:

"By means of the subtle vajra application, one who is concentrated in the yoga of the Buddha attains the supreme accomplishment as a practitioner of the Buddha-mudrā. Thus spoke the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Vajrapāṇi.
In this regard, here is the *Tathāgatakulasattvādhiṣṭhānayogasiddhitantra*.
"For the sentient being is indeed the self of all; he is established within my own self as well.
Having thus empowered himself and cultivating the thought "I am the sentient being" through the sense of ego, one attains accomplishment.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajrasattva, the Great Vehicle Realization of All Tathāgatas.
In this regard, here is the Yoga Tantra of the Vajra Empowerment of the Vajra Family:
"As are sentient beings, so are the mudrās; as are the mudrās, so am I.
By means of this yoga of contemplation, one should accomplish all mudrās. (2698)
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajradhara.
In this regard, there is this Yoga Tantra of the Empowerment of the Dharma of the Lotus Family:
"Through the application of the Dharma-seal and by means of the subtle vajra, there is meditation;
for all those seals of speech are indeed the samādhi of the Mahāsattva.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, the Noble Avalokiteśvara. (2700–2701)
In this regard, here is the Yoga Tantra of the Empowerment of the Activity of the Jewel Family:

Through the realization that "the Blessed One is [myself]," one should accomplish all the empowerments of the Buddhas, the offerings, the samayas, and the siddhis; meditating with the thought "the Blessed One is [myself]," one should accomplish the vajra-activities. (2702)

Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajrakarma. (2703) This is the extensive tantra of the ritual for the accomplishment of the meditation on the mudrās of all families. (2704) Then the Blessed Ones, all the Tathāgatas, having come together once again, gathered in assembly.
They gave their applause to the Blessed One, the Wheel-Turning Sovereign of all Tathāgatas, the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi:
“Excellent to you, O Vajrasattva; excellent to you, O Vajraratna!
Excellent to you, O Vajradharma; excellent to you, O Vajrakarman!”
This well-spoken sūtra is the unsurpassed Vajrayāna, the secret of all Tathāgatas, the compendium of the Mahāyāna.
(2707) Thus ends the detailed ritual procedure for the supreme secret tantra of all kalpas, from the *Sarvatathāgatatattvasaṃgraha*. (2708)
(Sarvakalpānuttaratantra) (2709) Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi spoke this verse:
"This secret is difficult to perceive for those who are dispassionate; it is not suitable for them."
"For the benefit of all sentient beings, I shall likewise explain the ritual procedures.

(2711) Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi again spoke at length on the ritual procedures for the service of all Tathāgatas: (2712) "In this regard, here is the detailed ritual procedure for the service of the Tathāgata family: (2713)"
In this regard, the detailed procedure for the ritual service of the heart-mantra is as follows:

having beheld the great maṇḍala, one should perform worship with incense, flowers, lamps, and perfumes by means of the mudrās; thereafter, one should begin the recitation (*jāpa*) with the Vajra-voice.
In this regard, the procedure for the recitation is as follows:
Remaining in one's place for four months, having performed worship as prescribed with incense and other offerings during the four junctions of the day,

and having praised all the Tathāgatas with the "One Hundred and Eight Names of the Mahāyāna Abhisamaya of All Tathāgatas," one should perform the worship of self-dedication while prostrating through the yoga of the four mudrās, using these four mantras.
Oṃ, I offer myself for the service and worship of all Tathāgatas;
O Vajrasattva of all Tathāgatas, grant me your empowerment!
Oṃ, I offer myself for the empowerment of the worship of all Tathāgatas.
Consecrate me with the vajra-jewels of all the Tathāgatas!
Oṃ, I offer myself for the sake of initiating the worship of all the Tathāgatas.
O Vajradharma of all the Tathāgatas, cause me to turn [the wheel of Dharma]! (2717–2718)
Oṃ, I offer myself for the rite of worship of all the Tathāgatas. Perform for me the vajra-activity of all the Tathāgatas!

(2719) Then, without being detached from any of the qualities of sensual pleasure, consuming all kinds of food and enjoying all desires, while from the perspective of the heart’s true meaning visualizing one’s own self as the image of a Buddha—even if only by way of speech—before oneself, and reciting the vajra-words eight hundred times according to one’s will, one quickly attains accomplishment. (2720)
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajrasattva. Now,
if one should desire the supreme accomplishment, then,
desiring it, one should have the Blessed Tathāgata depicted in the center of a cloth painting.

(2722) By means of the yoga of the maṇḍala of the four Great Beings (*mahāsattva*), the Great Beings— possessing colors and ornaments according to one's preference— and the Family Goddesses (*kuladevī*) should be depicted situated upon moon-discs in the corner sections.
(2723) Then, having performed a magnificent worship of the cloth painting (*paṭa*), one should recite [the mantra] according to the yoga of recitation for as long as four months.
Then, one should recite throughout the entire night.
Thereupon, at dawn, one attains the supreme accomplishment beginning with the reality (*tattva*) of all the Tathāgatas.
(2725) Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajradhara. (2726) Then, by one desiring the accomplishment of the mudrās, having bound the *sarvatathāgatasattvavajrī* mudrā,
In front of the cloth painting, one should recite with vajra-words one hundred thousand times, binding and releasing according to the requirements of one's desire;
(2727) then, at the end, one should recite while binding and releasing as prescribed, without resting for some time throughout the entire night.
Then the mudrā blazes, enters [the practitioner], rises up, and emits speech. Thus, by the binding of the mudrā, one flies up; one becomes capable of assuming any form at will.
It becomes invisible;
it performs all ritual actions (*karma*);
and all mudrās, as soon as they are bound according to the rules, perform all ritual actions.
(2730) Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajradhara.
(2731) Now, one who desires to master the meditative absorptions [should proceed as follows].
Starting from that subtle vajra, one should practice whichever meditative absorption (*samādhi*) one prefers through the yoga of the heart for as long as four months.

Then, at the end, one should remain seated in the cross-legged posture (*paryaṅka*) having entered that state throughout the entire night. Thereupon, all the Tathāgatas and all the accomplishments (*siddhi*) will become manifest.
"Therefore, whatever one's aspiration may be, such is the accomplishment," thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajrasattva. Now follows the ritual for the accomplishment of activity (*karmasādhana*).
In that same manner, one should recite for one month to accomplish the practice;
then, at the conclusion, one should recite throughout the entire night. (2737)
"Then one attains the accomplishment of all activities," said the Blessed One Vajradhara.
Now, the activities follow.
By reciting [the mantra] once, protection for oneself, one's kin, and one's city is achieved, as if clad in armor and so forth.

Furthermore, by means of fragrant sandalwood, one may cause [deities] to enter; by reciting it once, one causes all entities—including the vajra-hook, arrow, hand, jewel, sun, banner, row of teeth, lotus, sword, wheel, tongue, the all-vajra armor, fangs, and the fist-mudrā—to enter, whether they have been touched or not.
Furthermore, having pierced vajras with a peacock-feather quill, one should bind them.
Then, having pressed that peacock-feather quill with the Sattvavajrī mudrā, one should recite the mantra until it enters the mudrās of all the Tathāgatas.
Thereupon, one sees various forms emerging from the quill.
From that time forward, by means of that peacock-feather fan, he displays all forms according to the prescribed ritual.
By means of that very same fan, when whirled around while recited over once, he displays all his own forms.
With that very peacock feather fan, they display worldly magical feats;
they even display the images of Buddhas and Bodhisattvas.

In all Buddha-fields throughout the ten directions, they display the Tathāgatas performing the miraculous transformations of a Buddha—such as overcoming the hosts of Māra along with their armies, together with the circles of their retinues.
...until one becomes the form of a Buddha endowed with the excellence of all aspects.
(2746) One who desires to perform subjugation should bind the *sarvatathāgatasattvavajrī* mudrā and recite [the mantra] until that mudrā blazes.
From that point on, by means of binding the mudrā, one pleases even all the Tathāgatas and brings them under control; how much more so other sentient beings? (2747–2748)
Now, for one who desires to accomplish the supreme mundane siddhis, they should first recite in that same manner for one month with eight thousand recitations;
then, at the conclusion, having bound the mudrā, they should likewise recite throughout the entire night until the mudrā blazes. (2749)
From that time forward, by means of the binding of the mudrās, one attains either the mundane accomplishments (*laukikasiddhi*) or the accomplishments of the Vidyādharas (*vidyādharasiddhi*).
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajradhara. The detailed procedure for the ritual service of the Tathāgata family is hereby completed.
Now follows the detailed procedure for the ritual service (*upacāra*) of the Vajra family.
Therein, at the very outset, one should perform the preliminary service (*pūrvasevā*).
In that same context, one should recite [the mantra] one hundred thousand times according to one's desire.
(2753) Then, at the end, one should recite [the mantra] for the entire night. (2754)
From that time forth, one becomes capable of both subduing and favoring all sentient beings.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajradhara.
Then, by one who desires to accomplish [the rite], the cloth-painting must be consecrated according to the rule;
thereafter, having performed worship in that same manner,
For one month, consuming all desired foods, one should recite with vajra-voice eight thousand times at each of the four junctions of the day, performing whatever actions as one desires;
this should continue until, at the end of the month, having performed a grand worship of the cloth painting, [the goal is attained].
Having bound the great mudrā of Vajrahūṃkāra, one should recite [the mantra] until the sound of the syllable HŪṂ issues forth from that binding of the mudrā. (2759)
Then at dawn, Maheśvara and the other lords of the gods, together with their hosts and retinues, stood before him and awaited his command.
Then the Vidyādhara should speak thus:
"When I say, 'Come, do this,' then you must come and carry out my command. Thus it should be said.
From that time forth, he becomes the sovereign of the entire triple world.
At his will, he wanders for a mere moment commanding the whole of the three worlds;
furthermore, he returns again, exercising both restraint and grace.
Enjoying divine pleasures of the three worlds, he gratifies and enjoys all women, including the consorts of the lords of the gods and others, according to his every desire;
and no one at all is able to do anything to him. (2765)
And by means of the syllable *hūṃ*, one causes all wicked deities and others to fall; thereafter, one lives for thousands of intermediate eons.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajradhara.
Now, if one should desire the accomplishment of the mudrā: having performed the recitation as prescribed,
at the end of the month, one should bind the Vajra-hūṃkāra-samaya-mudrā and recite throughout the entire night.
Then, at dawn, the mudrās become accomplished.
Thereafter, by binding the mudrās according to the proper method, [the results follow].

By means of the application of the syllable *HŪṂ*, there is the attainment of traveling through space, the manifestation of all things, invisibility, the display of illusions, the possession of all beings, the summoning [of others], the subjugation [of others], the generation of universal satisfaction, the bringing forth of all jewels, the manifestation of great flames of splendor, the display of a rain of jewels, the uttering of a great boisterous laugh, the purification, cutting, and piercing of all sentient beings, the turning of the wheel of seasons, the awakening to reality as it truly is, the setting in motion of all activities, protection, the parching, the paralyzing, the terrifying, and the killing [of enemies], the sealing of all sentient beings, and the enjoyment of desires.
One performs all ritual actions, such as initiating activity, conferring empowerment, causing all beings to sing, causing them to dance, summoning, causing entry, piercing, and causing possession.
(2770–2775) Now, one should explain the means for attaining subtle gnosis.
By that practitioner, while practicing the Vajra-hūṃkāra-samādhi, it should be accomplished for one month using the same method of recitation (*jāpayoga*).
Then, at the conclusion, he should recite throughout the entire night by means of that very same samādhi.

"Until such time as, at dawn, one has become possessed of the five superknowledges (*pañcābhijñā*) and is capable of both favoring and restraining all sentient beings," so said the Blessed One Vajradhara.
Now, if one should desire the accomplishment of ritual action (*karmasādhana*):
(2780) Reciting in that very manner for one month, he should accomplish the practice.
(2781) Then, at the end, he should recite throughout the entire night.
"Then all ritual actions are accomplished," said the Blessed One, Vajradhara.
From that, actions come into being.
By reciting it even once with the desired intention, one performs all activities, such as protection and so forth.
(2784) The detailed procedure for the ritual service of the Vajra family is completed. (2785) Now follows the detailed procedure for the ritual service of the Lotus family:
In that regard, first of all, one should recite [the mantra] one hundred thousand times;
this constitutes the preliminary service (*pūrvasevā*).
Thereafter, the actual practice (*sādhana*) may be undertaken.

On the cloth, the Blessed Ones beginning with Sarvajagadvinaya and others are to be depicted; on all four sides of it, the four Great Beings are to be fashioned according to the arrangement of the four maṇḍalas, as well as the goddesses.
Then, that very same detailed procedure for recitation should be performed, and at the end of the month, one should recite throughout the entire night.
Then the Blessed One, the discipliner of the entire world, arrives;
at the appropriate time, he proceeds with the vajra.

Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajradhara. (2789) Now, if one should desire to accomplish the mudrā, one should likewise form the Padmavajrī mudrā and release it as prescribed; reciting eight thousand times, one should perform the recitation at the four junctions of the day.
Then, one should recite throughout the entire night while maintaining the seal-binding;
at dawn, success is attained.
Then, by means of binding the mudrās according to the rules, he brings about the discipline of the entire world. Thus spoke the Blessed One, Avalokiteśvara.
Now, if one should desire the accomplishment of the method of meditative concentration (*samādhi*),
one should likewise, at the end of the month, perform recitation throughout the entire night with whichever meditative concentration is desired.
Then, at dawn, all meditative concentrations will become manifest.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajradhara. (2794) Now, if one should desire the accomplishment of activity (*karmasādhana*),
one should likewise recite [the mantra] for a month, and at its conclusion, recite throughout the entire night.
"Thereupon, one becomes capable of all ritual actions," thus said the Blessed One Vajradhara.
The detailed procedure for the ritual service of the Lotus Family is completed.
Now follows the detailed procedure for the ritual service of the Jewel Family.
Therein, at the very outset, having performed the fourfold prostration to all the Tathāgatas, one should recite [the mantra] one hundred thousand times.
Then, one should likewise paint the Blessed One Sarvārthasiddhi upon a cloth using the yoga of the four-seal maṇḍala.
Then, having performed worship in that same manner, one should practice the sādhana in that same way.
At the end of the month, one should recite the mantra throughout the entire night.
Then at dawn, the Blessed One Ākāśagarbha, the Bodhisattva who is the Jewel of the Empowerment of All Tathāgatas, arrives and bestows empowerment.
By that empowerment, one becomes a universal monarch of the vidyādharas within the triple-thousand great thousandfold world system.
(2800) Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajradhara. (2801) Now, if one should desire the accomplishment of the mudrās:
By that same application of the Dharma-vajrī, the Vajra-ratna mudrā should be accomplished correctly; it becomes the performer of all desired actions.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajradhara.
Now, if one wishes to accomplish the knowledge of jewels (*maṇijñāna*),
one should likewise cultivate the *vajraratnodbhava-samādhi* according to the sequence [as follows]:
"How can there be the arising of a jewel from space, which is devoid of intrinsic nature?"
And as for how the body of a bodhisattva arises from the jewel:
one should cultivate this samādhi during the four junctions of the day and recite it as described above.
Then, at the end of the month, one should recite throughout the entire night with that very same meditative absorption (*samādhi*).
Then, at dawn, all the Tathāgatas will arrive and consecrate [the practitioner] according to their preference.
Thus spoke the Blessed One Ākāśagarbha.
Now, as for the ritual procedure (*karmasādhana*):
while reciting in that same manner, one should recite throughout the entire night at the end of the month.
Then, at dawn, the Blessed One Ākāśagarbha becomes the accomplisher of all aims.
(2808) Thereafter, one should perform all ritual actions.

Thus spoke the Blessed One, the Noble Vajradhara. (2810) The detailed procedure for the ritual service of the Jewel Family is completed. (2811) Now follows this detailed procedure for the ritual service of the means of accomplishment common to all families. (2812)
In that regard, first of all, there is the detailed procedure for the ritual service of the heart-mantras.

Having uttered, "May the heart-desires of all the Tathāgatas be accomplished," one should recite the heart-mantra as desired and perform the rite of accomplishment. In this context, the following is the procedure for the ritual service of the mudrās:

Having said, "May all mudrās be dear to me," and having bound the *samaya-mudrā*, one should recite [the mantra] as desired and according to one's ability. Then, success will come accordingly. (2815) In this regard, this is the procedure for the ritual service (*upacāra*) of all mantras.
"May speech free from conceptual proliferation be accomplished;
may the samādhis of all the Tathāgatas arise within me. Having said this, one should recite the mantra as desired. This is the accomplishment. (2816)
In this regard, the following is the procedure for the ritual application of the vidyā.

"Alas, these sentient beings are blinded by ignorance, whereas all Tathāgatas have attained the restraint of the realization of knowledge (*vidyā*). Having said this, one should recite the *vidyā* as desired and bring about the accomplishment (*sādhana*).
Thus spoke the Blessed One, the Noble Vajradhara.
Now follows the detailed procedure for the vajra-recitation (*vajrajāpa*) of all heart-seals (*hṛdaya*), mudrās, mantras, and *vidyās*, according to their respective functions.
"Whichever sentient being one should cause to accomplish the heart-seal, the mantra, or the vidyā—
for the sake of recitation, that very self or that sentient being to be accomplished will be perfected.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajrasattva.
The detailed procedure for the recitation common to all families is completed.
Now follows the detailed procedure for the accomplishments common to all families.
Herein, first of all, are the accomplishments of the Tathāgata family.

Namely: the accomplishment of the attainment of wealth, the accomplishment of supernatural power (*ṛddhi*), the state of a knowledge-holder (*vidyādhara*), and the great accomplishment (*mahāsiddhi*).
Among these, there occurs the accomplishment of the attainment of wealth.
Wherever there may be a suspicion of a treasure, one should bind the seal with one's own meditative absorption and gaze upon that location of the treasure with the vajra-vision.
If one sees the form of the vajra as if it were oozing forth, then it should be known: "The treasure is here.
Then, having bound the Vajrasphoṭa-samaya-mudrā, one should dig it up and take it according to one's desire.
"Before long, one attains [it]," said the Blessed One, Vajrasattva.
In that regard, the accomplishment of miraculous powers (*ṛddhi-siddhi*) occurs.
Having said, "One should accomplish whichever mudrā, there is the accomplishment of supernatural power (ṛddhisiddhi)," that supernatural power-accomplishment is fourfold.
Namely:
Walking and sitting upon water; manifesting all forms such as those of the Tathāgatas and so forth;
and remaining invisible for as long as one desires.
Moving through the sky, he leaps upward to the height of a thousand *yojanas* and travels back and forth below.
Having traversed all directions up to a distance of a thousand *yojanas* with whatever speed he desires, he returns;
and from that distance of a thousand *yojanas*, he knows the unspoken intentions of all sentient beings.
He sees all beings with his eyes and hears them with his ears; and from all directions, he brings to his own body all women desired by his mind, even from a distance of a thousand yojanas. (2831)
And he seizes all objects, including all gold, fine gold, jewels, pearls, and so forth.
And no one at all is able to do anything to him;
