he becomes unassailable even by a thunderbolt, let alone by others.

Possessing the strength of ten thousand men, eternally healthy, always enjoying every desire, perpetually youthful, and possessing a divine form, he beholds and worships all the Tathāgatas together with Vajrasattva, and through the supreme vajra-attainment, he lives for four thousand years.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, the Vajra-ṛddhi-siddhi of all Tathāgatas.
In this regard, this is the accomplishment of the siddhi of the Vajra-vidyādhara:
While accomplishing the mudrā, one should say, "I am a Vajra-vidyādhara."
Upon accomplishment, one becomes a universal monarch of the Vajra-vidyādharas.
Enjoying all sensual pleasures, he travels through a thousand buddha-fields in a single instant and returns.

Consuming every form of happiness, possessing a body like that of a sixteen-year-old, bearing hair in curled locks, and being a great Vajra-Vidyādhara, he beholds all the Tathāgatas together with Vajrasattva and remains for a great eon;
thus spoke the Blessed One, the Vidyādhara of all Tathāgatas.
In that regard, the accomplishment of the great siddhis occurs.
One should accomplish one’s own mudrā through the meaning of the heart.
Having become the form of the being of one’s own mudrā, in a single instant one becomes possessed of manifold forms throughout all world-systems in the ten directions, initiating manifold activities.

Having beheld all the Tathāgatas together with Vajrasattva, and having worshipped them with all the offerings of all the Tathāgatas endowed with the excellence of all aspects, and having accomplished the welfare of all sentient beings without exception or remainder, one returns once again.

"Enjoying all desires, all pleasures, and all mental happiness of all world-systems, endowed with the excellence of every aspect, the Great Bodhisattva becomes equal to Vajrasattva and possesses a lifespan of all great eons without exception or remainder.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, the Siddhi of All Tathāgatas.
In this regard, these are the siddhis of the Vajra Family:
Namely:
the accomplishment of the Conqueror of the Three Worlds,
and the accomplishment of all consecrations.
The accomplishment of all happiness and mental ease is the supreme accomplishment.
In that regard, there is the accomplishment of the Conqueror of the Three Worlds.
Having bound the trilokavijaya-mudrā and having stepped upon Maheśvara with the left foot, one should perform the practice. Then that image emits a sound;
thereupon, the syllable *hūṃ* should be employed.

(2843) Merely by the employment of the syllable *hūṃ*, Maheśvara and all other lords of the three worlds, together with their retinues, come before the practitioner and become subject to his commands. (2844) From that moment on, he becomes Vajradhara, the lord of the entire triple world.
He travels through space;
having circumambulated the entire wheel of the three worlds, he returns;
and he subdues wicked deities and others among all sentient beings with the syllable *hūṃ*.

(2845) Having the form of the *vajra-hūṃ* (or *huṃ*, ed. syllable of all Tathāgatas, causing the entire triple world to function by his command, beholding all Tathāgatas together with Vajrasattva, and pleasing them, he lives for a thousand years.
(2846) Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajra-hūṃkāra (or Vajrahuṃkāra, ed.). (2847)
In this regard, this is the accomplishment of all consecrations:
One should accomplish the mudrā.
Having first consecrated oneself with the Jewel Mudrā of the Empowerment of All Tathāgatas, one should accomplish it.
For each respective accomplishment, there is a fourfold empowerment.
These are the vajra initiation, the jewel initiation, the dharma initiation, and the action initiation.
(2849) Among these, when the vajra initiation is obtained, one becomes a Vajradhara of all the Tathāgatas;
with the jewel initiation, one becomes the sovereign of all jewels.
Through the empowerment of phenomena (*dharmābhiṣeka*), one becomes a King of Dharma;
through the empowerment of action (*karmābhiṣeka*), one attains the accomplishment of all mundane and supramundane activities.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, the Empowerment of All Tathāgatas.

In this regard, this is the accomplishment of pleasure and mental joy: namely, by constantly performing worship of all the Tathāgatas through secret worships, one attains the accomplishment of all the pleasure and mental joy of all the Tathāgatas.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, the Pleasure and Mental Joy of All the Tathāgatas.
In this regard, this is the supreme accomplishment.
"Namely, 'I am equal to the Holder of the Vajra,'" said the Blessed One, the Holder of the Vajra.
In this regard, these are the accomplishments of the Lotus Family:
Namely:
enchantment, subjugation, protection, and the accomplishment of the lotus. Among these, the accomplishment of enchantment occurs as follows.
By correctly meditating on the ruby [padmarāga], one becomes capable of inspiring passion in all sentient beings, beginning with all the Tathāgatas;
by recollecting oneself as Lokeśvara, one likewise becomes capable of bringing all sentient beings under one's influence.
(2858) By means of the samādhi of the pervasion of loving-kindness, one becomes capable of protecting, shielding, and guarding the entire world.

Having taken a lotus with a smile by means of the *Padma-samādhi*, one who accomplishes [the practice] in the form of Lokeśvara, endowed with the excellence of all aspects, lives for four thousand years;
thus said the Blessed One, the Lotus of All Tathāgatas.
In this regard, these are the splendors of the Maṇi family:
Namely:
the accomplishment of the empowerment of all families,
and the possession of great majesty.
The fulfillment of all hopes and the accomplishment of the jewel. (2862) Among these,
there is the accomplishment of the empowerment of all Tathāgatas.

Namely, the fulfillment of the perfection of giving lamps as an offering for one’s own consecration, and the accomplishment of the jewel according to one's ability; by means of these accomplishments, while worshipping all the Tathāgatas, one attains success before long—thus spoke the Blessed One, the Jewel of All Tathāgatas.
(2863) The detailed ritual procedure for the common accomplishments of all families is hereby completed. (2864–2865)
Then the Blessed One, the beginningless Being, said: "Now I shall explain the *Sarvakalpopāyasiddhi-tantra*.
(2866) [Therein, first of all, is the *Hṛdayopāyasiddhi-tantra*.
(2867) For whatever kind of being the world to be converted may be, such is the accomplishment desired for them.
In that regard, the seal (*mudrā*) is indeed the great means (*upāya*) that bestows all accomplishments (*siddhi*).
Herein is the *Mudropāyasiddhitanttra*.
The world is governed by detachment, yet the accomplishment of the *mudrā* arises from passion;
therein, meditative cultivation (*bhāvanā*) is the supreme means that brings about all accomplishments.
In this regard, there is this *Tantra of the Accomplishment of Means through Mantras*.
This world has fallen away from the truth; the accomplishment of mantras is not desired [by them].
But the means that is free from conceptual proliferation (*niṣprapañca*) is the supreme bringer of all accomplishments.
In this regard, there is this Tantra of the Accomplishment of the Means of Knowledge (*vidyopāyasiddhitantra*).
One who is attached to ignorance does not attain the accomplishment of knowledge;
however, in that regard, the noble means—which bestows all accomplishments—is supreme.
Thus [ends] the *Sarvakalpopāyasiddhitanttra*. (2871) Then the Blessed One, the Sarvatathāgata, said: "Now I shall further explain the *Sarvakalpapuṇyasiddhitanttra*. (2872–2873)
In that regard, first of all is the *Svahṛdayapuṇyasiddhi-tantra*.
Having performed the fourfold worship, one attains great merit;
even for those without merit, success is achieved through the worship of the Buddhas—of this there is no doubt.
Thus [it is said]. (2874) In this regard, here is the *Mudrāpuṇyasiddhi-tantra*.
But by guarding the secret pledge, one attains great merit;
for even if one has no merit, success will be swiftly achieved through the protection of that vow.
Thus it is said. (2875) In this regard, here is the *Mantrapuṇyasiddhi-tantra*.
One shall obtain great merit through uttering the names and other attributes of the Buddhas;
even from the gift of Dharma, one swiftly attains accomplishment, even regarding that which is not meritorious.
In this regard, there is this Tantra of the Accomplishment of the Merit of Vidyās:
Giving is indeed the foremost of meritorious deeds; by giving, one attains merit.
Having fulfilled the perfection of generosity, one swiftly attains Buddhahood.
Thus ends the *Sarvakalpapuṇyasiddhi-tantra*.
Now, I shall further explain the *Sarvakalpaprajñāsiddhi-tantra*.
"Thus spoke the Blessed One, the Tathāgata of All Tathāgatas. (2880) Therein, first of all, is the *Hṛdayaprajñāsiddhi-tantra*.
"By means of drawing in and entering [the syllable] *a*, one attains the consciousness of all syllables;
by meditating upon one's own face as another's face, one shall attain accomplishment.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, the Great Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī.
In this regard, here is the *Mudrāprajñāsiddhi-tantra*.
"Wisdom, known as 'penetrating,' is proclaimed as the condensed accomplishment.
By means of that, the mudrās are accomplished; by meditating upon them, one succeeds in an instant.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, the Foremost of Wisdom.
In this regard, here is the *Mantraprajñāsiddhi-tantra*.
"The samādhi called 'Following the Sound of Wisdom' [is attained] through the elaboration of speech;
by cultivating that, one will swiftly attain the accomplishment of mantra.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajrabuddhi.
In this regard, here is the Tantra of the Accomplishment of Knowledge and Wisdom.
"There is indeed no distinction among the various types of vidyās and mantras;
by cultivating them in this way through wisdom, accomplishment will swiftly and certainly be attained.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, the Wisdom-Knowledge of all Tathāgatas.
The Extensive Tantra of the Ritual Procedures for the Accomplishment of Wisdom and Knowledge of All Ritual Manuals.
(2889) Then the Blessed One Vajrapāṇi said, "I shall now explain the Tantra of the Accomplishment of the Accumulation for All Ritual Manuals.
(2890) In that regard, first of all is the Tantra of the Accomplishment of the Accumulation of All Heart-Essences.
While performing every kind of worship, the equipment for the accumulations increases;
from that, the accumulation of wholesome qualities is perfected.
In this regard, here is the *tantra* on the accomplishment of the equipment of mudrās:
And by entering many wheels and by the arrangement of many maṇḍalas, having fulfilled the equipment (*saṃbhāra*) of the mudrās, the great accomplishment (*mahāsiddhi*) proceeds.
In this regard, there is this Tantra of the Accomplishment of the Equipment of Mantras:
Through the practice of rejoicing and so forth, by reciting the true Dharma in that manner,
and by performing many recitations, the accomplishment of the mantra will certainly be attained.
Thus it is said.
(2893) In this regard, here is the *Vidyāsaṃbhārasiddhi-tantra*:
(2894) "Because ignorance has been thoroughly abandoned through the method of the perfection of generosity..."
But one who has fulfilled the accumulations attains accomplishment quickly.
Thus ends the *Sarvakalpasambhārasiddhi-tantra*.
The *Sarvakalpavidhivistara-tantra* is completed. (2897)
Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi proclaimed the Knowledge Tantra of the Origin of the Symbols of All Families:
"In that regard, how does the Vajra originate?
That very Blessed One, the Being, the Mind of all, is himself the Sovereign."
The Vajra of body, speech, and mind is the firm being of the self-arisen ones.
(2899) Among all beings, he is the supreme being; through the meditation on the vajra within the heart, he is renowned as Vajrasattva, established in that very vajra. (2890)
By means of the yoga of gnosis, that very [consciousness], having emerged from the heart, becomes the universal one, possessing universal form;
indeed, it becomes a Victor equal in number to the atoms of all realms. (2901)

From those indeed who possess vajra-bodies, Vajrasattva arises; from that very Primordial Being (Ādisattva), the emergence of all symbols occurs; from the symbols arise the Great Beings (Mahāsattvas), and from them comes this entire system.
Thus:
(2903) Whoever should hear this, have faith in it, hold it in their heart, and constantly cultivate it with joy, shall swiftly attain accomplishment. (2904)
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajrasattva.
This is the Extensive Tantra of the Ritual Procedures for the Knowledge Arising from the Reality of All Tathāgatas.
Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi proclaimed the Extensive Tantra of the Ritual Procedures for the Knowledge Arising from All Ritual Manuals.
In that regard, first of all, there is the Knowledge Tantra concerning the origin of the ritual manuals of all the Tathāgatas.
The wisdom of the Buddhas is indeed non-conceptual and eternal;
from that non-conceptual wisdom, conceptualization arises through conceptual thought.
In this regard, there is this *jñānatantro* concerning the origin of the ritual manual (*kalpa*) of the Tathāgata family.

Just as conceptual construction, being of the nature of construction and arising from imagination, is imagined, so too is Vajrasattva, the Great Being; therefore, it is called "construction. In this regard, there is this Knowledge Tantra concerning the origin of the ritual manual of the Vajra Family: (2909) Just as conceptual construction, being of the nature of construction and arising from imagination, is imagined, so too is Vajrasattva, the Great Being; therefore, it is called "construction. In this regard, there is this Knowledge Tantra concerning the origin of the ritual manual of the Vajra Family.
For that which, having been drawn, brings about ritual procedures (*vidhi*) and grants the accomplishment of those rituals,
is therefore called a *kalpa* by those whose nature is free from conceptual construction (*vikalpa*).
In this regard, here is the Knowledge Tantra (*jñānatatra*) arising from the *Kalpa* of the Lotus Family (*padmakula*).
Passion is born from conceptual construction, and it is established upon the lotus;
therefore, indeed, the accomplishments (siddhis) that endure for an eon arise from it.
In this regard, there is this Knowledge Tantra arising from the ritual manual of the Jewel Family.
The elephant is born from conceptual construction, and it is established upon a lotus.
(2913) %% This [verse] was caused by a scribal eye-skip; see verse 2911.
"For jewels are indeed free from conceptual construction, yet they are preeminent through their powers;
in this same way, divine accomplishments arise without being conceptually constructed.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajradhara.
The Knowledge Tantra of the Arising of the Ritual Manuals of All Families.
(2916) [Then, the Knowledge Tantra of the Arising of the Heart-mantras and so forth of All Ritual Manuals.
Then, the Knowledge Tantra of the Arising of the Heart-mantras of All Ritual Manuals.
Through the performance of desired rites, that which is desired is accomplished;

because it is the means for achieving meditative absorption (*samādhi*) and resides within the heart, it is therefore called the "Heart" (*hṛdaya*). (2917) Now follows the *Sarvamudrāsaṃbhavajñānatantra*.

Just as the supreme royal edict, marked with the seal of a great soul, is difficult to transgress and indestructible, so too is that which is celebrated as the "seal" (mudrā). (2918) [Now begins the *Mantrasambhavajñānatantra*. (2919)
For it is indeed untransgressible, difficult to pierce, and secret;
it is deliberated for the sake of secret accomplishment, and thus it is defined as *mantra*. (2920) Now follows the *Vidyāsaṃbhavajñāna-tantra*. (2921)

"Because it exists for the sake of destroying ignorance and for the sake of attaining the pinnacle of knowledge, and because it possesses the accomplishment of realization, it is proclaimed as 'knowledge' (vidyā).
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajradhara. (2922–2923)
The Knowledge Tantra of the Arising of the Heart-mantras and so forth of All Ritual Manuals.
(2924) Now follows the Tantra of the Arising of the Knowledge of All Ritual Manuals.
(2925) In that regard, first of all, there is the Tantra of the Arising of the Knowledge of the Heart-mantras.

The heart-mantra should be understood as that which, when recited, perceives and hears the past, present, and future—whether pertaining to oneself or another—and sees what is yet to be, what has been, and what will be.
In this regard, there is this *Mudrājñānotpattitantra*: (2926) [The text follows.]
Having bound one of the mudrās according to the prescribed rite for oneself,
one should observe the entire world as it is to be known hereafter.
Thus it is said.
In this regard, here is the Tantra for the Arising of Knowledge of Mantras:

"Whoever, reciting the mantra only once, speaks with their own tongue, shall bring all that— whether pertaining to the past, the present, or the future— to truth," so said the Blessed One Avalokiteśvara. (2928–2929)
In this regard, here is the tantra for the arising of knowledge and wisdom:
Having recited the vidyā just once, he who makes it known with his mind— just like the words of a vajra-command— [discerns] the past, present, and future.
Thus ends the *Sarvakalpajñānotpattividhivistaratantra* (The Extensive Tantra on the Procedure for the Arising of Knowledge of All Rituals).
Now follows the *Sarvakulasādhāraṇaguhya-kāyavākcittavajramudrāsādhanatantra* (The Tantra on the Means for Accomplishing the Secret Body, Speech, and Mind Vajra Mudrās Common to All Families).
In this regard, there is this *Tathāgatakulaguhyakāyamudrāsādhanatantra*.
"In whatever manner one is seated, one should practice in the full lotus posture;
in accordance with the visualized form, the Mahāsattva attains accomplishment.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajrasattva.
In this regard, there is this *Vajrakulaguhyakāyamudrāsādhanatantra*.

One should accomplish [the rite] while standing firmly in the *pratyālīḍha* posture according to the drawing, being thoroughly enraged; one will succeed, there is no doubt about this. Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajrahūṃkāra.
In this regard, there is this *Padmakula-guhyakāya-mudrā-sādhanatantra*.
"Seated in the vajra-paryaṅka posture with both hands in the vajra-bind, having become the body of meditative concentration, one should accomplish the birth from the lotus.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Padmasattva.
In this regard, there is this *maṇikula-guhyakāya-mudrā-sādhana-tantra*:

Whether standing, sitting, or walking, in whatever manner one may be, one attains accomplishment through the consecration of the Vajra-jewel; of this there is no doubt. Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajragarbha.

In this regard, here is the *Tathāgatakula-guhyavāṅmudrā-sādhanatantra*: (2941) With the tongue-tip vibrating from the navel and the two lips joined together, one should accomplish all ritual manuals (*kalpa*) through the adamantine speech (*vajravāk*), even when devoid of vocal sound. (2942)
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajravāca.
In this regard, here is the tantra for the practice of the secret speech-mudrā of the Vajra family.
"Resounding with the *hūṃ* (or *huṃ*) syllable like a rolling cloud, possessing speech as deep as a wrathful one,
steadfast, and bursting forth with fury— this Great Vajra, the Speech of the Vajra-Wrathful One, is accomplished.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajra-Hūṃkāra.
In this regard, here is the tantra for the practice of the secret speech-mudrā of the Lotus family.

Without even breathing out while breathing in— or rather, while breathing in without exhaling— one accomplishes all recitations clearly through subtle speech by means of that which has meditative concentration and gnosis as its core. (2946)
Thus spoke the Blessed One, the Essence of the Samādhi-Wisdom of All Tathāgatas.
In this regard, here is the tantra for the practice of the secret speech-mudrā of the Jewel Family:

"Always intent on prostration with very clear speech, and likewise through the Vinaya recitations, everything is swiftly accomplished. Thus spoke the Blessed One, the one whose activity is the extensive ritual for the worship of all Tathāgatas.
In this regard, here is the *Tathāgatakulaguhyacittamudrāsādhanatantra*:
For the Blessed One is Desire, who eternally bestows happiness upon all sentient beings.
By meditating on oneself as Vajrasattva himself, one swiftly attains accomplishment.
Thus spoke the Blessed One Kāma.
In this regard, here is the tantra for the practice of the secret mental mudrās of the Vajra family.
"For the sake of the welfare of all sentient beings, for the subduing of the wicked,
and for the protection of the Buddha's teaching, wrath is the supreme means of accomplishment.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Sarvatathāgatavajrahūṃkāra.
In this regard, here is the tantra for the practice of the secret mind-mudrā of the Lotus family.
"Just as a lotus, though possessing a beautiful color, remains unstained by the defects of its dwelling,
so too my passion, through the defects of passion, is perfected as passion within existence.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Padmarāga.
In this regard, here is the tantra for the practice of the secret mind-seal (*cittamudrā*) of the Jewel Family (*maṇikula*).

"When, for the sake of accomplishing all the purposes and activities of all sentient beings, will he, having become a perfected one, swiftly attain perfection by raining down showers of jewels? Thus spoke the Blessed One, the Noble Ākāśagarbha.
In this regard, here is the *Tathāgatakulaguhyavajramudrāsādhanatantra*:
Whether standing, sitting, or even wandering about in whatever manner,
one who holds the left mudrā with the hand succeeds in everything they do.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Sarvatathāgataguhyavajrapāṇi.
(2961) [In this regard, here is the tantra for the accomplishment of the secret vajra-mudrās of the Vajra family:
(2962) Whether remaining in whatever manner or acting in whatever way, [one should practice].
"By binding the Vajra-Krodha finger-gesture and covering it with a cloth, one attains accomplishment.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, the King of the Vajra-Krodhas of all Tathāgatas.
Herein is the tantra for the practice of the secret vajra-mudrā of the Lotus family.
"By forming the lotus-fist with the left hand while it is concealed, one shall swiftly attain the accomplishment of the lotus," said the Blessed One, Avalokiteśvara. (2966–2967)
In this regard, here is the *Maṇikula-guhyavajramudrā-sādhana-tantra*:
Having indeed formed the jewel-fist (*ratnamuṣṭi*), with the left hand covering the [right] palm...
"Through attendance according to one's desire, one shall attain the accomplishment of the jewels.
Thus spoke the Blessed One Ākāśagarbha.
In this regard, here is the tantra for the practice of the common secret mudrās of all families.
"By means of the application of the Great Seal (*mahāmudrā*) and the meditative absorption (*samādhi*) of one's own being,
through Vajra-speech and Vajra-vision, supreme accomplishment is attained without long delay.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, the Vajrasattva of all Tathāgatas.
The *Sarvakulasādhāraṇaguhyakāyavākcittavajramudrāsādhanatantra* is completed.
Then the Blessed One Vajrapāṇi, having summoned all the Tathāgatas, spoke thus: "O Blessed Tathāgatas, please proceed to empower this ritual manual."
Then all the Tathāgatas, having gathered together once more, again bestowed their words of praise:
(2976) "Excellent! To you, Vajrasattva; excellent! To you, Vajraratna; (2977) excellent! To you, Vajradharma; excellent! Excellent! To you, Vajrakarma!"
This well-spoken sūtra is the unsurpassed Vajrayāna,
the secret of all Tathāgatas, and the compendium of the Mahāyāna. Thus concludes the unsurpassed tantra of all ritual manuals from the *Sarvatathāgatatattvasaṃgraha*.
Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, rising from his seat, entreated the Blessed One with these one hundred and eight names:
"O Great Being of the Vajra Realm, whose supreme essence is the welfare of sentient beings;
O King of the Śākyas, of great wisdom, whose nature is the Vajra—homage be to you!"

[O source of beings, ultimate reality (or true meaning of the arising of beings), great method for the sake of beings! O you who are the being of beings, for the sake of the great being and for the sake of what is to be done, homage be to you! (2982)
O Buddha-dharma, Great Dharma, Turner of the Wheel of Dharma; O Great Speech, Supreme Vidyā, Great Being—homage be to you!
(2983) O Great Action, Great Protector, Accomplisher of all actions!
O Great-Souled One, foremost in the conduct of sentient beings, for the sake of all beings, homage be to you! (2984) [O you who have attained all perfections, O Buddha with the wisdom of omniscience!
[O you who possess great skillful means for all sentient beings, O you of great wisdom,] homage be to you! (2985)

O supreme among the most compassionate, whose very nature is compassion and mercy; O you who are always [endowed with] great loving-kindness, whose conduct encompasses all—homage be to you! (2986) O Lion of the Śākyas, Great Śākya, Śākya of the Śākyas, Great Sage!
O All-pervading One, Great Vinaya, you whose meaning is to be interpreted, the supreme Vinaya—homage be to you!
(2987) O Tathāgata who has attained equality with the *dharmadhātu*, O *dharmadhātu* itself; O Vajra Lord, Great Lord, mass of sentient beings—homage be to you! (2988)
O you of great radiance, great light, great heroism, and great strength;
O Great Hero, foremost among the brave, Śambhu, Śauri—homage be to you!
(2989) O Vast One, Self-Existent, Blessed One, Śākya Hero, Great Sage!

O Sage who embodies all, pure King of Dharma, homage be to you! (2990) Bodyless body, supreme body, accomplisher of the three bodies and the bodiless; universal body, great body, adamantine body—homage be to you! (2991)
O Speechless One, O Supreme Speech, O Revealer of the threefold speech!
O All-Speech, Great Speech, Vajra Speech, homage be to you! (2992) O Mindless One, Mind, Supreme Mind, O Revealer of the threefold mind and the mindless!
O All-Mind, Great Mind, O Vajra-Mind, homage be to you!
(2993) O Non-Vajra, Vajra, Foremost Vajra, Purifier of the Three Vajras and the Non-Vajra, O All-Vajra, Great Vajra, Vajra of Vajras, homage be to you! (2994)
O All-pervading One, Supreme above the Peak of Existence, Lord of Sugatas, Victor,
Great King of the Three Realms, Vairocana, homage be to you!
(2995) And whoever should hear these one hundred and eight names even once—
Whether one recites it or meditates upon it, one shall attain the state of all Buddhas.
(2996) O Protector, for the sake of the welfare of all sentient beings, I entreat you:
having generated great compassion, turn the wheel of Dharma! (2997)
Then the Blessed One Vairocana, having heard the words of the vow of the Lord of all Tathāgatas, summoned all the Tathāgatas and spoke thus:
"Proceed, O Blessed Tathāgatas, to return to the assembly. Then all the Tathāgatas, having returned to the assembly once more, spoke this verse:
For the sake of the welfare of all sentient beings, throughout all worlds and in every way,
may the wheel of Dharma be turned for the entire universe according to their respective needs.

As soon as this was spoken, the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Śākyamuni, manifested throughout all Buddha-fields, in all world-systems, before all sentient beings, and even within every circle of atoms, and set the wheel of Dharma in motion. (3000).
Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi spoke again this verse:
For the sake of the welfare of all sentient beings, throughout all worlds and in every way, let the universal vajra-wheel be set in motion according to the discipline of each.
Thus it was said.

(3001) Then, as soon as this had been spoken, in that very manner, throughout all the buddha-fields, even unto all the circles of the most minute atoms, the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Vajradhātu, set in motion all the vajra-wheels, beginning with the Vajradhātu.
(3002) Then, at that time, the Great Bodhisattva Trilokavijaya spoke this verse: (3003)
For the sake of the welfare of all sentient beings, throughout all worlds and in every way,
may they set in motion the universal wheel of wrath according to the needs of those to be disciplined.
Thus it was said.

(3004) Immediately upon these words being spoken, in all buddha-fields, even unto every circle of atoms, the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Trilokavijaya, set in motion the wheel of the wrathful deities of all the Tathāgatas.
(3005) Then the noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara spoke this verse: (3006)
For the sake of the welfare of all sentient beings, throughout all worlds and in every way,
may the universal lotus-wheel be set in motion according to the needs of those to be trained.
Thus it was said.
(3007) Then, as soon as this had been spoken, in all those buddha-fields, extending even to all the circles of atoms, the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Dharmarāja, set in motion the wheel of the Dharma.
(3008) Thereupon, the noble Mahābodhisattva Ākāśagarbha spoke this verse: (3009)
For the sake of the welfare of all sentient beings, throughout all worlds and in every way,
may the universal jewel-wheel be set in motion according to the needs of those to be trained.
Thus it was said.

(3010) Then, as soon as this had been uttered, all sentient beings—whether subtle or gross—who were dwelling within all the buddha-fields, beheld from every side the Tathāgata seated upon the lion-throne in the peaked pavilion atop the summit of Mount Sumeru, which is adorned with vajra-jewels and gems, and turning the wheels of the Vajradhātu and other mandalas.
(3011) Then, at that moment, the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi spoke these verses:
O Protector, act for the benefit of all sentient beings;
having descended into the human state, turn the supreme Wheel of Vajra.
Thus [he spoke].
(3012) Again, the Blessed One, having summoned all the Tathāgatas, spoke as follows:
"May the Blessed Tathāgatas proceed once more to assemble!
(3013) Then the Blessed Tathāgatas, having assembled again, entered the heart of the Blessed Vairocana. (3014)
Then the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Vairocana, having realized himself as the vajra of the body, speech, and mind of all Tathāgatas, spoke thus to Vajrapāṇi.
"Noble son, you too must enter completely into my heart, into the hearts of all Tathāgatas, into all the Vajra families, into all the maṇḍalas, and into the hearts of all Tathāgatas.
(3015) Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, authorized by all the Tathāgatas, spoke this verse: (3016)
For the sake of the welfare of all sentient beings,
I practice in every way in order to enter the vajra of the body, speech, and mind of all Buddhas.

Thus (3017), as soon as this had been spoken, as many Tathāgatas as there are atoms in all the world-systems throughout all the world-systems— each of those Tathāgatas, with bodies as numerous as the atoms in every world-system— entered the heart of the Blessed One Vairocana. (3018)

Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, having entered into all the bodies of all the Tathāgatas and the Blessed One Vairocana—in all places where speech proceeds, in all streams of the continuity of mind, in all diamond methods, in all major and minor limbs, in all locations, in all primary marks, in all secondary characteristics, in all pores of the skin, in all mandalas of atomic particles, and in their hearts—remained there. (3019)

Then the Blessed One, having recently attained perfect awakening, the Vajra of the body, speech, and mind of all Tathāgatas, realized himself as the body of all Tathāgatas. Departing from the summit of Mount Sumeru toward the seat of awakening (*bodhimaṇḍala*), he approached the foot of the Blessed One’s Bodhi tree; then, in accordance with worldly custom, he took up some grass and uttered this inspired utterance (*udāna*): (3020) "Aho! How supreme is the benefit for beings and for oneself among those who teach beings, that these steadfast ones abide even within the views of non-Buddhist heretics for the sake of those to be trained. (3021) Aho! How supreme is the benefit for beings and for oneself among those who teach beings, that these steadfast ones abide even within the views of non-Buddhist heretics for the sake of those to be trained.
By purifying the light of knowledge for the world that is undisciplined and blinded on all sides by wrong views, one shall attain the awakening of a Buddha.
Thus it was said.

(3022) Then the gods of the desire realm (*kāmāvacara*), not knowing the true reality, said to the Blessed One: "O sir, why do you seek refuge in such intense and bitter sufferings for the sake of awakening?"
the Blessed One, having spread those grasses and sat down, spoke thus to those gods:
"Proceed, friends, toward my attainment of awakening."
Thus it was said.
(3024) Then the gods belonging to the realm of desire, not understanding the meaning of what the Blessed One had spoken, approached Śakra, the lord of the gods.
Having approached, they reported this account to Śakra, the lord of the gods. (3025)

Then Śakra, the lord of the gods, surrounded by a host of deities belonging to the realm of all desires (*kāmāvacara*), reported this very matter to Mahābrahmā, the sovereign of the realm of form (*rūpāvacara*).
Then Mahābrahmā, together with all the deities of the realms of desire and form, reported that matter to Īśvara, the lord of the three worlds.
Thereupon Maheśvara, the lord of the three worlds, spoke thus to Nārāyaṇa and all the other lords of the gods.

(3028) "Friends, you should understand that the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the perfectly enlightened Buddha, having conformed to the ways of the world, will again manifest unexcelled, perfect enlightenment. (3029) Friends, let it not be thought that the Tathāgata is merely a human being."

In this very way, the Tathāgatas will come to be; they would strive for the attainment of the state of a god, but not for the state of a Tathāgata. Therefore, it is well that you should proceed there to pay them honor.
Then Maheśvara and all the other lords of the gods approached the seat of awakening (*bodhimaṇḍa*) and the Blessed One who was seated upon the seat of awakening;
having approached and bowed their heads at the feet of the Blessed One, they addressed the Blessed One in this way:
(3031) "Please, Blessed One, out of compassion for us, arise from this bed of craving, sit upon divine seats, and realize unexcelled, perfect, and complete awakening. (3032)
Then the Blessed One spoke thus to the lords of the gods:
"Friends, please grant me my unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment.
Then they spoke thus:
“O Blessed One, we are not capable of bestowing awakening. If we were capable, we ourselves would have already attained manifest perfect enlightenment. (3034)
Then the Blessed One, illuminating this very meaning, spoke further these verses:
"It is neither material nor immaterial, neither true nor false, and it is pure.
Having awakened to this knowledge, which is the awakening of the Buddhas, one becomes a Victor."
Thus (3036). Then those lords of the gods remained silent for a moment.
(3037) Then the Blessed One, rising from that grass seat, spoke thus to those gods:
"O sirs, strive to realize such knowledge as this.
They replied thus:
"We are not able, Blessed One," they said.
Then the Blessed One, sitting on that very seat, spoke this verse:
"Through the penetration of *namas*, make the thought of awakening (*bodhicitta*) firm;
having made the *vajra* firm within the being (*sattva*), meditate upon yourself as the Buddha."
Having said, "So be it," they all departed.

Then, when night had turned to dawn, the Blessed One—out of conformity with the world, having conquered Māra and awakened to unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment—praised Noble Vajrapāṇi, who dwells within his own heart and brings benefit and assistance to the entire realm of sentient beings without exception, with these one hundred and eight names:
"O Vajrasattva, Great Being, Mahāyāna, Great-Souled One, Great Light, Greatly Pure, Great Protector! Homage be to you!"
O Vajrarāja, Great Vajra, Vajra of all Tathāgatas,
Great Being, Great Hero, Great Skillful Means, homage be to you!
O Vajrarāga, Greatly Pure, All-Happiness, Great Bliss!
O supreme bliss, without beginning or end, Great Desire, homage be to you!
(3046) O Vajra-Excellent, Great Satisfier, you who grant the cry of "Well done!", O Great Joy, Great Delight, Perfect Rapture, homage be to you! (3047)
O Great King Vajraratna, O Great Lord of Self-Consecration!
O All-Jewels, O Great Splendor, O Ornament, homage be to you!
O Vajra-Tejas, O Great Tejas, O Great Radiance, O Great Luster!
Jinaprabha, Mahājvāla, Buddhaprabha—homage be to you! (3049) Vajraketu, Mahāketu, Mahādhvaja, Dhanaprada, Ākāśaketu, Mahāyaṣṭi, Tyāgadhvaja—homage be to you! (3050)
O Vajrahāsa, Great Laughter, Great Joy, Delighter;
O Prītivega, O Ratiprīte, O Dharmaprīte, homage be to you!
(3051) O Vajradharma, Great Dharma, Sattvadharma, Purifier!
O Buddha-dharma, supreme and most excellent Dharma, whose nature is passion, homage be to you!
(3052) O Vajra-sharp, great treasury, great-minded one of wisdom-knowledge, great weapon that cuts through evil, Buddha-weapon, homage be to you! (3053)
O Vajra-Cause, Great Wheel, Buddha-Wheel, Great Treasure!
O Foremost Dharma of all mandalas, Wheel of Dharma, homage be to you!
(3054) O Vajra-Speech, Great Speech, Non-proliferation, Great Syllable!
O syllable-less great recitation, speech of the Buddha, homage be to you! (3055) O Vajra-action, supreme good action, great action, performer of good action;
O secret worship, great worship, worship of the Buddha, homage be to you! (3056)
O Vajrarakṣa, great armor, supreme coat of mail, most firm;
O great protector, great essence, Buddha-vīrya, homage be to you!
(3057) O Vajrayakṣa, great wrathful one, terrifying to all the wicked!
O Great Expedient of all Buddhas, foremost Yakṣa, homage be to you!
(3058) O Vajra-junction, Great Seal, binder of the great samaya, O Great Fist, supreme among excellent seals, O Vajra-fist, homage be to you! (3059)
You are to be saluted, honored, worshipped, and likewise revered by the Tathāgatas,
because you are said to be the bodhicitta that is without beginning or end.
Having encountered you, all the Victors, as well as the Buddhas and the heroic Bodhisattvas, [attain their goals].
They have arisen and will arise as the supreme causes for the awakening of a Buddha.
(3061) Homage to you, Vajrasattva; homage to you, Vajraratna.
Homage to you, Vajradharma; homage to you, Vajrakarman. (3062)
By whatever merit is gained from praising you with noble names and bowing down with sincere devotion, may everyone indeed attain the enlightenment of a Buddha.
Whoever correctly recites these supreme one hundred and eight names, [shall obtain that same merit].
"Even with a single instance of sublime devotion, one shall attain the state of all Buddhas.
Thus spoke the Blessed Buddha.
Then the Great Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, together with all those Tathāgatas, bestowed shouts of "Well done! with a single voice.
Excellent for you, O Vajrasattva; excellent for you, O Vajraratna!
Excellent for you, O Vajradharma; excellent for you, O Vajrakarman!
This well-spoken sūtra is the unsurpassed Vajrayāna.
The secret of all Tathāgatas, the compendium of the Mahāyāna.

Thus spoke the Blessed One. All the Tathāgatas, together with the noble Bodhisattvas who were established within their own hearts, being uplifted in mind, rejoiced in what the Blessed One had spoken. Thus ends the Mahāyāna sūtra titled *Sarvatathāgatatattvasaṃgraha*, including its concluding tantra.
